The inverse of Archive RAW Images: pull raw camera files back into the working library after you archived and removed them.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Restore Archived Images panel.


Point the Archive or Backup File control at a raw-image archive ZIP (or an All Data and Artifacts backup that includes raw images) and click Restore Archived Images.
A window opens to validate the file and preview how many of its images are missing from your library; it restores only the missing ones — it never overwrites or duplicates photos you already have. Safe to run against any archive, any time you need the originals back.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The restore window, showing the validated archive and the missing-vs-restorable preview.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/backups/re.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Backups/Restore From Backup.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/backups/re.title: Restore From Backup
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/backups/re.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}CreateBackupRestore FromBackupArchive RAWImages


The Restore From Backup panel of  Restore brings a backup package back. Point the Backup File control at a Prisma backup .zip, then click Restore Backup.
This is also the supported way to bring an existing Calibration library into a new blank Prisma Suite. Create an All Data and Artifacts backup in the old app (including raw images if the new copy should retain them), then restore that ZIP in the blank Suite. Do not copy individual SQLite, asset, or model files into Calibration\Workspace.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The restore panel showing a validated package preview and the confirmation field.


It never restores blind
First the app validates the ZIP — checking that it is a Prisma package with an intact database — and previews what it contains and what restoring will replace. It then asks you to type the displayed confirmation phrase. Before replacing the database, the app creates a pre-restore Essential Data Only safety backup. The completed restore reports that backup’s path; it can be selected later through Restore From Backup if you need to return to the previous database state.
What gets replaced
Depends on the package (see Create Backup for the types):

Essential Data Only — replaces the database only. Managed images and geometry files stay in place.
All Data and Artifacts, with raw images — replaces everything, raw photos included.
All Data and Artifacts, without raw images — replaces everything else but keeps your current raw photos in place; the package has none to supply.

When it finishes, the app refreshes itself and the restored data is live. For migration, verify the Logbook, Images, Filaments, Geometries, and Modeling status before deleting or retiring the previous installation. Keep the source installation and backup until that review is complete.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/backups/in.title: Backup / Restore
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/backups/in.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}MaintenanceBackup /RestoreCreateBackupRestore FromBackupArchive RAWImagesRestore ArchivedImages


The top bar’s Backup / Restore button opens one dialog with four panels. Use these workflows to create supported, portable packages of the app’s managed database, geometry files, images, measurements, and model artifacts.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Backup / Restore dialog with its four panels.



Create Backup — package your work into a ZIP you can move somewhere safe.
Restore From Backup — bring a package back, after the app checks it and you confirm.
Archive RAW Images — move the bulky raw camera files out of the working library, safely.
Restore Archived Images — pull archived raw files back in when you need them.

Only one of these runs at a time, and none while a Maintenance job is running. Each is start-then-report: kick it off, watch the progress panel, and the dialog refreshes when it’s done.
The app also creates automatic SQLite restore points at startup when enough time has elapsed and prunes old restore points automatically. They contain only the database and are surfaced through the recovery screen if the database fails its startup checks. They are not portable backups and contain no images; the packages you create here remain the supported way to protect and move your work.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/calibratio.title: Tutorials
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/calibratio.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}TutorialsMaintenance




                  
                  Tutorial outline for the author 
                  
                

These walkthroughs need final screenshots, tested physical procedures, and real examples. The structure below is intentionally visible so those pieces do not disappear from the documentation backlog.


Your first calibration strip
Goal: carry one simple, single-geometry sample from an empty library to current calibration models.

Register the filament and explain each policy setting used.
Create or select a one-variable-role sample geometry.
Create the sample and label the physical strip with its sample ID.
Export, slice, and print the geometry without changing its dimensions or role assignments.
Capture a blank image and sample image in one fixed session.
Assign the images and open-side direction, process the sample, and review the extraction.
Inspect the sample under Modeling and run Fit Models.

Author material still needed: the final printer/slicer procedure, capture settings, and one representative accepted extraction.
A Geometry Bundle with Multi
Goal: create and keep custody of a batch produced by one Multi shared-filament assignment across a mapped Geometry Bundle.

Show the bundle’s shared-slot mapping.
Select Geometry Bundle, set one shared slot to Multi, and preview the resulting sample count.
Demonstrate a physical labeling or tray system before printing.
Place the batch’s photos in the Calibration Inbox, import them, and assign them with CSV Bulk Assignment.
Review how the batch appears under Modeling by filament.

A transparent strip that needs Manual Processing
Goal: show the expected recovery path when automatic strip detection cannot find a low-contrast sample.

Process the ready sample and identify its Failed or Flagged state.
Open Manual Process and place corners in the required order.
Accept the manual extraction candidate.
Perform the separate final Accept under Post-Processing Review.

Author material still needed: a real transparent-strip image and examples of good and bad corner placement.
Curate evidence and refit
Goal: investigate a suspect model comparison without automatically discarding useful evidence.

Compare measured and predicted Transmission and Appearance domains.
Check the source assignment and extraction before changing fit inclusion.
Demonstrate one justified swatch exclusion and one justified whole-sample exclusion.
Review Filament Coverage and run Fit Models again.

Author material still needed: real cases where disagreement means bad evidence and where it means valuable model coverage.
Back up, archive RAW images, and recover
Goal: demonstrate the difference between a portable backup, a RAW image archive, and an automatic SQLite restore point.

Create Essential Data Only and All Data and Artifacts backups.
Create and verify a RAW image archive before removing archived images from the active library.
Restore missing RAW images from the archive.
Preview a backup restore and identify the pre-restore safety backup.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/filaments/.title: Filaments
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/filaments/.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}FilamentsGeometries


The Filaments tab is the app’s filament library. Add a filament here before assigning it to a calibration sample.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Filaments tab.


Read the library
The line above the table shows the number of filaments and how many have a fitted profile. One row represents one filament:

Filament — the color name, with its color chip.
Manufacturer — the brand.
ID — the filament’s permanent identifier.
Samples — how many samples use it.
Processed — how many of those are measured.
Profile — pending (no data yet), strips only (measured but not yet fitted), or profiled.

Only Filament, Manufacturer, and Profile are sortable. A profiled filament may still be unavailable for new generation if it is excluded from model fits.
Add a filament
Click + New Filament, then fill in:

Filament — the color name. Required.
Manufacturer — the brand. Required.
Material — the material type, such as PLA.
Hex Color — the color chip shown in the app. It does not describe the filament’s measured optical behavior.
Notes — optional information you want to keep with the filament.

The drawer builds a permanent Generated ID from the manufacturer and color name. Review it before clicking Create — the drawer refuses to save if the ID already exists in the library, and the ID does not change if you rename the filament later.
Policy settings

White-cap eligible — allows the filament to serve as a white base or cap and identifies it as white during model fitting. Use this only for suitable white or near-white filaments.
Special role: Transparent and Special role: Black — descriptive tags. They do not exclude the filament from fitting.
Exclude from model fits — removes every sample containing this filament from model fitting and makes the filament unavailable for new generator runs. It does not delete the filament or its existing data.

Use Exclude from model fits to retire a filament without breaking samples that already reference it. To exclude one questionable sample instead, use the controls under Modeling.


                  
                  Camera Transform classification 
                  
                

White-cap eligible is also the filament classification used by The Camera Transform. There is no separate camera-classification control.


View, edit, or delete
Click a row to open its drawer. Used By lists every sample containing the filament. Click Edit to change its name, manufacturer, material, displayed color, policy, or notes.
Delete works only when the filament has no samples or fitted profile. Otherwise, exclude it instead.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Geometries/Export Sample Geometry.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.title: Export Sample Geometry
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ManageBundlesExport SampleGeometrySampleLogbook


This dialog writes a geometry’s printable 3D files. Reach it from Create + Export in the builder, or from Export in Geometry Details.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Export Sample Geometry dialog.


Give the export a name, then choose one or both formats:

Export STEP — one model containing a labeled solid body for each material role.
Export STLs — one file for each material role.

The bodies and files are labeled LR_01, LR_02, and so on. These are material roles, not individual printer layers. Match each label to the filament assigned to the same role in New Samples. LR_01 is the bottom material role.

Exports are written under Calibration\Output\Steps. STL sets use a named subfolder. If an export with the same name already exists, the app asks before overwriting it.
Once an export request starts, the dialog remains open and its name, close, and export controls stay disabled until the request succeeds or fails. Closing the window, pressing Escape, or clicking outside cannot hide a still-running export.
Print it faithfully
The physical strip must match its sample record:

Import the STEP as separate bodies, or import the complete set of role-specific STLs.
Confirm the slicer did not scale the geometry or change its units.
Assign each LR body exactly the filament recorded for that role in New Samples.
Inspect the sliced layer preview. Every role must remain present, and the variable swatches must retain their intended thickness progression.
Keep the printed strip associated with its sample ID.



                  
                  Printing procedure draft 
                  
                

Add the validated slicer workflow, printer profile assumptions, filament-change or multi-material procedure, and any required purge guidance here after testing the final release workflow.


Export several geometries
The Geometries toolbar’s Export Geometry Files button opens the batch export workflow:

Missing Only writes exports that do not exist.
Force Export may overwrite existing exports after confirmation.
Only Geometries Used By Samples limits the scope; All Geometries covers the library.
STEP and STL select the output formats.

Run the preflight, review its scope, then click Export Files.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.title: Geometry Details
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}New SampleGeometryGeometryDetailsManageBundles


Click any row on the Geometries tab to open that geometry’s details.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The geometry details drawer.


The drawer shows the geometry’s Alias, ID, Bundle membership, Last Modified, and a Used By list of every sample created from it. Two sections cover its files:

Exported Files — the print files written for you, in Prisma’s output folder. These are the ones you open in your slicer; each entry has a Copy Path button — click it, then paste straight into your slicer’s open dialog.
Managed Artifacts — a summary of the app’s internal copies. Leave these alone; the app maintains them itself.

Header actions

Export — write fresh print files for this geometry. See Export Sample Geometry.
Edit — switches to edit mode, with Save, Discard, and Delete.

Only the alias and bundle membership are editable — a geometry’s material roles and thicknesses never change after creation. Bundle membership can also be changed directly in the drawer; adding or removing it applies immediately. Delete is refused while any sample or bundle still uses the geometry.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.title: Manage Bundles
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}GeometryDetailsManageBundlesExport SampleGeometry


A bundle groups geometries and maps their material roles to shared filament slots. It lets one set of filament choices create coordinated samples across several geometries.
A bundle does not combine its geometries into one print file or arrange them on a print plate. Export and arrange each geometry separately.
Manage Bundles on the Geometries tab opens the bundle drawer: bundles on the left and the selected bundle on the right.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Manage Bundles drawer with a bundle selected.


Create the bundle

Enter a name in the new-bundle row and click Create.
Select the bundle.
Under Bundle Geometries, click Add Geometries… and choose its members.
Under Bundle Filament Mapping, click Edit Mapping.

Map shared filament slots
Each geometry has its own roles, such as LR_01 and LR_02. The mapping editor adds shared slots named Shared Filament A, Shared Filament B, and so on. Map every geometry role to one of these slots.
A shared slot means “use the same filament in every role mapped here.” The roles do not need the same LR number or role type.




















Shared slotGeometry 1Geometry 2Shared Filament ALR_01, FixedLR_02, VariableShared Filament BLR_02, VariableLR_01, Fixed
Selecting one filament for Shared Filament A during sample creation fills both mapped roles. A shared slot may also feed several roles in the same geometry.
Drag a shared-filament token onto a role, or select the token and then click the role. Add slots with + Add Shared Filament Slot. When every role is assigned, click Save Mapping.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Bundle Filament Mapping editor — member geometries on one side, shared filament slots on the other.


The bundle status reports its readiness:

Unmapped — no complete mapping has been saved.
Incomplete — one or more roles are not assigned.
Mapped — every role is assigned and the bundle can create samples.
Invalid — the saved mapping no longer matches the bundle’s current records.

Adding a geometry makes the bundle incomplete until its roles are mapped. You may save an incomplete mapping, but New Samples will not allow that bundle to be selected.
During sample creation, assigning one filament to every shared slot creates one sample per member geometry. Setting one shared slot to Multi creates one sample per geometry for every selected filament. See Creating New Samples for the count rules.
Rename, remove, or delete
Use a member’s remove control to take it out of the bundle. Select a bundle to Rename or Delete it. Deleting a bundle does not delete its geometries.
Figure for review

A shared filament slot follows the mapping, not a layer’s LR number or vertical position. Here one filament identity fills the only variable role in one geometry, a fixed bottom role in another, and a fixed top role in a third.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Geometries/New Sample Geometry.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.title: New Sample Geometry
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}GeometriesNew SampleGeometryGeometryDetails


+ New Sample Geometry on the Geometries tab opens the strip builder.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The New Sample Geometry builder, with layer cards and the live strip preview.


Before you build
Plan the material stack from bottom to top. LR_01 is the bottom material role. Higher numbers sit above it. These are material roles, not individual printer layers; each role may span many printer layers using one filament.
Every geometry requires exactly one Variable role. Add Fixed roles where the calibration design needs constant-thickness material above or below it.
If you need the sample to support Color Model v1, keep all fixed roles below the variable role. Color Model v1 does not use geometries with a fixed role above the variable role.
Build the strip

Under Strip Layout, set Swatch Width (mm), Swatch Height (mm), Number of Swatches, Spine Width (mm), and Spine Thickness (mm).
Under Variable Layer Increment, enter First Swatch Thickness (mm) and Swatch-to-Swatch Increment (mm), then click Fill Values to populate an even sequence. You can also edit the individual swatch values directly.
Click + Add Layer Role for each fixed role and enter its thickness.
Drag roles into the physical order shown in the preview. The builder displays the top of the stack first; LR_01 remains the bottom role.
Give the geometry an Alias. Bundle membership is optional.

The role types mean:

Variable — thickness changes across the swatches.
Fixed — one thickness continues across every swatch.

Fixed does not mean backing, support, white, or color. Those properties come from the filament assigned when a sample is created.
Spine Total
Spine Total is the spine’s total height, not the swatch stack’s height. The builder starts it at the tallest swatch stack plus 0.08 mm and will not allow a lower value. Any spine material above the swatches belongs to the topmost role, so review this value after reordering roles.

The Visual Preview updates as you work. The Top View shows the strip footprint and swatch divisions proportionally; the Side View uses the same horizontal scale and exaggerates thickness vertically so the layer structure remains visible. The Strip Diagram Preview retains the compact role/thickness summary. Confirm the role order and thicknesses there before saving.
Save the geometry

Create — save the geometry into the library.
Create + Export — save it, then open Export Sample Geometry.

The role order and thicknesses cannot be edited after creation. If they are wrong, create another geometry. Only the alias and bundle membership can change later.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.title: Geometries
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/geometries.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}FilamentsGeometriesSampleLogbookNew SampleGeometryGeometryDetailsManageBundlesExport SampleGeometry


The Geometries tab contains reusable calibration-strip designs. A geometry defines the strip’s swatches, material roles, and thicknesses. It does not specify which filaments fill those roles. Filaments are assigned when you create a sample in the Sample Logbook.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Geometries tab.


Understand the role stack
Each material role becomes a separate body in the exported model. Roles are labeled from the bottom of the printed stack upward: LR_01 is the bottom role, LR_02 is above it, and so on.
A geometry has exactly one Variable role. Its thickness changes from swatch to swatch so one strip measures several thicknesses. Every Fixed role keeps one thickness across the strip. Fixed describes thickness, not purpose: a fixed role may sit above or below the variable role and may contain any filament.
The builder displays the physical stack from top to bottom. Moving a role changes its position and updates its LR label. For a fuller explanation, see Sample Geometry.
Read the library
Each row shows the strip diagram, Alias, Bundle, # Layers (the number of material roles), Used by, and Last modified. Click a row to inspect its ID, bundle membership, exports, and samples.
What you do here

+ New Sample Geometry — design a new sample geometry. See New Sample Geometry.
Click a row — inspect its details, export it, rename it, or change its bundle membership. See Geometry Details.
Manage Bundles — map roles across several geometries for coordinated sample creation. See Manage Bundles.
Export Geometry Files — export STEP or STL files for geometries used by samples or for the whole library.

Geometry files
The geometry definition is the permanent record. Printable STEP and STL files are generated from it and may not exist until you export them. See Export Sample Geometry for the required role-to-filament matching.
Export Geometry Files opens a batch workflow. Missing Only creates absent files. Force Export can replace existing exports after confirmation. You may export Only Geometries Used By Samples or All Geometries, in STEP, STL, or both formats.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ass.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Images/Assign Images/CSV Assignment Import.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ass.title: CSV Bulk Assignment
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ass.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}AssignImagesCSV BulkAssignmentProcessingQueue


When you have many samples to set up, CSV Bulk Assignment assigns each sample’s image, blank image, and orientation from a spreadsheet. You will find it in the Image Inbox on Assign Images. Place every referenced image in the Calibration Inbox, click Import from Inbox, and import the images before opening this dialog; the spreadsheet refers to the imported filenames.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The CSV Bulk Assignment window.


It works in three steps: get the template, fill it in, then check and import.
1. Get the template
Download CSV Template saves a spreadsheet with four columns to fill in:

























ColumnWhat goes in itSample IDThe sample’s id (like exp-123), or just its number.Sample ImageThe sample image’s filename.Blank ImageA blank’s id, or a photo filename (an unregistered photo here becomes a blank).OrientationWhich way the strip’s open side faces: U, D, L, or R.
Fill one row per sample in any spreadsheet program, then save it.
2. Check it
Choose CSV loads your file. Validate CSV checks it without changing anything and shows a preview — how many rows are ready, how many are blocked, and which photos it would register as new blanks. A row is blocked (and skipped) when its sample or photo can’t be found, or the photo is already assigned somewhere else.
3. Import
Commit with Import Assignments (every row clean) or Import Valid Rows (skip the blocked ones). If any row names a photo that isn’t a blank yet, the app asks you to confirm registering those first.
Import only fills in fresh samples — it skips any sample that already has a photo, a blank, or results. So it’s a safe first pass, never a way to overwrite work you’ve already done.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ass.title: Assign Images
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ass.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ImagesAssignImagesProcessingQueueCSV BulkAssignment


Before the app can read colors from a sample, it needs two images: the sample image (the printed strip on the lightbox) and a blank image (the same lit lightbox with nothing on it). The blank image lets the app correct for uneven illumination.
For that to work, the app aligns the blank image with the sample image point by point — so the camera must not move, and the lighting must not change, between the blank and the samples in that session.
Capture one consistent session

Fix the camera and lightbox in place before capturing the blank image. If either moves, begin a new session with a new blank.
Keep exposure, focus, camera orientation, and lighting unchanged throughout the session. Disable automatic changes where your camera workflow allows it.
Let the lightbox reach a stable state before capturing the blank and samples.
Keep the complete strip and enough surrounding lightbox visible for extraction; do not clip the strip at the frame edge.
Preserve a reliable association between each image and its physical sample ID until assignment is complete.

The current Image Inbox imports .cr2, .dng, .tif, and .tiff files. Put
supported files in Calibration\Inbox before using Import from Inbox. If
you are unsure which installation is active, Open Inbox Folder opens the
exact folder used by this Calibration app.


                  
                  Capture procedure draft 
                  
                

Add the validated camera mode, exposure method, focus procedure, lightbox warm-up guidance, framing example, and session naming convention here after the final physical workflow is documented.



You capture everything on the lightbox outside the app; this screen connects those images to your samples. Open the Images tab and stay on the Assign Images subtab. It has three panes, left to right.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Assign Images subtab — Registered Blanks (left), Image Inbox (center), Assign Images and Blanks (right).


Image Inbox (center)
Where images enter the app. Put supported files in Calibration\Inbox, then
click Import from Inbox. Open Inbox Folder opens that location in File
Explorer. The top-bar Refresh Data action only refreshes the displayed
state; it does not import waiting files. Nothing on this screen can use an
image until you import it.
Imported images are grouped into Unassigned, Assigned, and Ignored. Each usable image has a rotate button and an × button to ignore it. Rotating an assigned image clears that sample’s open-side direction so it can be set again. Once a sample is measured, its image cannot be rotated until the result is rejected or reset.
Click a photo to select it. Below the grid, Selected Image names your pick, with two actions:

← Register as Blank turns the selected image into a lightbox reference (see the left pane).
Assign Image to Sample → attaches it to the selected sample as its sample image.

Registered Blanks (left)
Your list of registered blank images. Add one by selecting an image and clicking ← Register as Blank, or by dragging an image onto this pane.
Use one blank for every sample captured in the same unchanged session. Click a blank, then Assign Blank to Sample → to attach it to the selected sample. Click the small × on a blank card to unregister it.
Assign Images and Blanks (right)
Samples are split into Ready For Processing and Needs Assignment. Click a sample to make it the target for the → buttons in the other panes. Each card shows its strip diagram and filament list, plus an image slot and a blank slot. Click the small × on either slot to remove that assignment.
Every card also has a four-arrow control for the strip’s open-side direction. Choose the arrow that points toward the open side in the sample image so the app reads the swatches in the correct order. A sample is not ready until it has a sample image, blank image, and open-side direction. Ready samples show a ready badge.
You can also drag an image from the inbox directly onto a sample card’s empty image or blank slot.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

One sample card showing its image slot, blank slot, open-side direction control, and ready badge.


Before processing
For every sample, confirm that the physical strip, sample record, sample image, blank image, and open-side direction all agree. When each sample shows ready, continue to Processing Queue.
Doing more at once
Prisma keeps managed copies of imported images. Two Image Inbox actions operate on that managed set:

Clean Up Unused removes imported images that no sample uses from active custody and moves their source files to Removed Images inside the inbox.
CSV Bulk Assignment assigns sample images, blank images, and orientations
to many samples at once. See CSV Assignment Import.

To see how the blank is actually used when the app reads a strip, see Extraction.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/pro.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Images/Processing Queue/Manual Processing.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/pro.title: Manual Processing
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/pro.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ProcessingQueueManualProcessingModeling


When the app can’t find a strip on its own, you show it where the strip is by clicking the four corners. This happens most with very see-through filaments that blend into the lightbox. Open it with Manual Process on any sample in Failed or Flagged for Manual Processing (see Processing Queue).


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Manual Processing window — the sample image with the corner-clicking instructions.


The window shows the sample’s photo. Click the strip’s four corners in this order: top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. Placed corners can be dragged to nudge them.
The app reads the strip inside those corners and uses the sample’s open-side direction to order the swatches.
Then:

Extract & Process reads the strip from your corners and shows a preview. Nothing is saved yet.
Reset Corners clears them so you can start over.
Cancel stops a run in progress.

Once the preview looks right:

Accept commits the manual corner placement and extraction. In a batch, it moves you to the next sample.
Retry discards the preview so you can replace the corners.

The committed manual result still goes to Post-Processing Review like any other extraction. It does not become the trusted measurement until you give it the final Accept there (see Processing Queue).
To fix many at once, Manual Process All opens the same window as a queue that walks through every flagged sample in turn.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/pro.title: Processing Queue
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/pro.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}AssignImagesProcessingQueueModelingManualProcessing


This is where the app reads the colors out of your samples, and where you approve the results. Extraction runs as a batch; then you check each result and accept the good ones. Only an accepted result becomes the sample’s trusted measurement — the one the models are allowed to learn from.
Open the Images tab and switch to the Processing Queue subtab. A sample appears here once it is ready: it has a sample image, blank image, and open-side direction (see Assign Images).


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Processing Queue, showing its two panes — the queue on the left, the review on the right.


The screen has two panes. The left, Pre-Processing Queue, is work still to do. The right, Post-Processing Review, is finished results waiting for your yes-or-no.
Extract — the left pane
Samples ready to measure sit under Ready to Process. Each card shows the sample’s strip layout, sample image, blank image, and open-side direction — a last chance to spot a mismatched assignment before processing.
The one button you need is Process All, which measures every ready sample in one batch: it finds the strip in each photo, straightens it, corrects the lighting with the blank, and reads each swatch’s color. A progress panel names the sample being worked on and counts processed, flagged, failed, and remaining. (For what happens inside, see Extraction.)
Each card also has its own actions: Process (measure just this one), Flag (set it aside for hand placement — see below), and Reassign (detach the photo and send the sample back to Assign Images).
Only one extraction runs at a time. Start another while one is going — or while the models are being built — and the app asks you to wait. That’s expected, not an error.
Approve — the right pane
Every finished result lands in Post-Processing Review, and counts for nothing until you act on it. Each card shows the sample’s photo and blank, the strip the app cut out of the photo, and a mock strip built from the colors it read — with the measured thicknesses labeled — so you can compare at a glance:

Accept — keep this result as the sample’s trusted measurement. This is the step that matters: only accepted results feed the models.
Reject — throw it away and send the sample back to be measured again.

Accept All and Reject All apply the same choice to every card at once.
What to inspect before Accept

Confirm that the extracted strip includes the complete physical strip and is not cut off or dominated by surrounding lightbox.
Confirm that the swatches run in the same order as the sample record. A reversed order usually means the open-side direction is wrong.
Compare the extracted strip with the measured-color preview for obvious boundary, glare, contamination, or swatch-placement errors.
Confirm that the sample image and blank image came from the same unchanged capture session.

Reject an extraction when the image assignment, strip boundary, orientation, or measured swatches are wrong. Do not reject a sound measurement merely because it later disagrees with the current model; use Sample Comparison to investigate that separately.
When a sample won’t extract
Sometimes the app can’t find the strip on its own — most often with very see-through filaments that blend into the lightbox. Those samples don’t get measured; they land in one of two spots in the left pane:

Failed — the app tried and couldn’t. Nothing is saved.
Flagged for Manual Processing — you or the app set it aside for hand placement.

For these, click Manual Process to place the strip’s corners by hand — see Manual Processing. Each card also offers Reassign (send it back to Assign Images to fix the photo) and Unflag (put it back in the normal queue). Each group’s header has a Manual Process All button to walk the whole group through hand placement in one sitting.
In short

Process All to measure the ready batch.
Send anything in Failed or Flagged through Manual Processing.
Accept the good results, Reject the bad ones.
Accepted samples are now trusted measurements — continue to Modeling.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ind.title: Images
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/images/ind.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}SampleLogbookImagesModelingAssignImagesProcessingQueue


The Images tab is where the physical world enters the app. Everything before it is bookkeeping: the Sample Logbook records what you printed, but the app still knows nothing about how those strips actually behave. The photographs you took on the lightbox hold that information, and this tab turns them into numbers — one measured color for every swatch on every strip.
That happens in two steps, shown as two subtabs:

Assign Images — tell the app which sample image belongs to which sample. Each sample needs a sample image, a blank image of the empty lit lightbox, and an open-side direction so the app reads the swatches in the right order.
Processing Queue — the app finds each strip in its photo, straightens it, corrects the lighting, and reads the color of every swatch. You review what it read and Accept the results that look right.

Do them in that order: a sample can’t be measured until its photos are attached.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Images tab, showing its two subtabs — Assign Images and Processing Queue.


Why this step matters
A sample’s accepted extraction is its trusted measurement: the color of each swatch at each printed thickness. Modeling fits the calibration models from accepted measurements. The two checks on this tab — matching images to the correct physical strips and reviewing extractions before accepting them — determine which evidence reaches those fits.
Where you are in the loop
You arrive here after creating samples in the Sample Logbook and printing and photographing the strips. As you work, each sample’s status advances: unassigned → incomplete → ready (sample image, blank image, and open-side direction assigned) → processed (measured, awaiting review) → accepted. Once accepted, the sample is available to Modeling.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.title: Fit Models
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}StandardOperationsFitModelsRe-extractSample Images


This is the step that turns your accepted measurements into Calibration’s current working color models. Nothing you measure or curate reaches a future published library until you run it, but fitting alone does not change the library a Generator is already using.
You can start it from two places — the Fit Models button on the Modeling tab, or the Fit Models card in Maintenance. They’re the same job.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Fit Models workflow dialog.


What it builds
One run fits and atomically replaces Calibration’s current model set from the currently included evidence:

Color Model v1 and Color Model v2 — the two color models.
The Camera Transform — fitted when needed; Force Camera Transform fits it regardless of its current status.

When it finishes successfully, the status entries on Modeling return to Current. Generator still sees only its selected immutable published library. To make this fitted generation available there, use Publish Models in Calibration’s top bar, then select the newly installed library from Generator’s Models menu.
Running it
It follows the standard rhythm — Start Workflow → Run Preflight → Fit Models (see Standard Operations). Once fitting begins, it runs to completion: Prisma does not offer a Cancel button because the nested fitting and model-publication stages do not have one proven safe stopping boundary. Fitting does not change samples, measurements, or exclusions, but a successful run replaces Calibration’s current internal artifacts. It does not retain an operator-facing history of old working fits: if you need a stable generation for printing or comparison, publish it before fitting again. What a fit produces depends on the evidence you included, so review that first on Modeling.
Like every heavy job, it runs alone: it won’t start while an extraction, re-extraction, or backup is running, and the app says so rather than queueing it.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.filePath: Prisma Calibration/How To Use/Maintenance/Re-extract Sample Images.md
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.title: Re-extract Sample Images
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}FitModelsRe-extractSample ImagesBackup /Restore


Re-measures samples that already have accepted measurements — for example after the app’s measuring improved, or when a batch needs redoing. It’s built to be safe: your accepted measurements are untouched until you explicitly save, and you review every new result first.
Start it from the Re-extract Sample Images card in Maintenance.



                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Re-extract Sample Images dialog with its three scope controls.


Choosing the scope

Data — Complete, Transmission Only, or Appearance Only: which half of the color data to recompute (Transmission vs Appearance). Complete redoes both.
Coordinates — Use Accepted Coordinates reuses each strip’s already-accepted corner positions; Re-detect Strip finds each strip from scratch (and forces Data to Complete — a full re-detect has to redo everything).
Samples — All Accepted, or Selected Samples with a box for ids, separated by commas or spaces (e.g. exp-055, exp-056).

The run

Run Preflight — counts the targets and warns which ones will need hand-placed corners.
Extract Images — re-measures into a fresh candidate set. Nothing accepted has changed.
Samples the app couldn’t auto-detect come first as a manual step: place their corners by hand (same idea as Manual Processing), then Review Results.

Review, then commit


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Review Extracted Images screen, showing a before/after strip pair with the Save/Skip toggle.


Review Extracted Images lists every candidate with a before/after comparison of its strips. For each sample, choose Save (keep the new result) or Skip (keep the old one); failures offer Retry. You must decide every sample before you can commit.
Then:

Save Results — writes only the kept candidates over the old measurements, and shows the final counts.
Discard Results — throws the whole candidate set away; nothing changes.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.title: Standard Operations
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}MaintenanceStandardOperationsFitModels


Every Maintenance operation except Re-extract Sample Images runs through the same dialog, in the same three beats. Nothing is written until you’ve seen the preview and pressed the run button.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

An operation’s workflow dialog, showing preflight results above the run button.


1 — Start Workflow
Select the operation’s card and click Start Workflow. The dialog restates what the operation does and shows its options, where it has any:

Mode — for the rebuilds and exports: Missing Only (fix only what’s absent or broken) versus Force Rebuild / Force Export (redo everything in scope). Missing Only is the usual choice.
Export Options — for Export Geometry Files: Only Geometries Used By Samples or All Geometries, plus STEP / STL checkboxes.
Fit Options — for Fit Models: a Force Camera Transform checkbox (see Fit Models).

2 — Run Preflight
Run Preflight inspects your data and reports what the operation would do — a summary, warnings, and any blockers — without changing anything. If preflight finds a blocker, the run button stays disabled.
3 — Run
The run button is named for the job — Run Audit, Run Maintenance, Export Files, or Fit Models. Progress streams into the dialog. Operations that can stop safely show Cancel; after you click it, the button changes to Cancelling… and the dialog remains open until the current safe unit finishes. Operations labeled Runs to completion do not offer Cancel. A Result section then shows the outcome and where the report was saved. (Reports collect in the Activity Log.)
The one extra gate: running Export Geometry Files in overwrite mode asks you to type a confirmation phrase first, since it replaces existing files.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.title: Maintenance
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/maintenanc.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}TutorialsMaintenanceBackup /RestoreStandardOperationsFitModelsRe-extractSample Images


The top bar’s Maintenance button opens a dialog of housekeeping operations — checks, rebuilds, exports, and Fit Models. Operations appear as cards grouped by category; click one to select it, and Start Workflow appears on the right. Each card says whether it is Read-only or writes something. A grayed-out card is unavailable, with the reason shown.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Maintenance dialog with an operation selected.


Only one maintenance job runs at a time — and none while a backup or restore is running. Start a second and the app tells you what’s already going.
The operations

Audit — four read-only checks (Audit Library Integrity, Audit Missing Artifacts, Audit Orphaned Artifacts, Audit Source Image Custody). They report problems — missing files, stray files, photo custody gaps — without touching anything.
Images — Rebuild Image Previews and Rebuild Extraction Images Only regenerate the app’s derived images if they’re missing or broken; Re-extract Sample Images re-measures samples, with review — see Re-extract Sample Images.
Calibration Models — Fit Models builds the color models. See Fit Models.
Geometry Artifacts — Regenerate STEPs/STLs rebuilds the app’s internally managed geometry files; Export Geometry Files writes user-facing print files (the same workflow opened from the Geometries toolbar).
System Maintenance — SQLite Integrity Check (read-only database health check) and Quarantine Orphaned Artifacts (sets aside files nothing references — not deleted, moved into Calibration’s app-managed maintenance quarantine, where you can inspect or recover them through the reported path).

Everything except Re-extract runs through the same three-step rhythm — see Standard Operations.
The Activity Log
The dialog header’s Activity Log button lists every past run — Name, Type, Status, File Name — newest first. Each operation saves a report; this is where they live. Clear Log deletes only those report files — never your samples, photos, backups, or data.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Maintenance Activity Log window with a few past runs listed.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/c.title: Curating Samples
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/c.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ModelingOverviewCuratingSamplesFilamentCoverageSampleComparison


The Samples subtab of Modeling decides, strip by strip, what the models learn. One row per sample: Sample, Strip, Filaments, Fit State, and Extracted Appearance.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Samples subtab with its filters and Fit State column.


Exclude and Include
Click a row to open its comparison drawer. Under Sample Exclusion, use Exclude Sample or Include Sample to change whether the whole sample counts in the next fit. The measurement is not deleted; it is only withheld.
If only one swatch is suspect, use the controls under Swatch Exclusion in the same drawer. The sample’s Sample Record provides the same per-swatch control. Changing either kind of exclusion marks affected models Stale; run Fit Models after you finish curating.
Finding the rows you care about

The Filter dropdown narrows the list: All, Included, Excluded, Filament Excluded, Has Excluded Swatches, Stale, and Missing Model.
Filaments… opens a picker; chosen filaments appear as chips and the list shows only samples containing them. Clear removes them. Use it to review every strip a suspect filament touched.
Click the Sample, Filaments, or Fit State column heading to sort; the controls row counts how many rows are showing.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/f.title: Filament Coverage
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/f.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}CuratingSamplesFilamentCoverage


The Filaments subtab of Modeling answers a different question than the other two: does each filament have enough included evidence to be modeled well? Read it as a gap-finder.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Filaments subtab with its Health column.


One row per filament: Filament, Brand, Samples, Fit Samples, Incl. Swatches, Excl. Swatches, and Health. Every column is sortable.
Health sums up the row:

Good — at least eight swatches are currently included. This is a coarse evidence-count check, not a guarantee that the evidence spans every useful thickness or role.
Sparse — fewer than eight swatches are currently included.
Excluded only — it appears in samples, but every one is excluded, so it contributes nothing.
Excluded — the filament carries the permanent exclude flag from Filaments.
Stale — a model needs rebuilding.

The detail view
Click a row for the filament’s coverage detail: Summary, Coverage (included/excluded sample and swatch counts), Model State, and Samples. Show In Samples jumps to the Samples subtab pre-filtered to this filament so you can act on what you found.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The filament coverage detail drawer, showing the Summary and Coverage blocks.


For Sparse, first check whether useful samples or swatches were excluded. If the included evidence is genuinely thin, print and measure more strips. Excluded only means the existing samples cannot contribute until a sample or the filament itself is included again.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/m.title: Modeling Overview
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/m.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ModelingModelingOverviewCuratingSamples


The Overview subtab of Modeling summarizes the evidence and model state before you run Fit Models.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Overview subtab — the Current Evidence cards and the Needs Attention list.


Current Evidence
Four cards summarize what the next build would learn from:

Evidence Samples — included samples over total (e.g. 41 / 55). The first number counts samples with an accepted measurement and at least one included swatch; the second is every sample you have, measured or not — so a gap between them isn’t necessarily a problem.
Swatches — included swatches over total.
Excluded Samples — how many you’ve switched off.
Excluded Swatches — how many single swatches are sidelined.

Needs Attention
This list combines two different kinds of attention:

A Stale or Missing model means the model needs fitting. This is a reason to run Fit Models, not a blocker you must clear beforehand.
Samples blocked by excluded filaments cannot contribute while one of their filaments has Exclude from model fits selected.
Samples without accepted extraction counts every sample record that does not yet have an accepted measurement, including unassigned and incomplete samples as well as results waiting in the Processing Queue. Those samples do not contribute to the current fit.

Review the list to confirm that the included evidence is intentional, then run Fit Models (Fit Models). The empty-state message is No immediate blockers, but the list does not need to be empty merely because a model is stale or missing.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/s.title: Sample Comparison
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/s.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}CuratingSamplesSampleComparisonFilamentCoverage


Click any row on the Samples subtab to open a side-by-side comparison for that sample: what was measured, next to what each model predicts for the same strip. The drawer also contains the sample and swatch exclusion controls.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The comparison drawer showing both domains, prediction errors, and the exclusion controls.


The drawer shows Transmission Domain and Appearance Domain side by side. Each domain contains:

Measured Transmission or Measured Appearance — the accepted measurement.
Predicted Transmission (Color Model V2) / Predicted Appearance (Color Model V2) — the Color Model v2 prediction.
Predicted Transmission (Color Model V1) / Predicted Appearance (Color Model V1) — the Color Model v1 prediction.
Prediction Error — an OKLab error graph comparing each prediction with the measurement, swatch by swatch.

Color Corrections: On/Off changes the displayed predictions without changing the measurements. Both domains remain visible; see Transmission vs Appearance for what they mean.
Reading it

If both predictions broadly track the measurement, the sample is behaving consistently with the current models.
If one swatch is clearly inconsistent with its neighbors, inspect the extraction and physical strip before excluding only that swatch under Swatch Exclusion.
If the whole strip disagrees, verify its geometry, filament assignments, sample image, blank image, and open-side direction before using Exclude Sample.

Treat the comparison as evidence, not an automatic pass/fail score. A high prediction error may identify a bad sample, but it may also reveal useful evidence that the current models do not yet represent well.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/i.title: Modeling
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/modeling/i.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}ImagesModelingModelingOverviewCuratingSamplesFilamentCoverage


Everything upstream produced measurements; this tab is where you decide which measurements the color models learn from, then fit Calibration’s current models. A separate publication step turns an exact current generation into a stable Generator library.



                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Modeling tab — the model status list, the Fit Models button, and the three subtabs.


The header — model status and Fit Models
The header shows the status of each current working model — Color Model v1, Color Model v2, and Camera Transform — as:

Current — up to date with your evidence.
Stale — evidence or a fit control that contributed to the retained model has changed since it was built. A Fit Models needed banner appears. This is normal; it just means “build again.” Newly accepted evidence does not by itself rewrite the existing model.
Missing — never built yet.

Fit Models fits Color Model v1 and Color Model v2 from the currently included evidence. It also fits the Camera Transform when needed, or whenever Force Camera Transform is selected. See Fit Models. What the models are is covered in Color Model v1, Color Model v2, and The Camera Transform.
Two ways to keep data out

Here (and on the Sample Record): exclude one sample or one swatch from the next fit. These controls are reversible and suit one suspect strip or swatch.
On Filaments: Exclude from model fits removes a filament wholesale until the setting is cleared. Use it for a retired or mis-measured filament. The same setting also makes that filament unavailable for new generation.

The subtabs

Overview — is the evidence healthy? Your pre-build checklist.
Samples — include or exclude each sample; compare measurements to the models.
Filaments — does each filament have enough data to be modeled well?

The usual loop: read the Overview, spot-check and curate Samples, check coverage on Filaments, then Fit Models. A stale or missing model is a reason to fit; it is not something you must clear first.
Publish the exact current generation
Fit Models and Publish Models are deliberately different operations:

Fitting replaces Calibration’s internal working models. Those models remain under Calibration’s exclusive ownership and may become stale or be rebuilt as evidence changes.
Publishing creates a new immutable Generator library from the exact current Color Model v1, Color Model v2, Camera Transform, and public filament catalog. It never modifies a previously published copy.

Press Publish Models in the app’s top bar. The dialog checks all four required components and blocks publication if a model is missing, stale, invalid, changed on disk, or inconsistent with the others. When it reports Ready to publish, enter a required Library name, Version, and Publisher or author; description and release notes are optional.
Choose one action:

Publish to Generator validates and installs a new library in this Suite’s Generator\Model Libraries. It is installed inactive so the running Generator cannot change underneath an open session. Open Generator’s Models menu and choose Activate and Restart Prisma when ready.
Export Library Package writes a validated ZIP under Calibration\Output\Published Models. Send that unchanged ZIP to another Generator, or distribute it as a model-library update; the receiving user installs it through Models → Install Library….

Both actions build the same payload. The published library contains only the public filament catalog and runtime artifacts for the three model families—not Calibration’s SQLite database, sample records, raw photographs, per-sample predictions, notes, or other working evidence.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.title: Creating New Samples
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}SampleLogbookCreating NewSamplesSampleRecord


+ New Samples on the Sample Logbook creates records for the physical strips you will print. Each sample combines one geometry with one filament assignment for every material role.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The New Samples drawer — the form on the left, the live Sample Preview on the right.


Before you start
The required filaments must exist under Filaments. The required strip designs must exist under Geometries. To use a bundle, it must have a Mapped status under Manage Bundles.
Choose a source
Under Select Geometry Source, choose:

Single Geometry — create samples from one strip design.
Geometry Bundle — create samples from every geometry in a mapped bundle.

A bundle does not create one combined print. It creates a separate sample record for each member geometry.
Assign filaments
For a single geometry, assign a filament to each LR role. For a bundle, assign filaments to its shared slots, such as Shared Filament A. One shared assignment fills every geometry role mapped to that slot, even when those roles have different LR numbers or one is fixed and another is variable.
Each role or shared slot has two modes:

Single — use one filament for every sample in this set.
Multi — create a separate set for each selected filament.

Only one role or shared slot can be Multi. Select at least two filaments for it; all other roles remain Single and require one filament each.
Know how many samples will be created

























Source and assignmentResultOne geometry, all roles Single1 sampleOne geometry, one role Multi with N filamentsN samplesBundle with G geometries, all shared slots SingleG samplesBundle with G geometries, one shared slot Multi with N filamentsG × N samples
For example, a three-geometry bundle with four filaments selected for one shared slot creates 12 samples.

Review and create
Selected Geometry Preview shows the source. Sample Summary and Sample Preview show the exact number of records, their new sample IDs, geometry, and role assignments. Check these before continuing. Optional Notes apply to every sample in the set.
Click Create. The records appear in the Sample Logbook as unassigned.
Print and identify the strips
Export the geometry files and match every LR body or file to the same role shown in the sample preview. See Export Sample Geometry. Print at full size.
Keep each physical strip associated with its sample ID. This is especially important for Geometry Bundle and Multi runs, where many similar strips are created at once.


                  
                  Physical sample custody draft 
                  
                

Before printing, prepare one labeled location for every sample ID: a tray position, bag, envelope, or other container that cannot be confused with its neighbors. Move each strip directly into its labeled location after printing. Keep the label with the strip through photography and review, and do not mark the swatches or any area used for extraction.


Once the strips are printed and photographed on the lightbox, continue to Images.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.title: Sample Record
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}Creating NewSamplesSampleRecordImages


Click any sample in the Sample Logbook to open its record — everything the app knows about that strip, in one drawer. It opens read-only, with the sample’s ID and status in the header and an Edit button; click Edit to change anything, which swaps in Save, Discard, and Delete.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

A sample record, expanded, showing the form sections on the left and the measured results on the right.


The sections

Filaments — which filament fills each layer. Changeable in Edit mode.
Images — the assigned photo and blank; in Edit mode, Unassign source and Unassign blank detach either.
Strip — a preview of the calibration strip.
Sample Geometry — which geometry this sample uses (changeable in Edit mode), with a Copy Path button that copies the geometry’s folder location.
Notes — free text.
Model Fit — see below.

The expand button in the header widens the drawer to show the sample’s measured results: the extracted strip image beside the colors the app read from it.

Changing the strip changes the measurement. If you change a measured sample’s geometry or filaments, the app throws its measurement away — the old numbers described the old strip. You’ll need to re-photograph and re-process it.

Model Fit — keeping a measurement out of the models
Two controls decide what this sample contributes the next time you run Fit Models:

Exclude this sample from model fits — withholds the whole sample from model fitting. The measurement stays; it just does not count. Reversible any time.
Per-swatch toggles — in the expanded view, each measured swatch has its own Included / Excluded toggle for withholding one swatch without losing the rest of the strip.

The Sample Comparison drawer under Modeling provides the same sample and per-swatch exclusion controls beside the model comparisons.
Delete removes the sample entirely. Prefer excluding — it keeps the data without letting it influence anything.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.title: Sample Logbook
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/sample-log.content:
.htu-localnav svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-localnav a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-localnav a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-localnav a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}GeometriesSampleLogbookImagesCreating NewSamplesSampleRecord


The Sample Logbook (the Logbook tab in the app) lists every sample: one sample geometry filled with specific filaments. Each record tracks one physical calibration strip from creation to accepted measurement.


                  
                  📸 Screenshot to capture 
                  
                

The Logbook tab, with several samples in different statuses.


The list
One row per sample: ID, Strip, Filament, Brand, Image, Blank, and Status. ID, Filament, Brand, and Status are sortable. The line above the table counts your samples and how many are measured. A red chip in the Image or Blank cell means that image file cannot be found — re-attach it on the Images tab.
Status tells you where each sample is:

unassigned — just created; no photos yet.
incomplete — has some of its sample image, blank image, or open-side direction, but not all three.
ready — has a sample image, blank image, and open-side direction; waiting in the Processing Queue.
processed — measured, waiting for your Accept in the Processing Queue.
accepted — a trusted measurement; it can feed the models.
failed / flagged — automatic measurement didn’t work or was set aside; see Manual Processing.

What you do here

+ New Samples creates samples from a geometry — see Creating New Samples.
Click a row to open that sample’s record — its filaments, photos, notes, and measurement controls. See Sample Record.

The usual path: create samples here, print the strips, then attach their photos on the Images tab.

prisma-calibration/how-to-use/index.title: How To Use
prisma-calibration/how-to-use/index.content:
The calibration app measures how your filaments pass light, so the generator can reproduce their colors in a print. You photograph printed filament strips on a lightbox, the app reads the color out of each photo, and once you’ve checked the results it builds the color models the generator prints from.
The steps run in order. You set up the library — your filaments and sample geometries — once. Everything after that you repeat for each new set of strips.
The workflow


.htu-diagram svg text{font-family:inherit;font-size:13px}.htu-diagram a rect{transition:stroke .15s ease}.htu-diagram a:hover rect{stroke:var(--secondary);stroke-width:2}.htu-diagram a:hover text{fill:var(--secondary)}Set up onceRepeat for each batch of stripsFilamentsGeometriesSampleLogbookImagesModelingGuides and toolsTutorialsMaintenanceBackup /Restore


Every box is a page. The top row is the workflow, left to right: set up Filaments and Geometries once, then run Sample Logbook → Images → Modeling for each batch of strips. Maintenance and Backup / Restore live in the top bar and work from any tab.

Filaments — add each filament you want to test.
Geometries — design the calibration strips you will print.
Sample Logbook — fill a geometry’s material roles with filaments to create samples.
Images — give each sample its lightbox photos, then pull the colors out.
Modeling — check the measurements, then build the color models.

Steps 1 and 2 are one-time setup. Steps 3–5 are the loop you run for every batch of strips.
One heads-up: the app’s own tab strip is arranged for day-to-day use — Logbook first, then Images, Filaments, Geometries, Modeling — so the two setup tabs sit in the middle of the strip, not at the left.
Top-bar tools
These top-bar buttons work from any tab:

Refresh Data — reload the app’s current data when a view looks out of
date. It does not import files that are waiting in the Image Inbox; use
Import from Inbox on the Images page for that.
Maintenance — housekeeping jobs, and the button that builds the models.
 Restore — save a copy of your work, or bring one back.

Getting set up

Getting Started — installing and launching the app, and a first run end to end.
Tutorials — full walkthroughs from start to finish.

Good to know
Only one heavy job runs at a time — extracting colors, fitting models, or making a backup. Start a second and the app asks you to wait. That’s expected, not an error.
Nothing you measure reaches a print until you run Fit Models from the Modeling tab. To understand what a measurement is or how the models work, see How It Works.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/c.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/CSV assignment import and commit lifecycle.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/c.title: CSV assignment import and commit lifecycle
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/c.content:
The CSV importer is a SQLite-only, two-request workflow for assigning a source image, a registered blank, and an open-side orientation to otherwise unassigned samples. The implementation is split between csv_assignment_import.py (calibration.csv_assignment_import) and two FastAPI routes in server.py.
HTTP contract
GET /api/samples/assignment-template.csv returns a header-only UTF-8 CSV named prisma_sample_assignment_template.csv. Its columns are exactly Sample ID, Sample Image, Blank Image, and Orientation.
POST /api/samples/assignment-import/validate reads the uploaded file and calls validate_assignment_csv. The route requires the SQLite backend. A successful response contains row counts, valid_rows, error_rows, warnings, and pending_blank_registrations, plus a random preview_token. The server keeps the commit specifications, upload digest, validation errors, and pending blank references in the process-local _csv_assignment_previews dictionary, guarded by _csv_assignment_previews_lock.
The preview expires after _CSV_ASSIGNMENT_PREVIEW_TTL_SECONDS and is pruned when either assignment route is called. The upload digest is recorded but is not used by the commit route to reread the file: commit uses the stored internal row specifications from the preview.
POST /api/samples/assignment-import/commit accepts the preview token and register_unregistered_blanks. It rejects an expired token with 409, rejects a preview with no valid rows with 400, and converts domain-level stale-preview failures to 409. On success it removes the token and reports committed_count, skipped invalid rows, and any blanks registered during the commit.
Parsing and resolution
The parser decodes UTF-8 with an optional BOM (utf-8-sig). Header matching is case-insensitive and ignores spaces, underscores, and hyphens. Missing required columns, duplicate normalized headers, invalid encoding, an empty file, and a file with no nonblank assignment rows are errors. Extra columns are ignored and returned as warnings; blank CSV rows are skipped.
Sample IDs resolve first by exact ID, then by an unambiguous numeric suffix for IDs shaped like exp-N. Image and blank values must be identifiers or filenames, not paths. Images resolve by asset ID, exact filename, or an unambiguous filename stem. Blanks resolve by blank ID, exact filename, or stem. If the selected value resolves to a managed image that is not registered as a blank, the row becomes valid-but-pending and the preview reports a blank-registration confirmation requirement.
Orientation accepts U/T as zero rotations, R as one clockwise quarter-turn, D/B as two, and L as three. The public error text names the supported UI values as U, D, L, or R.
Every row is checked against current state. A sample must be unassigned, have no source image, blank, or orientation, and have no measurements or extraction result. The sample image must exist in managed storage, not be ignored, and not already be assigned to another sample. The blank must exist and have a present managed path. Cross-row validation rejects duplicate samples, duplicate sample images, and a sample image used as the selected blank. Invalid rows remain in the preview and do not prevent valid rows from being offered for commit.
Commit and stale-preview protection
commit_assignment_rows reconstructs current samples, images, blanks, existing sample-image assignments, and extraction-result membership before writing. It validates every stored row specification again. This is the concurrency boundary: changes made after preview—such as another assignment, image removal/ignore, extraction output, or a sample becoming ineligible—cause CsvAssignmentError("CSV assignment preview is stale.") and no sample assignment is saved.
If pending blank registration was requested but register_unregistered_blanks is false, commit stops before writing. With confirmation, each distinct managed image is registered through SQLiteDataStore.register_blank_from_image. The registration is a database relation to the existing image asset; it does not copy a second image file. The row specifications are then normalized from image ID to the newly allocated blank ID.
Finally, each valid row mutates a Sample in memory: assigned_image receives the image asset ID, assigned_blank_id receives the blank ID, and orientation_rots receives the normalized integer rotation. recompute_sample_status sets the sample to assigned when all three evidence fields are present. SQLite saves the collected samples through save_samples in one write transaction. The preview token is removed only after that save succeeds.
The blank-registration step and the later sample save are separate write operations. The code does not provide a rollback that unregisters a blank if a later commit failure occurs; this is an implementation boundary worth preserving when changing the importer.
Ownership and compatibility
The live SQLite path uses image_assets, registered_blanks, sample_evidence_assignments, and the samples workflow state. The JSON DataStore has resolver fallbacks for older filename-shaped assignments, but the HTTP importer is explicitly rejected for that backend. The Architecture page calibration.csv_assignment_import is generated from the module; this page documents the cross-module server lifecycle.
