prisma-calibration/technical-reference/d.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Data access and persistence.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/d.title: Data access and persistence
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/d.content:
In one sentence: packaged Calibration owns Calibration/Workspace/calibration.sqlite3 plus a materialized Workspace/Assets root fronted by SQLiteDataStore (calibration.sqlite_data_access, sqlite_data_access.py:265); visible Inbox/Output directories are siblings of that app-managed Workspace; the older JSON-tree DataStore (calibration.data_access) is retained for migration tools and tests only; and two different safety nets sit on top — operator-driven ZIP backups (calibration.backup_restore) and internal automatic SQLite restore points (calibration.sqlite_restore_points).

This page is the code-level map of where calibration data is stored and which backend reads it. For the operator’s view of packaging and restoring data, see Backup and restore. For how the web layer opens a store at startup and dispatches jobs against it, see Web API and job orchestration; for the batch operations that mutate the store in place, The maintenance backend.
Related: calibration.sqlite_data_access · calibration.data_access · calibration.models · calibration.backup_restore · calibration.sqlite_restore_points
The backend split — SQLite is production, JSON is migration-only
There are two store implementations and they are not peers. Backend selection is explicit and refuses to guess: _configured_backend (calibration.server, server.py:305) reads the PRISMA_CALIBRATION_BACKEND env var (or a local .backend file) and raises if neither is set, so “a launch cannot silently fall back to legacy JSON” (server.py:310-314). _create_store (server.py:336) then builds one of:

json → DataStore (server.py:355-356) — the legacy filesystem tree. Its own header comment states it exists so “JSON can still be constructed intentionally for migration tests/tools, but it is never selected as an implicit fallback” (server.py:344-347).
sqlite → SQLiteDataStore(sqlite_path, asset_root=...) (server.py:368) — the production store. Both the database path and the asset root must be configured (env var or local pointer file) or construction errors out (_configured_required_path, server.py:324).

The module module-level _store is typed DataStore | SQLiteDataStore (server.py:203) and every request handler treats them polymorphically, but on a live install the object is always the SQLite one. Read the rest of this page with that in mind: sqlite_data_access.py is the live path; data_access.py is dormant except during migration.
The production store — SQLiteDataStore
SQLiteDataStore (sqlite_data_access.py:112) is the production SQLite-backed store. Its module/class header still contains transitional “Stage 1” wording (sqlite_data_access.py:1-6, :113-118), but that wording is stale relative to the implemented runtime: the class now provides the live geometry, filament, sample, image, extraction, bundle, and model-fit read/write paths described below. Its class attribute backend = "sqlite" (:120) is what the server checks to gate SQLite-only behavior.
The two-root design — database + materialized assets
The constructor takes two paths and keeps them apart (__init__, sqlite_data_access.py:265):

self.sqlite_path — the single SQLite database file (:148).
self.root — the materialized asset root, a directory tree of the binary/large artifacts that do not belong inside the database (:149).

Structured rows live in SQLite; bytes live under the asset root. The store exposes the asset layout as path properties so callers never hardcode subpaths:













































PropertyLocation under rootHoldssystem_dirroot/_system (:584-:586)internal system filesmanaged_images_dirroot/images (:620-:622)onboarded (managed) source imagesmanaged_step_dirsystem_dir/step_artifacts (:624-:626)compatibility STEP artifacts_profile_path(id)root/filaments/profiles/{id}.jsonfitted per-filament spline profile JSONinbox_dirpackaged: Calibration/Inbox (:589-:614)user-facing image-import inbox and Removed Images areastep_export_dirpackaged: Calibration/Output/Steps (:629-:632)user-facing geometry exportsbackup_dirpackaged: Calibration/Output/Backups (:634-:638)user-created backup and RAW archive packages
The packaged shape is recognized only when the asset root is exactly Calibration/Workspace/Assets (portable_calibration_root, sqlite_data_access.py:589-:598). This keeps user-facing files outside the internal asset tree without making them external to the portable Suite. Source-maintenance/migration roots retain their compatibility path derivation.
Fitted spline profiles are still JSON files on the asset root, not database rows — the profile artifact format survived the SQLite changeover unchanged.
Startup validation and schema migrations
Construction is fail-closed. _validate_paths (:155) requires the database file and asset root to already exist; then two idempotent in-place schema migrations run — _migrate_bundle_mapping_schema (:221) and _migrate_raw_archive_custody_schema (:361) — followed by _validate_schema (:441), which reads sqlite_master and hard-fails if any of the 22 tables in _REQUIRED_TABLES (:122-:145) is missing. There is no _migrate_filament_classification_schema in the current implementation. A store either opens against a database with the required schema or refuses to open.
Connections are split by intent: _connect_readonly opens the file mode=ro for projections (:165-:169), while writes go through _connect_write with foreign keys enabled (:171-:175) inside _write_transaction, which wraps every mutation in BEGIN IMMEDIATE and commit/rollback (:177-:188).
Domain accessors — the shape, not the catalog
The class is large (~9k lines) because it holds every read projection and write path for the whole domain, but the surface is regular. Representative accessors, most returning the pydantic models from calibration.models (a few return raw dicts or a Path, noted inline):

Filaments — list_filaments (:1481), get_filament (:1532).
Samples — list_samples (:2783), get_sample (:2809).
Geometries — surfaced as StepRecords via list_step_records (:4326) / get_step_record (:4329), with the reconstructed GeometryDefinition from get_geometry_definition (:2090). See Geometry and strip definition for what a geometry is.
Blanks — list_blanks (:5725).
Extraction — get_extraction_result (:3244, returns a dict) / save_extraction_result (:3676, returns a Path).
Bundles — list_bundles (:4526, returns list[dict]).

The remaining compatibility gaps are explicit rather than silently redirected: list_strip_filaments returns an empty list and get_strips returns None (:4314-:4318); _step_record_from_components, save_steps_registry, and set_image_ignored call _not_implemented (:497-:502, :4367-:4371, :5881-:5883). The implemented SQLite paths do not use those legacy operations.
Current working models — the three model kinds
Fitting outputs are recorded as model fits in the model_fits / model_artifacts tables, gated to exactly three kinds by _MODEL_KINDS = {"camera_transform", "legacy_spline", "photo_stack_v2"}. The internal helper name publish_model_fit means “make this Calibration fit current”; it is not the user-facing act of publishing a Generator library. In one transaction it inserts the replacement current fit, contributors, and artifacts, then deletes the previous fit row for that family; foreign-key cascades remove old child rows. The tables therefore retain one replaceable working fit per family, not operator-selectable historical fits.
The separate calibration.model_library_publication boundary validates exactly one current fit per family plus the public filament catalog, copies only the allowlisted runtime payload, and either installs a new inactive immutable Generator library or writes a transfer ZIP. It does not change the current-fit transaction above and never grants Generator access to this database or asset root.
Currentness still has a real invalidation role. Contributor/evidence or fit-control mutations can update the retained row from current to stale with a reason (_mark_model_fits_stale_for_sample_in_tx, :1111-:1165; fit-control variant :1205-:1240). This means the fit no longer reflects the current state of model inputs that were in its fitting corpus; it does not mean that merely adding unconsumed evidence invalidates yesterday’s fit. Appearance refresh separates model inputs from provenance metadata: changed RGB values, inclusion-relevant correlation/error state, or orientation can stale Camera Transform, while a decoder-version (decode_environment) metadata refresh with identical model inputs is persisted without invalidating the fit. The stale row and files remain until replacement publication succeeds. prune_superseded_model_fits (:4368) is startup compatibility cleanup for databases that still contain multiple rows from the earlier history-retaining implementation.
The legacy JSON store — DataStore (off the production path)
DataStore (data_access.py:56) is the original filesystem backend: “Read/write operations for all domain objects … all file I/O scoped to a configurable DATA_ROOT” (data_access.py:1-6). Instead of a database it materializes a directory tree — _ensure_dirs (:65) creates filaments/, filaments/profiles/, samples/, strips/, images/, segmentation/, extraction_results/, blanks/, and _system/ — with one JSON file per object.
It is dormant on a live install. It is constructed only when the backend is explicitly json (server.py:355), which the production launch never selects. Its Imported by list on calibration.data_access is dominated by processing/migration code (processing.backfill, processing.processor, maintenance, sample_mutations) and it is the only importer of the legacy notebook-era strip generator strips.generator (data_access.py:30); it also imports the strips.step_parser filename reader (:31), which the server imports too — see the “legacy strip generator” section of Geometry and strip definition. Treat DataStore as the read/write shape the SQLite store had to reproduce, and as the backend that migration tools (e.g. the one-shot processing/backfill.py, calibration.processing.backfill) still drive — not as a runtime option.
The shared domain models — models.py
Both stores read and write the same pydantic v2 models in models.py (calibration.models), “data shapes for API requests, responses, and internal domain objects” (models.py:1-5). The module has no intra-project imports — it is the foundational leaf that everything else depends on. Two families live here:

Domain objects — Sample (models.py:64, “central domain object — a calibration sample”), Filament (:104), Blank (:94, a registered flatfield reference), StripGeometry (:22) / StripDefinition (:30), Measurements (:56), and the sidecar ExtractionResult (:505) with its per-swatch measurement payload.
Request/response models — the *Request classes (AssignImageRequest, CreateSampleRequest, BackupCreateRequest, BundleMappingSaveRequest, …) that the FastAPI handlers validate against. These are contract types for Web API and job orchestration, not persisted state.

Because the models are backend-agnostic, a Sample loaded from SQLite and a Sample loaded from the JSON tree are the same object — which is exactly what made the migration verifiable.
User backups — backup_restore.py
backup_restore.py (calibration.backup_restore) is the operator-facing packaging layer: it snapshots the SQLite database and, for working-state packages, managed assets and step exports into a validated ZIP, then restores one through a staged apply. It imports calibration.path_safety for destructive filesystem boundaries. The package taxonomy is a set of module constants (backup_restore.py:22-:25), and the server exposes the core-library and working-state families:

“Essential Data Only” → core_library (CORE_LIBRARY_PACKAGE_TYPE, :22). create_core_library_backup (:1598) packs only sqlite/calibration.sqlite3 — no images, model artifact files, STEP/STL exports, or raw archives.
Working state with or without RAW images → working_state_with_raw or working_state_no_raw (:23-:24). create_working_state_backup (:1228) packs the SQLite snapshot plus collected asset files and step-export files. include_raw_images selects the package type; a no-RAW manifest explicitly lists omitted source files.

Other formats: create_raw_image_archive packages just RAW source images; create_emergency_core_library_backup and create_emergency_pre_restore_backup create safety packages. Restore is staged: stage_restore_package validates and unpacks into a private staging area, then apply_restore moves current state aside, replaces the parts described by PackageSemantics, audits references, and rolls back on failure. Backup collection, RAW local-release, and restore refuse an asset or STEP tree containing symlinks, junctions, or other reparse points; restore checks configured path components before moving current files aside. resolve_package_type describes whether a package replaces SQLite, managed assets, or step exports. ZIP handling is bounded by total-size, per-file, and compression-ratio ceilings. The operator walkthrough is Backup and restore.
Every SQLite snapshot passes through _normalize_model_fit_lifecycle (backup_restore.py:972) before packaging. It retains the current row for each family—or the newest row when an older database has no current row—and deletes other fit, contributor, and artifact rows from the private snapshot only (:978-:1004). Backup creation does not mutate the live database. Working-state validation then requires and hash-checks only artifacts owned by those retained rows (_retained_model_artifact_rows, :950; _validate_referenced_assets, :2990). This prevents obsolete database history from requiring already-garbage-collected model files.
For a working-state restore, apply_restore keeps the displaced SQLite/assets/exports under a temporary restore_previous_* directory until reference auditing and the optional smoke check pass (:3350-:3389). An exception before that boundary triggers _restore_previous_state. After a successful smoke check, safe_rmtree clears Windows read-only flags as needed while removing the rollback tree. Any cleanup exception is converted into a restore_previous_cleanup_failed warning containing the residual path and error; it does not turn an otherwise successful restore into a rollback attempt after cleanup may have partially removed the old tree.
Automatic restore points — sqlite_restore_points.py (a different mechanism)
Do not conflate restore points with backups. sqlite_restore_points.py (calibration.sqlite_restore_points) makes “internal SQLite-only snapshots … intentionally separate from user-facing Backup/Restore packages: no RAW images, no derived artifacts, and no ZIP packaging” (sqlite_restore_points.py:1-7). Their job is to keep a recent known-good database around for corruption recovery, not to be handed to a user.
They are created at startup, debounced, and pruned, not on demand:

startup_restore_point_check (:372) runs during post-store startup checks (invoked by _run_sqlite_restore_point_startup, server.py:390, from _run_post_store_startup_checks, :449-:473). It validates database integrity first and skips creation with reason "debounced" when the latest point is younger than DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (6 hours, sqlite_restore_points.py:36, decision :406-:421).
Otherwise create_sqlite_restore_point (:267) writes a new snapshot, then prune_restore_points (:317) trims to DEFAULT_MAX_COUNT (12) and DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_DAYS (30), defined at :37-:38.
Recovery is apply_sqlite_restore_point (:520), which first calls preserve_current_sqlite_for_recovery (:472) to set the about-to-be-replaced database aside. Those output/restore-points/recovery/ copies are emergency filesystem preserves, not additional selectable restore points: prune_recovery_copies_for_paths applies the same default 12-copy/30-day bounds as normal restore points. Linked roots and runs are refused rather than traversed. Restore points reuse backup_restore.validate_sqlite_readonly for integrity checking.

So: backups are explicit, packaged, and can carry every managed artifact; restore points are silent, database-only, startup-cadenced, and self-pruning. SQLiteDataStore also refuses to open a symlinked or multiply-hardlinked mutable database, because ordinary SQLite writes through a hardlink would mutate every linked pathname. These are complementary safety layers, not the same feature.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Extraction artifact sinks and blank registration.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.title: Extraction artifact sinks and blank registration
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/e.content:
Extraction produces visual artifacts through a small sink protocol, while blank registration establishes the flatfield reference used by extraction. These are related filesystem concerns but different ownership layers: thumbnails are derived output; a registered blank is durable evidence metadata pointing at an image asset.
Artifact sink contract
ExtractionArtifactSink in processing/artifact_sinks.py (calibration.processing.artifact_sinks) exposes one operation: write_image(sample_id, kind, image_bgr, max_dim=800) -> Path. The allowed kinds are source, blank, strip, appearance, and transmission_roi. Sample IDs are restricted to alphanumeric characters plus _, ., and -; the kind is an allow-list, so the sink does not accept arbitrary path components.
write_thumbnail_image bounds the largest image dimension to max_dim using OpenCV INTER_AREA when downscaling, creates the parent directory, and writes a JPEG at quality 80. It does not report or raise on the boolean result returned by cv2.imwrite; the returned path is the intended artifact path.
LiveThumbnailSink writes {data_root}/thumbnails/{sample_id}/{kind}.jpg. The normal processor and manual extraction path default to this sink when no test/staging sink is supplied. SampleArtifactDirectorySink ignores sample_id and writes {sample_dir}/{kind}.jpg; it is for a caller that owns a fixed staging directory and is not the live per-sample tree.
processor.py uses the sink for source, strip, blank, transmission ROI, and appearance thumbnails. The processor still computes thumb_dir and retains a legacy direct-save path for appearance output; this is compatibility behavior in the current implementation, not a second artifact naming scheme. The manual path similarly defaults to LiveThumbnailSink and passes its sink through preview/commit helpers.
Lifecycle and cleanup
The sink writes derived visual files before or alongside extraction-result publication. Re-running or regenerating thumbnails can recreate them from source evidence. JSON invalidation removes the sample thumbnail directory; SQLite invalidation deletes the durable extraction result during the save transaction, while the live thumbnail cleanup behavior is owned by the surrounding processing/recovery paths rather than by the sink itself. The sink has no database transaction and does not register, publish, or delete extraction results.
Blank registration: SQLite production path
POST /api/blanks/register dispatches to SQLiteDataStore.register_blank_from_image when the selected backend is SQLite. The method resolves a managed image_assets row, rejects an already registered asset, allocates the next blank ID, and inserts a row into registered_blanks in a write transaction. It returns a Blank view whose storage_path is the image asset’s managed relative path. No duplicate file is copied into blanks/.
list_blank_assets exposes the join needed by current consumers: blank ID, image asset ID, original filename, managed path, path existence, and UI ignore state. get_blank_storage_path resolves the registered blank back to its managed image path. A blank cannot be unregistered while a sample_evidence_assignments row references it. Image rotation also checks assigned sample workflow states and refuses rotation for processed, failed, or flagged samples.
Blank registration: JSON compatibility path
The JSON DataStore route calls processing.blank_registry.register_blank_image. That path resolves a filename through get_image_path, rejects duplicate original filenames, best-effort extracts EXIF DateTimeOriginal, allocates a blank ID, copies the source into root/blanks/{blank_id}{suffix}, and registers a legacy Blank containing storage_path=blanks/{blank_id}{suffix}. If registration fails, it deletes the copied file. This path remains for migration tools and tests; it is not the production SQLite custody model.
The CSV assignment importer can register an unregistered blank as part of an explicitly confirmed commit, but it does so through the SQLite managed-image method. That relationship must not be documented as a copy into blanks/ when describing the live backend.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Geometry and strip definition.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.title: Geometry and strip definition
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.content:
In one sentence: a calibration strip’s shape is a single frozen dataclass, GeometryDefinition (calibration.geometry_builder, geometry_builder.py:42), validated to a strict canonical form, hashed into a structural_fingerprint that is its identity, and turned into a build-independent body plan that the STEP/STL exporters render — everything else (the notebook-era strips/generator.py) is off the production path.

This page is the code-level map of how a strip geometry is represented and exported. For the concept — what a swatch, a role, and the spine are, and why the strip is shaped the way it is — see Sample Geometry. How a sample points at its geometry, and where geometries are persisted, is in Data access and persistence.
Related: calibration.geometry_builder · calibration.lightweight_step · calibration.strips.generator · calibration.strips.step_parser · Sample Geometry
The source-of-truth definition
Everything hangs off three frozen dataclasses in geometry_builder.py, deliberately independent of the CAD library (geometry_builder.py:1-5):

GeometryDefinition (:42) — the whole strip: layout_rows × layout_columns, per-swatch and spine dimensions in millimeters, a tuple of roles, and a tuple of swatch_slots. swatch_count is just rows * columns (:59-61).
GeometryRoleDefinition (:21) — one bottom-to-top material layer, tagged role_kind "fixed" or "variable", with a role_index and (for fixed roles) a fixed_thickness_mm.
GeometrySwatchSlotDefinition (:32) — one swatch cell’s position (row_index, column_index) and its variable_thickness_mm (the thickness the single variable role takes at that swatch).

Note what is absent: there is no layer height and no layer count. Thicknesses are absolute millimeters; the definition never knows about a slicer’s layer grid. (The legacy generator below does snap to a layer height — a key difference.)
The canonical invariants
validate_geometry_definition (:124) is the gatekeeper; it accumulates every violation and raises one ValueError. The invariants worth knowing, because they are what “a valid geometry” means everywhere downstream:

Roles are contiguous from 1. role_index values must be exactly 1..len(roles) (:331-334).
Exactly one variable role. Not zero, not two — one (:340-342). This is the layer whose thickness varies swatch to swatch; every other role is a fixed backing.
Role labels are unique and, if set, must equal LR_%02d of the index (:336-338, :353-355).
Fixed roles carry a positive thickness; variable roles carry none (:347-351).
Slots tile the layout exactly. len(swatch_slots) must equal rows * columns, swatch_index must be contiguous from 0, and no two slots may share a (row, column) (:360-379).
The spine is tall enough. spine_total_thickness_mm must be ≥ the tallest swatch stack (:150-155, stack height summed in _slot_stack_height :411).

Structural fingerprint — the identity
compute_structural_fingerprint (:201) is how the system decides whether two geometries are “the same shape.” It builds a canonical_geometry_payload (:161) — layout, roles (variable roles force fixed_thickness_mm to null), and slots, every float rounded to 6 places (_canonical_float :394) — serializes it with sorted keys and no whitespace, and SHA-256s it (:203-204). Because the payload is canonicalised (roles and slots sorted, floats rounded), two definitions that differ only in field order or float noise fingerprint identically; any real structural change produces a new hash.
build_geometry_body_plan re-derives the fingerprint and refuses to build if a definition arrived carrying a structural_fingerprint that no longer matches its content (:214-215) — a cheap guard against a stored geometry being edited out from under its hash.
The live API and persistence path
The production web path is the structured-geometry API, not the older STEP-record generator. The server exposes GET /api/geometries, GET /api/geometries/{geometry_id}, POST /api/geometries, PATCH /api/geometries/{geometry_id}, and DELETE /api/geometries/{geometry_id} (server.py:5352-5408). These routes call the corresponding SQLiteDataStore methods — list_geometry_definitions, get_geometry_definition, create_geometry_definition, update_geometry_metadata, and delete_geometry_definition — and serialize the dataclass through _geometry_payload.
SQLiteDataStore.create_geometry_definition (sqlite_data_access.py:2196) accepts the structured roles and swatch slots, computes the fingerprint through _definition_from_create_command (:2109-2194), and inserts one geometry row plus its geometry_roles and geometry_swatch_slots rows in one write transaction. Updating metadata changes only alias and notes (:2276-2309); changing dimensions, roles, or slots means creating a different definition. Deletion is rejected when the geometry is referenced by a sample or bundle (:2311-2326).
The server still exposes GET /api/steps and returns StepRecord objects. In SQLite, that is a compatibility projection reconstructed by _step_records_by_id / _step_record_from_geometry (sqlite_data_access.py:2579-2606, :2497-2552), not a second geometry store. The projection supplies compatibility values such as file_name = {geometry_id}.step and _COMPAT_LAYER_HEIGHT_MM (:2494-2495, :2540); layer height is not part of the source-truth GeometryDefinition.
The old POST /api/steps/generate route (server.py:5234-5269) is not the SQLite production creation path. _guard_sqlite_unimplemented_write rejects it with HTTP 501 for the SQLite backend because the route still targets the legacy DataStore/STEP-record workflow (server.py:475-488). The structured replacement is POST /api/geometries, followed by the structured artifact endpoint described below. This is a current compatibility boundary, not evidence that SQLite geometry artifact generation is absent.
The body plan
build_geometry_body_plan (:207) turns a definition into a GeometryBodyPlan (:95) of GeometryBodyPlanItems (:80) — axis-aligned RectPrisms (:64) grouped by role, in canonical builder coordinates. It has no CAD dependency; it is pure geometry the exporters consume. Two body families:

Swatch bodies (_swatch_bodies :457). Each role is laid down as a z-interval stacked from 0 upward in role order (_role_intervals_for_slot :415). A fixed role that spans every swatch at the same z-interval collapses to one swatch_area prism over the whole grid (:484-498); otherwise the role emits one swatch prism per slot (:500-513). This keeps the common fixed-backing case a single solid instead of N identical boxes.
Spine bodies (_spine_bodies :518). The surrounding frame (left, right, top borders — _spine_interval_bodies :568) is split into z-intervals, each owned by the topmost role present at that height (_spine_owner_for_interval :551, owner_index = max(present_indexes)), with adjacent same-owner intervals merged (:539-543). So the spine’s material at each height matches whatever the tallest swatch stack reaches there.

Footprint is columns * swatch_width + 2 * spine_width wide and rows * swatch_height + spine_width tall (_footprint_width :429, _footprint_height :433).
Export — lightweight STEP and per-role STL
geometry_builder.py delegates production serialization to lightweight_step.py; neither path imports a CAD kernel:

export_geometry_step (geometry_builder.py:230) calls export_geometry_step_lightweight and writes one role-grouped STEP.
export_geometry_stls (geometry_builder.py:241) calls export_geometry_stls_lightweight and writes one binary STL per material role, named {prefix}_{role}.stl.
export_geometry_artifacts (geometry_builder.py:261) is the convenience wrapper that emits a STEP plus a stl/ subdirectory in one call and returns a GeometryExportResult (geometry_builder.py:106).

build_lightweight_geometry (lightweight_step.py:79) groups the body plan’s axis-aligned prisms by role and computes exact boundary components for each union. Every component is validated as a closed, positively oriented rectilinear solid with the expected volume before serialization (lightweight_step.py:488). write_lightweight_step emits millimeter, planar AP214-style BREP records and labels each role’s product and solid (:232-:313, component entities :569-:625). write_lightweight_stl triangulates those same validated quad boundaries into atomic binary STL files (:184-:229). STEP and STL therefore share one geometry model instead of asking two independent exporters to reinterpret the strip.
The packaged Calibration runtime excludes build123d, OCP, and VTK. Build123d remains a development/test dependency only for independent parity comparisons; it is not on the production structured-geometry path.
SQLite artifact lifecycle
POST /api/geometries/{geometry_id}/artifacts calls SQLiteDataStore.generate_geometry_artifacts. The store rebuilds the definition with an empty stored fingerprint, recomputes the builder fingerprint, and stages managed artifacts beside their final _system/geometry_artifacts/{geometry_id}/{fingerprint} directory. The managed STEP also has a staged compatibility copy destined for _system/step_artifacts/{geometry_id}.step.
Each generation writes manifest.json into the staged fingerprint directory. The manifest records the database and builder fingerprints, builder_version, the complete managed STEP/STL inventory, the subset requested by the current API call, body names, and remembered public export paths. get_geometry_artifact_summary resolves the manifest-owned filenames back inside the current fingerprint root rather than trusting historical absolute roots; it reports a missing/unreadable manifest, missing STEP, absent or incomplete STL set, and absent or incomplete body labels separately. The Maintenance missing-artifact audit and regeneration preflight consume that same health classification.
When export_to_output is true, the public destinations are under store.step_export_dir (Calibration/Output/Steps in the packaged Suite): {export_name}.step and an {export_name}/ directory containing the per-role STL files. A request without overwrite=true returns HTTP 409 when those destinations conflict. With overwrite enabled, Prisma stages every requested public file before publication and removes only obsolete STL paths recorded as owned by the previous manifest; unrelated files in an existing export directory are preserved.
Publication is one rollback-capable filesystem transaction across the staged fingerprint directory, compatibility STEP, requested public STEP/STLs, and manifest-owned stale removals. Existing targets are displaced to short sibling rollback paths, staged targets are promoted with os.replace, and any later failure removes promoted replacements and restores every displaced path. Generation or manifest-staging failure occurs before this boundary and cannot alter live files. The transaction rejects filesystem links and hardlinked mutable file targets; managed trees are inspected for nested links before replacement. A rollback failure preserves and reports its recovery path instead of deleting it. POST /api/steps/{step_id}/ensure-artifact remains the compatibility repair endpoint and calls this same structured generator.
The public endpoint can generate STEP, STL, or both, but it rejects a request that selects neither. Unrequested managed file types already present in the current fingerprint directory are retained and inventoried, while the response’s legacy step_path/stl_paths fields continue to describe the types requested by that call. The lightweight serializer collects every disconnected component of one role into the same role product/file, so STL export still produces one file per role.
Geometry bundles and sample creation
Bundles are SQLite records that group geometry definitions and map each geometry role to a shared material slot. They are not CAD artifacts. geometry_bundles and geometry_bundle_members store the bundle and ordered geometry membership; geometry_bundle_material_slots and geometry_bundle_role_slot_mappings store the material-slot vocabulary and role assignments (sqlite_data_access.py:315-344).
_bundle_detail_in_tx derives mapping_status as unmapped, incomplete, invalid, or mapped and exposes creation_eligible only for the fully mapped state (sqlite_data_access.py:4373-4524). save_bundle_mapping validates the draft against the member roles and rewrites the slot and mapping rows transactionally (:4562-4725). create_samples_from_bundle_slots refuses any bundle that is not mapped, then creates samples for every bundle member, with optional multiple variable-filament values for a batch material slot (:4727-4847). The bundle API is therefore a role-assignment and sample-generation layer above geometry definitions; it does not alter the geometry fingerprint.
Role labels in STEP
Role labeling is now part of serialization rather than post-export string surgery. write_lightweight_step creates one named PRODUCT and ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION per role (lightweight_step.py:272-:293), while _add_component_geometry gives every component’s MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP the same role-derived name (:569-:625). Fusion/OrcaSlicer therefore receive role identity directly from the generated STEP entities.
The legacy strip generator (off the production path)
strips/generator.py (calibration.strips.generator) is the older geometry code, self-described as “Used by experiment_builder.ipynb” (strips/generator.py:1-4). It hardcodes a fixed 8-swatch strip with baked physical constants (SWATCH_W = 12.0, N_SWATCHES = 8, strips/generator.py:13-17) and snaps thicknesses to a layer height (snap_offset :22) — the opposite of the flexible, layer-height-free GeometryDefinition. It has its own generate_step / generate_stls, and is imported only by the JSON DataStore (data_access.py), not by the production SQLite path — so on a live install it is dormant. The live geometry consumers are sqlite_data_access.py and maintenance.py, both of which use geometry_builder.py (see the Imported by list on calibration.geometry_builder).
strips/step_parser.py (calibration.strips.step_parser) is a small compatibility helper that parses metadata (variable_thicknesses_mm, fixed_layers, layer_height_mm, layer_count) back out of legacy STEP filenames, tolerating both the current double-underscore and the legacy single-underscore naming (step_parser.py:1-6, parse_step_filename :12). It is a filename reader, not part of structured geometry construction. The SQLite projection does not need it to reconstruct a geometry; it reads the normalized role and slot tables instead.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Geometry-bundle role mapping and sample creation.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.title: Geometry-bundle role mapping and sample creation
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/g.content:
Geometry bundles group normalized geometry definitions and add a mapping layer from each member’s canonical geometry roles to shared material slots. They do not change a geometry’s structural fingerprint. The live mapping and sample-creation path is SQLite-only and is implemented in SQLiteDataStore.
Bundle detail and mapping state
GET /api/geometry-bundles/{bundle_id} returns _bundle_detail_in_tx output. Each member has a stable geometry_bundle_member_id, an ordered geometry_id, and the roles loaded from geometry_roles. Each role carries geometry_role_id, contiguous role_index, role_label (normally LR_%02d), role_kind, fixed thickness when applicable, and its mapped material_slot_id.
Material slots are bundle-local rows with stable IDs, positions, keys, and labels such as Shared Filament A. Role mappings are bundle-member-specific: the same geometry_role_id value is checked against the member’s geometry, and a mapping row is invalid if its member, role, or slot foreign reference is missing or inconsistent.
The derived mapping_status is:

unmapped when there are no material slots or mappings;
invalid when a member, geometry role, or material-slot reference is inconsistent;
mapped when every role across the members has a valid slot; or
incomplete for a remaining partial state.

creation_eligible is true only for mapped. This state is computed from current database rows; it is not a manually editable flag.
Saving a mapping
PUT /api/geometry-bundles/{bundle_id}/mapping accepts draft slot IDs and a role map for every current bundle member. save_bundle_mapping optionally checks expected_updated_at for an optimistic-concurrency conflict, requires the submitted member set to match the current members, rejects duplicate or foreign role IDs, and rejects unknown draft slots. Unless allow_incomplete is true, every role must be assigned.
The save deletes and rebuilds the bundle’s material-slot and role-mapping rows in one write transaction. Only draft slots used by an assignment are retained. They are normalized to persisted slot IDs based on position, with canonical keys and labels. The bundle updated_at changes after the rewrite. An incomplete mapping can therefore be saved for editing, but it cannot be used for sample creation.
Creating samples from slots
POST /api/samples/from-geometry-bundle requires the SQLite store’s create_samples_from_bundle_slots. It refuses a missing bundle, a non-mapped bundle, unknown/duplicate/missing slot assignments, and unknown filament IDs. Every persisted material slot must receive a filament unless it is the selected batch_material_slot_id; batch mode requires at least two batch_filament_ids and substitutes each batch filament into that slot.
For each batch value—or once when not batching—the store walks every bundle member. For each role it looks up the mapped material slot, creates an explicit {role_index, filament_id} assignment, identifies the single variable role, and collects fixed-role thicknesses. It then builds and inserts one sample per member. With batching, the result is one sample per member per batch filament. Allocation and inserts occur in one SQLite write transaction, and the created samples are reloaded from the database before returning.
The route returns only sample summaries (sample_id, name, step_id, and step_file) and an empty errors list on success. The ordinary POST /api/samples/from-bundle route is a separate compatibility/list-based bundle workflow; it can accept per-step role assignments, but it does not consume the persisted material-slot mapping described here.
Boundary with geometry source truth
GeometryDefinition owns the physical roles and swatch slots; the bundle mapping assigns filaments to those roles for a group of geometries. A bundle’s material_slot_id is not a filament ID and is not a role index. The resulting sample stores canonical role assignments and legacy-shaped variable/fixed fields derived from them. Changing a geometry definition is a different operation and is guarded by geometry persistence rules; mapping a bundle does not rebuild geometry artifacts.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.filePath: Prisma Calibration/Technical Reference/Model workflow, publication, and review.md
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.title: Model workflow, publication, and review
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/m.content:
In one sentence: the Fit Models maintenance operation drives execute_model_fit_workflow (calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow, model_fit_workflow.py:409), which fans out to the three fitters in a fixed order, replaces Calibration’s current working fit for each family through publish_model_fit (calibration.fitting.model_publication), and leaves one artifact set per family that modeling_review.py (calibration.modeling_review) reads back — while the separate Publish Models workflow copies an exact, validated snapshot into an immutable Generator model library.

This page is the hub that ties the three model fitters together. It maps the unified fan-out and preflight, Calibration’s replaceable one-current-fit-per-kind contract, the separate immutable-library publication boundary, the read side that powers the operator’s modeling surface, and the three shared modules every fit calls before it touches color data. In older implementation names, publish_model_fit means “make this Calibration fit current”; it does not mean “publish a library to Generator.” It does not re-derive any model’s math — the physics of each fit lives in its own page and in How It Works. For the three fitters themselves see Spline model fitting (v1), Photo-stack model fitting (v2), and The camera transform fitter; for the model forms, Color Model v1 / Color Model v2 / The Camera Transform.
Related: calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow · calibration.fitting.model_publication · calibration.model_library_publication · lib.standard_model_library · lib.model_library_store · calibration.modeling_review · calibration.fitting.physical_stack · calibration.fitting.filament_roles · calibration.fitting.filament_exclusions
The unified fan-out — one button, three fitters
“Fit Models” is the operator label for the maintenance operation refit_calibration_models (app/app.js:9572 maps the id to the button text). It is registered as a maintenance operation, so it runs through the same preflight/execute pair as every other operation: _preflight_refit_calibration_models (maintenance.py:2772) and _execute_refit_calibration_models (maintenance.py:2793), both of which are thin wrappers that call into model_fit_workflow.py via options_from_scope, build_model_fit_preflight, and execute_model_fit_workflow (imported at maintenance.py:48-50). The workflow preflight is SQLite-only; non-SQLite stores are returned as blocked rather than being sent through the fitters (model_fit_workflow.py:214-231).
The workflow recognizes three model kinds, named by module constants (model_fit_workflow.py:49-51): MODEL_LEGACY_SPLINE = "legacy_spline", MODEL_PHOTO_STACK = "photo_stack_v2", MODEL_CAMERA_TRANSFORM = "camera_transform". execute_model_fit_workflow (:409) runs them in a fixed sequence and short-circuits on the first failure:

Legacy spline (v1) — run_legacy_spline_fit_all(..., publish=True) (:444), from calibration.fitting.legacy_spline_fit_job. Detail: Spline model fitting (v1).
Photo Stack (v2) — run_photo_stack_fit_job (:496), then publish_artifact_directory_model_fit (:502). Detail: Photo-stack model fitting (v2).
Camera Transform — run_camera_transform_build_job (:542), then publish_artifact_directory_model_fit (:548). Detail: The camera transform fitter.

The three fitters are parallel siblings on a shared spine, not layered: each loads its own evidence, fits, and independently replaces its current Calibration fit; the workflow just orders them and aggregates status. The legacy-spline and photo-stack stages always run; the camera-transform stage runs only when its plan says so (below). A _stage_progress adapter (:321) rescales each fitter’s inner progress into an overall bar sized total_stages (:418), and _cancelled checks (:429, :480, :524) let the operator abort between stages.
Workflow options and the preflight
ModelFitWorkflowOptions (:49) is a frozen two-field dataclass: force_camera_transform and use_fit_exclusions (the latter pinned to True). options_from_scope (:97) builds it from the request scope, reading only force_camera_transform — the per-run fit-state exclusions are always on for this workflow.
build_model_fit_preflight (:206) is the gate. It first refuses any non-SQLite backend outright (:212-223, “Fit Models requires the SQLite backend”), then builds a model_plan (:245) for the three kinds. Legacy and photo-stack are hardwired to action: "run" with reason always_refit_color_models (:246-255) — the two color models are always refit. The camera transform is the only conditional stage: _build_camera_transform_plan (:141) compares the live fit-input fingerprint against both the stored artifact manifest and the current model-fit record, and returns run (forced, missing artifact, no current fit, fingerprint_mismatch, old_fingerprint, or input_changed) or skip (up_to_date) (:151-164). The preflight also computes a plan_digest (_build_plan_digest, :183) — a SHA-256 over the scope, per-kind action/reason, and each fitter’s input hashes. execute_model_fit_workflow recomputes the preflight and refuses to run if the stored plan_digest no longer matches (:414-415, “Model fitting plan changed. Run preflight again”), so a plan the operator reviewed can’t silently change under them.
The result envelope carries status, per-kind model_results, a historically named partial_publication map recording which kinds actually got a new current model_fit_id (:428-432), and a ui_refresh directive (_model_ui_refresh, :72) that invalidates the model-artifact caches for all three kinds. Current-fit replacement is not a transaction spanning all three fitters: the spline stage can complete before Photo Stack or Camera Transform fails, and cancellation after a completed stage returns the earlier replacement with a targeted refresh (:451-486, :488-500, :572-579). No immutable Generator library is created by Fit Models.
Direct fitter entry points
The unified operation is the main fan-out, but the server also exposes separate asynchronous jobs: POST /api/photo-stack/start (server.py:8216), POST /api/camera-transform/build (:8243), and the spline /api/profiles/fit-all routes (:6434-6463). These paths run one fitter and replace its current result through the same internal store boundary; they are not alternate model kinds and do not publish a Generator library. The server uses _try_begin_model_fit_run / _end_model_fit_run around these jobs (:7313-:7377, :7460-:7524) and the direct spline routes, so overlapping model-fit jobs are rejected with a conflict rather than allowed to replace the same working state concurrently. The unified maintenance job also claims the maintenance_model_fit owner and is checked by the same blocker logic.
Internal current-fit replacement — one fit per kind, staleness aware
calibration.fitting.model_publication holds the shared publish helpers that every fitter routes through. It has no intra-project imports — a pure boundary layer over the store. Two entry shapes:

Directory publish primitive — publish_artifact_directory_model_fit (model_publication.py:98) walks an artifact directory (model_artifacts_from_directory, :63), converts every file to a store-relative POSIX path (store_relative_posix_path, :13, which raises if a path escapes the data root), and calls the store’s publish_model_fit.
Coordinated directory-model publishers — publish_photo_stack_fit (:127) and publish_camera_transform_fit (:172) activate the staged filesystem pointer, invoke the directory primitive, roll the pointer and staged directory back if SQLite publication fails, and garbage-collect the prior run/generation only after both layers succeed.
Legacy-spline publish — production fitting uses publish_staged_legacy_spline_fit (:218), which swaps a complete staged profiles directory and staged pair_corrections.json into place, calls publish_legacy_spline_fit (:351), and restores the old files if database publication fails (:241-:288). The lower-level publisher records one spline_profile:{fid} artifact per fitted filament plus the shared pair-correction file. publish_legacy_spline_artifact_set (:291) is the sibling that republishes the current files outside the staged fit path, guarded by profile_file_is_publishable (:33): excluded filaments and profile JSON carrying stale / stale_reason / stale_at are omitted.

All of them converge on the store’s historically named publish_model_fit (sqlite_data_access.py:4103), which treats a model family as one replaceable current Calibration fit, not a fit-history archive. Before writing, it collects every existing row for the same model_kind (:4127-:4137). In one write transaction it inserts the replacement fit, contributors, and artifacts as current (:4139-:4201), then deletes all prior parent rows (:4203-:4210); foreign-key cascades remove their contributor and artifact rows. The return payload reports those deleted ids as superseded_model_fit_ids (:4212-:4215), but there is no durable superseded activation state. model_kind is validated against _MODEL_KINDS = {"camera_transform", "legacy_spline", "photo_stack_v2"} (sqlite_data_access.py:49) and current-fit replacement requires at least one contributor (:4121-:4123).
stale means something different from superseded. A currently retained fit is marked stale when evidence or fit controls that contributed to it are changed, so its artifacts no longer describe the corpus state from which it was fitted. Adding newly processed evidence does not retroactively make an existing fit incorrect merely because that evidence was not among its contributors. A stale row remains available to status/review code until a successful current-fit replacement deletes it. Startup also calls prune_superseded_model_fits (server.py:449-:457, sqlite_data_access.py:4368) to collapse databases created under the older history-retaining lifecycle to one row per family.
User publication — one-way immutable copy to Generator
The topbar Publish Models workflow is a separate ownership boundary implemented by calibration.model_library_publication, lib.standard_model_library, and lib.model_library_store. It never changes Calibration’s current-fit lifecycle. GET /api/models/publication/readiness (server.py:8822) verifies that all three required fits are current, their registered artifacts still match their hashes and schemas, the combined contract is consistent, and the public filament catalog is available. A missing, stale, changed, or incomplete component blocks both publication actions.
After the operator supplies the library name, version, and publisher (plus optional description and release notes), the dialog offers two copies of that exact current generation:

Export Library Package calls POST /api/models/publication/export (server.py:8836) and writes a validated ZIP under Calibration/Output/Published Models.
Publish to Generator calls POST /api/models/publication/install (server.py:8855) and installs a new immutable library under Generator’s Model Libraries folder. It is deliberately inactive; the operator must open Generator’s Models dialog and choose Activate and Restart Prisma.
Open Published Models Folder calls the local-only POST /api/models/publication/open-folder (server.py:8875).

The allowlisted payload contains the public filament manifest/catalog plus the runtime artifacts for legacy spline v1, Photo Stack v2, and Camera Transform. It does not contain Calibration’s SQLite database, source or extracted images, samples, raw evidence, per-sample calibration predictions, or private notes. Publication stages and validates a copy, then either packages it or lets the Generator library store install it; Calibration does not retain a mutable published-model tree and cannot later modify or activate the installed copy (model_library_publication.py:83, :93, :261, :289). Generator likewise cannot see or alter Calibration’s working artifacts.
The read side — what the Modeling page renders
calibration.modeling_review is the read half: it never fits anything, it loads Calibration’s current working artifacts and compares them against observed color. It is imported only by calibration.server, which exposes it at /api/models/status and the overview/sample/filament review endpoints (server.py:8276, :8282-:8343). Its six public builders back The Modeling page:

build_model_status_payload (modeling_review.py:63) — per-kind currentness (state, generated_at, stale_reason) via _model_currentness_payload (:38), labeled by the display map MODEL_LABELS (:20-24): legacy_spline → "Color Model v1", photo_stack_v2 → "Color Model v2", camera_transform → "Camera Transform".
build_modeling_overview (:555) — inclusion counts (samples/swatches included vs excluded) plus an attention block.
list_modeling_samples (:669) / get_modeling_sample (:702) — the per-sample review, whose detail (_sample_model_detail, :435) is the heart of the comparison.
list_modeling_filaments (:769) / get_modeling_filament (:815) — the per-filament view.

_sample_model_detail (:435) is where observed and predicted meet. It loads the current camera transform as the display transform (_load_display_transform, :250), then builds two predictions: _photo_stack_model_domains (:324, reads the latest v2 sample_predictions.json artifact) and _legacy_spline_model_domains (:367, recomposes v1 on the fly through composition.compose using the sample’s canonical geometry). Both, plus the measured values, are emitted in two domains — transmission (raw linear-to-hex) and appearance (the camera transform applied, _model_domains_from_linear, :271) — each with corrected and uncorrected variants. So the page shows measured vs v1 vs v2, in the transmission and camera-appearance domains, with pair corrections on or off. The Camera Transform’s role here is the appearance transform applied to all three series (not a fourth per-swatch prediction); when it is missing the appearance domain is returned unavailable (:284-290). The transform math is The Camera Transform; the modeling surface is The Modeling page.
Shared foundation 1 — the sample→stack bridge
calibration.fitting.physical_stack is the single bridge from a sample record to a canonical bottom-to-top layer stack; its docstring is explicit that callers “must not reconstruct stack order from legacy fixed/variable convenience fields” (physical_stack.py:1-7). Both v1 and v2 go through it (its Imported by list is fitting and the v2 evidence module).
physical_stack_for_swatch (:172) reads sample.roles in canonical role_index order, pulls the one variable role’s thickness from the swatch’s variable series, validates exactly one variable role (:233-236), and returns a frozen PhysicalStack (:53) of RoleLayers (:27). Along the way _model_role_hints (:120) assigns each layer a semantic role from physical position: a white below all color is base_white, white above is cap_white, color is color, and a white sandwiched between non-white layers is rejected as ambiguous (:148-152). physical_stacks_for_sample (:275) maps it over every swatch. Two predicates round it out: has_fixed_above_variable (:294) and is_legacy_spline_supported_stack (:314, true only when the variable role is physically topmost) — the latter is how v1 decides whether it can interpret a geometry at all. Failures raise PhysicalStackError (:23) rather than guessing. The optics of stacking these layers is Color Model v1 / Color Model v2.
Shared foundation 2 — filament role and white classifiers
calibration.fitting.filament_roles supplies the explicit model-white classification used by the color-model fitters:

White — model_white_filament_ids (filament_roles.py:41) returns the set of filaments flagged white_cap_eligible; is_model_white (:99) tests membership. This is the set physical_stack’s role-hint logic uses to tell base white from cap white.
Crucially, the module also bakes classifier provenance into a color-model fit. filament_role_snapshot captures each filament’s white_cap_eligible and exclude_from_model flags; filament_role_snapshot_hash hashes that snapshot; photo_stack_bundle_classifier_metadata packages the white-classifier schema, version, id list, and snapshot hash into the v2 runtime bundle. require_known_filaments fails loudly if evidence references a filament absent from the library. Camera Transform validation instead groups only by sample and measured transmission.

Shared foundation 3 — per-filament model exclusion
calibration.fitting.filament_exclusions is a small, always-on, stateless dropper (filament_exclusions.py:1-13): a filament flagged exclude_from_model in the registry is removed from every production fit. It is imported by all three fit paths (v1 fitting, v2 evidence, CT corpus).
The precise semantic is the load-bearing part. excluded_filament_ids (:19) reads the flagged ids from the registry. sample_references_excluded_filament (:58) drops a sample if the excluded filament appears in ANY role — variable or fixed backing — via _sample_filament_ids (:34), which walks the canonical sample.roles table and returns every referenced filament id, not just the characterized (variable) one. So excluding a white backing filament removes not only its own solo strips but every overlay sample that stacks on top of it. samples_excluded_by_filament (:65) precomputes that whole-corpus set of dropped samples; only the v1 spline fit unions it in directly (fitting.py:1190). The v2 photo-stack (evidence.py:227) and the camera-transform corpus (corpus.py:520) instead read excluded_filament_ids and apply the same rule per sample via sample_references_excluded_filament — row by row rather than from the precomputed set.
This is distinct from the per-run fit_exclude / fit_state toggles (which are UI-gated on use_fit_exclusions): exclude_from_model is a permanent property of the filament, ungated, replacing the old hardwired SKIP constant. Where the flag is set and what it means operationally is Managing filaments.

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/p.title: Photo-stack model fitting (v2)
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/p.content:
In one sentence: the calibration side of Color Model v2 is a thin driver — live datastore samples become canonical fit evidence (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.evidence), that evidence is bridged into the vendored research numerical fitter and renamed into the public contract (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit), a fit-job boundary writes a staged candidate (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job), and the shared publication boundary coordinates its latest.json activation with SQLite replacement before deleting the old run — while the heavy model math lives entirely in lib.photo_stack_model.*.

This page is the code-level map of the v2 (photo-stack) fit driver. It maps the modules, the data flow, and what is live versus vestigial. It does not re-derive the model itself — for what an optical-density curve, a white-context term, or a pair correction is, and why the model is shaped the way it is, read the How It Works page Color Model v2 — model and correction layer both — (and, for the earlier spline model, Color Model v1). The shared numerical model — fitting, prediction, and artifact I/O — lives in lib.photo_stack_model.model, lib.photo_stack_model.predict, and lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts; calibration only feeds it and files its output. How this fit is triggered, published, and reviewed within the unified model-fit workflow is Model workflow, publication, and review; the operator’s-eye view is The Modeling page.
On this page, publish_photo_stack_fit and similar code names mean “make this Calibration fit current.” They replace Calibration’s working generation and do not create, activate, or mutate an immutable Generator model library; user-facing publication is the separate Publish Models boundary.
Related: calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.evidence · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.write_artifact · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.photo_stack_engine · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.metrics · calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.smoke_fit_job
The driver pipeline at a glance
One public entry point strings four stages together. run_photo_stack_fit_job (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.fit_job, fit_job.py:350) is a six-step job (total = 6, :362):

Build evidence — build_photo_stack_evidence(store, …) (fit_job.py:365 → evidence.py:213).
Fit — fit_live_photo_stack_bundle(evidence) (fit_job.py:378-388 → live_fit.py:516), run under a heartbeat so a long fit still emits progress.
Fit the correction layer — apply_or_build_photo_stack_correction(…) (fit_job.py:399), which lives in the shared lib.photo_stack_model.correction_layer.
Write the candidate — write_photo_stack_candidate(…, update_latest=publish) (fit_job.py:484-:496 → write_artifact.py:14). Both production callers pass publish=False, leaving activation to publish_photo_stack_fit after the fit returns (model_fit_workflow.py:504-:511; server :7475-:7482).

Steps in between assemble a measured-vs-predicted review payload (_build_sample_predictions, fit_job.py:202) and a review summary (_review_summary, fit_job.py:310). The reached-from edges are on the fit-job node’s Imported by list: calibration.fitting.model_fit_workflow (the unified workflow that calls it live), calibration.server, and the dev harness smoke_fit_job — see the Model workflow, publication, and review page for the workflow wiring.
Stage 1 — evidence: live samples → canonical fit rows
build_photo_stack_evidence (evidence.py:213) walks store.list_samples() and emits one canonical evidence document: a summary, an input_fingerprint, per-sample records, and per-swatch records. It is strict by design — the docstring notes geometry must be annotated, with no swatch-index fallback (evidence.py:219-224). Failures raise EvidenceBuildError (evidence.py:41).
What the adapter does, and does not, decide:

It filters, it does not fit. Samples are skipped (recorded in skipped_samples, not silently dropped) for referencing an exclude_from_model filament (evidence.py:249-252), not being processed (:253-255), or missing measurements / strip definition (:256-261).
Measured color comes from the sidecar, not the sample. _MEASURED_SOURCE = "sidecar" (evidence.py:174) makes the per-swatch linear RGB read from the extraction-result sidecar via _sidecar_swatch_map (evidence.py:191), which fails loud if the sidecar is absent or malformed. Fit-control state (fit_state, exclusion_reason) stays a live read off the sample. use_measured_source("legacy") (evidence.py:178) can temporarily flip back to the Sample.measurements color path. For what the sidecar is, see Extraction and Data access and persistence.
It classifies the physical stack. Each swatch’s realized bottom-to-top layer stack (from physical_stack_for_swatch) is tagged by _classify_realized_stack (evidence.py:120) into evidence classes (white_only, naked_single_filament, color_over_white, single_color_sandwich, cross_color_multilayer_sandwich, …) that the fitter later uses to pick a role family.
It fingerprints its inputs. input_fingerprint (evidence.py:389) hashes the samples directory, the filament registry, the filament-role snapshot, and the evidence itself — this is what makes a re-fit on unchanged data reproducible downstream.

use_fit_exclusions (default False, evidence.py:216) controls whether excluded samples/swatches are marked included=False; the live workflow passes True (see Stage 3). The color math here (linear→OKLab, optical density) is inlined deliberately “without importing the spline runtime” (_linear_to_oklab, evidence.py:48) — it is bookkeeping, not the model.
Stage 2 — live_fit: the bridge to the vendored fitter
live_fit.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit) is, in its own words, “the Prisma-owned bridge from calibration datastore evidence to the accepted research numerical fitter. The research math is vendored unchanged … this wrapper handles only live evidence adaptation, candidate metadata, runtime bundle export, and translation of the research engine’s output names into the public photo-stack contract” (live_fit.py:1-8). The model math is not here — the fitter is imported from the vendored research engine package (live_fit.py:46-48) and the public model/predict/artifact surface is lib.photo_stack_model.model / lib.photo_stack_model.predict / lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts.
fit_live_photo_stack_bundle (live_fit.py:516) does three things:

Reshape. evidence_payload_to_photo_stack_rows (live_fit.py:274) flattens the canonical evidence into the wide pandas row schema the research fitter expects, reading each swatch’s explicit bottom-to-top model_layer_triples (_model_layers_from_swatch, live_fit.py:203) rather than inferring stack order from legacy fixed/variable columns. It raises if there is not at least one included swatch (live_fit.py:390-391).
Fit on the full corpus — no holdout. The rows are passed straight to research_fit.full_fit_predictions(rows, …) (live_fit.py:526); the model is fit and predicted on the same included rows. There is a fold = sample_num % 5 column (live_fit.py:379), but the live fit does not split on it — predictions are in-sample. Excluded swatches are dropped upstream (Stage 1) via the included flag, not held out for validation here.
Rename into the public contract. Because the vendored engine stamps its own codenames, _sanitize_public_payload (live_fit.py:78) and _rename_research_prediction_columns (live_fit.py:98) rewrite research identity tokens to the public photo_stack / v2 names. Only strings change; numbers are untouched, so “the artifact stays numerically identical” (live_fit.py:78-83). The assembled _build_bundle (live_fit.py:440) validates against the shared lib.photo_stack_model.bundle schema and stamps a reproducible fingerprint (live_fit.py:497) that deliberately excludes wall-clock timing fields (_fingerprint_payload, live_fit.py:134). The return value is a frozen LiveFitResult (live_fit.py:113).

Stage 3 — fit_job: orchestration, correction layer, review payload
Back in fit_job.py, after the live fit the job:

Validates the bundle is a live source-of-truth artifact (_validate_live_fit_bundle, fit_job.py:303).
Builds/refits the correction layer by handing the live predictions to the shared apply_or_build_photo_stack_correction (fit_job.py:399), producing the photo_stack_v2_corrected model (CORRECTED_MODEL_NAME, fit_job.py:31). What the correction layer does is covered by Color Model v2’s correction-layer section; the code lives in lib.photo_stack_model.correction_layer.
Assembles the review payload — _build_sample_predictions (fit_job.py:202) turns the corrected full-fit rows into per-sample, per-swatch measured-vs-predicted chips (with stack diagrams and OKLab deltas), and _review_summary (fit_job.py:310) rolls up mean / p90 / max ΔE. This is the JSON the review UI renders; see The Modeling page.
Emits progress through _emit / _run_with_heartbeat (fit_job.py:39, :52) so the six phases surface in the webapp job stream.

When the unified workflow drives this job it passes use_fit_exclusions=True (model_fit_workflow.py:508), so operator sample/swatch exclusions are honored; the standalone default is False (fit_job.py:354).
Stage 4 — staged write and coordinated publication
write_photo_stack_candidate (write_artifact.py:14) is a thin pass-through to the shared writer write_candidate_artifact in lib.photo_stack_model.artifacts — its only job is to write a candidate without touching legacy spline profile outputs. Everything structural happens in the shared writer:

Candidates land under data_root/filaments/photo_stack_models/<run_id>/ (candidate_root, artifacts.py:33), written atomically: files go to .tmp-<run_id>, required files and the runtime bundle are validated, then os.replace publishes the complete directory (artifacts.py:278-:367).
write_candidate_artifact still supports update_latest=True for direct/compatibility callers (:291, :357-:375), but that is not the production webapp publication path. The workflow and standalone server job deliberately write with publish=False.
publish_photo_stack_fit (model_publication.py:127) validates the staged directory, atomically advances latest.json with activate_candidate_artifact, and then calls SQLite publish_model_fit (:144-:163). If SQLite publication fails, it restores the prior pointer and deletes the staged run (:164-:167). Only after both pointer and database replacement succeed does it garbage-collect superseded run directories, keeping one (:168).

There is no operator-facing commit step, but there is an internal publication transaction with compensating filesystem rollback. A successful fit becomes the sole runtime run and sole retained photo_stack_v2 database fit; a database publication failure leaves the prior run and fit selected.
Vestigial and support modules
Three modules in this package are not on the live fit path:

photo_stack_engine.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.photo_stack_engine) is largely vestigial. Its docstring states outright: “Live fitting now happens in fitting.photo_stack_model.live_fit” (photo_stack_engine.py:1-7). What fit_job still imports from it is only the status constant ENGINE_STATUS_READY (fit_job.py:13); the constants themselves are defined at photo_stack_engine.py:22-23. The pending-payload machinery — build_pending_photo_stack_candidate_payload (:99), build_context_index (:55), require_photo_stack_runtime_ready (:167) — describes an “engine not yet wired” era and is diagnostic-only; its Imported by list is just the fit job.
metrics.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.metrics) is a near-stub. Its single function summarize_metric_rows (metrics.py:8) returns {"row_count": …} and nothing more; the module’s docstring calls it a helper “for future photo stack fitting jobs.” Its Architecture node shows it is not imported by any other calibration module.
smoke_fit_job.py (calibration.fitting.photo_stack_model.smoke_fit_job) is a developer CLI. Its docstring: “a developer smoke harness, not a user-facing webapp command” (smoke_fit_job.py:1-4). It constructs a raw DataStore (smoke_fit_job.py:30) and runs the fit job from a --data-root argument (:25); it is not imported by anything.

(For contrast, the sibling legacy_spline_fit_job.py — the v1 driver — is live despite its name, reached through the same unified model-fit workflow; that is documented on the Color Model v1 fitting page, not here.)

prisma-calibration/technical-reference/s.title: Sample mutations, invalidation, and profile staleness
prisma-calibration/technical-reference/s.content:
Sample evidence and provenance changes are handled by sample_mutations.py (calibration.sample_mutations) and by the SQLite-aware routes in server.py. The important invariant is that a meaning-changing mutation must not leave measurements, extraction artifacts, review state, or fitted profiles looking current.
Status is derived only for unprocessed samples
recompute_sample_status(sample) leaves processing_status unchanged when sample.measurements is present. Otherwise it assigns assigned only when assigned_image, assigned_blank_id, and orientation_rots are all set; any incomplete evidence assignment becomes unassigned. This helper does not inspect the database extraction-result table.
The server’s _maybe_mark_assigned is an older local helper and is not the main mutation seam for the current assignment routes. assign-image, assign-blank, image swapping, rejection, and provenance updates call invalidate_sample_processing when their meaning changes, then save through the selected store.
What counts as processing output
_has_processing_outputs treats any of the following as output: in-memory measurements; status processed, failed, or flagged; a SQLite extraction result; a legacy JSON thumbnail directory; or a JSON extraction-result sidecar. A pending SQLite extraction result therefore counts even if the model object has no measurements yet.
When invalidation finds no output, it only recomputes assignment status. When output exists, it clears measurements, flag_reason, review_accepted, excluded_swatches, and, by default, fit_exclude. It then recomputes assigned/unassigned from the evidence fields.
For the JSON backend, invalidation also removes thumbnails/{sample_id} and the extraction-result sidecar. If the previous sample could have contributed to a fit—its measurements existed or its status was processed—the previous sample’s variable and fixed filament IDs are passed to flag_profile_stale.
For SQLite, invalidate_sample_processing itself does not call mark_profiles_stale_for_sample and does not delete the extraction row. SQLite performs those durable operations inside SQLiteDataStore._save_sample_in_tx when the changed sample signature is saved: geometry, role assignments, evidence, and certain processed-state changes can trigger model-fit staleness and extraction-result deletion. This split is intentional in the current code path: callers must save the mutated sample for the SQLite invalidation to become durable.
Evidence routes
POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/assign-image verifies the managed image, clears orientation when the image changes unless the request explicitly supplies one, and invalidates on image or orientation changes. POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/assign-blank verifies the blank and, for SQLite, rejects a missing non-active blank source. It invalidates when the blank changes.
POST /api/samples/swap-images swaps the two image fields, clears both orientations because orientation is source-photo-specific, invalidates both samples, and uses SQLite save_samples when available. POST /api/samples/{sample_id}/reject invalidates the sample and saves it for reprocessing. Deletion marks profiles stale directly for samples with measurements or processed status before deleting the sample.
Provenance mutation
PUT /api/samples/{sample_id} resolves a StepRecord, validates explicit role assignments, and can update the geometry reference, variable/fixed filament fields, notes, and review acceptance. In SQLite, canonical role_assignments are required for writes that change sample geometry or roles; the legacy variable/fixed fields are compatibility payloads and cannot remap a SQLite sample by themselves. A role assignment must cover exactly the selected geometry’s role indices, resolve every filament, contain exactly one variable role, and preserve the role’s role_kind.
When geometry or role provenance changes, the route compares the old and new role/geometry signatures, calls invalidation with a reason naming the changed fields, and saves with the explicit role payload. SQLite’s save transaction compares the current database signature with the new signature, deletes the extraction result when the signature meaningfully changes, marks affected model fits stale, rewrites role rows, updates the evidence relation, and writes fit controls as needed.
The lower-level apply_sample_update function is retained as domain logic for older callers. It has a compatibility-era geometry rebuild that supplies fallback strip dimensions rather than the canonical StepRecord.strip_geometry; the live SQLite route contains the authoritative explicit-role path. The function also documents that its notes request field is not represented by the current Sample model, so callers should not treat it as the SQLite write seam.
Profile ownership
sample_profile_filament_ids returns the sample’s variable filament and all nonempty fixed filament IDs. That set is the dependency set used by JSON invalidation and by direct deletion handling. It is not a claim that every profile used every layer; it is the conservative ownership relation exposed by the current model.
