prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Palette suggestion search and ranking
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: given an image’s color signature and a pool of calibrated filaments, this precomputes single/pair gamut distances, searches palette subsets exhaustively or by multi-start greedy refinement, and returns distinct candidates ranked by either mean error or a hole-penalising robust score.

This page covers the search (how palettes are explored) and ranking (how palettes are scored and ordered) halves of generator.palette.suggest. For how the image is turned into the color signature that drives it, see Automatic palette suggestion. For the filament-gamut clouds the search scores against, see Automatic palette suggestion.
All code references are to generator/palette/suggest.py unless noted.

How to drive it (user-facing)
The generator web app’s Auto-suggest flow (POST /api/palette/suggest, generator/server.py:3798) takes these knobs from PaletteSuggestPayload (generator/server.py:3496):













































FieldDefaultEffectn_filaments7Target palette size (color filaments, white not counted).top_k5How many distinct candidate palettes to return. This is a contract — see below.filament_idsnullRestrict the search pool; null = all profiled non-white filaments.max_swapsnullIf set, run the swap-tier sweep instead of a single-size search.palette_mode"standard""standard" or "luminance_detail" (chroma-emphasized). Normalized by the payload validator.improvement_thresholdnullCoverage gain (%) required to justify another swap tier.force_all_tiersnullEvaluate every swap tier even if improvement stalls.
The web app always runs the thorough search. There is no current search_mode parameter in suggest_palettes; the endpoint payload forbids unknown fields, so the removed search_mode/quality_weights fields are rejected. The current function dispatches directly to _thorough_search (suggest.py:1745 onward).
The job runs on a background thread; poll status at GET /api/palette/suggest/status (generator/server.py:3996) and cancel via POST /api/palette/suggest/cancel (generator/server.py:4010).

Current search strategy
suggest_palettes() (suggest.py:1745) prepares the palette-search context, including all single/pair gamut distance vectors, then calls _thorough_search (suggest.py:1806). Because trial palettes use those precomputed vectors, scoring is a cheap array reduction rather than a fresh KD-tree build/query.
_thorough_search() (suggest.py:1159) chooses between two strategies by combination count:

Exhaustive when C(n_available, n_filaments) <= 500,000 (_EXHAUSTIVE_COMBO_LIMIT, suggest.py:67) → _exhaustive_search() (suggest.py:1213) enumerates every combination and retains a bounded candidate buffer before diverse selection.
Multi-start greedy otherwise → _multi_start_search() (suggest.py:1387). It seeds from up to the best eight individual filaments, runs greedy-build plus local-swap refinement from each seed, and deduplicates candidates by filament set before the final selection.

Both branches use _select_diverse_candidates() (suggest.py:1121) for the final result. It prefers candidates whose filament sets differ by at least two members, never returns duplicate sets, and then fills from rejected distinct candidates if the diversity floor would prevent returning top_k.

Trap: there are unrelated “greedy”/“beam-search” implementations elsewhere in the generator (post-solve grouping/scheduling). The greedy here is palette-selection greedy over filament subsets — it has nothing to do with layer grouping.


Ranking: mean vs robust
Every trial palette is scored from precomputed distances by _score_palette_metrics() (suggest.py:1011), which returns (mean_de, max_de, pct_above_threshold, p90_de). The single scalar used to order palettes comes from _palette_rank_score() (suggest.py:1046):




















ModeObjectiveCode"mean"mean_de onlysuggest.py:1046 onward"robust"mean_de + 0.35·p90_de + 0.15·max_de + 0.03·(pct_above_threshold/100)suggest.py:1046 onward
Robust mode deliberately penalises visible holes (a high 90th-percentile or worst-case centroid distance), not just the average — a palette with a great mean but one badly-missed color region ranks worse than its mean alone suggests.
Default ranking is data-driven (suggest.py:1677): "robust" when a gamut_backend is supplied (the model-backed web-app path), "mean" otherwise. Any value other than "mean"/"robust" raises (suggest.py:1680).
The component metrics:

mean_de — weight-averaged nearest-gamut OKLab distance across signature centroids.
max_de — worst single centroid distance.
pct_above_threshold — % of image weight whose nearest-gamut distance exceeds de_threshold (default SUGGESTION_COVERAGE_DE_THRESHOLD = 0.02, suggest.py:61, ~1 JND). Coverage surfaced to the UI is 100 - pct_above_threshold, computed in the response formatter (generator/server.py:3565); the swap-tier sweep computes the same quantity internally (suggest.py:1878).
p90_de — weighted 90th percentile via _weighted_percentile() (suggest.py:780).

The final candidate sort key is (rank_score, mean_de, max_de) (_candidate_sort_key, suggest.py:966) — rank score first, with mean and max as tie-breakers.

The requested-count distinctness contract
N requested = N distinct palettes whenever the pool allows. This is an explicit user contract, not a best-effort. The danger is that multi-start greedy converges to the same optimum from many seeds — and near-equal color error is not user-equivalence (color-distance metrics are not the final word; the right palette is the one the user picks).
When the multi-start branch converges to fewer than top_k candidates, _multi_start_search() adds scored swap neighbors (suggest.py:1595 onward). The common _select_diverse_candidates() pass then removes duplicate sets and fills the requested count from additional distinct candidates when the pool allows.

Note: distinctness is by set of filament IDs (frozenset), not by recipe. Two palettes with the same filaments but different thickness assignments are the same candidate here — thickness is decided downstream by the solver, not by suggestion.


Swap-tier sweep
suggest_palettes_swap_aware() (suggest.py:2258) models the reality that an AMS unit only holds a few filaments at once, so reaching more colors means mid-print filament swaps. It sweeps tiers 0..max_swaps:

Tier t computes one or more palette sizes from _tier_palette_sizes() (suggest.py:1967), based on the per-load color capacity and available filament count.
For each tier/size it runs _thorough_search() and packages a SwapTierResult (suggest.py:1942) carrying candidates, best mean dE, and coverage.
Early stop: after tier 0, if coverage improvement over the previous tier is below improvement_threshold it stops, unless force_all_tiers (suggest.py:2258 onward).

Endpoint wiring
The /api/palette/suggest job (generator/server.py:3798) builds a common_kwargs dict once — white profiles, de_threshold, the excluded-filament set, and gamut_luminance_weight — then branches on max_swaps.

max_swaps set → suggest_palettes_swap_aware(...), result formatted by _format_tier_response (generator/server.py:3651).
max_swaps unset → suggest_palettes(...), formatted by _format_candidate_response (generator/server.py:3619).

Two availability guards run before any palette is suggested: a configured white base/cap that is exclude_from_model raises 400 up front, and the color pool is filtered through excluded_filament_ids(...) so an excluded filament can never enter a suggestion. suggest_palettes() also filters to filaments the gamut backend supports() (suggest.py:1669–1672).

Dead printability heuristics (flagged)
suggest.py defines three “printability metrics” under a # ── Printability metrics ── banner (suggest.py:1733):

























FunctionLocationLivenessestimate_fragmentationsuggest.py:1881Dead in productionestimate_grouping_costsuggest.py:1903Dead in productionestimate_swap_costsuggest.py:1925Dead in production
A whole-repo grep for these three names finds callers only in tests/generator/test_palette_suggest.py and their own definitions — no production code path imports or calls them. They are not wired into suggest_palettes(), suggest_palettes_swap_aware(), the rank score, or the server endpoint. None of the ranking objectives (suggest.py:1046) reference fragmentation, grouping cost, or swap cost; ranking is purely color-error driven. These are vestigial heuristics kept alive only by their unit tests.

Caveat: “dead” here means no production caller as of this audit. The functions still pass their tests and could be revived. Do not delete blindly — confirm the tests’ intent first.


Quick reference: key symbols

































































SymbolLocationRolesuggest_palettessuggest.py:1745Top-level entry; prepares context and runs thorough search._thorough_searchsuggest.py:1159Exhaustive-vs-multi-start chooser (500k threshold)._exhaustive_searchsuggest.py:1213Enumerate all C(N,k)._multi_start_searchsuggest.py:1387Multi-start greedy + local swap + distinctness fill._select_diverse_candidatessuggest.py:1121Deduplicate and apply the two-member diversity preference._palette_rank_scoresuggest.py:1046Mean vs robust objective._score_palette_metricssuggest.py:1011Mean/max/pct/p90 from precomputed distances._precompute_centroid_distancessuggest.py:928Per-centroid nearest-gamut distance tables.suggest_palettes_swap_awaresuggest.py:2258Swap-tier sweep with early stop.SwapTierResultsuggest.py:1942Per-tier result record.POST /api/palette/suggestgenerator/server.py:3789HTTP route (always thorough).
Related

Color signature extraction — the OKLab centroid signature this search scores.
Palette gamut backends — PhotoStackPaletteGamutBackend and single/pair gamut clouds.
The requested count is a contract: top_k distinct results is non-negotiable.
generator.palette.suggest — module-level architecture node.
lib.photo_stack_model.model — the appearance predictor behind the model-backed gamut.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Preprocessing operators
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: five self-registering image operators (A1, B1, B3, C1, C2) that condition the solve-grid raster before the solve — every one ships off by default — plus two shared helpers, feature_scale (a nozzle-derived spatial anchor) and hue_interp (circular hue interpolation).

Preprocessing operators
These operators live in the preprocessing slot, a chain that runs on the loaded image before the color solve. They are discovered from the filesystem under preprocessing/operators/ (no hand-maintained name list — _discover_preprocessing_operators, pipeline/registry.py:33; the “no hand-maintained tuple” rationale is at pipeline/registry.py:101), self-register via the @register_preprocessing decorator (pipeline/registry.py:123), and each subclasses PreprocessingModule (pipeline/base.py:73).
The slot is executed by run_preprocessing_pipeline (preprocessing/runner.py:210), called once from the live solve path at pipeline/runner.py:1016 — the same run_pipeline that hands off to the staged backend (run_staged_backend_path, pipeline/runner.py:1222–1225). So these operators are live in the webapp solve, not legacy CLI-only code. They run on the post-profile-load raster, before target-cloud computation and the staged solve.
Related: Feature scale anchor · Palette metadata and protect masking · preprocessing slot runner · PreprocessingModule contract · Module management
Class defaults and persisted state
Every operator declares default_enabled = False on its class — that is the fallback when no persisted toggle exists. _get_all_defaults reads the attribute for each registered operator (pipeline/modules.py:34) and load_module_state fills any operator missing from the live toggle file with it (pipeline/modules.py:38). The live enable state lives in app/modules.json, which the module manager rewrites as you toggle operators per-run; it is not a fixed all-off manifest. In the current checkout, c2_soft_gamut_compress is persisted enabled while the other four built-ins are false. Nothing here is guaranteed to be part of a baseline run unless the persisted state enables it.









































OperatorClass · nameorderNeeds palette?A1 bilateral denoiseA1BilateralDenoise · a1_bilateral_denoise (a1_bilateral_denoise.py:37)120.0 (:76)no (:77)B1 print-scale bilateralB1PrintscaleBilateral · b1_printscale_bilateral (b1_printscale_bilateral.py:85)210.0 (:91)no (:90)B3 TV flattenB3TvFlatten · b3_tv_flatten (b3_tv_flatten.py:72)220.0 (:78)no (:77)C1 achievable tonemapC1AchievableTonemap · c1_achievable_tonemap (c1_achievable_tonemap.py:210)310.0 (:216)yes (:217)C2 soft gamut compressC2SoftGamutCompress · c2_soft_gamut_compress (c2_soft_gamut_compress.py:318)330.0 (:327)yes (:328)
order controls chain position; the conventional bands are Wing A 100–199, Wing B 200–299, Wing C 300–399 (pipeline/base.py:79-81). So if you enable several, they run A1 → B1 → B3 → C1 → C2 regardless of the order you toggled them.
All five declare input_domain = output_domain = "srgb_f32" (e.g. a1_bilateral_denoise.py:74-75), i.e. float32 sRGB in [0, 1]. The Wing-C operators convert internally to OKLab and back (c1_achievable_tonemap.py:307, c2_soft_gamut_compress.py:130) but hand sRGB back out. Domain definitions: preprocessing types.

A1 — bilateral denoise (Wing A)

Edge-preserving denoise of the solve-grid raster via a single OpenCV bilateralFilter.

apply (a1_bilateral_denoise.py:108) runs cv2.bilateralFilter once with d = 2*radius_px + 1 (:123), sigmaColor = sigma_range, sigmaSpace = sigma_spatial (:124-129). It is the simplest operator: no palette, no OKLab — purely spatial sRGB smoothing.
It computes a “flat-region” mask up front (Rec.709 luma, local 5×5 std ≤ 0.02 — a1_bilateral_denoise.py:12-13, :30-32, :119) but uses it only for the reported metrics (flat-patch variance before/after, :141-142); the filter itself is applied globally, not gated by the mask.





























ParamDefaultRangeMeaning (from params, :39-72)radius_px31–8Bilateral radius in px; diameter is 2r+1.sigma_range0.040.005–0.25Range sigma in srgb_f32 units (intensity).sigma_spatial2.00.5–10.0Spatial sigma in px.
Constructor re-validates each param against the same bounds and raises ValueError on out-of-range (:85-92, :97-98). Emits debug_maps={"delta_abs_luma": ...} (:147) for the diff visualization.

B1 — print-scale bilateral (Wing B)

Bilateral flatten whose spatial sigma is tied to the printer’s physical feature scale, not a raw pixel count.

The key difference from A1: B1’s spatial sigma is derived in millimeters from the nozzle, then converted to pixels using the solver’s fine pitch. In _resolve_bilateral_params (b1_printscale_bilateral.py:38): sigma_spatial_mm = feature_scale_multiplier * feature_scale_mm (:44), then sigma_spatial_px = sigma_spatial_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm (:45), clamped to [0.5, 15.0] px (:15-16, :46-52), and the kernel diameter is 2*round(sigma_spatial_px)+1 (:53). feature_scale_mm comes from resolve_feature_scale_mm(context) (:176) — see feature_scale below; solver_fine_pitch_mm defaults to 0.20 if absent (:177-179).
The filter can run multiple passes (:72-78), then clips to [0, 1] (:79).





























ParamDefaultRangeMeaning (:92-135)feature_scale_multiplier1.00.5–2.0Multiplies the shared nozzle-derived feature scale (2×nozzle). 1.0 = blur exactly at print-feature scale; <1 preserves detail; >1 flattens more.sigma_range0.050.005–0.25Intensity sigma on [0,1]. Set higher than A1’s because B1 is a flattener, not a denoiser.passes11–3Bilateral-filter passes; 2–3 strengthen flattening at the cost of edge softness.
Reported metrics include the resolved feature_scale_mm, sigma_spatial_mm/px, kernel_d_px, and flat-region variance before/after (:202-218).

B3 — TV flatten (Wing B)

Total-variation (Chambolle) denoise that drives regions toward piecewise-constant patches, optionally in OKLab.

apply (b3_tv_flatten.py:224) runs denoise_tv_chambolle from scikit-image (:53, called through _tv_denoise). The wrapper reflectively adapts to the installed skimage API (max_num_iter/n_iter_max, channel_axis/multichannel) at :57-65, so it survives version drift.
Weight autoscaling is the Wing-B signature: with weight_autoscale=True, effective_weight = tv_weight * (feature_scale_mm / 0.40) (_effective_weight, :152-166; baseline _AUTOSCALE_BASELINE_MM = 0.40 at :20), then clamped to [0.005, 0.30] (:21-22, :157-159) with a warning if it clamps (:160-165). The 0.40 baseline is the default-nozzle feature scale, so at a 0.2 mm nozzle autoscale is a no-op and the weight you set is the weight applied.



































ParamDefaultRangeMeaning (:79-132)tv_weight0.040.005–0.40TV regularization weight; higher = stronger, more piecewise-constant.weight_autoscaleTrueboolScale weight by feature_scale_mm/0.40 so TV strength tracks the print-feature scale.channel_axisoklab_L_absrgb_rgb · oklab_L_ab · oklab_L_onlyColor space for TV: per-channel RGB; perceptual OKLab L+a+b (default); or OKLab-L only (flatten luminance, keep chroma).n_iter_max10020–500Chambolle iteration cap.
_run_tv (:168) branches on channel_axis: srgb_rgb denoises RGB directly (:176-183); oklab_L_ab converts to OKLab and denoises all three channels (:186-192); oklab_L_only denoises just L and re-attaches the original a/b (:193-200), then converts back to sRGB and clips (:201-205).
Reported metrics are the resolved feature_scale_mm, tv_weight, effective_weight, channel_axis, and n_iter_max (_metrics, :209-222).

C1 — achievable tonemap (Wing C)

Palette-aware tonal compression: remaps source luminance (OKLab L) into the range the chosen filament palette can physically reproduce.

C1 is the first operator that requires palette context (required_context = frozenset({"palette_metadata"}), c1_achievable_tonemap.py:217); it raises ValueError if context.palette_metadata is None (:301-304). The palette supplies the achievable black/white L (:311-312).
How it works: source is converted to OKLab (:307); shadow/highlight anchors are taken as percentiles of source L (:314-317); a 3-anchor PCHIP curve maps [shadow, midpoint, highlight] source L onto [achievable_black, midtone_target, achievable_white] (_build_core_curve, :35-55), where the midtone target is placed via 0.5 ** midtone_contrast (:43). Pixels outside the anchor range are extended by linear tails using the curve’s end slopes (_linear_tail_remap, :58-99), then clamped into the achievable range. The remap is blended with the original L by strength (_tonemap_pass, :156-159), and only the L channel is rewritten — a/b are preserved (:161-162).



































ParamDefaultRangeMeaning (:218-259)strength1.00.0–1.0Blend between source L and the achievable-range remap.shadow_percentile0.50.0–10.0Source-L percentile treated as the shadow anchor.highlight_percentile99.590.0–100.0Source-L percentile treated as the highlight anchor.midtone_contrast1.00.5–2.0Three-anchor PCHIP midpoint placement (0.5**contrast).
The constructor additionally requires shadow_percentile < highlight_percentile, raising otherwise (:281-284). Degenerate guards: C1 returns the input unchanged in two cases — if the achievable range collapses (white <= black + 1e-4, with a degenerate_palette metric, :319-328) or if shadow/highlight L coincide (no degenerate_palette flag, :330-338); both route through _zero_result (:175). C1 declares a preview_key (:211) so it can drive a preview tile. Debug maps: delta_L, clamp_mask (:371-373).

C2 — soft gamut compress (Wing C)

Hue-preserving soft-knee chroma compression: pulls over-saturated pixels in toward the palette’s per-hue maximum chroma without shifting their hue.

Also palette-required (required_context = frozenset({"palette_metadata"}), c2_soft_gamut_compress.py:328). It reads the palette’s chroma envelope from metadata — hue bin centers hue_degrees, lightness bin centers l_bin_centers, and the 2-D max_chroma_by_hue_l bound table (with 1-D max_chroma_by_hue retained as a fallback) (:391-406). For each source pixel it computes OKLab hue + chroma (_hue_and_chroma, :100-105) and queries the chroma bound at that hue and lightness via circular hue interpolation (_query_chroma_bound → interpolate_circular_degrees, :28-96) — see hue_interp.
The soft knee (_run_compression_pass, :147): compression starts at knee_start_ratio * chroma_bound (:153); above the knee, output chroma follows a tanh curve filling the remaining “room” up to the bound (:168-171). The code comment at :166-167 pins this exact tanh form (“Consensus R6 pins this tanh form exactly; do not substitute”). Hue is preserved by scaling a/b uniformly (chroma_scale, :187-203); L is untouched (:205-206).























ParamDefaultRangeMeaning (:329-356)knee_start_ratio0.850.50–1.00Fraction of the hue-local chroma bound at which soft compression begins.knee_softness0.500.05–1.50Soft-knee curvature; higher spreads the transition across a wider input-chroma range.
Degenerate guard: if the palette supplies no hue/chroma samples (or the bound table is mis-shaped or ≈ 0 everywhere) C2 returns identity with degenerate_palette (:409-416, _identity_result at :286). Debug maps: chroma_scale, over_bound_mask (:278-280).

feature_scale — the Wing-B spatial anchor

A single helper that turns the active nozzle diameter into a millimeter “print-feature scale” so B1 and B3 share one definition of “blur at print scale.”

resolve_feature_scale_mm(context, explicit_mm=0.0) (feature_scale.py:45) returns:

explicit_mm verbatim if > 0.0 (a per-call override; :65-66);
otherwise nozzle_diameter * 2.0 — the constant _FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE = 2.0 (:37, applied :72-73), encoding the heuristic that a reliably reproduced feature is ~2 bead widths wide;
otherwise (missing / non-numeric / non-positive nozzle) the fallback _DEFAULT_FEATURE_SCALE_MM = 0.40 (:42, returned :71, :74).

So at the default 0.2 mm nozzle, feature scale = 0.40 mm (2 × 0.20). Callers are exactly the two Wing-B operators (b1_printscale_bilateral.py:8, b3_tv_flatten.py:14) and the evaluation harness — confirmed via grep. The module header notes printer_min_line_width_mm is deliberately not the anchor (it’s the extrusion floor, ~0.8×nozzle, a different quantity; feature_scale.py:15-17). This 0.40 mm value is also the _AUTOSCALE_BASELINE_MM baseline B3 divides by, which is why autoscale is a no-op at the default nozzle. Detail page: Feature scale anchor.

hue_interp — circular hue lookup

Wrap-aware linear interpolation of a per-hue value array, used by C2 to query the chroma envelope at any OKLab hue angle.

interpolate_circular_degrees(query_degrees, sample_degrees, sample_values) (hue_interp.py:19) linearly interpolates sample_values (indexed by hue bin centers) at arbitrary query hues, wrapping continuously across the 360°→0° seam. Mechanics: queries are normalized mod 360 (:62); a single sample short-circuits to a constant (:64-65); otherwise the sorted bins are wrap-extended by one bin on each side (last −360°, first +360°, :79-80) so a plain np.interp handles the seam without per-query branching (:82). Output is float32, same shape as the query (:82-83). Its only live caller is C2 (c2_soft_gamut_compress.py:13, used at :40) — confirmed via grep; the docstring notes it sits next to feature_scale.py as shared Wing-C infrastructure (:9-10).

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Preprocessing, detail cap, and luminance runtime
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
The generator has three separate runtime boundaries that are easy to conflate: the F1 preprocessing chain changes the source raster before target computation; the luminance handler supplies optional source-driven cap guidance; and Stage 4 detail-cap cleanup modifies only the luminance detail cap. The server configuration layer controls all three, but they do not share the same enablement mechanism.
F1 preprocessing state
Preprocessing operators are discovered from preprocessing/operators/, registered by @register_preprocessing, and sorted by (order, fully-qualified class name). run_preprocessing_pipeline validates the chain, converts between declared color domains, runs each operator, validates its output, records a PreprocessingTraceStep, accumulates debug maps, and optionally publishes view-only snapshots. The live solve calls it after profile load and before compute_solve_target_cloud; an empty chain is a legal no-op.
The class defaults are all default_enabled = False, but that is only the fallback when no persisted toggle exists. load_module_state normalizes the discovered registry against Prisma/generator/app/modules.json, dropping retired keys and filling missing keys from class defaults. In the current checkout, c2_soft_gamut_compress is enabled in that file and the other four built-in operators are disabled. The live API exposes the current descriptors and state through GET /api/modules, and persists changes through POST /api/modules/toggle or PUT /api/modules/state.
Preprocessing parameters are separate from module toggles. preprocessing_params is normalized as a dictionary keyed by module ID and is carried in settings profiles/config; it does not itself enable an operator. C1 and C2 require palette metadata, resolved once for the chain only when an enabled operator declares that context requirement.
Product configuration forcing
_force_mandatory_product_settings is applied at multiple server boundaries, including config egress, solve-config construction, export materialization, and settings-profile normalization. It removes retired quiet-dropped extras, rounds the minimum cap to a whole layer, forces model_domain_ingress, printability enforcement, cap-continuity cleanup, printable color-region targeting, detail-cap construction, and the Stage 2/Stage 4 printability gates on.
detail_cap_enabled is therefore not a product feature switch. ConfigPayload rejects false, settings profiles reject a false persisted value, and runtime forcing restores true. detail_cap_smoothing_enabled remains a separate setting with a true default, but its effect is conditional on luminance handling.
The server also normalizes luminance_mode to standard or luminance_detail. Selecting luminance_detail applies a preset: cap_mode becomes smooth_variable, the luminance handler is enabled, its mode and strength defaults are set, luminance detail authoring is enabled, and detail-cap construction remains mandatory. Standard mode resets the handler off when the preset is applied with reset_standard=True. Retired cap_mode="fixed" is rejected rather than translated.
Luminance handler lifecycle
The handler is default-off in PipelineConfig and SolveConfig. When enabled, run_pipeline configures it twice: once after target-cloud/white-rescale preparation as a provisional pre-LUT boundary authority, and again after gamut mapping as the final post-mapping authority. This runtime authority feeds effective_boundary_d_wc_max, so Stage 2 and Stage 4 share a bounded boundary-cap ceiling.
LuminanceHandler.build_reference samples the active white-base/white-cap appearance curve, maps target OKLab L or boundary luminance into layer-quantized cap references, computes an optical boundary authority, and optionally folds banded white fill into the references. LuminanceHandler.build combines the raw solver-implied cap with those references to return boundary_cap_request_mm and detail_cap_reference_mm. The detail reference is clipped by remaining t_max headroom and the full cap limit; it is not a separate color-stack solve.
The configured appearance provider matters here: when the configuration requests photo_stack_bundle, LuminanceHandler refuses a missing or different provider rather than silently sampling the historical spline provider.
Stage 4 detail-cap smoothing
_build_stage4_cap_plan computes remaining cap budget from t_max - color_ceiling, derives boundary and detail requests, and applies printability floors/gates. _apply_stage4_detail_cap_smoothing runs only when all three conditions hold: luminance handling is enabled, detail_cap_enabled is true, and detail_cap_smoothing_enabled is true. In standard mode it is a no-op even though the smoothing flag defaults true.
When active, the helper converts detail height to integer layer counts, calls smooth_detail_cap_layers, converts back to millimeters, and clamps the result to the remaining budget and any desired final cap target. The smoother removes exact-height speckles and cleans small components/holes in cumulative detail masks. It does not modify color maps, the boundary cap, or recipe topology. The post-smoothing detail is still subject to the Stage 4 printability gates.
Anchors

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: one webapp solve runs a fixed five-step spine (run_pipeline) with one pluggable slot (preprocessing, inside Load) plus an optional two-pass swap-banding path that fires before LUT build when the palette overflows the AMS color slots — and the heavy lifting in the Solve step is the staged Stage 0–5 backend (run_staged_backend_path), not the legacy CLI engine.

This is the wiring diagram for one full solve. For the narrative walk-through read How a Solve Works; for the optics read The Transmission Model and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve; for the overflow two-pass read AMS grouping and swap planning. The Mermaid below renders natively in Obsidian and in a Quartz-published site, so it travels with the docs.
Page boundary: this page owns the one-run wiring diagram and nested stage order. What Actually Runs owns liveness classifications; The Solve Facade owns entry-point/config translation; The Joint LUT building and querying owns LUT construction/query implementation. Details below are included only where they explain a connection in this graph.
Two layers: the spine, and the staged backend inside the Solve step
There are two nested orchestrators, and it matters which one you are looking at:

The spine — run_pipeline in pipeline/runner.py:736. Five fixed steps: load → build LUTs → gamut → solve → stats, always in this order. When the palette has more colors than AMS color slots (FULL_PRESET only), the runner inserts a scout → band-plan → prepare two-pass between Load and Build LUTs (_swap_banding_requested, runner.py:50); the full story is in AMS grouping and swap planning.
The staged backend — run_staged_backend_path in pipeline/staged_runner.py:11163. This is the spine’s Solve step. Internally it runs its own Stage 0–5 sequence. The webapp always takes this path (runner.py:1222-1225); the “6-step” engine in solve.py is the legacy CLI engine and is not what the web app runs.

Fixed spine vs. the two optional expansions
The orange nodes are the only parts of the spine that vary per run: the preprocessing slot (module-toggled) and the swap-banding two-pass (fires by palette size, no toggle). Everything else is hard-wired.

Preprocessing resolution happens once, in the facade: _resolve_pipeline_slots reads saved module state and returns the preprocessing chain (facade.py:475). There is no pluggable grouping module and no grouping_enabled preset flag anymore — the legacy pluggable grouping slot (GreedyGrouping/GroupBudgetGrouping) was deleted; swap grouping is now the built-in banded two-pass, engaged purely on AMS overflow. See AMS grouping and swap planning.

Appearance provider — the color oracle on the side

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Joint LUT and Staged Solve
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the transmission model only runs forward (recipe → color), so the generator inverts it by precomputing a table of achievable recipes and, for each target pixel, picking the recipe whose color is the nearest neighbor in OKLab.

This page is the conceptual bridge between the color you want and the print recipe that makes it. It deliberately stays at that altitude — how the table is built and queried lives in The Joint LUT building and querying, and how the per-pixel ideal recipes become a printable plan lives in The staged backend (Stage 0-5).
Page boundary: this page explains why the inversion is joint and how it connects to the staged solve. It is not the liveness authority or a second LUT implementation reference; use What Actually Runs for caller status and The Joint LUT building and querying for builder/query mechanics.
The inversion problem
The forward model is easy: give it a stack of filament thicknesses and it returns a color (model.py compose_stack). Solving needs the reverse — given a color, find a stack — and there is no clean closed-form inverse. Too many filament/thickness combinations can land near the same color, and the achievable set is a discrete, budget-constrained lattice, not a smooth function you can analytically invert.
The generator sidesteps this entirely. It enumerates the achievable recipes once, records the color each produces, and at solve time treats inversion as a nearest-neighbor lookup: the target color goes in, the closest precomputed entry’s recipe comes out. That table is the The Joint LUT and Staged Solve.
”Joint” — cap and color together
Each entry fixes both a white-cap thickness and a color-layer recipe at once, and stores the OKLab of the full stack:
oklab( T_wb × T_wc(d_wc) × ∏ T_ci(d_ci) )

Cap and color are solved in one shot rather than in two separate passes — that is what “joint” means. Two consequences follow directly from the entry layout (lut.py:161, LUTEntry):

The white base T_wb is baked into every entry (lut.py:533, lut.py:601). The solve target is therefore the full-stack color, and T_wb is never divided back out at query time (model.py:141 — “T_wb is NOT divided out … already included in every LUT entry”). The stale docstring at the top of lut.py:13 still describes an old target = T_source / T_wb query; the live model.py ingress contradicts it.
An entry carries its color filament subset, the per-filament color thicknesses, the cap thickness, and the OKLab color (lut.py:163–lut.py:166) — so one nearest-neighbor hit returns a complete, printable recipe, with the cap surfaced under __white_cap__ in the query result (lut.py:1782).

Nearest neighbor in OKLab
The match runs in OKLab, a perceptually-uniform space, so “closest color” means “closest to how the eye sees it.” Each LUT subset holds a SciPy KDTree over its OKLab points (lut.py:167); the solve queries every tree for k=1 and keeps the global best across subsets (query_luts_batch, lut.py:1691). The returned ΔE is plain Euclidean OKLab distance.
One twist worth knowing as a user: chroma weight. When chroma_weight != 1.0, the L* (lightness) axis is divided by the weight before the tree is built and before each query (lut.py:1721–lut.py:1725), so the nearest-neighbor search prioritizes hue/chroma over exact lightness. The reported ΔE is always recomputed unweighted so quality numbers stay comparable (lut.py:1774, lut.py:1783–lut.py:1785).
A pixel whose nearest entry is still far away (ΔE above de_threshold, default 0.05; state.py:66) is flagged out of gamut — no recipe reproduces it well. That flag feeds Gamut mapping; see staged_runner.py:785.
From “ideal per-pixel recipe” to a printable plan
The nearest-neighbor lookup gives the ideal recipe for each pixel in isolation. A lithophane printed that literally would be unmanufacturable — single-pixel color islands, sub-nozzle features. So the webapp solve does not stop at the lookup. It feeds the per-pixel targets into the staged backend (run_staged_backend_path, staged_runner.py:11163, reached from runner.py:1225), which groups pixels into printable color regions, scores candidate recipes per region against this same Joint LUT, and plans the white cap — all under the active printer’s minimum feature sizes.
That is the division of labour this page bridges:

























LayerJobWhere it’s documentedTransmission modelrecipe → color (forward)The Transmission ModelJoint LUTenumerate recipes + colors; nearest-neighbor invertThe Joint LUT building and queryingStaged backendper-pixel ideal → printable region/cap planThe staged backend (Stage 0-5)

Liveness note for developers. The webapp solve runs the staged backend, whose only LUT entry point is the batch query query_luts_batch (staged_runner.py:784). The fixed-cap and cap-curve variants in lut.py (query_luts_fixed_cap, cap_curve_lookup_batch, build_cap_curve) are not called by the staged path — their only callers are the legacy CLI engine solve.py and pipeline_cli.py (e.g. solve.py:434, pipeline_cli.py:665). Do not assume the staged solve uses them. build_hull_from_luts, by contrast, is live on the runner path — the gamut-mapping stage _apply_target_gamut_mapping builds the hull (runner.py:284).

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Solve Facade
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the facade (generator.facade, facade.py) is the thin front door to the solver — it takes a typed SolveConfig, picks a quality preset, resolves the preprocessing chain, translates everything into a PipelineConfig, and hands off to the one orchestrator (run_pipeline) that runs the staged backend.

This page is about the handoff layer, not the solve itself. For the solve walked end-to-end, see How a Solve Works; for the inversion math, The Joint LUT and Staged Solve; for the stage-by-stage diagram, Pipeline Map. Here we stay at contract altitude: what the entry points are, what they translate, and which one is dormant.
Page boundary: this page owns the facade’s typed API and config translation. What Actually Runs is the liveness authority; Pipeline Map owns stage ordering; the LUT and staged-backend pages own numerical and artifact internals.
Why a facade exists
The module docstring (facade.py:2) names a stale filename (lith_facade.py) — ignore it. The real job, stated in the same header block (facade.py:4–10), holds up against the code: callers (chiefly the web server) should never reach into pipeline internals. They build one SolveConfig, call one of three functions, and get back a SolveResult. Everything between — module-state resolution, the SolveConfig → PipelineConfig translation, the conversion of the runner’s PipelineState back into a SolveResult — lives here so the rest of the app doesn’t have to know it exists.
The three live entry points
All three production entry points have the same shape: (img, config, progress=None, modules_path=None, module_state=None), returning a SolveResult (solve_compare returns a list). They differ only in the quality preset they pass and, for compare, the per-palette loop.

































Entry pointDefinedUsed forPresetServer call sitesolve_previewfacade.py:823fast low-res gamut checkPREVIEW_PRESETserver.py:4052solve_fullfacade.py:891the real production solveFULL_PRESETserver.py:4961solve_comparefacade.py:915batch preview across several palettesCOMPARE_PRESETserver.py:4149
Liveness is confirmed from callers, not docstrings. solve_preview, solve_full, and solve_compare are all imported in server.py:79–81 and invoked at the call sites above. solve_full has a second live caller in the preprocessing evaluation harness (evaluation/preprocessing_harness.py:166). These are the production solve surface.
Each one does the same four-step dance:

Resolve the preprocessing chain — _resolve_pipeline_slots (facade.py:475) loads module state and returns a (module_state, preprocessors) pair — just the ordered preprocessor chain. There is no grouping slot anymore; swap grouping is now an automatic banded solve inside the runner (see Grouping is now an automatic banded solve).
Translate config — _to_pipeline_config (facade.py:497) maps SolveConfig → PipelineConfig.
Run — run_pipeline (runner.py:736) executes the staged backend.
Convert back — _state_to_solve_result (facade.py:785) turns the returned PipelineState into a SolveResult.

solve_compare (facade.py:915) wraps steps 1–4 in a loop over palettes: it loads module state once (facade.py:927), then for each palette clones the config with the new palette via _replace_solve_config (facade.py:651), runs the four steps with palette_index/palette_count threaded into the runner for progress reporting (facade.py:959), and catches per-palette exceptions — a failing palette becomes a {"error": ..., "palette": ...} dict in the result list rather than aborting the whole batch (facade.py:972). Empty palettes short-circuit to an error dict before solving (facade.py:936).
Quality presets
A QualityPreset is a tiny named record — just name and max_layers (state.py:29-33). The old grouping_enabled flag is gone. Three are defined as module constants:





























Presetnamemax_layersDefinedPREVIEW_PRESET"preview"15state.py:36FULL_PRESET"full"None (auto)state.py:41COMPARE_PRESET"compare"15state.py:46
The preset is the only thing distinguishing the three entry points. It is passed through _to_pipeline_config onto PipelineConfig.preset (facade.py:647) and read back inside the runner. Two effects:

Layer ceiling. max_layers=15 caps preview/compare solves to a cheap low-resolution height stack; None means full solve lets the config derive it from t_max (see SolveConfig.effective_max_layers, facade.py:165).
Banded-solve gate. The preset name also decides whether swap grouping runs. There is no preset flag for it; instead the runner triggers a two-pass banded solve only for the full preset and only when the palette overflows the color slots — _swap_banding_requested (runner.py:50-55) requires preset.name == "full" and len(palette) > color_slots(). Preview and compare never band. See Grouping is now an automatic banded solve.

Note the preset name also drives diagnostics: the palette-fit best-case diagnostics in _compute_palette_fit_diagnostics only compute when preset.name == "full" (facade.py:666-669), so the “solver loss” overlay is a full-solve-only artifact.
The dormant fourth entry point
solve_preview_progressive (facade.py:849) is the one to know about. Its own docstring (facade.py:857–865) says the progressive-solve HTTP feature and its mid-solve snapshot emitter were removed in the “Stage 3 cleanup,” and that the function survives only to thread an optional SnapshotPublisher (generator.pipeline.snapshot) into the preprocessing preview hook. This docstring is accurate — and verified independently from callers, not taken on faith:

No production code imports or calls it. A repo-wide grep finds it imported/called only in two tests: tests/generator/preprocessing/test_facade_threading.py:286 and tests/generator/preprocessing/test_f1_smoke.py:169.
The server’s only remaining mention of “progressive” is a static-file route comment (server.py:6476) that serves cached diagnostic/preview PNGs — there is no progressive solve endpoint.
The one other hit is a stale traceback in Prisma/output/generator.log (a log artifact, not live code).
A removal plan exists for it: Prisma/generator/docs/legacy_audit/12_WEBAPP_DEAD_BACKEND_CANDIDATES_REMOVAL_PLAN.md:59 lists removing solve_preview_progressive from facade.py.

So: DORMANT in production, retained only as a test vehicle. It runs FULL_PRESET (facade.py:873), and unlike the three live entries it forwards a snapshot_publisher into run_pipeline (facade.py:882; the runner accepts it at runner.py:742 and attaches it to the state at runner.py:1220). The _progressive suffix is, per its docstring, a historical artifact and a rename candidate. Do not wire new code to it without reviving the publisher path.
Resolving the preprocessing chain
_resolve_pipeline_slots (facade.py:475) returns a (module_state, preprocessors) pair — grouping is no longer a resolved slot. It first loads module state via _load_module_state (facade.py:425) — which prefers an in-memory module_state dict, else reads modules_path through load_module_state, else returns None. The server passes modules_path=_MODULES_PATH so the live solve reads the on-disk module configuration.
Preprocessing — _resolve_preprocessing_from_state
_resolve_preprocessing_from_state (facade.py:438) builds the ordered list of enabled preprocessing operator instances (legacy callers with no module state simply get an empty list, facade.py:452-453). It walks the operator registry (generator.pipeline.registry), keeps each operator whose module-state flag is on (falling back to the operator’s default_enabled, facade.py:460), passes the operator’s params block from config.preprocessing_params as constructor kwargs, then sorts by each operator’s order with ties broken by import path (facade.py:466-471). The chain is threaded into the runner’s preprocessing slot. Class defaults are disabled, but persisted module state may enable operators; the current checked-in state enables C2. See How a Solve Works for where the chain runs inside the pipeline.
Grouping is now an automatic banded solve
The pluggable grouping slot was removed. GroupBudgetGrouping, GreedyGrouping, and _resolve_grouping_from_state no longer exist, and grouping/ now holds only band_plan.py and banded_export.py. Grouping is not something the facade resolves — the runner performs it automatically whenever a full-preset solve’s palette overflows the color slots. Inside run_pipeline (generator.pipeline.runner):

_swap_banding_requested (runner.py:50-55) fires for preset.name == "full" with len(palette) > color_slots().
A bounded-resolution scout solve runs first (_run_swap_banding_scout, runner.py:84) to measure per-filament color usage.
choose_band_plan (generator.grouping.band_plan, called runner.py:940) partitions the canonical dark-first palette into consecutive exact-height swap bands from those scout maps.
The plan is stored as a swap_grouping dict on the state (_swap_grouping_metadata, runner.py:130; assigned runner.py:947) — keys include groups, band_layers, canonical_palette, pause_z_mm, and cap_limit_mm.
The real solve then runs with that band structure fixed; the per-band white fill comes from band_fill_maps (generator.grouping.band_plan), which the facade calls when reconstructing images (facade.py:334, facade.py:367, facade.py:717, facade.py:753).

The full banded story — slot budget, band planning, and export-time swap instructions — is AMS grouping and swap planning.

Disambiguation: the experimental beam-search / greedy schedulers under generator.scheduling.policies are unrelated to swap grouping and were not removed. They quantize an already-solved plan into per-layer orderings and are wired only into one offline eval script — see Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental).

The config translation — _to_pipeline_config
_to_pipeline_config (facade.py:497) is the big, boring, load-bearing function: it copies the dozens of fields from a SolveConfig (generator.facade) into a PipelineConfig (generator.pipeline.state) and attaches the resolved preprocessors, preprocessing_params, and preset (facade.py:645-647). A few translation facts worth knowing:

Resolution is canonical-pitch only. The translation passes image_sample_pitch_mm and solver_fine_pitch_mm (facade.py:580–581) plus the stage-1 coarsening/lattice-offset fields; there are no legacy resolution fields. The SolveConfig.__post_init__ applies a resolution backstop first (facade.py:153–154, via config.resolution_schema). See Settings, resolution, and the config contract and generator.config.resolution_schema.
Color-model ingress passes through verbatim. model_domain_ingress and model_domain_ingress_lut_path ride along (facade.py:529) to the Model-domain ingress step; appearance_model_provider selects the Appearance provider (facade.py:575).
de_threshold defaults differ across layers. SolveConfig.de_threshold defaults to 0.01 (facade.py:97) while PipelineConfig.de_threshold defaults to 0.05 (state.py:72) — but the translation always copies the SolveConfig value through (facade.py:523), so the config you build wins; the PipelineConfig default only matters for direct construction.
Everything else is a near-mechanical 1:1 copy — whites, layer height, t_max/k_max, gamut mode, chroma weight, the full luminance-handler block, the staged-backend stage-2/stage-4 knobs, cap mode, and the printability fields. The list is long because SolveConfig is the kitchen-sink settings object; the translation is where it narrows to what the runner reads.

What comes back — SolveResult
run_pipeline returns a PipelineState; _state_to_solve_result (facade.py:785) converts it into the SolveResult dataclass (facade.py:234) that callers actually consume. The result carries the thickness maps (normalized to a typed ThicknessMaps in __post_init__, facade.py:277), the color/white profiles, aggregate SolveStats, the original SolveConfig, the appearance provider, diagnostics (dE map, gamut mask — preferred from the diagnostics dict, falling back to thickness maps, facade.py:282–290), grouping result, the canonical SolvedMaterialPlan, and the blueprint-triage printability report.

Disambiguation: SolveResult.blueprint_triage is the blueprint-triage PrintabilityReport (generator.pipeline.blueprint_triage.report), imported at facade.py:37. That is a different class from the mesh-side printability report (generator.mesh.printability). Don’t conflate them.

Two reconstruction methods live on SolveResult and matter for the UI’s color views:

predict_image (facade.py:313) composes the full backlit sRGB image (base × colors × white cap) — routing through the appearance provider when it isn’t the historical spline, else predict_image_fast (generator.solve).
predict_image_color_only (facade.py:406) composes base + colors with the white cap dropped (every cap term zeroed via _cap_zeroed_thickness_maps, facade.py:386) so the cap’s luminance shaping doesn’t drown out the color story. A zero cap thickness is the multiplicative identity in the transmission model, so this cleanly removes the term without touching the composition math. This is what feeds the recipe viewer’s color-only render.

What this layer does not do

It does not run the legacy solve.py “6-step” engine. run_pipeline always dispatches to run_staged_backend_path (generator.pipeline.staged_runner) at runner.py:1222, for every preset. The 6-step engine in generator.solve is the separate CLI engine; the webapp path is the staged backend. (predict_image_fast from solve.py is still used for fast forward prediction — that is just the composition helper, not the solve engine.)
It does not decide resolution, gamut mode, or which operators are enabled — those come in on the SolveConfig / module state. The facade only resolves and translates.
It does not persist anything. Saving runs, naming, archives, and caches are the server’s job (generator.server, generator.run_store).

Progress reporting
The facade no longer defines a progress-tracker class — progress is delegated to the generator.progress module. The facade imports coerce_progress_reporter from it (facade.py:34), and the reporting split is:

The three simple entry points thread the caller’s raw progress callback straight into run_pipeline; the runner is what emits the per-stage updates the UI shows.
solve_compare wraps the caller’s callback with coerce_progress_reporter once up front (facade.py:929) so it can thread each palette’s palette_index/palette_count alongside the runner’s stage updates — those two fields are what solve_compare populates per palette.

See generator.progress for the reporter’s structure (stage key/label/index/count, percent, ETA).

The Joint LUT and Staged Solve — the inversion the staged backend performs

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The pipeline orchestrator and shared state
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: pipeline/ is the small framework layer — a single orchestration function (run_pipeline) that loads profiles, runs an optional preprocessing chain, optionally scouts a swap-banding plan when the palette overflows the AMS color slots, builds LUTs, hands the heavy solve to the staged backend, and finalises one shared PipelineState carrier, with one pluggable slot (preprocessing operators) that self-registers from disk and persists its on/off state to JSON.

This is the developer companion to the generator.pipeline.runner package. It covers the data carriers, the fixed-spine design, the preprocessing plugin base class, parameter self-description, registry auto-discovery, and module on/off persistence. It also flags two seams (revalidate() and snapshot.py) that are wired but dormant in production.

What changed: the old pluggable grouping slot (GreedyGrouping / GroupBudgetGrouping, a grouping_enabled preset flag, a grouping registry) was deleted. Swap grouping is now the built-in two-pass swap-banding path in the runner, engaged purely on AMS overflow — no module, no toggle. The full story lives in AMS grouping and swap planning; this page describes only where it plugs into the spine.

Related: generation_pipeline (narrative walkthrough) · generator.facade (the entry layer above this) · generator.pipeline.staged_runner (the solve engine below it) · The staged backend (Stage 0-5) · AMS grouping and swap planning · Module management and settings.

How to drive it (users)
You never call this package directly — you change its behavior through the Modules panel and Settings in the generator web app (port 8010). Two knobs land here:

Preprocessing operators — a chain of optional image-cleanup / gamut steps that run on the source raster before color solving. Several can be on at once. This is the only module-toggled slot.
Quality preset — preview vs full vs compare; controls how many layers. (Swap banding is not a knob — it fires automatically on FULL_PRESET when the palette overflows the AMS color slots.)

Toggling a preprocessing module in the UI writes to a JSON file (modules.json) so the choice survives a restart. The contract is enforced server-side: see Module on/off persistence below.

The shared carriers (pipeline/state.py)
Everything the pipeline produces is accumulated on one mutable object that is threaded through every stage. There are four dataclasses, all defined in pipeline/state.py.
PipelineState — the bag of solve state
pipeline/state.py:224 defines the object passed through all stages. The runner constructs it once (pipeline/runner.py:808) and mutates it in place. Fields, grouped by who fills them:

See AMS grouping and swap planninglutsLUT spinepipeline/runner.py:1082 / :1111 / :1160 (banded or plain, spline or provider)observed_target_oklab, solve_target_oklabrunnertwo grids; see Observation vs solve gridthickness_maps (ThicknessMaps)staged finalisecopied from the staged bundle at pipeline/runner.py:702solved_plan (SolvedMaterialPlan)staged finalisecanonical export artifact, pipeline/runner.py:686staged_resultstaged finaliseraw staged-backend bundle, pipeline/runner.py:682diagnosticsrunnerthe SOLE canonical home for __de__ / __gamut_mask__ on this path (pipeline/state.py:269)stats (SolveStats)_compute_statspipeline/runner.py:456cap_qualitystaged finalisepipeline/runner.py:730source_image, preprocessing_trace, preprocessing_metricspreprocessing slotonly populated when the chain is non-emptysnapshot_publisherrunner (write-only)set at pipeline/runner.py:1220, never read — see Dormant seamsblueprint_triage (PrintabilityReport)reset to None on the staged path (pipeline/runner.py:698)NB: this is the Blueprint triage the unwired engine report class, not the unrelated mesh PrintabilityReport
The diagnostics dict is load-bearing and the comment at pipeline/state.py:262-269 is code-true: on the staged/webapp path __de__ and __gamut_mask__ live in state.diagnostics, never mirrored into thickness_maps. _compute_stats reads diagnostics first and only falls back to thickness_maps for legacy/CLI-style states (pipeline/runner.py:470-471).
PipelineConfig — the frozen request
pipeline/state.py:52 is the full parameter set for one solve. It is built by the facade’s _to_pipeline_config (facade.py:497), not by hand. Beyond the ~120 plain fields it carries the preprocessing-slot members and a set of effective_* resolver methods:

preprocessors: List[Any] (pipeline/state.py:156) — the ordered list of enabled operator instances. Sorting happens in the facade resolver, not here.
preprocessing_params: Dict[str, Dict] (pipeline/state.py:157) — the FULL per-operator params dict (every registered operator’s block at its default), rides along for fingerprinting.
preset: QualityPreset (pipeline/state.py:159) — defaults to FULL_PRESET.

(There is no grouping field anymore — the pluggable grouping slot was removed. When swap banding fires, its plan lives on PipelineState.swap_grouping, not on the config.)
The effective_* methods compute derived values so callers never duplicate the arithmetic: effective_max_layers() (pipeline/state.py:174) lets the preset cap layers, effective_white_cap() falls back to the base white, effective_d_wc_max() / effective_boundary_d_wc_max() derive cap authority (the latter also clamps to the runtime swap-band cap limit when banding is active), color_slots() (pipeline/state.py:219) = ams_slots - effective_white_slots() — the same threshold that gates swap banding. __post_init__ (pipeline/state.py:161) canonicalizes the palette order and applies a resolution backstop from config.resolution_schema.
ProfileSet and QualityPreset
ProfileSet (pipeline/state.py:21) is a trivial three-field bundle of loaded filament profiles: color_profiles, wb_profile, wc_profile. QualityPreset (pipeline/state.py:29) now carries just name and max_layers — the old grouping_enabled flag was removed. Three named instances exist:

























Presetmax_layersAnchorPREVIEW_PRESET15pipeline/state.py:36FULL_PRESETNone (unbounded)pipeline/state.py:41COMPARE_PRESET15pipeline/state.py:46
The only thing QualityPreset controls is a layer ceiling. Whether swap banding runs is not a preset flag — it is decided by _swap_banding_requested, which requires preset.name == "full" and len(palette) > color_slots() (pipeline/runner.py:50-55).

The orchestrator: fixed spine plus two slots (pipeline/runner.py)
run_pipeline (pipeline/runner.py:736) is the whole orchestration. The structure is a fixed spine of always-run stages, with the preprocessing slot woven into Load and an optional swap-banding two-pass inserted before LUT build on AMS overflow. Reading the function top to bottom:



























































#StageKindAnchor1Load — validate palette, load profiles, create appearance provider, run the optional swap scout/band plan and preprocessing chain, then compute target cloudsspine + optional expansionspipeline/runner.py:838-1067—Swap-banding two-pass — scout solve → choose_band_plan → write state.swap_groupingAMS overflow onlypipeline/runner.py:888-970—F1 Preprocessing — run the enabled operator chain, overwrite state.imageslotpipeline/runner.py:991-1029—Target clouds + white-point/luminance setupspine detailpipeline/runner.py:1034-10542Build LUTs — spline or provider path, plain or bandedspinepipeline/runner.py:1069-11843Gamut — _apply_target_gamut_mapping + final luminance-authority passspinepipeline/runner.py:1193-11984Solve — run_staged_backend_path then _finalize_staged_backend_statespinepipeline/runner.py:1222-12305Stats — _compute_statsspinepipeline/runner.py:1247-1248
Two facts that the stale module header hides (cite the line anchors, not the header):

The webapp solve is the STAGED backend. The Solve stage calls run_staged_backend_path from pipeline.staged_runner (pipeline/runner.py:1222-1225). It does not run solve.py’s legacy “6-step” CLI engine. _finalize_staged_backend_state (pipeline/runner.py:677) copies exactly one staged result bundle onto the legacy-facing state fields, and recomputes dE via _recompute_de_diagnostics straight into state.diagnostics (pipeline/runner.py:726).
The preprocessing slot and the banded two-pass are the only conditional parts. The preprocessing slot is a legal no-op when config.preprocessors is empty (pipeline/runner.py:991 — the whole block is guarded). The swap-banding two-pass runs only when _swap_banding_requested(config) is true (pipeline/runner.py:745, :889); when it does, the spine’s five reported stages expand to eight (load, scout, band_plan, prepare, lut, gamut, solve, stats — the phase plan is selected at pipeline/runner.py:748-795). There is no post-solve grouping stage.

Observation vs solve grid
The runner is the single owner of target-cloud computation (compute_solve_target_cloud, pipeline/runner.py:1034-1037). observed_target_oklab lives on the observation grid (image_sample_pitch_mm); solve_target_oklab is projected onto the solve grid (solver_fine_pitch_mm) and is what the solve path and dE recomputation both consume. The white-point rescale (_apply_target_white_rescale, reassign at pipeline/runner.py:224) and the gamut map (_apply_target_gamut_mapping, reassign at :307) rewrite solve_target_oklab in place, so it is not necessarily the original projection array.
Progress reporting
Progress is delegated to the generator.progress module — the old facade-level _ProgressTracker class is gone. run_pipeline calls coerce_progress_reporter(progress, stage_count=…) (pipeline/runner.py:749; a plain callback, an existing ProgressReporter, or None all coerce cleanly) and then carves per-stage child reporters through a local _phase(key, label) helper (pipeline/runner.py:797). Each stage’s emit(...) sends a dict with stage, stage_index, stage_count, overall_pct, elapsed_s, and palette index/count; the reporter enforces monotonic overall progress and cooperative cancellation checkpoints. No callback ⇒ the reporter is None and nothing is emitted. The per-run phase weights (5-stage vs 8-stage swap-banding, and the photo-stack variants) are the phase_specs tables at pipeline/runner.py:756-795.

The module plugin contract (pipeline/base.py)
One abstract base class defines what a pluggable module is: PreprocessingModule. (The old GroupingModule ABC was deleted along with the pluggable grouping slot.) It is an ABC with one abstract method and a describe() that serializes the module for the UI.
PreprocessingModule (F1)
pipeline/base.py:72. An image preprocessing operator. Class attributes the slot runner reads:








































AttributeMeaningAnchorname, descriptionidentity / UI textpipeline/base.py:87-88params: Dict[str, ParamDef]self-described tunablespipeline/base.py:89default_enabled: booldefault on/offpipeline/base.py:90input_domain / output_domain (ColorDomain)color-domain contract; the slot runner inserts conversions between adjacent operators whose domains differpipeline/base.py:91-92order: floatposition in the chain; conventional bands Wing A 100–199, B 200–299, C 300–399, D 400–499; ties resolve by lex import pathpipeline/base.py:93required_context: FrozenSet[ContextKey]optional shared services (e.g. palette metadata) the runner resolves before apply()pipeline/base.py:94
(There is no longer a supports_protect_mask attribute — the subject-protect-mask feature was removed.)
Abstract method: apply(image, *, context, progress) -> PreprocessingResult (pipeline/base.py:96). The live operators all live under preprocessing/operators/ and self-register — e.g. a1_bilateral_denoise, b1_printscale_bilateral, b3_tv_flatten, c1_achievable_tonemap, c2_soft_gamut_compress (each @register_preprocessing at e.g. preprocessing/operators/a1_bilateral_denoise.py:35). See generator.preprocessing.
Swap grouping is no longer a module
There is no GroupingModule base class, no greedy_optimize/group_budget implementations, and no grouping entry in the registry. AMS swap grouping is now the built-in two-pass swap-banding path run directly by run_pipeline (scout solve → choose_band_plan from grouping/band_plan.py → state.swap_grouping), engaged purely on AMS overflow. It is not toggled and not registered. The full mechanism is documented in AMS grouping and swap planning.

Worth knowing: pipeline/__init__.py re-exports ParamDef, ProgressCallback, the state classes/presets, and run_pipeline / revalidate (pipeline/__init__.py:2-17) — but not PreprocessingModule or the preprocessing registry helpers. Preprocessing operators import the registry decorator directly from pipeline.registry.

ParamDef — parameter self-description
pipeline/base.py:24. A dataclass that lets a module describe one tunable to both the solver and the frontend renderer in one place. Core fields: name, label, type ("int" | "float" | "bool" | "choice" | "html" | "computed_text"), default, plus choices/choice_labels/min/max/description. UI-only fields: unit, tooltip, group, show_when (conditional visibility keyed on another param’s value), and order (pipeline/base.py:40-44). to_dict() (pipeline/base.py:46) emits the JSON the API/UI consumes, omitting None-valued optional keys. This is why the Modules panel can render parameter forms without any hand-written per-module frontend code.

Registry and auto-discovery (pipeline/registry.py)
The registry is now a single module-level dict — _PREPROCESSORS (pipeline/registry.py:12) — populated by a class decorator at import time. @register_preprocessing (pipeline/registry.py:106) stores cls under cls.name and adds its name to PREPROCESSING_MODULE_IDS. (The grouping registry — _GROUPINGS, register_grouping, the hand-listed _KNOWN_GROUPING_* sets — was removed with the grouping slot.)
Preprocessing discovery is filesystem-driven. _discover_preprocessing_operators (pipeline/registry.py:23) walks preprocessing.operators with pkgutil.iter_modules, imports every public (non-_, non-package) submodule in lex-sorted order (pipeline/registry.py:42-52), and that import position becomes each operator’s order tiebreaker. An empty operators/ package is legal — the slot becomes a no-op (pipeline/registry.py:30). Discovery runs once per process: _ensure_preprocessing_populated (pipeline/registry.py:88) re-discovers only when _PREPROCESSORS is empty, and _ensure_registry_populated (pipeline/registry.py:101) is its only wrapper.
Public accessors all call _ensure_registry_populated first: get_preprocessing (pipeline/registry.py:115), list_preprocessings (:120), and list_all_modules (pipeline/registry.py:131) which instantiates each class via cls.__new__ and returns its describe() dict. _clear_registry (pipeline/registry.py:125) is testing-only.

Module on/off persistence (pipeline/modules.py)
pipeline/modules.py reads and writes the JSON file of {module_name: enabled} flags. This is fully live — the generator server wires every endpoint to it. It now handles preprocessing operators only.

























FunctionBehaviorAnchorload_module_state(path)read JSON, fill missing keys with defaults, normalizepipeline/modules.py:38save_module_state(path, state)normalize then writepipeline/modules.py:47toggle_module(path, id, enabled)flip one flag, validate the id against _PREPROCESSORS, normalize, persist, return full statepipeline/modules.py:55
One normalization rule remains, since preprocessing is the only slot:

Preprocessing is non-exclusive. _normalize_module_state (pipeline/modules.py:14) fills defaults for every registered operator and drops retired keys; _get_all_defaults (pipeline/modules.py:24) collects each module’s default_enabled. Operators each contribute independently and several may be on at once. The zero-enabled case is a legal no-op. (The old grouping-exclusivity rule, _normalize_grouping_slot, was removed.)

The server side (all reading _MODULES_PATH): the modules-list endpoint (server.py:2884-2886), the toggle endpoint calling toggle_module (server.py:2895-2901), a bulk save calling save_module_state (server.py:2912), and several solve paths that snapshot load_module_state into the run record (e.g. server.py:2063, :2141, :2170). The facade’s _load_module_state (facade.py:425) is the resolver-side reader that feeds _resolve_pipeline_slots (facade.py:475), turning the flag dict into the resolved preprocessors chain for PipelineConfig.

Dormant and test-only seams
Two seams in this package are wired but not exercised by the production webapp solve. Both confirmed by grepping callers.
revalidate() — a test/compatibility seam with no production caller
revalidate(state) (pipeline/runner.py:447) recomputes __de__ from the current thickness maps against the solve-grid target, writing straight into state.diagnostics['__de__'] (no longer touches thickness_maps). It is a thin wrapper over _recompute_de_diagnostics (pipeline/runner.py:327), which it calls at pipeline/runner.py:453.
Liveness: run_pipeline never calls the wrapper. The production solve path calls _recompute_de_diagnostics directly during staged finalisation (pipeline/runner.py:726). With the pluggable grouping slot deleted there is no post-grouping dE branch left — config.grouping no longer exists, so the old “revalidate after a grouping substitution” path is gone. The public revalidate symbol is still re-exported (pipeline/__init__.py:7) but its only callers are the test suite. Historically it was the post-refinement dE hook for the long-removed refinements slot. Status: test/compatibility seam; no production caller.
snapshot.py / SnapshotPublisher — one live hook, one dormant field
SnapshotPublisher (pipeline/snapshot.py:27) writes preprocessed source-image preview PNGs and their URLs into a shared progress dict via publish_image_preview (pipeline/snapshot.py:47). Liveness, two halves:

The preview hook is live but only reachable via a dormant facade entry point. publish_image_preview is called by the preprocessing runner per enabled operator (preprocessing/runner.py:281), which receives the publisher as a direct parameter (preprocessing/runner.py:216, threaded from pipeline/runner.py:780). A publisher reaches run_pipeline only through facade.solve_preview_progressive(..., publisher=...) (facade.py:849, forwarded into the run at :886). That facade function has no production caller — grep finds only its own definition (facade.py:849); the production webapp uses solve_full (server.py:4961), which never passes a publisher. Its own docstring marks it “currently dormant in production, exercised by the preprocessing preview tests” (facade.py:860-864).
The state.snapshot_publisher field is write-only and dead. The runner assigns it (pipeline/runner.py:1220) but nothing reads it back — grepping .snapshot_publisher across Prisma/ finds only that single write. The live preview path threads its publisher as a function parameter, not via this field. The progressive-solve snapshot emitter (maybe_publish) was removed in the Stage 3 cleanup; the field’s docstring at pipeline/state.py:282-285 is code-true about this. A standing removal candidate is documented in Prisma/generator/docs/legacy_audit/12_WEBAPP_DEAD_BACKEND_CANDIDATES_REMOVAL_PLAN.md. Status: publish_image_preview hook = live but production-dormant (test-only entry); state.snapshot_publisher field = dead (write-only).
