prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: What Actually Runs
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: this is the single liveness map for the generator backend — which solve path actually executes, which modules are legacy or dormant, and which symbols survive only as test scaffolding — with every verdict confirmed by grepping the call graph, not by reading docstrings (most of which are stale).

The generator backend is large and has accreted dead ends: removed features that left remnant functions, experimental subsystems wired only into tests, and two whole modules that look live but no production caller touches. Module headers and docstrings are an unreliable guide — many still cite filenames and ports that no longer exist (see Stale headers — do not trust them). This page is the authority. Other liveness/printability pages link here rather than re-deriving each verdict.
How to read the status column:

LIVE — on the production solve or export path; runs on a normal web-app solve.
LEGACY — real, working code, but only reachable through the old CLI engine, not the web app.
DORMANT — imported and constructable, but no production path invokes it; wired only to tests/scripts.
REMNANT — a leftover of a removed feature; survives because something cheap still references it.
SUSPECTED INERT — strong evidence of no live caller, but the reference graph is subtle and a prior audit was burned by missing callers; treat as a hint, re-verify before deleting.

This page owns liveness verdicts. The Solve Facade owns the typed entry-point and configuration handoff; Pipeline Map owns one-run wiring and stage order; The Joint LUT and Staged Solve owns the conceptual inversion boundary. Those pages should link here for LIVE/LEGACY/DORMANT claims instead of maintaining separate liveness tables.
The map




























































SubjectStatusEvidence (caller-confirmed)Staged backend (run_staged_backend_path)LIVE — the only solve enginerunner.py:1222-1225 imports and calls it unconditionally for every preset; runner.py is reached by all three facade entries, which server.py imports (server.py:76-82) and calls at server.py:4052, 4149, 4961.solve_image (solve.py:480)LEGACY — CLI engine onlySole caller is pipeline_cli.py:646 (imported pipeline_cli.py:46). No web-app path imports it.blueprint_triage package (analyze_triage/apply_fixes)DORMANT — test-only; state field always Nonestate.blueprint_triage is set to None in runner.py:698 and never otherwise written on the live path; analyze_triage/apply_fixes have only test callers (tests/generator/blueprint_triage*).scheduling package (Prisma/generator/scheduling/)DORMANT — experimental, offlineNo production module imports it; the only reference in source is a comment (state.py:253). Driven only by tests/scripts.geometry package (extract_regions, simplify_regions, ColorRegion)DORMANTUsed only inside its own package (geometry/__init__.py:13-15, geometry/simplify.py:117). No external production caller imports geometry.mesh.build_printability_report + the mesh.PrintabilityReport/classification ladderSUSPECTED INERTModule’s own note at printability.py:1061-1070. Grepping the call graph: the only caller of build_printability_report (printability.py:1071) is tests/generator/test_mesh_printability.py. scripts/characterize_mesh_printability.py touches only the lower-level summarize_printability (printability.py:727), not the export roll-up. Re-verify exhaustively before touching.mesh.canonical_mesh (canonical_triangle_array)SUSPECTED INERTReached only via its canonical_mesh_hash wrapper, whose sole non-test caller is scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py:123; no Prisma/generator source path outside canonical_mesh.py consumes it.Reference-bundle replay (photo-stack default bundle)rejected for live — replay onlyappearance_model.py:232-236 raises unless an explicit live candidate/runtime path is given; a reference path is “for replay only”.solve_preview_progressive (facade.py:849)REMNANT of removed progressive solveNot imported by server.py; only test callers (tests/generator/preprocessing/test_facade_threading.py, test_f1_smoke.py). Docstring at facade.py:857-867 says the HTTP feature and its emitter were removed.SnapshotPublisher.maybe_publishREMOVEDThe progressive-solve snapshot emitter was deleted in the Stage 3 cleanup (snapshot.py:6); no runner call site remains in runner.py.
The live solve path, end to end
When you press Solve, server.py calls one of three facade functions — never solve_image:

























Facade entryServer call sitePresetsolve_preview (facade.py:823)server.py:4052PREVIEW_PRESETsolve_full (facade.py:891)server.py:4961FULL_PRESETsolve_compare (facade.py:915)server.py:4149COMPARE_PRESET
All three translate their SolveConfig to a PipelineConfig and funnel into run_pipeline (runner.py:736). Inside run_pipeline, after the load / LUT / gamut stages, the solve stage does exactly one thing: it imports and calls run_staged_backend_path (runner.py:1222-1225). There is no branch here — the staged backend is not one solver among several, it is the solver. _finalize_staged_backend_state (runner.py:677) then copies that one result bundle onto the legacy-facing PipelineState fields the rest of the app reads. See How a Solve Works for the stage-by-stage walk and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve for what the staged backend does internally.

The “6-step” engine in solve.py is not this. solve.py’s module docstring (solve.py:2-18) describes a “joint LUT + two-pass cap smoothing” pipeline in six numbered steps. That is the legacy CLI engine (solve_image, solve.py:480), reached only through pipeline_cli.py. The web app never runs it. A few utilities from solve.py are still imported by the live runner (e.g. gamut_map_hull_batch / gamut_map_hue_preserving_batch, imported locally at runner.py:282 and called at runner.py:288, 299, and predict_image_fast re-exported through generator.facade at facade.py:31), but the solve_image orchestration body is legacy.

Dormant and inert subsystems
blueprint_triage (printability triage) — dormant, and not the mesh report
pipeline/blueprint_triage/ is a full printability-triage subsystem (analyze_triage, plan_fixes, apply_fixes, its own PrintabilityReport/PrintabilityError). On the live path it never runs: _finalize_staged_backend_state sets state.blueprint_triage = None (runner.py:698) and nothing on the staged path writes a real report; application.py:13-14 likewise only ever clears it. The facade carries the field through for compatibility (facade.py:267, 815) and the server reads it (server.py:4808, 5013) but always finds None. Its analysis/apply functions are exercised solely by tests/generator/blueprint_triage*.

Two unrelated PrintabilityReport classes. pipeline/blueprint_triage/report.py defines one (a triage report, with PrintabilityError, at report.py:180); mesh/printability.py:680 defines a completely different one (an export-facing mesh summary). They share a name and nothing else — printability.py:1069-1070 warns against conflating them. When a page says “PrintabilityReport,” it must say which.

scheduling — experimental offline layer scheduling
Prisma/generator/scheduling/ evaluates post-solve layer-swap schedules under fixed-budget policies (scheduling/__init__.py). No production module imports it — the only mention in source is a forward-looking comment in state.py:253. It is offline/experimental research code driven by tests.

Beware the scheduling package’s beam-search names. The live grouping on the solve path is the banded two-pass plan — choose_band_plan in grouping/band_plan.py, invoked from runner.py:940 (see AMS grouping and swap planning); grouping/ now contains only band_plan.py + banded_export.py. The old pluggable grouping (GroupBudgetGrouping/GreedyGrouping and their grouping/beam_search.py, grouping/greedy_optimize.py modules) was deleted — do not describe it as live. The scheduling package still exports its own setup_beam_search_policy / layer_sparse_greedy_policy (scheduling/__init__.py:48-50) — those names survive here, but the subsystem is off the solve path.

geometry — dormant region containers
Prisma/generator/geometry/ extracts vector ColorRegion polygons from a SolvedMaterialPlan (geometry/extract.py:210) and simplifies them (geometry/simplify.py). The package is internally consistent (__init__.py re-exports extract_regions/simplify_regions) but no module outside the package imports it — it is dormant. (The unrelated mesh/geometry_policy.py and assorted shapely.geometry imports are a different thing.)
mesh printability + canonical mesh — suspected inert
mesh/printability.py is a measurement-only toolkit (footprint alignment, inter-mesh seal, thin-island risk). The low-level measurement functions may be consumed by other mesh code, but the export-facing roll-up — build_printability_report (printability.py:1071) and the pass/warn/fallback/block + next_action=do_not_export classification ladder (in _classify_printability_summary, printability.py:1016-1038) — is flagged suspected inert in a code comment at printability.py:1061-1070. The code comment lists both the dedicated test and scripts/characterize_mesh_printability.py as callers, but grepping confirms the script imports only summarize_printability / render_summary_markdown (printability.py:727, 1139), not build_printability_report itself — so the export roll-up’s sole confirmed caller is tests/generator/test_mesh_printability.py. That comment is deliberately cautious because an earlier audit declared this “dead” after missing real references. Treat “inert” here as a hint, not a fact, and re-verify across tests, scripts, the config chain, and the separate blueprint_triage module before removing anything.
mesh/canonical_mesh.py (canonical_triangle_array, canonical_mesh.py:43) computes an order-insensitive geometry hash for output-equivalence checks. It is reached only through its canonical_mesh_hash wrapper (canonical_mesh.py:76), whose only non-test reference in the tree is scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py; no Prisma/generator source path calls it on a live export — suspected inert by the same standard.
Reference-bundle replay — rejected for live solves
The photo-stack Appearance provider (PhotoStackBundleAppearanceProvider, appearance_model.py:210) requires an explicit live calibration candidate or its runtime_bundle.json. Passing a bare reference bundle path is allowed only as replay; the constructor raises otherwise (appearance_model.py:232-236: “select a live calibration candidate or pass a reference path for replay only”). A bare reference bundle is therefore never the live appearance model. The default provider is "photo_stack_bundle" (SolveConfig.appearance_model_provider, facade.py:126; wired into the runner at runner.py:869 via create_appearance_provider), so a solve at defaults uses the photo-stack model and needs a selected live calibration candidate.
Removed-feature remnants
The progressive solve feature (mid-solve snapshots streamed to the browser) was deleted in the Stage 3 cleanup. What survives:

solve_preview_progressive (facade.py:849) — not imported by server.py (absent from the server.py:76-82 import block). Its docstring (facade.py:857-867) explains it is retained only as the facade-level vehicle that threads a SnapshotPublisher into the preprocessing preview hook, dormant in production, exercised by tests/generator/preprocessing/test_facade_threading.py and test_f1_smoke.py. Computationally it is identical to solve_full (both use FULL_PRESET); the _progressive suffix is a historical artifact and a queued rename candidate.
SnapshotPublisher.maybe_publish — the actual snapshot emitter — was removed; snapshot.py:6 records this and no maybe_publish call site remains in runner.py. The surviving snapshot_publisher threading (runner.py:742, 1021, 1220) is the preprocessing image-preview path — the publisher is passed into run_preprocessing_pipeline (runner.py:1021), deliberately preserved as a cheap dormant hook, not the removed progressive-solve renderer.

Stale headers — do not trust them
Liveness can never be read off a module header in this codebase; cite line anchors instead. Confirmed stale headers:



































FileHeader saysRealitysolve.py:2lith_solver.pyfile is Prisma/generator/solve.pyfacade.py:2lith_facade.pyfile is Prisma/generator/facade.pymodel.py:2lith_model.pyfile is Prisma/generator/model.pyserver.py:1-9”unified_generator/pipeline”, “port 8001”real dir Prisma/generator, port 8010grouping/__init__.py:1, pipeline/base.py:1, pipeline/registry.py:1, pipeline/state.py:1# lithophane_generator/... pathsall under Prisma/generator/
Likewise, solve.py’s six-step pipeline docstring and the appearance-model “appearance-named” method docstrings describe shapes that no longer hold: the appearance methods are pass-through (they return model-domain values, not display-converted ones) after the projection-slot retirement (appearance_model.py:218-221). When in doubt, grep the caller.
Related pages

The Joint LUT and Staged Solve — what the staged backend does inside.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.filePath: Prisma Lithophane Generator/Technical Reference/Output/AMS grouping and swap planning.md
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: AMS grouping and swap planning
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: when the solved palette needs more color filaments than fit in one AMS load, the generator runs a two-pass banded solve — a scout pass measures color usage, a deterministic planner partitions the palette into consecutive fixed-height swap bands, each band’s leftover height is topped up with white, and export emits per-band AMS slot tables plus OrcaSlicer M600 pauses at each band boundary.

This page covers everything that happens when the palette is too big for a single AMS. It serves both the user driving the wizard and the developer tracing how the band planner, the persisted swap_grouping block, and the export instruction writer fit together.

This replaced the old pluggable grouping. The former GreedyGrouping / GroupBudgetGrouping modules (grouping/greedy_optimize.py, grouping/beam_search.py) and the swap.optimize_grouping / plan_filament_groups / reconcile_export_groups machinery have been deleted. grouping/ now holds only band_plan.py and banded_export.py, and grouping is an automatic banded solve, not a post-solve module the facade wires. Do not confuse this with the offline Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental) scheduler, which is unrelated.

Related: From solve to mesh the export pipeline · generator.grouping.band_plan · generator.grouping.banded_export · generator.swap · generator.pipeline.runner · generator.facade · Print constraints

The slot budget
A printer has a fixed number of AMS slots. Some are reserved for white; the rest hold color. The budget is computed on the solve config:

ams_slots (default 4) and white_slots (default 1) — pipeline/state.py:90, pipeline/state.py:91.
effective_white_slots() bumps the white reservation to 2 when the white base and white cap are different filaments (they need two physical slots), otherwise keeps white_slots — pipeline/state.py:214-217.
color_slots() = ams_slots - effective_white_slots() — pipeline/state.py:219-220.

So with the default 4-slot / single-white setup you get 3 color slots. Pick a white cap filament that differs from the base and you drop to 2 color slots (one extra slot is spent on the second white). The same accessors exist on the facade SolveConfig (facade.py:200-206) and are read through config in the runner.

When banding triggers
Banding runs only when the palette overflows one load. _swap_banding_requested (pipeline/runner.py:50-55) returns true only when all three hold:

the preset is "full" (preview/compare never band),
this is not itself a scout sub-solve (_swap_banding_scout is not set), and
len(config.palette) > config.color_slots().

If everything fits in one load, none of this page happens — the run exports as a single group with no swaps. There is also a hard ceiling: swap-band planning stops at MAX_EXHAUSTIVE_FILAMENTS = 10 colors (grouping/band_plan.py:13); a larger palette raises before any solve (pipeline/runner.py:894-898, grouping/band_plan.py:165-168).

The two-pass banded solve
When banding is requested, run_pipeline does a scout → plan → solve sequence (generator.pipeline.runner):

Scout — _run_swap_banding_scout (pipeline/runner.py:84) runs the ordinary unbanded pipeline at bounded resolution (_downsample_swap_scout_image, pipeline/runner.py:69) with _swap_banding_scout=True so it does not recurse into banding. Its thickness maps are the measurement of how much of each color the image actually uses.
Plan — choose_band_plan (grouping/band_plan.py:149, called pipeline/runner.py:940) partitions the palette from those scout maps (below).
Store — the plan is serialized onto the state: state.swap_grouping = _swap_grouping_metadata(...) (pipeline/runner.py:947).
Solve — the real solve then runs with the band structure fixed. The remaining height above the color bands is reserved for the white cap: cap_limit_mm = t_max - d_wb - sum(band_layers)·layer_height (pipeline/runner.py:953–957), stored on the block (pipeline/runner.py:959) and applied by the staged backend to cap d_wc_max (_banded_luminance_cap_limit_mm, pipeline/staged_runner.py:9273–9277) so total Z stays within t_max.


The band plan — choose_band_plan
choose_band_plan (grouping/band_plan.py:149) receives the palette already in canonical dark-first order and keeps that order within and across bands, including filaments the scout never used:

Group count = ceil(len(palette) / color_slots) (grouping/band_plan.py:181).
Candidate partitions — _canonical_partitions (grouping/band_plan.py:40) enumerates each constrained partition of the ordered palette into that many groups of at most color_slots filaments, once each, in canonical order.
Band height — for each group, the band’s height in layers is ceil of the 0.99 quantile (BAND_HEIGHT_QUANTILE, grouping/band_plan.py:12) of that group’s summed per-pixel thickness over active pixels, floored at one layer (_height_layers, grouping/band_plan.py:83-86). The active mask is total color thickness > 1e-9 (grouping/band_plan.py:189).
Objective — the partition minimizing (total band layers, predicted white-fill volume, canonical key) wins (grouping/band_plan.py:216, grouping/band_plan.py:223): fewest layers of print height first, least wasted white second, a deterministic tiebreak third.
Budget clamp — if the winning plan’s total band layers exceed the color budget (effective_max_layers()), _clamp_band_layers scales each band down proportionally (grouping/band_plan.py:89-96); it raises if the budget cannot give every band at least one layer (grouping/band_plan.py:92-93).

The result is a frozen BandPlan (grouping/band_plan.py:28) carrying groups, band_layers, unclamped_band_layers, per-group usage stats, and the clamped flag.

Per-band white fill — band_fill_maps
Because each band is a fixed committed height, any pixel whose color stack is shorter than its band height is topped up with white. band_fill_maps (grouping/band_plan.py:119) computes, per band, fill = band_layers·layer_height − sum(group color thickness), clamped to >= 0 (grouping/band_plan.py:137-140); it raises if any pixel’s color exceeds its assigned band height (grouping/band_plan.py:138-139). This white fill is what makes every band exactly its planned height regardless of local color, so the swap-band boundaries sit at constant Z across the whole print. The facade calls band_fill_maps when reconstructing preview/solve images (facade.py:334, facade.py:367, facade.py:717, facade.py:753); the staged backend uses it for the actual fill geometry.

The persisted swap_grouping block
_swap_grouping_metadata (pipeline/runner.py:130) turns the BandPlan into a JSON-serializable dict (version = "swap_banding_v1") that is the single source of truth for export — nothing downstream re-derives band boundaries from the solved thickness maps. Its keys:













































KeyMeaninggroupslist of filament-id lists, one per band (canonical order)band_layerscommitted integer layer height of each bandunclamped_band_layerspre-clamp heights (diagnostic)band_heights_mmband_layers · layer_heightpause_z_mmZ of each band boundary: d_wb + cumulative_layers · layer_height (pipeline/runner.py:131-135)canonical_palettethe dark-first order the plan was built onlayer_height_mm, d_wb_mm, quantilereconstruction constantsper_group_scout_usage, scout_resolution, clamped, predicted_fill_volume_mm_pxdiagnosticscap_limit_mmremaining white-cap budget, added at pipeline/runner.py:959

Export-time swap planning
Group geometry and swap instructions are produced at export time from the persisted block. The endpoint is GET /api/export/swap-instructions → get_swap_instructions (server.py:6397), which delegates to _build_swap_instruction_payload (server.py:6291). Sequence:

Read AMS capacity from current config, not the cached solve — ams_slots/white_slots come from _cfg() because the user may have changed printers after solving (server.py:6303-server.py:6305).
Parse the persisted block — _swap_grouping_from_solve (server.py:1290) feeds banded_export_plan_from_metadata (grouping/banded_export.py:51, called server.py:6320), which validates the JSON into a frozen BandedExportPlan (grouping/banded_export.py:22). It returns None for an unbanded run; a partially populated block is a hard error (grouping/banded_export.py:60-62), because guessing a band boundary could put a color below the wrong pause.
Assign fixed color slots — band_slot_tables (grouping/banded_export.py:159, called server.py:6336) maps each band’s filaments to color slots 1..N and never swaps white; it raises if a band’s group exceeds the active printer’s color-slot capacity (grouping/banded_export.py:166-167).
Generate instructions — generate_swap_instructions (swap.py:16, called server.py:6343).
Generate pause G-code — generate_orcaslicer_pause_gcode (swap.py:49, called server.py:6383).

The banded payload returns banded: True with per-band groups (z_start/z_end from BandedExportPlan.band_floor_mm / band_ceiling_mm), pause_z_mm, instructions, and gcode. For an unbanded run (the palette fit one load, so there is no band plan), export falls back to _build_static_swap_instruction_payload (server.py:6193): banded: False, a single group, no pauses, and "; No filament swaps needed".
Instruction text and M600
generate_swap_instructions renders through _generate_banded_swap_instructions (swap.py:84): print dimensions, total height, per-band AMS slot assignments, one SWAP block per band boundary, then a white-cap section. Total lithophane height is final_color_ceiling_mm + max(wc_map) so the tallest color/fill stack and the thickest local cap need not coincide (swap.py:117). The number of mid-print swaps is len(pause_z_mm) (swap.py:119). Each swap’s height is the band boundary’s pause_z, converted to an approximate layer via max(1, round(pause_z / layer_height)) (swap.py:160), and the block diffs the two bands’ slot tables so the user sees exactly which color slot to unload/load. White slots are declared fixed for the whole print (_fixed_white_slot_lines, swap.py:55); a distinct white-cap filament requires two dedicated white slots (swap.py:103-106).
The actual pause command is M600. _generate_banded_orcaslicer_pause_gcode (swap.py:189) emits M600 ; pause for filament change at each band boundary (swap.py:201); with no boundaries it returns "; No filament swaps needed" (swap.py:192-193).

Quick reference



































You want to…KnobAnchorGet more color slotsUse a single white (base == cap)pipeline/state.py:214-217Avoid banding entirelyKeep palette size ≤ color slotspipeline/runner.py:50-55Understand band heightsScout usage → choose_band_plangrouping/band_plan.py:149Trace the persisted planswap_grouping blockpipeline/runner.py:130See the swap planExport → swap-instructions endpointserver.py:6397

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Color-region geometry (dormant)
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: Prisma/generator/geometry/ turns a solved plan into first-class vector color-region polygons (ColorRegion/RegionGeometry), and mesh/canonical_mesh.py hashes meshes for order-insensitive equivalence — both are real, tested code with no production caller, so they do not feed STL/3MF output today.

This page exists to stop a reader from assuming these two well-built subsystems are on the live print path. They are not. The export path is documented in Exporting Print Files; what is actually wired end-to-end is cataloged in What Actually Runs. This page is the explicit “wired-but-unused” record for the geometry package and the canonical_mesh oracle.
The geometry package — what it does
Prisma/generator/geometry/ derives connected, same-stack color regions from a SolvedMaterialPlan and expresses each as an explicit boundary polygon in solved image-domain millimeters.






























SymbolModuleRoleColorRegiongenerator.geometry.regionOne connected same-stack component: exterior ring + hole rings (mm), segment_ids, area_mm2, bbox_mm. frozen dataclass (geometry/region.py:22).RegionGeometrygenerator.geometry.regionContainer of all regions + image-domain dimensions + solve pitch (geometry/region.py:65). Accessors n_regions (geometry/region.py:88) and regions_for_stack (geometry/region.py:91).extract_regions(plan)generator.geometry.extractThe entry point: plan → RegionGeometry (geometry/extract.py:210).simplify_region / simplify_regionsgenerator.geometry.simplifyRamer-Douglas-Peucker contour reduction in mm space (geometry/simplify.py:73, geometry/simplify.py:117).
How extract_regions works (developer view)
extract_regions (geometry/extract.py:210) reads three things off the plan and produces region polygons:

It expands the per-segment stack assignment into a full per-pixel stack-label image by indexing segment_stack_id with segment_id_map (geometry/extract.py:229). Those two arrays are the plan’s identity/assignment split — segment identity is immutable, the stack assignment is the mutable material choice (pipeline/solved_material_plan.py:99, pipeline/solved_material_plan.py:100).
For each distinct stack label it runs scipy.ndimage.label (imported geometry/extract.py:18, called geometry/extract.py:239) so that disconnected patches of the same stack become separate ColorRegions — one connected component per region, never fused.
For each component it traces a rectilinear, pixel-corner-aligned boundary by walking mask edges (_mask_to_grid_polygon, geometry/extract.py:38) and unions them with shapely (geometry/extract.py:143), deliberately avoiding marching-squares half-pixel offsets (rationale stated geometry/extract.py:8). The largest ring becomes the exterior and the rest become holes (_extract_rings, geometry/extract.py:153; exterior-vs-hole selection geometry/extract.py:194).
Coordinates are converted to mm using solver_fine_pitch_mm (geometry/extract.py:227) and emitted Y-down in array convention (geometry/region.py:11 documents the convention; the Y flip back to Y-down is applied in _to_y_down, geometry/extract.py:179).

Provenance survives: each region carries the source segment_ids it covers (geometry/extract.py:247, stored at geometry/extract.py:268).
How simplification works
simplify_regions(geometry, tolerance_mm) is the public sweep (geometry/simplify.py:117); it delegates to simplify_region per region (geometry/simplify.py:73), which RDP-simplifies the exterior and each hole ring via the internal _rdp (geometry/simplify.py:25). Contracts worth knowing:

tolerance_mm <= 0 is an exact identity — the original objects are returned untouched (geometry/simplify.py:128 for the sweep, geometry/simplify.py:84 per region).
Closure is preserved, and a ring that would collapse below 4 vertices is left un-simplified to stay a valid polygon (geometry/simplify.py:67).
It is explicitly not printability cleanup — it only re-represents an already-accepted boundary, it never decides whether a region should exist (stated geometry/simplify.py:11). Printability lives elsewhere; see Exporting Print Files.
bbox_mm and area_mm2 are recomputed from the simplified rings (geometry/simplify.py:93, geometry/simplify.py:103), reusing _signed_area imported back from the extract module (geometry/simplify.py:101).

Liveness: wired-but-unused
The package is internally complete — geometry/__init__.py re-exports ColorRegion, RegionGeometry, extract_regions, and simplify_regions (geometry/__init__.py:13-geometry/__init__.py:15). But a grep for any importer outside the package itself finds none in Prisma/generator/. The only consumer anywhere in the tree is the test suite:

tests/generator/test_phase4_region_extraction.py:16 imports extract_regions, ColorRegion, RegionGeometry and exercises them across ~12 cases (test_phase4_region_extraction.py:62 onward), including an end-to-end run_pipeline → extract_regions case (test_phase4_region_extraction.py:285).

No staged_runner, server, facade, or mesh/export module imports geometry. So despite the package docstring calling these objects the “downstream geometry of record for color-layer export” (geometry/__init__.py:4), nothing exports through them — that header is aspirational, not a description of the current wiring. Trust the line anchors above, not the prose at the top of the file. This matches the audit note in Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract and the dormancy entry in What Actually Runs.


                  
                  Do not confuse with the live export geometry 
                  
                

The STL/3MF that OrcaSlicer opens is built by the mesh/export path described in Exporting Print Files, driven from the staged backend (The staged backend (Stage 0-5)). The shapely.geometry imports in mesh/rectilinear_interval.py and mesh/printability.py are unrelated to this geometry package — same word, different code. The historical plans that wanted region geometry to become the export authority (e.g. the 2026-04-11 “geometry-native printability” sketches) were never wired in.


Status — geometry package: WIRED-BUT-UNUSED (test-covered, no production caller). Confirmed by grep over Prisma/generator excluding the package and the test that imports it.
canonical_mesh — a test/verification equivalence oracle
mesh/canonical_mesh.py answers one question: “are these two meshes the same shape, ignoring face order, vertex order within a face, and vertex renumbering?” It is a verification helper, not part of building geometry.

























FunctionAnchorBehaviorcanonical_triangle_arraymesh/canonical_mesh.py:43Quantize each triangle (XY at mesh pitch, Z at layer height — _quantize_triangles, mesh/canonical_mesh.py:30), sort the 3 vertices within each triangle (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:67), then sort triangles lexicographically (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:72).canonical_mesh_hashmesh/canonical_mesh.py:76SHA-256 over that array, domain-separated by the quanta and face count (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:101-mesh/canonical_mesh.py:108). Accepts (vertices, faces) arrays or a trimesh.Trimesh (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:87).canonical_mesh_equalmesh/canonical_mesh.py:112True iff two (vertices, faces) meshes hash equal.
The criterion is spelled out at mesh/canonical_mesh.py:10-mesh/canonical_mesh.py:19: intentionally insensitive to face/vertex ordering and index renaming, while still catching any real geometric difference. It exists so an emitter rewrite that reorders faces can be proven output-preserving even when byte-identical STL is no longer available (mesh/canonical_mesh.py:6).
Liveness: suspected inert on the live path
Grep across the whole tree finds these symbols referenced only in: this file, the Architecture node generator.mesh.canonical_mesh, two docs/mesh_printability/ plan/validation write-ups, the doc agent’s knowledge files, and exactly one runnable caller — scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py:23 imports canonical_mesh_hash and calls it at scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py:123 to fingerprint exported objects in a benchmark. No Prisma/generator/ source path calls it on a live export, and (unlike the geometry package) no test in tests/ imports it — a grep for canonical_mesh under tests/ returns nothing.
Status — canonical_mesh: SUSPECTED INERT on the live path. Its sole non-doc caller is the standalone benchmark script scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py; it was the equivalence oracle for the white-cap vectorised-emitter work (docs/mesh_printability/validation/white_cap_step3_vectorised_emitter_2026-04-20.md) and survives as a reusable check, not as a runtime gate.
If you want to revive either

To put region geometry on the export path you would add a caller that takes state.solved_plan (The pipeline orchestrator and shared state), runs extract_regions, optionally simplify_regions, and feeds the polygons to an emitter — none of that wiring exists today.
To use canonical_mesh as a CI gate, import canonical_mesh_hash/canonical_mesh_equal in a test and assert two emitter variants agree; the benchmark script (scripts/benchmark_mesh_export_heavy_options.py) shows the call shape.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Export request lifecycle and artifact ownership
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
POST /api/export/files/start is the live webapp export entry point. It resolves a completed solve, materializes a fresh export bundle from the cached solve, calls export_solve_bundle, optionally packages the in-memory mesh bundle as 3MF, writes swap instructions, and returns file URLs plus the manifest. POST /api/export/files is the synchronous equivalent retained for direct callers and tests.
Request and target selection
ExportFilesPayload accepts geometry_source (field_derived by default or exact_raster), field_scale (2, 4, 8, or 16; default 4), output_format (3mf by default or stls), validate_written_meshes (false by default), and an optional card_id. _resolve_export_target selects the current or saved solve. The current target must still match the solve-owned fingerprint; a changed solve-owned setting produces HTTP 409 and requires a new solve. Supplying card_id selects a saved card and bypasses this current-session staleness check.
Before materialization, _prepare_export_materialization applies _force_mandatory_product_settings and calls prepare_export_material_maps. The material-map helper now makes shallow dictionary/list copies and preserves the solve maps and ordering; the removed translucent-underfill promotion is not part of export.
Background job lifecycle
The start route stores export state in session["export"], creates a UUID job_id, and launches a daemon thread. The thread reports ExportProgressEvents through _progress_dict_from_export_event, which converts stage index/fraction into an overall percentage. GET /api/export/files/status returns the job state, progress detail, elapsed time, and completed result. POST /api/export/files/cancel sets cancel_requested; the progress callback raises ExportCancelled at the next progress event. The job becomes complete, error, or cancelled in the session state.
Cancellation and failure are not a transactional artifact rollback. The export directory may contain partially written files or a manifest from work completed before the exception; a later export starts by deleting same-family files and the previous stls/ directory for its newly selected export ID. The code does not promise cleanup of a cancelled directory.
Materialized bundle and mesh export
_materialize_post_solve_export_bundle_from_cached_solve writes arrays.npz, run_template.json, prediction_replay_metadata.json, and stageA_field_bundle_summary.json under the current run’s post_solve_export_bundle. It requires the canonical white-cap field target, white-boundary/detail fields, physical geometry metadata, and a valid persisted swap_grouping when present. Missing or stale canonical export fields fail with HTTP 409 instead of silently reconstructing them from obsolete maps.
export_solve_bundle then builds the immutable ExportMeshBundle and writes export_manifest.json. STL output is written only when output_format == "stls", under stls/, one file per nonempty mesh object. The optional written-mesh validation reloads those STLs and records reload quality; it is disabled by default. The build-time quality gates and geometry-source details remain on From solve to mesh the export pipeline.
For output_format == "3mf", the server does not write STLs first. It passes the in-memory bundle through coalesce_color_quarantine_for_3mf_bundle, which may combine a color parent with same-material quarantine objects for packaging, then calls write_export_mesh_bundle_as_3mf. The 3MF writer bakes object transforms into vertices and writes a single OPC package. The package path is {export_id}.3mf, and _write_3mf_packaging_manifest_update adds format_packaging["3mf"] to the already-written manifest. That packaging report explicitly records that package meshes are not revalidated after coalescence.
3MF material slots are package-local: _filament_assignments_for_export assigns one-based slots in first-seen material order, while _material_display_names_for_export resolves registry display names. These assignments are separate from the active AMS slot tables used by swap instructions; a 3MF slot number is not a promise about the printer’s current AMS layout.
Swap instructions and returned artifacts
After mesh export, _build_swap_instruction_payload reads the persisted swap_grouping plan without recomputing band boundaries. It reads the current printer’s ams_slots and white_slots, validates that each band fits, assigns band-local color slots, and renders text plus M600 pause G-code. If there is no plan, it emits the single-load payload. If the plan is unavailable or invalid for the current printer, the endpoint returns an unavailable payload or HTTP 409; it does not regroup the solved plan.
The export response lists the manifest, swap instructions when available, STL files or the 3MF package, and URLs rooted at /api/export/files/{filename}?dir={export_id}. GET /api/export/files-zip packages the files in that export directory, including export_manifest.json, swap_instructions.txt, the 3MF package, and any stls/*.stl files. File serving uses _safe_path, so the :path route still rejects traversal outside the selected output directory.
Anchors





































ContractSourcePayload validationserver.py:712-739Materialization and product safety boundaryserver.py:805-835, :4564-4760Synchronous/background/cancel/status routesserver.py:6070-6200Export orchestration and 3MF packagingserver.py:5813-6067Persisted plan validation and swap payloadserver.py:6291-6423Mesh bundle construction and manifestmesh/post_solve_export.py:2549-2870STL/3MF serializers and quarantine coalescencemesh/export_serializers.py:90-420

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental)
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the scheduling/ package is a deterministic research harness that quantizes an already-solved material plan into per-layer filament/white assignments and scores competing ordering policies, but it is wired only into one offline eval script and its tests — nothing in the live solve or export path calls it.

This page is the status note for the fixed-budget layer scheduler. It exists to answer two questions a future reader will have: does the print I export actually use this? (no), and what does it compute if I run it by hand? (per-layer schedules plus setup/tiny-presence metrics). The aliasing target [[Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental)]] resolves here.
Liveness: NOT in the live solve/export path
The package lives at Prisma/generator/scheduling/ with three implementation modules plus a re-export shim:

























FileRolescheduling/model.pydataclasses + quantization, derives cases from a SolvedMaterialPlanscheduling/policies.pysix deterministic ordering policies + a registryscheduling/metrics.pybudget/reserve checks + setup-change / tiny-presence costsscheduling/__init__.pyre-exports everything, adds build_schedule_case / evaluate_policy convenience entry points
Grepping the whole tree for importers of the package, the only non-package, non-test caller is one offline script: scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py. That script’s own header states it does not export STL / 3MF geometry and does not mutate repo-tracked configuration or pipeline state (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:7-8).
Confirmed by grep — these live entry points contain zero references to scheduling, LayerSchedule, setup_beam_search, etc.:








































SubjectStatusEvidenceLive webapp serverdoes not call schedulingno matches in Prisma/generator/server.pyStaged backend (the real solve engine)does not call schedulingno matches in pipeline/staged_runner.pySolve facade / CLI enginedoes not call schedulingno matches in facade.py, runner.py, solve.pySolveStatementions scheduling only in a commentpipeline/state.py:256 (“consumed by export, triage, and scheduling”) — no import, no callOffline eval scriptonly runtime callerscripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:106-111, :1556Test suiteimports the packagetests/generator/test_layer_scheduling.py:8 (12 test functions)
The state.py:256 comment is aspirational wording, not a wiring. The schedule outputs are never meshed: the live mesh/export path is documented in From solve to mesh the export pipeline and the staged backend in The staged backend (Stage 0-5); neither touches this package.

Disambiguation: the experimental setup_beam_search / layer_sparse_greedy policies here belong to this offline scheduler and are unrelated to swap grouping. The pluggable grouping beam-search/greedy modules that once lived under grouping/ have been deleted; grouping is now the automatic banded solve that The Solve Facade describes (generator.grouping.band_plan / generator.grouping.banded_export). Do not confuse this offline scheduler with that live path.

What “fixed-budget” means
The scheduler never decides how much of each filament a region gets — the solve already committed that. It only decides layer order within a fixed material budget. A budget is committed material thickness; quantization turns thickness into an integer layer count via round(thickness_mm / layer_height_mm), rejecting any non-zero thickness whose reconstruction error exceeds a 1e-6 mm tolerance (scheduling/model.py:65-73, tolerance QUANTIZATION_TOLERANCE_MM at :34). White is tokenized as WHITE_LAYER_TOKEN = "__white__" (scheduling/model.py:35); in an absolute schedule, white is represented as None (scheduling/model.py:195-196).
Deriving a case from a solved plan
derive_fixed_budget_schedule_case(plan, ordering, layer_height_mm, d_wc_min_mm, ...) (scheduling/model.py:375) reads an immutable SolvedMaterialPlan (generator.pipeline.solved_material_plan) and produces a FixedBudgetScheduleCase. Steps:

Quantize each stack’s color budgets into ordering-stable positive (filament_id, count) tuples (scheduling/model.py:407-422 calling _ordered_positive_color_layers at :77). Any stack filament with positive thickness that is missing from ordering raises (scheduling/model.py:411-415).
Quantize the per-pixel cap-height map into integer white-cap layer counts (scheduling/model.py:424-433).
Label each pixel by stack via committed_stack_label_map(plan) (scheduling/model.py:435, defined in generator.pipeline.derived_views at derived_views.py:33), and build a total_layers_map = stack_total_layers[labels] + cap_levels (scheduling/model.py:440).
Derive an anisotropic white surface reserve from cliff geometry (see below) and take the elementwise max against the flat d_wc_min-derived reserve (scheduling/model.py:441-448).
Group identical (stack_index, cap_layers, effective_reserve, sidewall_reserve, sidewall_band) pixels into unique signatures with their pixel counts and area_mm2 (scheduling/model.py:450-490).

If top_white_reserved_layers is not given, it defaults to ceil(d_wc_min_mm / layer_height) (scheduling/model.py:393-394) — i.e. the minimum white cap implied by the solve’s d_wc_min. min_printable_line_width_mm defaults to the plan’s solver_fine_pitch_mm (scheduling/model.py:397-401), and the sidewall band width in pixels is ceil(line_width / fine_pitch) clamped to ≥1 (scheduling/model.py:402-405).
derive_unique_layer_budget_signatures(...) (scheduling/model.py:505) is the thin wrapper returning just the signatures tuple.
The anisotropic sidewall reserve
derive_anisotropic_white_surface_reserve(total_layers, band_width_px=...) (scheduling/model.py:355) returns (reserve_layers, sidewall_band_mask). It finds, per pixel, the local positive height drop to its lower 4-neighbors (_internal_cliff_drop_layers, :317), then propagates that reserve inward only across the high side of a cliff for band_width_px - 1 steps (_propagate_sidewall_reserve, :329). The intent: a tall region adjacent to a short one exposes a vertical wall that needs a white shell, and that reserve should not spill onto the lower face. This is the only geometry-aware part of the model; everything else is pure integer bookkeeping.
The signature dataclass (the unit of work)
LayerBudgetSignature (scheduling/model.py:94) is a frozen dataclass holding one committed (stack, cap) combination:









































FieldMeaningstack_indexwhich committed color stack (:107)orderingthe global filament order tuple (:108)color_layers((fid, count), ...), all counts > 0 (:109)white_layersquantized white-cap layer count (:110)top_white_reserved_layerscontiguous white run the schedule must keep on top (:111)base_top_white_reserved_layersthe flat d_wc_min-derived component (:112)sidewall_white_reserved_layersthe cliff-derived component (:113)sidewall_bandwhether this signature sits in a sidewall band (:114)
__post_init__ enforces non-negativity, ordering membership, no duplicate filaments, positive counts, and that the effective top-white reserve covers both the base and sidewall reserves (scheduling/model.py:116-158). Convenience: total_color_layers (:165), total_layers (:169), full_layer_budget_map() which adds the __white__ token (:185).
A LayerSchedule (scheduling/model.py:191) pairs a signature with absolute_layers — a bottom→top tuple of filament-id-or-None, plus the policy_name that produced it (:199-201).
The six policies
All policies take a FixedBudgetScheduleCase and return one LayerSchedule per entry. They are deterministic and bounded. The registry is POLICY_REGISTRY (scheduling/policies.py:640); get_policy_registry() returns a copy (:650).








































Policy nameFunctionBehaviorbaseline_top_white_only:470Control: fixed global ordering, all white on top (_fallback_schedule, :43).white_envelope:484Same color order, but bury surplus white below the color block, keep only the reserved run on top (_white_envelope_schedule, :79).absorber_strength_global_order:491Re-order colors strongest-absorber-first, then fixed top-white (absorber_strength_order, :108).layer_sparse_greedy:514Greedy case-level scheduler: pick one area-weighted-preferred filament per absolute layer; signatures take it when they can, else white, with a repair pass that re-fills white slots to preserve totals exactly (:603-625).setup_beam_search:344Bounded beam search (width _DEFAULT_BEAM_WIDTH = 12, :28) over per-layer family templates, ranked by (setup_cost, active_count, tiny_penalty, prefix_len) (_BeamState.rank_key, :70). Falls back to baseline if the beam empties (:422-423).setup_beam_guarded:445Runs beam search and baseline, evaluates both, and keeps the beam result only if it strictly beats baseline on (setup_change_cost, total active, tiny_penalty, transition_cost) (_report_rank_key, :436; comparison :465-467).
absorber_strength_order (scheduling/policies.py:108) ranks filaments by 1 - mean(predict_transmission(profile, layer_height)) — i.e. how much a single layer of that filament darkens — loading profiles via the shared model.load_profile / predict_transmission (generator.model, imported policies.py:20), with an lru_cache on per-filament strength (:93-105).
Every policy enforces the white-on-top reserve by appending exactly min(white_layers, top_white_reserved_layers) None layers at the top (_top_white_layers_used, scheduling/policies.py:31).
The metrics
metrics.py scores a (case, schedules) pair. The headline costs:



































MetricFunctionWhat it countsBudget preservationbudget_preserved (metrics.py:81) / budget_preservation_deltas (:49)Whether observed layer counts exactly match the signature’s full_layer_budget_map(); deltas list any mismatch. A correct schedule has zero deltas.Top-white reserve OKtop_white_reserve_ok (metrics.py:89)Whether the schedule’s own top reserve layers are all white (:100).Setup-change costsetup_change_cost (metrics.py:218)Minimum family-change cost with carry-over loaded state across adjacent layers — a tiny DP over which family is “loaded” after each layer (:231-248). Start family defaults to white.Adjacent-layer transition costadjacent_layer_filament_set_transition_cost (metrics.py:206)Symmetric-difference size of the active non-white filament set between neighboring layers (:213-214).Tiny-presence penaltytiny_presence_penalty (metrics.py:251)For each family/layer whose total area is below min_area_mm2 (default 1.0, :255), adds threshold - area (:262-266).
Area is aggregated per absolute layer either including white (family_area_by_absolute_layer_mm2, :103) or excluding it (filament_area_by_absolute_layer_mm2, :134 — note: white is deliberately dropped here because the metric tracks chromatic activity, :140-142). Setup/tiny costs use the white-inclusive aggregation; “active filament” counts use the white-exclusive one.
evaluate_case_schedules(case, schedules, ...) (metrics.py:270) bundles all of the above into a frozen ScheduleEvaluation (scheduling/model.py:285), aligning schedules to entries by signature first (_align_schedules, metrics.py:22). The tiny-presence threshold here defaults to 1.0 mm² (metrics.py:275).
Driving it by hand
There is no UI and no CLI flag. Two ways to exercise it:
1. Package convenience API (scheduling/__init__.py):

build_schedule_case(payload) (:68) — dispatches to a synthetic fixture (build_swap_pressure_case / build_synthetic_equal_budget_case) or, given a solve_result carrying a solved_plan, calls derive_fixed_budget_schedule_case (:91-103).
evaluate_policy(case, policy_name) (:117) — runs one named policy and returns a flat dict of costs (setup_change_cost, active_count, tiny_presence_penalty, top_white_penalty, budget_ok, the schedules, etc., :124-145). Policy-name aliases map short names to canonical ones (POLICY_NAME_ALIASES, :54).

2. The offline eval script (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py):
python scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py --out-dir <dir> \
    --cases synthetic_swap steve cafe \
    --policies baseline white_envelope absorber_strength_order \
               layer_sparse_greedy setup_beam_search setup_beam_guarded

It performs a real bounded solve per case (solve_full, :441) under a fixed recommended_v2 posture (dual_resolution_v2 + greedy grouping, :68-73), builds a scheduling case through a defensive adapter (SchedulerAdapter, :181; module discovery _load_scheduler_adapter, :482), evaluates every policy, and writes report.md + summary.json plus per-case stack_strips.png / layer_activity.png visuals (:1612-1616, _write_case_visuals :1492). It picks a “winner” with a weighted chooser whose weights (setup_change_cost 40, active_count 25, tiny_presence_penalty 20, top_white_penalty 10, printability_proxy 5) live in CHOOSER_COMPONENTS (:98-104) — note these chooser weights are the script’s, not the package’s. The adapter tries module names ("scheduling", "layer_scheduling", "schedule_evaluation", "evaluation.scheduling") (:106-111); only scheduling exists, so the others are dead fallbacks.
The synthetic fixtures build_swap_pressure_case (scheduling/model.py:589) and build_synthetic_equal_budget_case (:526) are also the basis of much of the test suite (tests/generator/test_layer_scheduling.py, 12 tests).
Stale-header warnings

The module docstrings are accurate here, but the package-status framing in scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:12-15 (“expected to land separately from this runner”) and the adapter’s import-failure message (scripts/evaluate_layer_schedules.py:578-579, “once the new scheduling package lands”) are stale — the package has landed; the adapter’s multi-name probing is now vestigial.
The pipeline/state.py:256 comment listing scheduling as a plan consumer overstates reality: no live code path consumes scheduling output.

See also

Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract — the plan this scheduler reads
From solve to mesh the export pipeline — the path that does produce printed geometry (and does not call this)
The staged backend (Stage 0-5) — the real solve engine
The Solve Facade — the live solve path; its swap grouping is the automatic banded solve, not this offline scheduler

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: From solve to mesh the export pipeline
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: export_solve_bundle reads a materialized solve bundle off disk, decides whether to print the exact solved raster or a smoother field-derived white cap, builds one watertight mesh object per material into a single ExportMeshBundle, and serializes it as per-object STL files or one packed 3MF — writing an export_manifest.json that records every object’s geometry, material, and mesh quality.

This page is the backend mechanics of export. For the user-facing webapp flow (HTTP routes, polling, AMS swap plan) read Exporting Print Files; this page follows what happens inside the one entry point that page calls. The whole contract lives in generator.mesh.post_solve_export and is deliberately free of any FastAPI/UI dependency — geometry is built before serialization, and format writers only serialize already-built meshes (mesh/export_mesh_bundle.py:1).
The boundary: MeshObject and ExportMeshBundle
Everything funnels through two frozen dataclasses in generator.mesh.export_mesh_bundle. They are the export boundary: mesh generation happens before them, format writers only consume them.
A MeshObject (export_mesh_bundle.py:16) is one positioned mesh in the shared coordinate frame. It carries raw vertices/faces arrays plus four identity strings — object_key, material_key, role, mesh_style — an optional 4×4 transform, and free-form metadata. It is built from a trimesh via MeshObject.from_trimesh (export_mesh_bundle.py:29), which copies vertices as float64 and faces as int64. to_trimesh (export_mesh_bundle.py:55) reconstructs a trimesh.Trimesh with process=False and applies the stored transform lazily, so the transform is only baked at serialization time.





























MeshObject fieldMeaningobject_keyUnique handle; also the STL filename stem and a thickness-map lookup keymaterial_keyWhich filament the object prints in (drives 3MF extruder slot)roleSemantic tag (white_base, color, combined_white_cap, white_cap_slab, …) used for display namesmesh_styleHow it was built (flat_plate, rectilinear_interval, primitive_frame, hybrid styles)transformOptional 4×4; None until a border shift or hybrid placement applies one
An ExportMeshBundle (export_mesh_bundle.py:73) holds the tuple of MeshObjects plus the export-wide metadata: image_domain_width_mm/height_mm, layer_height_mm, xy_quantum_mm, the object_coordinate_frame string, a mesh_build_report, a per-object quality map, color_export_details, and source_blueprint_fingerprint. The frame string is the constant OBJECT_COORDINATE_FRAME = "x-left-to-right_y-bottom-to-top_z-build-plate-mm" (post_solve_export.py:63). object_by_key (export_mesh_bundle.py:90) is a linear lookup over the tuple.
Note the bundle is immutable: every transformation (_with_mesh_build_report at post_solve_export.py:1138, _with_export_border at post_solve_export.py:1185) constructs a new ExportMeshBundle rather than mutating one.
The ten-stage pipeline
export_solve_bundle (post_solve_export.py:2549) is the integration entry point. The webapp calls it from _perform_export_files (server.py:5813, at the call site server.py:5884); the heavy-benchmark harness and the export tests call the same function. It walks a fixed ten-stage progress sequence, DEFAULT_EXPORT_STAGES (post_solve_export.py:199), emitting an ExportProgressEvent per stage and timing each scope with an ExportTimingCollector (post_solve_export.py:167).




























































#Stage idWhat happens in export_solve_bundle1load_bundleResolve the bundle dir, load arrays.npz and the JSON sidecars (post_solve_export.py:2583)2detect_solve_modeDetect standard vs luminance; pull pitch / layer height / base thickness / border from metadata (post_solve_export.py:2591)3prepare_material_mapsCopy color maps, build the RectilinearExportConfig (post_solve_export.py:2651)4build_geometry_sourceBranch on exact-raster vs field-derived (post_solve_export.py:2686)5build_color_base_meshesWhite base flat plate + one z-slab object per color filament6build_white_cap_meshesExact white cap (with topology fallbacks) or hybrid field cap7validate_banded_geometryFor swap-banded plans, audit band geometry via audit_banded_export_geometry (post_solve_export.py:2769); no-op otherwise8serialize_outputsWrite per-object STLs (3MF packing is done by the caller afterward)9validate_meshesOptional reload-and-recheck of written STLs10write_manifestBuild and write export_manifest.json
Web publication is a directory transaction
export_solve_bundle writes to the directory its caller supplies. The web server never supplies the final user-facing directory directly: _perform_export_files creates a private .export-stage-{export_id}-{nonce} sibling under OUTPUT_DIR and sends every STL, 3MF, manifest, and swap-instruction write there. _finalize_staged_export computes the response against final paths, rewrites absolute staging paths in the manifest to their final equivalents, and issues a final publish_outputs progress event. That event is the last cooperative cancellation checkpoint.
Only after every deliverable, manifest update, size check, and response record succeeds does the server rename the complete staging directory to {export_id}. The destination must still be absent; an independently created directory is never replaced. Failure or cancellation before that rename recursively removes the private stage and leaves no user-visible partial export. No fallible export work occurs after the rename. Download and individual-file GET routes resolve requested directories without creating missing ones.
Stage 1 — Load the bundle
_resolve_solve_bundle_dir (post_solve_export.py:2279) accepts either an arrays.npz file, the directory containing it, or a parent that holds exactly one such directory; it raises FileNotFoundError if it cannot find a unique one. _load_bundle_arrays (post_solve_export.py:2295) loads arrays.npz with allow_pickle=False. Three JSON sidecars are read with _load_json_file (post_solve_export.py:2269): stageA_field_bundle_summary.json (the summary), prediction_replay_metadata.json (the replay, which names the color filament ids), and run metadata via _bundle_run_metadata (post_solve_export.py:2303, preferring run_template.json then run.json). The webapp writes all of these in _materialize_post_solve_export_bundle_from_cached_solve before calling export — the replay block records color_thickness_filament_ids (server.py:4724).
Stage 2 — Detect the solve mode
detect_solve_mode_from_metadata (post_solve_export.py:266) returns a SolveMode enum — STANDARD or LUMINANCE (post_solve_export.py:74). Solve mode is not a user export toggle; it is detected. The signal is a required luminance_mode key, searched across run/bundle metadata and their nested export_metadata physical_geometry / white_cap_field_target sections (post_solve_export.py:300); standard maps to STANDARD, any other value to LUMINANCE. If no luminance_mode is present anywhere it raises ExportPreparationError (post_solve_export.py:305) — the old array-key fallback is gone, and array_keys is now ignored (post_solve_export.py:274). This stage also reads pitch, layer height, and white-base thickness from the solved bundle’s physical_geometry metadata via _required_physical_float (post_solve_export.py:2363, sourced by _physical_geometry_metadata_from_run at post_solve_export.py:2343); border settings come from _first_config_float (post_solve_export.py:2382) / _first_config_bool (post_solve_export.py:2408), which search a priority chain of metadata containers. If border is disabled, both border dimensions are forced to zero (post_solve_export.py:2646).
Stage 3 — Prepare material maps (now a near no-op)
_bundle_color_maps (post_solve_export.py:2450) unpacks the (F, H, W) color_thickness_maps array into a {filament_id: 2D map} dict keyed by the replay’s color_thickness_filament_ids, raising if the count mismatches (post_solve_export.py:2464). A RectilinearExportConfig (post_solve_export.py:214) is assembled from the resolved dimensions; its export_policy() (post_solve_export.py:232) produces a GeometryExportPolicy (generator.mesh.geometry_policy, geometry_policy.py:96) carrying the canonical printability pitch.
The separate module prepare_export_material_maps (generator.mesh.material_maps, material_maps.py:9) is the historical “prepare material maps” step but is now intentionally a near no-op: it returns shallow copies of the maps and ordering unchanged (material_maps.py:19). Its docstring confirms it previously promoted a solve-only translucent-underfill placeholder into a real filament map, but that feature was removed (material_maps.py:15). Liveness: this function is still wired — the webapp calls it through _prepare_export_materialization (server.py:805 → server.py:811), which runs before the bundle is materialized, not inside export_solve_bundle. So in the webapp path the maps are prepared (copied) once on the server side and the in-bundle “prepare_material_maps” stage just rebuilds the config. The two are distinct steps that happen to share a stage name.
Stage 4 — Choose the geometry source
GeometrySource (post_solve_export.py:67) is the one genuinely user-visible export choice: FIELD_DERIVED or EXACT_RASTER, normalized by normalize_geometry_source (post_solve_export.py:246). The branch is at post_solve_export.py:2686.

Exact raster loads the combined white-cap thickness map from the bundle via _bundle_white_cap_map (post_solve_export.py:2474) and calls build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle (post_solve_export.py:1535).
Field derived reconstructs the white-cap height field from the bundle arrays via reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays (generator.mesh.field_white_reconstruction) (post_solve_export.py:2710). It validates the field is an integer uniform upscale of the solve grid (post_solve_export.py:2725), derives field_scale, builds a finer-pitch RectilinearExportConfig and a HybridWhiteCapConfig, and calls build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution (post_solve_export.py:2748).

Stages 5–6 — Build the geometry
Both geometry sources share _base_and_color_objects (post_solve_export.py:1298) for the base and color stacks:

The white base is a single flat plate via generate_flat_plate (post_solve_export.py:1319), object key __white_base__ (post_solve_export.py:55), role white_base, style flat_plate.
Each color filament is meshed as a rectilinear interval body that floats on the accumulating floor (the running sum of layers below it) via _mesh_rectilinear_interval (post_solve_export.py:472, delegating to generator.mesh.rectilinear_interval mesh_interval_map). Color order follows the ordering, skipping any __-prefixed keys (post_solve_export.py:1333).
If a color body fails the strict reload-quality check, it is rebuilt defensively — first as a same-material topology quarantine (_build_color_quarantine_parts, post_solve_export.py:1109), and if that still fails as constant-Z slab bodies (_build_color_z_slab_parts, post_solve_export.py:992). This exists because a clean single-body mesh can become non-manifold after STL vertex welding; splitting at snapped plateaus keeps geometry exact while avoiding reload pinches (post_solve_export.py:1006).

The white cap differs by source:

Exact raster (build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle, post_solve_export.py:1535) meshes the combined cap as one rectilinear interval (post_solve_export.py:1566). If it passes strict quality it ships as a single combined_white_cap object (post_solve_export.py:1597). If not, it falls through a cascade: forced slabs (_build_exact_white_cap_slabs, post_solve_export.py:506), then a topology quarantine (_build_white_cap_quarantine_parts, post_solve_export.py:781), then a recursive adaptive Z-partition that splits only failing Z ranges (_build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts, post_solve_export.py:602). Each branch records its selected_strategy.
Field derived (build_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution, post_solve_export.py:1987) keeps color stacks and base on the exact solve grid, nearest-upsamples only the combined color-top witness map to the field resolution (post_solve_export.py:2080), then builds a hybrid guard/freeform white cap via build_overlap_white_cap_mesh (generator.mesh.hybrid_white_cap) (post_solve_export.py:2081). It asserts the color/field/hybrid configs agree on solve pitch, layer height, and base thickness (post_solve_export.py:2036).

Both builders finish through _bundle_from_objects (post_solve_export.py:2138), which stamps the mesh_build_report with geometry source, detected solve mode, geometry policy, and per-object vertex/face totals, then optionally wraps the bundle with a printable border frame via _with_export_border (post_solve_export.py:1185). When a border is enabled, the content objects are translated inward by the border width and a __border__ frame object (post_solve_export.py:62) is appended, printed in the white-cap material (post_solve_export.py:1254).
Stage 7 — Audit swap-banded geometry
For swap-banded plans only, export_solve_bundle audits the banded geometry with audit_banded_export_geometry, folds the result into the mesh_build_report and manifest validation block, and raises ExportPreparationError if the audit fails. The audit checks the stored band plan against the emitted color floors/ceilings, pause planes, and total non-border surface. Exact-raster export derives the expected surface from the solve-grid cap map; field-derived export deliberately substitutes the maximum of the reconstructed field-resolution cap actually used to build the mesh (post_solve_export.py:2696-2737, :2783-:2797). This prevents a valid field-derived swap export from being rejected against the different solve-grid cap maximum while preserving all band/pause checks. It does not write a duplicate standalone audit JSON. When there is no band plan the stage is a no-op. The banded solve/plan story itself lives in AMS grouping and swap planning.
Stage 8 — Serialize per-object STL (3MF is the caller’s job)
If write_stls is true, export_solve_bundle imports and calls write_export_mesh_bundle_as_stls (generator.mesh.export_serializers, export_serializers.py:90) into an stls/ subdirectory (post_solve_export.py:2808). That writer skips empty objects, maps each object_key to a filename via _object_filename (export_serializers.py:20), and bakes the transform by exporting obj.to_trimesh(copy_arrays=False) (export_serializers.py:105). It returns {object_key: Path}.
The 3MF path is not inside export_solve_bundle. When the user picks 3MF the webapp passes output_format == "3mf", so export_solve_bundle is called with write_stls=(output_format == "stls") — i.e. False for 3MF (server.py:5889) — and the caller packs the in-memory bundle with write_export_mesh_bundle_as_3mf (export_serializers.py:373) afterward (server.py:5929). That writer builds one OPC-packaged zip: a [Content_Types].xml, a _rels/.rels, and 3D/3dmodel.model (export_serializers.py:413). Each object becomes a <object> with a slic3rpe:extruder slot (export_serializers.py:134) and an identity-transform <build> item; transforms are baked into vertices before writing (export_serializers.py:129). The extruder slot per object comes from filament_assignments — the webapp builds these by assigning one slot per distinct filament id via _filament_assignments_for_export (server.py:4768), and human-readable names via _material_display_names_for_export (server.py:4751), passed at server.py:5934–5935. Liveness: both STL and 3MF writers are live — STL via export_solve_bundle, 3MF via the webapp 3MF branch and the dedicated test tests/generator/test_export_3mf_filename.py.
Stage 9 — Validate quality
Mesh quality is computed at build time per object with check_mesh_quality (generator.mesh.quality, quality.py:20), which reports watertightness, open edges, pinch edges (counts != 2), and winding consistency. The export uses two stricter local gates: _quality_passes (post_solve_export.py:344, requires watertight + zero open + zero pinch) and _strict_processed_quality (post_solve_export.py:352), which re-welds the mesh with process=True and counts non-2-valence edges — emulating what a slicer-reload would see. This stage itself is optional reload validation: only if validate_written_meshes is true does it re-load every written STL from disk through _reload_quality_for_path (post_solve_export.py:2525) and record reload_quality (post_solve_export.py:2815); otherwise it is disabled by default (post_solve_export.py:2823). In the webapp this is driven by payload.validate_written_meshes (server.py:5890).
Stage 10 — Write the manifest
build_export_manifest (post_solve_export.py:2187) assembles the JSON-serializable manifest (schema post-solve-export-manifest-v1, post_solve_export.py:2208). Its status is "ready" unless any object’s quality shows open edges, pinch edges, or non-watertightness, in which case "mesh_quality_failed" (post_solve_export.py:2211). It records the content/export footprint, border, grid, geometry policy, a per-object list (with STL paths if written), the full quality map, and the mesh_build_report. _jsonable (post_solve_export.py:310) coerces enums, numpy scalars/arrays, and Paths. write_export_manifest (post_solve_export.py:2262) writes it pretty-printed and sorted to export_manifest.json. The performance timings dict (ExportTimingCollector.as_dict, post_solve_export.py:191) is attached before writing (post_solve_export.py:2856).
The white-cap field-target contract
The field-derived path and solve-mode detection are governed by generator.white_cap_contract (white_cap_contract.py), a dependency-free module of shared export-contract constants that post_solve_export imports directly. It fixes the canonical field-target array key white_cap_field_target_upper_surface_map and metadata key white_cap_field_target (white_cap_contract.py:7-10) under schema white-cap-field-target-v1, alongside the physical_geometry metadata key that carries pitch / layer height / base thickness. detect_solve_mode_from_metadata and _field_target_metadata_from_run read these keys; a field-derived export is rejected unless the run metadata names this exact field target (post_solve_export.py:2336). The module also enumerates the three per-mode white-cap policies (white_cap_contract.py:12-16) — POLICY_STANDARD_SMOOTH_VARIABLE_CANONICAL, POLICY_STANDARD_APPEARANCE_BOUNDED_STRUCTURAL_SPLIT, and POLICY_LUMINANCE_DETAIL_CANONICAL — and exposes quantized_cover_floor_mm (white_cap_contract.py:19), the smallest layer-quantized cap thickness at or above a minimum cover.
What you get back
export_solve_bundle returns a PostSolveBundleExportResult (post_solve_export.py:86): the in-memory bundle, the manifest dict and its written manifest_path, the output_paths map ({object_key: Path} for written STLs), the tuple of progress_events, and reload_quality. The webapp reuses result.bundle directly to pack the 3MF, so the meshes are never re-read from disk for that format.
Progress and timing plumbing
ExportProgressReporter (post_solve_export.py:126) emits an ExportProgressEvent (post_solve_export.py:101) per stage; the webapp adapts these to its polling shape in _progress_dict_from_export_event (server.py:5754), turning stage index + fraction into an overall percentage. ExportTimingCollector.scope (post_solve_export.py:175) is a context manager that records wall-clock per labeled stage for performance audits, surfaced under manifest["performance"].
Related
