prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Robust rectilinear meshing
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the generator turns each filament’s grid-aligned thickness map into a closed, slicer-safe triangle shell by walking every column’s vertical material intervals, assigning corner vertices to local occupied 2x2x2 sectors so the solid can touch itself at a point or edge without welding into a non-manifold blob, then merging flat faces, splitting bad fans, stitching open edges, separating coincident vertices, and filling residual holes — with a per-material fallback ladder (single body → topology-quarantine → Z-slab / adaptive-Z) that escalates only when a body fails the strict watertight check.

This page covers the geometry engine in generator/mesh/. It serves two readers: the user who just wants STLs that slice cleanly, and the developer who needs to know exactly how the shell is built and why a body sometimes splits into extra parts.
Where this runs (liveness)
The webapp’s export worker _perform_export_files (server.py:5813, called by the export routes) is the live entry point. It calls export_solve_bundle (mesh/post_solve_export.py:2549), which loads the solve bundle, detects the solve mode, and dispatches on geometry source:




















Geometry sourceBuilderWhite capEXACT_RASTERbuild_exact_raster_mesh_bundle (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1535)rectilinear interval map of the combined cap, with the fallback ladderFIELD_DERIVEDbuild_field_derived_mesh_bundle_mixed_resolution (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1987)hybrid: rigid rectilinear guard + freeform surface
Both builders call the same color-stack mesher (_base_and_color_objects, mesh/post_solve_export.py:1298). The field path additionally reconstructs the cap thickness map from solve fields (reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:196) and meshes it with build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:768).
All seven source modules named below are reachable from this one entry point — confirmed by import-and-call grep, not by module headers (which are stale: several still frame the code as “future webapp wiring” or a “sandbox” trial even though the webapp path is live).
The core mesher: mesh_interval_map
mesh_interval_map (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:778) is the workhorse. It takes a floor map and a thickness map (both H×W, in mm) plus the XY pitch_mm, and returns one closed single-material trimesh.Trimesh plus a RectilinearMeshStats audit record (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:34). Every color layer, the exact-raster cap, and the hybrid rigid guard go through it.
1. Z levels and per-slab occupancy
A column is “active” when its thickness exceeds eps (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:813). The set of distinct floor-and-top heights across all active columns becomes the global Z level array (_global_z_levels, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:122) — so every height where any column starts or stops material is a shared cutting plane. Each gap between consecutive Z levels is a “slab”; _occupancy_by_slab (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:131) marks, per column, which slabs are filled, using searchsorted on the column’s floor and top. The result present is an H×W×K boolean occupancy grid.
Optional z_snap_decimals rounds floor/top to a fixed decimal grid before level extraction (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:802), with top clamped >= floor so rounding can’t invert an interval (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:807). The export config defaults to z_snap_decimals = 6 (mesh/post_solve_export.py:218); the hybrid config defaults to 6 as well (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:47). Snapping makes adjacent layers share exact plane heights so their walls coincide instead of leaving a sub-micron crack.
2. Exposed faces
_neighbor_masks (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:163) shifts present in all six directions. A face is emitted wherever a filled cell has an empty neighbor: present & ~neighbors[dir] for east/west/north/south/top/bottom (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:844). _append_quads (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:186) turns each exposed cell-face into a quad, recording four corner grid indices (row, col, z) plus a 3-bit local code identifying which of the eight surrounding cells owns that corner. Corner winding order deliberately mirrors the legacy per-pixel emitter (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:209).
3. The 2x2x2 sector trick (the heart of it)
This is the mechanism that keeps a self-touching solid closed instead of pinched. Around every grid corner there are eight surrounding cells, forming a 2x2x2 neighborhood. _corner_patterns (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:149) packs the 8 occupancy bits of that neighborhood into one 8-bit code per corner (stored in a uint16 array, but only the low byte is ever set, so the lookup tables are sized 256). SECTOR_LOOKUP (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:114, built by _sector_lookup, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:80) is a 256×8 table that, for each of the 256 patterns, runs a connected-component flood over the occupied corners (6-connected adjacency, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:91) and labels which sector each occupied cell belongs to.
When two material regions of the same filament meet only at a corner point or along a single edge, the 2x2x2 pattern has two disconnected occupied components, so that corner gets two distinct sector labels. Each face vertex is keyed by (row, col, z, sector) (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:916), so the two regions get separate vertices at the same coordinate instead of one shared vertex. That prevents a single point/edge from being incident to too many faces — the classic non-manifold pinch that slicers reject. SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:115) precomputes how many sectors each pattern splits into; _split_count (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:455) sums the “extra” sectors across the whole grid for the diagonal_or_corner_splits stat.
4. Vertex assembly
Quad corners are encoded into a single integer key (((row·(W+1)+col)·K + z)·8 + sector) (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:916), uniquified, and split into two triangles per quad (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:925). The key is decoded back into (x, y, z) world coordinates by reversing the packing (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:935), with y flipped to image-up orientation (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:943). The mesh is built process=False (no auto-weld) and only duplicate/degenerate faces are dropped (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:949).
5. Horizontal-face merge (optional, default on)
With merge_horizontal_faces=True (config default mesh/post_solve_export.py:217), top and bottom faces are not emitted as per-cell quads; only the four side directions are (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:863). Instead, _append_horizontal_merged_faces (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:409) treats each slab’s top/bottom mask as a region to be triangulated as a whole, drastically reducing triangle count on flat plateaus.
Per connected component (ndi.label with 4-connectivity, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:329), _component_ring_groups (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:250) traces the exact pixel-corner boundary rings with trace_mask_grid_rings (mesh/grid_rings.py:9) rather than Shapely booleans — deliberately, so long collinear boundary runs are kept and the merged face shares exact edge vertices with the unmerged side-wall quads (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:255). Rings are grouped into [outer, holes...] by signed area (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:263) and point-in-polygon containment (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:273). The polygon is triangulated by shapely.constrained_delaunay_triangles (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:357), falling back to mapbox_earcut if that raises (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:362). Every triangle vertex is re-mapped back to its occupied 2x2x2 sector via _component_vertex_key (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:279) so merged faces use the same sector-keyed vertices as the walls. flip controls bottom-vs-top winding (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:398).
trace_mask_grid_rings itself (mesh/grid_rings.py:9) walks boundary half-edges with a left-turn rule (mesh/grid_rings.py:38) to produce oriented loops; _trace_mask_grid_rings is an alias (mesh/grid_rings.py:86).
The cleanup pipeline (post-construction, in order)
After the raw shell exists, mesh_interval_map runs a fixed sequence (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:957–991):















































StepFunctionWhat it doesAnchorOverfull fan split_split_overfull_edge_fansonly on the merged path: splits the face fan at any edge used by >2 faces, cloning the shared vertex per connected fan group (union-find over incident faces)mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:559, called :958Open-edge stitch_stitch_duplicate_open_edgeswelds geometrically-coincident open (count-1) edge pairs left by sector splitting, via union-find on vertex coords rounded to 9 decimalsmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:652, called :961Re-split (merged)_split_overfull_edge_fanssecond fan split after stitching, merged path onlymesh/rectilinear_interval.py:963Separate duplicates_separate_duplicate_verticesnudges topologically-distinct coincident vertices apart by a sub-micron XY offsetmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:722, called :965Hole fill (≤2 passes)trimesh.repair.fill_holesfills any remaining count-1 edges, then re-runs fan-split + separation on added facesmesh/rectilinear_interval.py:972–989Fix normalstrimesh.repair.fix_normalsconsistent outward winding (fix_normals defaults True)mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:990
The unmerged quad path skips the first fan split entirely (fan_splits = 0, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:960) because sector-keyed quads can leave duplicate open edges but cannot create an over-full edge — see the inline rationale at mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:951. Merged horizontal triangulation can produce unpredictable fans, so the splitter is kept for it.
Why separate, don’t weld
_separate_duplicate_vertices (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:722) exists because STL does not preserve vertex identity — a slicer re-welds any two vertices at the same coordinate on import, which would undo the sector split and recreate the pinch. So at already-split contacts it shifts each duplicated vertex by offset_mm along the in-plane direction toward its incident-face centroid (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:767), introducing a tiny XY-only geometric gap (Z is never touched) without changing topology. Default offset is 0.001 mm (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:787, config mesh/post_solve_export.py:219). The hybrid module carries its own identical copy of this routine (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:519).
The hole-fill loop only triggers when count-1 (open) edges remain (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:974) and stops early if a pass adds no faces (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:979); newly-added fill faces get the same fan-split + separation treatment (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:984).
Mesh quality gates
check_mesh_quality (mesh/quality.py:20) is the product quality summary: it counts per-edge face references (edge_face_counts, mesh/quality.py:8), reports n_open_edges (count == 1) and n_pinch_edges (non-2 minus open) plus is_watertight. A mesh passes when watertight with zero open and zero pinch edges (_quality_passes, mesh/post_solve_export.py:337).
Because the exported (separated) mesh must survive a slicer’s reload-weld, there is a stricter second gate. _strict_processed_quality (mesh/post_solve_export.py:345) rebuilds the mesh with trimesh process=True — which does weld coincident vertices, simulating the slicer — and re-checks edges. _strict_processed_quality_passes (mesh/post_solve_export.py:371) requires watertight with zero strict-non-2 and zero open edges. A body is only accepted as-is when it passes both gates (color: mesh/post_solve_export.py:1343 via _color_mesh_quality_passes at :1098; white cap: mesh/post_solve_export.py:1454). Passing the loose gate but failing the strict one is the signal that “this will pinch after import” — and that triggers the fallback ladder.
The white-cap fallback ladder
When a single-body interval mesh fails the strict gate, the orchestrator escalates by splitting the body into multiple same-material parts that each survive welding. The escalation differs between the white cap and color layers.
White cap (exact-raster path), build_exact_raster_mesh_bundle
The decision is at mesh/post_solve_export.py:1454:

Single interval — if force_exact_white_cap_slabs is off and both gates pass, ship the one body (selected_strategy = "single_interval", mesh/post_solve_export.py:1459).
Forced slabs — if force_exact_white_cap_slabs is on (config default False, mesh/post_solve_export.py:220), skip straight to constant-Z slabs via _build_exact_white_cap_slabs (mesh/post_solve_export.py:499, dispatched :1471). Each gap between snapped Z levels becomes one flat-bottomed slab body.
Topology quarantine — otherwise, _build_white_cap_quarantine_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:774). This cleaves only the risky columns into a second same-material body, leaving the rest intact. If that yields a ready result, ship it (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1494).
Adaptive-Z partition — if quarantine still fails, _build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:595, dispatched :1500).

Topology quarantine, _build_interval_topology_quarantine_parts
The shared quarantine engine (mesh/post_solve_export.py:807) first asks topology_risk_column_mask (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:485) which solve-grid columns sit adjacent to a multi-sector corner (a SECTOR_COMPONENT_COUNT > 1 vertex touching an occupied slab, mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:530–541). With no risk columns it reports no_risk_columns and bails (mesh/post_solve_export.py:834). Otherwise it tries six partitions of those risk columns — row_even/odd, col_even/odd, checker_even/odd (mesh/post_solve_export.py:847) — meshing the “main” body (risk cells removed) and the “quarantine” body (only risk cells) separately (mesh/post_solve_export.py:866). It accepts the first partition where both bodies pass both gates (mesh/post_solve_export.py:963); status is "ready" only if no part failed (mesh/post_solve_export.py:967). The idea: separating the touching cells into a different body means their welded-together vertices belong to different shells, so the pinch never forms.
Adaptive-Z partition, _build_exact_white_cap_adaptive_parts
This recursively bisects the Z range (build_range, mesh/post_solve_export.py:651). It clips the cap to [z0, z1] with _clipped_interval_map (mesh/post_solve_export.py:571), meshes it, and if it passes both gates accepts it as one part (mesh/post_solve_export.py:689). If it fails and spans more than one Z level, it splits at the midpoint and recurses (mesh/post_solve_export.py:751). A single-level range that still fails is shipped anyway tagged white_cap_slab_failed (mesh/post_solve_export.py:743) — the strategy emits everything and records leaf failures rather than aborting the export.
Color layers, _base_and_color_objects
Color materials use a slightly different ladder (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1346):

Single body if both gates pass (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1343).
Else topology quarantine via _build_color_quarantine_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1102); shipped if status == "ready" (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1356).
Else Z-slab fallback via _build_color_z_slab_parts (mesh/post_solve_export.py:985) — one same-material body per snapped material plateau (mesh/post_solve_export.py:1021).

The white base plate is never an interval mesh; it is a single make_box plate (generate_flat_plate, mesh/primitives.py:50; called mesh/post_solve_export.py:1304).
The hybrid white cap (field-derived path)
build_hybrid_white_cap_meshes (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:621) builds the cap as two same-filament bodies so the layer-exact region near the color stacks stays rigid while the rest follows the smooth field surface:

Rigid guard — a rectilinear interval body (mesh_interval_map again, mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:651) that exactly caps the color columns and laterally shields them out to guard_width_mm. Its intervals come from derive_hybrid_white_cap_intervals (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:150): guard floor sits on the color top (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:194), and the lateral guard domain is the air ring within guard_width_mm of color (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:176) raised to the neighboring color top (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:187).
Freeform surface — mesh_freeform_cap_surface (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:402) builds a continuous top+bottom skin over the optically-free region. Per active cell it emits two top triangles and two bottom triangles (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:473) plus boundary walls (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:480). It has its own 2x2x2-style diagonal handling: at a checkerboard contact (NW+SE occupied, NE+SW empty, or the mirror) it assigns the shared corner a sector bit so the two diagonal cells get distinct vertices (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:432, :439), counted as diagonal_corner_splits. Corner heights are averaged from incident cells (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:450), then the surface is separated + hole-filled like the rigid path (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:503).

validate_hybrid_white_cap_intervals (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:298) sweeps layers and checks the guard+free union never removes reference-white coverage and never leaves color exposed; guard_coverage_status is "pass" only when zero exposed-color and zero removed pixels (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:391). The result’s status property (mesh/hybrid_white_cap.py:116) returns mesh_quality_failed if any cap body has open/pinch edges, else coverage_review if coverage didn’t pass, else ready.
Field reconstruction (upstream of the hybrid mesh)
reconstruct_field_white_cap_from_arrays (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:196) converts solve-bundle scalar fields into the cap thickness map the hybrid mesher consumes. It picks a target upper surface per solve mode (_target_upper_surface, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:177), where both standard and luminance now read a single canonical target field (WHITE_CAP_FIELD_TARGET_UPPER_SURFACE_KEY) via _canonical_target_upper_surface (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:144), upsamples to a finer grid by field_scale (default 4, mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:33), then collapses layer-by-layer into integer layer counts (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:257). Each layer’s white mask is cleaned by _cleanup_white_mask (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:73): tiny internal air voids are filled and tiny positive features removed, with thresholds from GeometryPrintabilityPolicy (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:210). It stops before mesh construction by design (mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py:5).
Printability policy
Thresholds are resolved once into GeometryPrintabilityPolicy (mesh/geometry_policy.py:21). The solve-grid pitch is the hard minimum positive width — a 0.2 mm grid means 0.2 mm minimum feature (mesh/geometry_policy.py:23). Derived defaults: lateral guard width defaults to that min width (mesh/geometry_policy.py:47), max internal empty-hole area defaults to 0.5·width² (mesh/geometry_policy.py:54), min positive feature area to width² (mesh/geometry_policy.py:64). GeometryExportPolicy (mesh/geometry_policy.py:95) bundles pitch/layer-height/white-base and enforces that any supplied printability policy agrees on the solve pitch (mesh/geometry_policy.py:120). These policy objects do not read UI state — callers resolve settings first and pass resolved numbers in (mesh/geometry_policy.py:1).
The audit record
Every interval mesh emits RectilinearMeshStats (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:34), serialized via as_dict (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:56) into the export manifest’s per-object stats. Useful fields when debugging a non-manifold report: diagonal_or_corner_splits (sector splits), nonmanifold_edge_fan_splits, duplicate_open_edge_stitches, separated_duplicate_vertices, filled_hole_faces, and the three topology_risk_* preflight counts (mesh/rectilinear_interval.py:466). The fallback reports also carry single_interval_quality / single_interval_strict_processed_quality so you can see why the single body was rejected before the ladder kicked in.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Blueprint triage the unwired engine
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: pipeline/blueprint_triage/ is a complete, tested printability-analysis engine — seven defect detectors, a CLEAN/WARNINGS/DISQUALIFYING verdict, and a fix planner with counterfactual-dE costing — that the live solve never calls (the state slot it would fill is hard-wired to None), so today it runs only under its own test corpus.

Blueprint triage: the unwired engine
This page documents the blueprint_triage package at design-intent altitude. It is not an exhaustive API reference for every helper, because the whole subsystem is computed-but-unwired: no live solve or export path constructs an AnalysisContext or calls analyze_triage. Read it to understand what was built and how it was meant to work, and as a map for anyone considering wiring it in.
Liveness up front — this is dormant, test-only
The state slot that would hold a triage report is PipelineState.blueprint_triage, declared Optional["PrintabilityReport"] = None at pipeline/state.py:280. Its full lifecycle in the live path:






























SiteWhat happensAnchorDeclaredblueprint_triage: Optional["PrintabilityReport"] = Nonepipeline/state.py:280Written (live)Stage-5 bridge of the staged backend sets state.blueprint_triage = None — never a real reportpipeline/runner.py:566Read (live)Facade passes it straight through: blueprint_triage=getattr(state, "blueprint_triage", None)facade.py:906Asserted dormantA real run_pipeline test asserts state.blueprint_triage is None after solvingtests/generator/blueprint_triage/test_runner_invocation.py:31
The engine’s three public entry points — analyze_triage, plan_fixes, apply_fixes — have zero callers outside the package and its tests. A repo-wide grep for those symbols excluding blueprint_triage/** returns only one legacy-audit markdown doc (Prisma/generator/docs/legacy_audit/07_COMPATIBILITY_MAPS_AND_EXPERIMENTAL_BRIDGE.md), never production code. The only generator-code reference to the package at all (outside state.py/runner.py/facade.py above) is server.py:98, which imports only PrintabilityError — see the disambiguation trap below; that import is unrelated to the triage engine’s verdict path.
The detectors, planner, and costing are nonetheless substantially tested: ~30 test modules under tests/generator/blueprint_triage/ plus four sibling suites (blueprint_triage_cliff, blueprint_triage_gate, blueprint_triage_line_width, blueprint_triage_sub_feature). So the code is exercised and presumed correct in isolation — it is simply not invoked by the product.

Calling it “Lane A/D” etc.: the source carries internal lane labels (e.g. application.py:42 references “Lane D”; planning.py:459 references “D.3”). These are development-phase tags, not user-facing concepts.

How it would work (the intended flow)
SolvedMaterialPlan + ExposureContext
        │
        ▼
AnalysisContext.from_state(...)          fields.py:131
        │
        ▼
analyze_triage(plan, context)            api.py:18
        │   runs 7 detectors → classifies → builds verdict
        ▼
PrintabilityReport (verdict + hazards + summary + fingerprints)   report.py:180
        │
        ├── plan_fixes(report)           planning.py:25   → ranked FixCandidate list
        │       (counterfactual_cost per candidate)        costing.py:15
        ▼
apply_fixes(plan, candidates, state=...) application.py:19   → mutated plan + cache invalidation

AnalysisContext — the precomputed input bundle
AnalysisContext (fields.py:110) is the immutable bundle every detector reads. The classmethod AnalysisContext.from_state(state, *, exposure) (fields.py:131) builds it from a solved pipeline state; it requires state.solved_plan and raises ValueError otherwise (fields.py:138). What it precomputes:


















































FieldBuilt byMeaningcolor_ceiling_mapcolor_ceiling_from_plan (cap_quality.py:58), called at fields.py:146per-pixel top of colored material (white base + color stack)top_surface_maptop_surface_from_fields (cap_quality.py:70), called at fields.py:147color ceiling + white-cap heightinterval_schedule_build_interval_schedule (fields.py:222)per-pixel ordered MaterialInterval column: white base → colors (palette order) → white capper_filament_masks_build_per_filament_masks (fields.py:283)boolean occupancy per filament id; white base omitted (everywhere by construction), __white_cap__ added where cap > 0salience_build_salience_fields (fields.py:314)Sobel luminance/chroma gradients on the solve-grid OKLab targetfidelity_prior_build_fidelity_prior (fields.py:361)residual proxy = __de__ raster scaled by normalized salienceconfigTriageConfig (config.py:22)triage-owned thresholds + ranking weightscolor_profiles / wb_profile / wc_profile_resolve_profiles (fields.py:204)forward-model spline profiles, needed only for counterfactual prediction
The interval schedule is the spine of the structural detectors. Each pixel column is a list of MaterialInterval(z_start_mm, z_end_mm, material_id) (fields.py:20), starting with MaterialInterval(0.0, d_wb, "__white_base__") (fields.py:254) and ending with a "__white_cap__" interval from the color ceiling to ceiling+cap (fields.py:264).
ExposureContext (fields.py:47) carries edge-exemption data: an exempt_outer_perimeter flag and an optional exempt_edge_mask of shape (H, W, 4) in direction order (up, down, left, right) (fields.py:50). ExposureContext.from_export_bundle (fields.py:94) derives the inset border-exemption mask from a print’s border width — this is the one piece a test exercises directly (tests/generator/blueprint_triage_gate/test_orchestration_gate.py:20).
The seven detectors
analyze_triage (api.py:18) runs seven detectors and assembles a PrintabilityReport. Detectors split across detect/general.py (structural column invariants), detect/features.py (xy footprint geometry), and detect/cliffs.py (color-step exposure). All return lists of Hazard dataclasses (report.py:34).





























































#DetectorSourceWhat it flagsDefault severity1Voiddetect_voids (detect/general.py:15)a pixel column with no schedule (MissingColumnHazard, general.py:22) or a positive-z gap between stacked intervals (general.py:33)always DISQUALIFYING2Floatingdetect_floating (detect/general.py:48)column starts above z=0 unsupported (general.py:56), or an interval doesn’t abut material below it (general.py:69)always DISQUALIFYING3Overlapdetect_overlaps (detect/general.py:86)non-finite / negative-thickness interval (general.py:92), or adjacent intervals overlapping in z (general.py:109)always DISQUALIFYING4Sub-featuredetect_sub_features (detect/features.py:29)xy connected component below min printable area/width, per material per z-layer, deduped by (material_id, bbox)graded — see below5Narrow stranddetect_narrow_strands (detect/features.py:107)skeletonized footprint segments thinner than the soft line-width thresholdgraded — see below6Cliffdetect_cliffs (detect/cliffs.py:20)a color step where one pixel’s color ceiling is exposed to air above a shorter 4-neighbor (cliffs.py:188)graded by exposure depth in analyze_triage7Skyscraperidentify_skyscrapers (detect/cliffs.py:38)isolated tall thin plateau among cliff high-sides (prominence + isolation gated)structural metadata only
The structural trio (void/floating/overlap) walk context.interval_schedule.intervals directly and treat any breach as a hard invariant violation — they always emit Verdict.DISQUALIFYING. The column epsilon is max(1e-6, layer_height_mm * 0.01) (general.py:127).
Graded severities (sub-feature, narrow strand, cliff)
The footprint detectors classify against hard/soft thresholds in TriageConfig:

Sub-feature (_sub_feature_severity, detect/features.py:196): DISQUALIFYING below hard_min_feature_area_mm2 or hard_min_feature_width_mm; WARNINGS below the soft_* equivalents; otherwise None (no hazard).
Narrow strand (_strand_severity, detect/features.py:214): DISQUALIFYING below hard_min_line_width_mm; WARNINGS below soft_min_line_width_mm. Uses skimage.morphology.skeletonize (features.py:124) and an EDT-derived local width.
Cliff: detectors emit raw CliffRegions; severity is decided in analyze_triage itself by comparing region.max_exposure_depth_mm against cliff_block_depth_mm / cliff_warn_depth_mm (api.py:42, api.py:50), wrapping each into a CliffHazard (report.py:130).

Skyscrapers and salience
identify_skyscrapers (detect/cliffs.py:38) clusters cliff high-side pixels into cap-floor-coherent components (_cluster_high_side_pixels, cliffs.py:372), then gates each on footprint area, width, prominence (skyscraper_prominence_mm) and isolation score (skyscraper_isolation_threshold) — cliffs.py:90–cliffs.py:98. Survivors get a blended feature_salience_score mixing the cliff salience, local feature support (score_noise_vs_feature, cliffs.py:136), prominence, and target-vs-ring contrast, with an isolation penalty (cliffs.py:108–cliffs.py:115). Crucially, skyscrapers are not a verdict input — analyze_triage never adds them to blocking_hazards or warnings; they only inform fix planning.
Salience itself is image-driven: _build_salience_fields (fields.py:314) takes Sobel derivatives of the solve-grid OKLab target (fields.py:334), with chroma being the gradient norm over the (a,b) channels (fields.py:344) and combined = hypot(luminance, chroma) (fields.py:351).
The verdict
analyze_triage aggregates into a PrintabilityReport (report.py:180). The verdict logic (api.py:67–api.py:71):
blocking_hazards = voids + floating + overlaps
                 + DISQUALIFYING sub-features + DISQUALIFYING narrow-strands + blocking cliffs
warnings         = WARNINGS sub-features + WARNINGS narrow-strands + warning cliffs

verdict = DISQUALIFYING if blocking_hazards
          else WARNINGS if warnings
          else CLEAN

Verdict is the three-value enum CLEAN / WARNINGS / DISQUALIFYING (report.py:12). The report also carries a ReportSummary of per-category counts (report.py:167), plus a plan_fingerprint and context_fingerprint (api.py:94, api.py:95) so a verdict can be checked for staleness against a (plan, exposure) pair. That check is the job of ValidatedBlueprintToken (report.py:199): from_report snapshots the fingerprints + verdict + summary, and is_valid_for(plan, context_fingerprint) re-hashes the plan and compares (report.py:214). No live code constructs or consumes such a token today.
Fix planning, costing, and application
If the verdict is not clean, the engine can propose and cost repairs. None of this runs in production; it is the most elaborate dormant part.
Fix types
FixType (report.py:18) enumerates ACCEPT, SHORTEN, WALL, SMOOTH, HYBRID, TRANSLUCENT_SMOOTH, TRANSLUCENT_HYBRID, BULLDOZE. Of these, only a subset is actually implemented end-to-end:





















































FixTypeGenerated in plan_fixes?Applied in apply_fixes?Simulated in costing?ACCEPTyes (every hazard)no-op (application.py:27)n/aSHORTENyes_apply_shorten (application.py:84)yes (costing.py:86)WALLcliff only_apply_wall (application.py:103)yes (costing.py:95)SMOOTHcliff only_apply_smooth (application.py:111)yes (costing.py:99)HYBRIDcliff only_apply_hybrid (application.py:146)yes (costing.py:107)BULLDOZEskyscraper onlyrouted through _apply_shorten (application.py:29)yes (costing.py:86)TRANSLUCENT_*never generatedNotImplementedError (“see Lane D”, application.py:41)NotImplementedError (costing.py:137)
plan_fixes — candidate generation and ranking
plan_fixes(report, policy=None) (planning.py:25) iterates cliff / skyscraper / sub-feature / narrow-strand hazards (planning.py:33–planning.py:36), generates candidates per hazard via _generate_candidates (planning.py:77), and scores them in two passes:

Heuristic pass — _heuristic_scores (planning.py:343) fills a FixScoreBreakdown (report.py:147) from cheap proxies: material cost (pixel area), a per-FixType workflow_cost table (planning.py:376), a shape_cost table keyed on feature salience (planning.py:383), and a printability_gain (planning.py:425).
Counterfactual pass — for the top-N viable candidates per hazard (counterfactual_top_n_per_hazard, default 3, planning.py:40), it replaces the heuristic image_cost with the true counterfactual_cost (planning.py:57) and re-finalizes the composite (planning.py:64).

The composite score (_composite, planning.py:414) is a weighted sum:
image·w_image + material·w_material + shape·w_shape + workflow·w_workflow − printability_gain·w_gain, with weights from TriageConfig. Candidates are then ranked (planning.py:66), and a phase-2 refinement (_apply_phase2_refinement, planning.py:600) folds the cheapest realized fix cost back into each region’s feature_salience_score.
counterfactual_cost — the dE penalty of a fix
counterfactual_cost (costing.py:15) answers “how much does this fix hurt the image match on the pixels it touches?” It:

simulates the fix on a copy of the plan (_simulate_fix, costing.py:67),
runs the forward model on just the affected pixels (_predict_oklab_for_pixels, costing.py:196, via predict_transmission + to_oklab from generator.model),
compares the modified per-pixel dE against the baseline dE (__de__ raster or recomputed baseline, costing.py:47),
returns the mean positive increase in dE — an improvement scores 0 (costing.py:40).

This is the only part of the engine that needs the forward-model profiles on the context; if they are missing it raises ValueError (costing.py:205).
apply_fixes — mutation and cache invalidation
apply_fixes(plan, candidates, *, state=None) (application.py:19) first asserts the batch’s target masks don’t overlap (_assert_non_overlapping, application.py:69), then dispatches each candidate to its _apply_* mutator. When a state is passed it invalidates derived caches (invalidate_triage_cache, application.py:12 — sets state.blueprint_triage = None and state.plan_derived_cache = None) and rebuilds state.thickness_maps via compatibility_thickness_maps (application.py:48), preserving any __de__ / __gamut_mask__ diagnostics (application.py:60). The shared SMOOTH/HYBRID geometry builder is build_smooth_target_cap_height_map (application.py:182), a linear distance-falloff cap raise reused by both planning.py and costing.py.
TriageConfig — the knobs
TriageConfig (config.py:22) holds only triage-owned thresholds and ranking weights; physical printer constraints stay on PipelineConfig. TriageConfig.from_pipeline_config (config.py:54) derives them: the hard floors come from the printer’s minimum extrusion width (config.py:55), while the soft (warning) band uses the nozzle-derived feature scale _FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE * nozzle_diameter from generator.preprocessing.feature_scale (config.py:68). Cliff depths key off layer height: cliff_warn_depth_mm = layer_height, cliff_block_depth_mm = max(2·layer_height, layer_height) (config.py:73).
Two PrintabilityError, two PrintabilityReport (trap)
There are two unrelated PrintabilityError and PrintabilityReport symbols in the generator — do not conflate them:




















SymbolThis page’s moduleThe other, unrelated onePrintabilityReportblueprint_triage/report.py:180 (verdict + hazards)mesh/printability.py mesh-export classification (build_printability_report, mesh/printability.py:1071)PrintabilityErrorblueprint_triage/report.py:29reused by the mesh-exposure gate
The single live raise of blueprint_triage’s PrintabilityError is not in the triage engine at all: server.py:98 imports it, and _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2369) raises it when a white-cap solve exposes colored filament. Even that gate is flagged suspected-inert / test-only by an in-code note (server.py:2362) — during a live solve only the non-raising audit runs. Likewise, mesh/printability.py:1061 carries an explicit warning that its export classification is suspected inert and that its PrintabilityError/PrintabilityReport must not be confused with this module’s. See Printability three layers for how these distinct printability mechanisms relate.
Related

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Printability three layers
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the generator has three separate “printability” subsystems at three abstraction levels — a per-pixel-column triage (blueprint_triage, test-only/dormant), a per-layer staged diagnostic + Stage 4 gate (staged_printability, the one that actually runs on every web solve), and a mesh-level measurement roll-up (mesh/printability.py, suspected inert) — and only the middle one is on the live path.

This is the orientation page for everything named “printability” in the generator. The name is overloaded: three unrelated modules share it, two of them define their own PrintabilityReport class, and most module docstrings are stale. Before trusting any liveness claim, read the master liveness map in What Actually Runs — this page links there rather than re-deriving each verdict, and adds the per-module physical detail the map omits.
The three subsystems differ in what they look at and whether they run:

































LevelModuleLooks atOutputStatusPer-pixel columngenerator.pipeline.blueprint_triage.apiMaterial intervals in each pixel column (voids, floats, overlaps, cliffs)A triage PrintabilityReport + fix candidatesDORMANT — test-only, never written on the live pathPer-layer stagedgenerator.pipeline.staged_printabilityConnected components inside each color/cap/detail layerA BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic report and an in-place Stage 4 repair gateLIVE — runs on every web solveMesh measurementgenerator.mesh.printabilityBuilt trimesh.Trimesh geometry (footprint, seals, thin islands)A different PrintabilityReport + export verdict ladderSUSPECTED INERT — only tests/scripts call the roll-up
Level 1 — per-pixel column triage (blueprint_triage) — dormant
pipeline/blueprint_triage/ walks the solved plan one pixel column at a time. Each column is a stack of MaterialIntervals, and the detectors flag structural hazards by inspecting those intervals: an empty column raises a MissingColumnHazard (“Pixel column has no material schedule.”, pipeline/blueprint_triage/detect/general.py:24), a positive-z gap inside a column is a VoidHazard (detect/general.py:37), and adjacent intervals that overlap become an OverlapHazard (detect/general.py:114). analyze_triage (pipeline/blueprint_triage/api.py:18) runs all detectors — voids, floating, overlaps, sub-features, narrow strands, cliffs, skyscrapers — and assembles them into a Verdict of CLEAN / WARNINGS / DISQUALIFYING (api.py:67-71) inside the triage PrintabilityReport (pipeline/blueprint_triage/report.py:180). A separate plan_fixes (pipeline/blueprint_triage/planning.py:25) proposes FixCandidates and apply_fixes (pipeline/blueprint_triage/application.py:19) mutates the plan.
It looks like a full repair pipeline, but nothing on the live solve invokes it. analyze_triage, plan_fixes, and apply_fixes have only test callers (tests/generator/blueprint_triage*); the sole non-test references to those three functions inside Prisma/generator are their own package re-exports (pipeline/blueprint_triage/__init__.py:1, :2, :17) — no production code calls them. (Other symbols from the module are imported on the live path — server.py:98, facade.py:37, and state.py:14 pull in PrintabilityError/PrintabilityReport — but only as a type or exception class, never the analyzer/fixer functions.) The runner clears the carrier field: _finalize_staged_backend_state sets state.blueprint_triage = None (pipeline/runner.py:698) and the staged path never writes a real report there. So the field threads through the facade and is read by the server, but always reads None. See What Actually Runs > blueprint_triage (printability triage) — dormant, and not the mesh report.

Its PrintabilityError is a different gate. blueprint_triage/report.py:29 defines PrintabilityError and the server imports it (server.py:98). The one place that raises it on a solve-shaped path is _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2426), and even that is flagged suspected inert in the code comment at server.py:2420–2424 — during a real solve only the non-raising _run_material_exposure_audit runs. Do not assume PrintabilityError ⇒ blueprint triage ran.

Level 2 — per-layer staged diagnostic + Stage 4 gate (staged_printability) — LIVE
This is the printability layer that actually executes. It works on the staged blueprint’s per-layer occupancy, not pixel columns. build_layered_blueprint_view (pipeline/staged_printability.py:163) derives a read-only LayeredBlueprintView (staged_printability.py:31) — one boolean/label map per color layer, cap layer, and detail layer — from the staged artifacts (VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan, CapSynthesisPlan). resolve_blueprint_printability_settings (staged_printability.py:71) resolves the physical thresholds (minimum extrusion width, minimum line length, pitch, layer height) from the solve config.
It has two distinct jobs:
(a) The diagnostic report. run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic (staged_printability.py:401) labels the connected components inside each layer, grades each via grade_blueprint_component (staged_printability.py:264, which flags tiny_component / narrow_width / short_length against the physical minima), additionally runs a morphological-opening neck test (_opening_width_loss / _opening_width_loss_is_structural, staged_printability.py:303, :317) and a vertical-support check, and returns a frozen BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (pipeline/staged_artifacts.py:502) carrying per-surface hard-fail pixel maps and a list of BlueprintPrintabilityComponentFacts (staged_artifacts.py:478). On the live path this is gated by emit_blueprint_printability and runs at staged_runner.py:11569 onward, attaching the result to cap_plan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic.
(b) The Stage 4 enforcement gate. The same grading helpers are re-exported publicly (opening_width_structure / opening_width_loss / opening_width_loss_is_structural, staged_printability.py:349, :353, :361) precisely so Stage 4 can apply the identical neck criterion as an in-place repair. _apply_stage4_boundary_cap_printability_gate (staged_runner.py:5263) grows or suppresses boundary-cap coverage and _apply_stage4_detail_printability_gate (staged_runner.py:5973) suppresses hard-failing detail material. _printability_enforcement_enabled (staged_runner.py:3386) selects the enforcement flag used by these passes.
Why it is LIVE, with defaults pinned. On the web app the relevant config flags are all forced on, not user-toggleable:






























FlagLive defaultAnchor_enforce (drives both enforce_printability and stage4_printability_gate_detail)True unconditionallyserver.py:994–998 (“Product printability is mandatory”)enforce_printabilityTrueserver.py:1036, resolved-config default server.py:401stage4_printability_gate_detail_enforce (→ True)server.py:1052, default server.py:411emit_blueprint_printabilityTrueserver.py:1033, default server.py:398
So the gate repairs the blueprint and the diagnostic reports on it on every normal solve. The diagnostic results surface to the UI as performance counters (server.py:2338-2345) and overlay maps (server.py:5087-5096). See How a Solve Works for where Stage 4 sits and The Joint LUT and Staged Solve for the staged backend internals.

VisibleRecipe vs StackDefinition. The view builder consumes VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:73) thickness-by-filament records. This is a near-duplicate of StackDefinition — same shape, different role. When citing one, name it explicitly; do not assume they are interchangeable in a given call.

Level 3 — mesh-level measurement (mesh/printability.py) — suspected inert
mesh/printability.py is a measurement-only toolkit over already-built trimesh.Trimesh objects — it never mutates meshes or alters export behavior. It answers geometry questions the other two levels cannot: do the per-filament STLs share an XY origin (compare_xy_footprints, mesh/printability.py:78); does the top of one layer meet the bottom of the next or is there a measurable gap/overlap (inter_mesh_gap_overlap, :359, bucketed by classify_seal_severity, :458); are there connected XY components below a printable footprint area (thin_island_risks, :601).
The export-facing roll-up is what is flagged inert. build_printability_report (mesh/printability.py:1071) aggregates the measurements and classify_printability_report (:1041) maps them onto a pass / warn / fallback / block ladder with a next_action such as do_not_export (_classify_printability_summary, :916), wrapping it in this module’s own PrintabilityReport dataclass (:680). A code comment at mesh/printability.py:1061-1070 records that no live solve/export path appears to consume this classification — the only known callers are tests/generator/test_mesh_printability.py and scripts/characterize_mesh_printability.py.

Treat “inert” as a hint, not a fact. That same comment (:1066-1069) warns that an earlier audit declared this “dead” after missing real references, so the reference graph is subtle. Re-verify exhaustively across tests, scripts, the config chain, and the separate blueprint_triage module before removing or disabling anything. See What Actually Runs > mesh printability + canonical mesh — suspected inert.

The two PrintabilityReport traps
These two classes share a name and nothing else — keep them straight:























ClassDefined atWhat it isLives whereTriage PrintabilityReportpipeline/blueprint_triage/report.py:180Per-column hazard report with Verdict + PrintabilityError (report.py:29)Level 1, dormantMesh PrintabilityReportmesh/printability.py:680Export-facing mesh summary with status/severity/next_actionLevel 3, suspected inert
The middle (live) level uses neither — its report type is BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (staged_artifacts.py:502), a third, separately-named dataclass.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The live staged printability diagnostic
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: after the staged solve builds the white cap, the generator re-derives the layered plan, grades every connected component on every layer against the printer’s physical min-feature thresholds, and records a read-only diagnostic (per-pixel fail maps + worst-component facts) that the UI overlays — while a separate, always-on audit counts any color filament left exposed to air.

The live staged printability diagnostic
This is the plan-level printability check that runs as part of a production solve. It does not repair geometry — it measures it. Two distinct things live here, both wired into the live solve path:

The blueprint printability diagnostic — a layer-by-layer grade of every connected component against resolved physical thresholds (min extrusion width, min line length, plus a neck, clearance, and vertical-support audit). Built in generator.pipeline.staged_printability.
The material exposure audit — a 3D face-count of color filament left touching air, plus the mandatory white boundary-shield floor implied by color-height cliffs. Built in generator.pipeline.material_exposure.

The diagnostic is read-only. The enforcement passes inside generator.pipeline.staged_runner (Stage 4 boundary-cap and detail repair) reuse the same grading helpers so a component the diagnostic flags is the same component the gates repair — see Reuse by the enforcement passes. For the stage that owns those gates see The staged backend (Stage 0-5).
How to drive it
You do not call any of this directly. It runs automatically inside run_staged_backend_path (the live webapp solve engine, pipeline/staged_runner.py:11163; the only caller is the runner at pipeline/runner.py:1222–1225 — not the legacy solve.py CLI engine). The diagnostic stage is gated on one flag and bounded by a handful of physical settings you set per run:





























KnobDefaultWhere setEffectemit_blueprint_printabilityTruefacade.py:59, server.py:398, state.py:106, app.js:335Master on/off for the diagnostic stage (staged_runner.py:11569).printability_minimum_extrusion_width_mmNone → 0.40resolver staged_printability.py:79Min printable feature width; from the active nozzle’s min_line_width (app.js:6544).printability_minimum_line_length_mmNone → derivedresolver staged_printability.py:84-88Min printable feature length; defaults to max(0.40, width + 0.10).
When emit_blueprint_printability is off the diagnostic stage is skipped entirely; the exposure audit (below) still runs on every solve.
Step 1 — Resolving physical thresholds
resolve_blueprint_printability_settings (staged_printability.py:71) collapses the user/printer config into a frozen BlueprintPrintabilitySettings (staged_printability.py:20) carrying four numbers in millimeters: minimum_extrusion_width_mm, minimum_line_length_mm, pitch_mm, layer_height_mm.
The resolver is forgiving — each field falls through a chain of candidates via _first_positive (staged_printability.py:58), which returns the first strictly-positive value:

Width: printability_minimum_extrusion_width_mm → printer_min_line_width_mm → hard floor 0.40 (staged_printability.py:78-83).
Min line: explicit value, else max(0.40, width + 0.10) (staged_printability.py:84-88).
Pitch: the pitch_mm argument → solver_fine_pitch_mm → image_sample_pitch_mm → 0.20 (staged_printability.py:89-94). The live call passes pitch_mm=solver_fine_pitch_mm (staged_runner.py:11434) so grading happens at the true fine solve resolution.
Layer height: layer_height → 0.08 (staged_printability.py:95).

Pitch is the linchpin: every pixel-count is converted to physical area/width/length by multiplying by pitch_mm, so the thresholds are compared in millimeters regardless of solve resolution.
Step 2 — The layered blueprint view
build_layered_blueprint_view (staged_printability.py:163) derives a read-only per-layer occupancy view (LayeredBlueprintView, staged_printability.py:31) from two staged artifacts: the VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan (color recipes per zone) and the CapSynthesisPlan (white cap + detail heights). It splits the plan into three surface families:

Color layers — each visible recipe’s per-filament thickness is quantized into integer layer counts (_positive_layer_counts, staged_printability.py:125; note ≥ 1 layer for any positive thickness, staged_printability.py:131), expanded into an ordered label stack per recipe (_recipe_color_layer_table, staged_printability.py:135), then scattered across the image via the recipe label map (staged_printability.py:184-186). Material ordering follows the declared palette, with any stragglers appended (_ordered_material_ids, staged_printability.py:106).
Cap layers — the boundary cap, computed as cap_height_mm − detail_height_mm clamped at 0 (staged_printability.py:192-196), sitting on top of the color ceiling (color_ceiling = cap_boundary_top_mm − boundary_cap_height, staged_printability.py:198-201).
Detail layers — the detail cap, stacked on color_ceiling + boundary_cap_height (staged_printability.py:241-248).

Each surface is materialized into a stack of boolean layer masks anchored to an absolute Z grid (absolute_layer_masks, staged_printability.py:204), so the support audit (Step 4) can look downward through the stack.
Step 3 — Grading a component
grade_blueprint_component (staged_printability.py:264) is the atomic check. Given a connected component’s pixel count and bounding-box height/width in pixels, it computes three physical measures and returns a grade:

























MeasureFormula (staged_printability.py)Compared againstarea_mm2pixel_count · pitch² :272min_extrusion_width · min_line_length :275-278width_mmmin(h, w) · pitch :273minimum_extrusion_width_mm :283length_mmmax(h, w) · pitch :274minimum_line_length_mm :285
Grades and their reason flags:

hard_fail if area below min_area (tiny_component), or width below min (narrow_width), or length below min (short_length) — any one trips it (:281-288).
pass otherwise (:289).

Bounding-box width/length alone cannot catch a fat blob joined by a one-pixel neck, so the diagnostic adds two more per-component checks on top of the bbox grade.
The opening-width neck criterion
grade_blueprint_component only sees the bounding box; a dumbbell shape (two wide lobes joined by a sub-width neck) passes its width test. The neck is caught by a morphological opening with a square structuring element sized to the minimum printable width:

_minimum_width_px (staged_printability.py:292) → ceil(min_extrusion_width / pitch) pixels; _opening_width_structure (:298) builds an N×N all-ones kernel.
_opening_width_loss (:303) opens the component and returns the pixels the opening removed — the kernel cannot fit there, i.e. sub-width features. A 1×1 kernel is a no-op (:311-312).
_opening_width_loss_is_structural (:317) decides whether the loss matters: opening also rounds harmless exterior corners. The loss is structural only if removing the lost pixels destroys the component or splits it into more than one piece (:333-340). Only structural loss escalates to hard_fail with narrow_width (:530-538); harmless corner rounding is ignored.

These three helpers are public re-exports (opening_width_structure :349, opening_width_loss :353, opening_width_loss_is_structural :361) precisely so the enforcement passes apply the identical criterion — the comment at :343-348 spells out why.
Step 4 — The full diagnostic run
run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic (staged_printability.py:401) walks every layer of every surface and accumulates per-pixel fail maps plus component-level facts. The inner consume_mask closure (:449) does the work for one (surface, layer, material) mask:

Connected-component labeling with 4-connectivity (ndi.label, structure from :446), iterating bounding boxes via find_objects (:489-493).
Bbox grade via grade_blueprint_component (:500).
Center clearance — a distance transform in mm gives each pixel’s clearance to the nearest edge (_component_center_clearance_mm, :368; applied :514-521). Recorded as max_center_clearance_mm, not itself a fail.
Opening-width neck — structural loss escalates to hard_fail and marks width_loss_map (:523-538).
Vertical support — see below. Any unsupported pixel escalates to hard_fail with low_vertical_support (:551-560).

Every non-pass component becomes a BlueprintPrintabilityComponentFacts (:564, dataclass at staged_artifacts.py:477) carrying its bbox, physical measures, grade, reason flags, clearance, width-loss pixels, and support fraction. The full set is sorted hard-fail-first then by pixel count (:683-694) and the worst max_worst_components (default 128) are kept (:776).
Support-fraction checks
A color pixel printed with nothing under it overhangs. _support_fraction_for_layer (staged_printability.py:383) measures, for layer k, the mean occupancy of the window of layers below it (window_layers=3, :388; layer 0 is treated as fully supported on the base, :391-392). Inside consume_mask, the per-pixel support map is sampled over the component; the mean is its support_fraction (:540-546), and any pixel with support < 1.0 is unsupported (:551).
Support sources differ per surface (:628-671):

























SurfaceSupport mapSource (staged_printability.py)colorrolling 3-layer occupancy below_support_fraction_for_layer(color_occupancy, …) :632-636cap (boundary)full support (sits on the color ceiling)full_support :656detailthe union of all boundary-cap layerscap_any_support :659-671
Projected clustering
Beyond per-component facts, the run projects all hard-fail pixels down to a 2D map and clusters them (projected_cluster_summary, :695) at two radii: tight (:716-718) and dilated by a cluster_radius_px derived from min_line_length / pitch (:719-730). This surfaces “many small fails packed into one region” as a single large-cluster fraction — the color_hard_fail_largest_cluster_fraction family on the result.
The result object
The run returns a BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (staged_artifacts.py:501): the resolved hard thresholds, per-surface layer/mask/fail counts, the tiny/narrow/short tallies, the projected-cluster summaries, the worst-component tuple, and a stack of float32 per-pixel maps (hard_fail_map, narrow_width_map, short_component_map, color_hard_fail_map, cap_hard_fail_map, detail_hard_fail_map, center_clearance_map, width_loss_map, low_support_map).
Where it goes
In the live solve the diagnostic is attached to the cap plan (cap_plan.blueprint_printability_diagnostic = blueprint_printability, staged_runner.py:11447) and its scalar counts are timed/recorded into the run’s performance profile (staged_runner.py:11448+). The bridge (Step 5 of the staged backend) copies the float maps into the solve’s debug-map dict under blueprint_printability_* keys (pipeline/staged_bridge.py:383-427), which is how they reach the generator’s overlay viewer. A subset of the scalar counts is also promoted into run_metadata["stats"] for display (server.py:2336-2349). This is purely diagnostic — it gates nothing and raises nothing.
Reuse by the enforcement passes
The diagnostic is the measurement; the Stage 4 boundary-cap and detail repair passes are the enforcement, and they reuse the diagnostic’s grading helpers so the two stay in lockstep:

grade_blueprint_component is imported by staged_runner.py:74 and called from the enforcement graders — e.g. _stage2_component_physical_grade (staged_runner.py:3383), _component_physical_grade_with_opening (:3404), a local growth grader (:3810), and the vectorized layer-failure scan _stage4_layer_failures_vectorized (:5849).
opening_width_structure / opening_width_loss / opening_width_loss_is_structural are imported (staged_runner.py:75-77) and applied in those same passes (:3435-3438, :5901-5905) so the neck criterion is identical. The header comment at staged_printability.py:343-348 is explicit that bbox/area/length-only gates would let a 1-pixel neck slip past.

The material exposure audit
This page owns material_exposure.py. It is a separate, always-on audit (independent of emit_blueprint_printability) that asks one question: does any color filament touch air in the final print? It is geometry-agnostic — it audits the raster material occupancy the export path will use, and it never smooths or repairs (material_exposure.py:1-7 header; trust the line behavior, not the prose).
The boundary-shield floor
lateral_boundary_shield_floor_layers (material_exposure.py:72) computes, per pixel, how many white cap layers are mandatory to shield internal color-height cliffs. For each 4-neighbor pair it compares color-layer counts: the lower side must carry enough white cap to cover its neighbor’s color-height excess; the higher side needs none for that pair (:88-102). This floor is enforced in the live solve — lateral_boundary_shield_floor_layers (staged_runner.py:7178) runs unconditionally on every staged solve, and the result feeds the implied cap heights as minimum_cap_height_mm (staged_runner.py:7186-7193). With the fixed cap mode retired, the non-fixed gate is gone and the shield floor is now always computed.
The color-air exposure count
audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_layer_counts (material_exposure.py:106) counts exposed color faces in 3D without building a voxel stack, given color and white-cap layer-count maps:

























Face typeWhat it countsCodelateral_internal_face_countcolor stack on one side taller than the total (color + cap) stack of a 4-neighbor:122-127top_face_countpixels with color but zero white cap on top:129exterior_face_countcolor layers on the four image borders (no neighbor to shield them):130-135
A MaterialExposureAudit (material_exposure.py:29) bundles these counts plus the exposed-color pixel count and stack maxima. Its passes property (:51) is True only when the total exposed face count is zero (:53). The height-based entry point audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_heights (:177) just quantizes mm → layer counts first; audit_colored_filament_exposure_from_thickness_maps (:189) sums every exposure-relevant material map (exposure_relevant_material_keys, :222 — everything not prefixed __, minus explicit exclusions, :248-251) and resolves the white cap from WHITE_CAP or WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP + WHITE_DETAIL_CAP (:258-269).
How the audit is wired
In the live solve, server.py calls the non-raising _run_material_exposure_audit (server.py:2408, invoked during solve completion around :5427) once per solve. It excludes the white base/cap ids (_white_ids, server.py:768). The summary lands in run_metadata["material_exposure_audit"] and the boolean white_cap_exposure_safe for display — it records, it does not block.
A second, assert-form gate _assert_material_exposure_safe_for_product (server.py:2369) does raise PrintabilityError on exposure, but per the in-code note at server.py:2361-2368 it is suspected inert on the live solve path (no confirmed live caller found; appears exercised only by tests/generator/test_material_exposure_product_gate.py). Treat that as unconfirmed — the note itself asks for a full reference re-check before relying on it.
Disambiguation (do not confuse)

The blueprint BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic here is unrelated to the mesh-side PrintabilityReport classes. There are two unrelated report types in the codebase (blueprint-triage vs mesh) — this page is strictly the blueprint/plan-level one.
VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:73) is the per-zone recipe the layered view consumes; it is a near-duplicate of StackDefinition but not the same type — the view reads recipe.to_mapping() (staged_artifacts.py:105) and recipe.thickness_by_filament (:76).

Related

generator.pipeline.material_exposure — module node for the exposure audit
generator.pipeline.staged_runner — the enforcement passes that reuse the graders
Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract — the artifacts the layered view reads
minimum feature width — the 0.2mm physical floor doctrine

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The white cap
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the white cap is the clear/white skin laid on top of the solved color stack, and its per-pixel thickness is whatever height is left under the t_max total-height contract — optionally biased toward the source image’s dark regions by a default-off luminance prior.

The color stack the solver picks decides each pixel’s color ceiling (white base + committed color layers). The white cap is everything above that ceiling, up to the total object height. This page covers how that cap thickness is determined: the color ceiling, the budget contract, the optional luminance prior, the boundary-vs-detail split, and the Stage 4 detail smoothing.
Related: The live staged printability diagnostic owns material_exposure and the live printability fields — it does not use the cap-ceiling helpers below. The dormant Blueprint triage the unwired engine is the only consumer of color_ceiling_from_plan / top_surface_from_fields. generator.pipeline.height_budget, generator.pipeline.luminance_handler, generator.pipeline.detail_cap_smoothing, generator.pipeline.cap_quality are the modules described here.
The color ceiling
Every pixel sits under a color ceiling = white base thickness plus the total committed color thickness of its solved stack. color_ceiling_from_plan builds this from the solved plan: it maps each pixel to its committed stack via committed_stack_label_map(plan) and adds d_wb to that stack’s total_color_thickness_mm (pipeline/cap_quality.py:58, summed at pipeline/cap_quality.py:61-67). Pixels with no color stack get a ceiling of just d_wb (pipeline/cap_quality.py:66).
This function is computed-but-unwired: its only product caller is the dormant blueprint-triage engine at pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:146, which also composes the top surface with top_surface_from_fields (pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:147; the composer itself is color ceiling + visible cap at pipeline/cap_quality.py:70-78). No live solve or export path constructs an AnalysisContext or calls analyze_triage, so neither helper actually runs in production today — see Blueprint triage the unwired engine. Do not confuse this with the genuinely-live printability diagnostic in pipeline/staged_printability.py, which builds its own layered view and never touches these two helpers.
The total-height budget contract
t_max is the total object height, white base included. The only headroom the white cap may occupy is whatever is left above the color ceiling. generator.pipeline.height_budget is the whole policy:

























HelperContractAnchormax_cap_height_for_color_thicknessscalar headroom = t_max - d_wb - color_thickness, optionally clamped by a max-cap ceiling, floored at 0pipeline/height_budget.py:12, computed :20-23max_cap_height_map_for_color_ceilingper-pixel headroom = t_max - color_ceiling, optional d_wc_max clamp, floored at 0pipeline/height_budget.py:26, :34-37clamp_cap_height_map_to_budgetclamp any cap map so total height never exceeds t_maxpipeline/height_budget.py:40, :48-54
The scalar form is live in the solve: Stage 2 cap precompute calls max_cap_height_for_color_thickness per unique stack to find the printable cap range, then marks over-budget cap steps as inf so the optimizer can’t pick them (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:116, masked at pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:125). Note that call passes d_wc_max_mm=cfg.effective_boundary_d_wc_max() (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:120) — the boundary ceiling, not the full one.
What sets the cap maximum
Three config accessors define the ceilings (defaults in pipeline/state.py):

effective_d_wc_max() — explicit d_wc_max if set, else t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min (pipeline/state.py:191-194).
effective_boundary_d_wc_max() — the full max, then clamped down by (a) the runtime luminance boundary authority if one was computed and (b) an explicit boundary_cap_authority_mm, always floored at d_wc_min (pipeline/state.py:196-203).
effective_white_cap() — the cap filament; falls back to the white base when white_cap is unset (pipeline/state.py:181-182).

Relevant defaults: d_wb=0.20, d_wc_min=0.08, t_max=3.0, layer_height=0.08 (pipeline/state.py:66,67,70,64).
The default-off source-luminance prior
generator.pipeline.luminance_handler gives the cap an optional bias toward darker source regions (a thicker cap dims the backlight, so dark image areas request more white). It is default-off: gated by luminance_handler_enabled reading cfg.luminance_handler_enabled (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:47-49), whose default is False (pipeline/state.py:82).
It is wired into the live solve when enabled. Two entry points:

Before LUT building, configure_luminance_handler_runtime computes a reference and stashes the boundary authority on the config so effective_boundary_d_wc_max can clamp to it (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:544, authority set at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:570). Returns None early if disabled or if state lacks profiles/target (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:553-560).
In Stage 4, the staged runner calls LuminanceHandler(cfg, state.profiles).build(...) to get boundary and detail cap references (pipeline/staged_runner.py:9243, gated by luminance_handler_enabled(cfg) at :9242). When disabled, Stage 4 falls back to quantizing the raw solver-implied cap directly (pipeline/staged_runner.py:9277-9289).

How the prior is built (LuminanceHandler.build_reference, pipeline/luminance_handler.py:174):

Source luminance is the OKLab L of the solve target (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:189).
It samples the white-base × white-cap appearance curve over the printable cap-step range (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:402; photo-stack provider path at :417, historical-spline fallback at :422-429).
Mode boundary_prior (the default, pipeline/state.py:83) maps source darkness into a cap-mm request: floor + darkness × (available range) (full-image at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:227-230, boundary at :231-234). Mode absolute_optical instead interpolates the appearance curve directly (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:201-222).
“Darkness” is a percentile-normalized, optionally toe/shoulder-shaped inverse of luminance (_darkness_map pipeline/luminance_handler.py:487; response curves linear/smoothstep/smootherstep/gamma/sqrt at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:523-537).
Every cap map is layer-quantized and clamped to [floor, d_wc_max] via _quantize_cap_map (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:107); the floor is the smallest layer-grid multiple ≥ d_wc_min (_quantized_cap_floor, pipeline/luminance_handler.py:99).

Boundary authority
The handler also derives a single boundary authority (mm) — a ceiling on how thick the boundary cap may go. It is the smaller of an optical authority (the cap thickness reaching a configured fraction, default 0.75, of the achievable OKLab swing — _optical_authority pipeline/luminance_handler.py:461; fraction default pipeline/state.py:85) and, in absolute_optical mode, a percentile of the boundary prior (_boundary_authority pipeline/luminance_handler.py:449). An explicit boundary_cap_authority_mm clamps it further (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:254-262). This authority is what feeds back into effective_boundary_d_wc_max (above).
Boundary cap vs detail cap
LuminanceHandler.build emits two references that Stage 4 consumes (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:303):




















TierMeaningBuilt atboundary_cap_request_mmthe smooth cap thickness at segment boundaries, ceilinged by the boundary authoritypipeline/luminance_handler.py:324-346detail_cap_reference_mmthe per-pixel detail cap, ≥ boundary request, ceilinged by the full d_wc_max and never exceeding remaining t_max headroompipeline/luminance_handler.py:348-368
Three blend modes set the boundary request: blend_solver (alpha-blend raw vs prior), boundary_ceiling (min of raw and a blended ceiling), and the default else-branch (floor + strength × (prior − floor)) at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:325-340. The detail reference defends the t_max contract directly: it subtracts the color ceiling from t_max and clips against that remaining budget before quantizing (remaining at pipeline/luminance_handler.py:355-358, then np.minimum at :359). Stage 4 reads both back out at pipeline/staged_runner.py:9253-9254.
Cap mode and the Appearance budget
cap_mode decides how the standard (non-luminance) solve splits the cap between a structural boundary cap and a variable detail cap. Two values remain; cap_mode='fixed' was retired and is now rejected (_normalize_cap_mode, server.py:880–896, rejection at :888):

appearance_bounded_smooth (UI “Detail Aware”, the default — server.py:464 in _DEFAULT_CONFIG, ConfigPayload field server.py:632). It keeps the boundary cap structural and pushes tonal relief into the detail cap, but only up to an Appearance budget: a perceptual dE ceiling boundary_cap_de_budget (default 0.008, server.py:465/633) on how far the boundary cap may drift.
smooth_variable (UI “Smooth”) lets the whole cap vary smoothly with no structural split.

The structural-split path is gated by appearance_structural_split_enabled = cap_mode == "appearance_bounded_smooth" and not luminance_handler_enabled(cfg) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10312–10316). In Luminance mode cap_mode is forced to smooth_variable (server.py:912), so the split never runs there.
The white-cap export contract
The solved cap does not export as a uniform thickness — it exports as a field target: a per-pixel upper-surface map plus a small metadata block, defined canonically in white_cap_contract.py. The contract fixes the metadata keys and schema "white-cap-field-target-v1" (white_cap_contract.py:7-10), the three per-mode policies (white_cap_contract.py:12-16), and the layer-quantized cover floor quantized_cover_floor_mm — the smallest cap thickness at or above d_wc_min (white_cap_contract.py:19).
pipeline/staged_bridge.py assembles the field target (staged_bridge.py:163-191): the upper-surface map is cap_plan.final_visible_top_mm, and the policy is chosen by mode (staged_bridge.py:153-161) — POLICY_LUMINANCE_DETAIL_CANONICAL in luminance-detail mode, POLICY_STANDARD_APPEARANCE_BOUNDED_STRUCTURAL_SPLIT for standard + Detail Aware, else POLICY_STANDARD_SMOOTH_VARIABLE_CANONICAL. The quantized cover floor is recorded as required_cover_floor_mm (staged_bridge.py:162,:190). The mesh export consumes this metadata to rebuild the white cap from the field (mesh/post_solve_export.py:42, reconstruction in mesh/field_white_reconstruction.py).
Detail-cap smoothing (Stage 4)
generator.pipeline.detail_cap_smoothing is a live cleanup that removes single-pixel topographic noise from the detail cap only — it never touches color maps, boundary cap, or stack topology. It moved out of server.py and now runs inside Stage 4 of the staged runner:

Entry: _apply_stage4_detail_cap_smoothing (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10216), invoked while building the Stage 4 cap plan at pipeline/staged_runner.py:10671.
Gated to the luminance handler plus the two enable flags: luminance_handler_enabled(cfg), detail_cap_enabled (now mandatory-True, server.py:688–693), and detail_cap_smoothing_enabled (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10231 onward). The smoothing flag defaults on (server.py:390), but the luminance handler is default-off (luminance_handler_enabled=False, pipeline/state.py:82) — so on a default run the gate short-circuits and the smoothing is a no-op; it only acts once the run is switched into luminance-detail mode, which forces luminance_handler_enabled=True (server.py:912–914).
It converts the detail map to integer layer counts, smooths, converts back, then clamps the smoothed detail to the remaining cap budget (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10245 onward) before Stage 4 folds it back into the cap plan.

The smoothing itself (smooth_detail_cap_layers, pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:100) does two passes on the integer layer map: replace exact-height speckles (≤1 px by default) with the local ring mode (pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:117, remove_exact_height_speckles at :139), then on cumulative material masks drop tiny components and fill tiny holes (pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:122, cleanup_cumulative_detail_masks at :167). Defaults: max 8 layers, 1-px speckle, 2-px component, 2-px hole (DetailCapSmoothingSettings, pipeline/detail_cap_smoothing.py:12-20), built from config by _stage4_detail_cap_smoothing_settings (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10063-10088).
Legacy: the cap quality scorecard
generator.pipeline.cap_quality also contains analyze_cap_quality (pipeline/cap_quality.py:576), which computes a full cap scorecard — exposed-color cliffs, island/pinhole risks, boundary/neighbor deltas, dE stats. This is test-only. Grepping the product tree, analyze_cap_quality, compare_assignment_stability (pipeline/cap_quality.py:724), and metric_subset (pipeline/cap_quality.py:761) are referenced only by tests/generator/test_cap_quality.py outside their own module. The sub-analyzes they drive — find_cap_island_risks (:306), find_cap_pinhole_risks (:318), exposed_color_cliff_analysis (:330), default_line_profile (:536) — are reachable in product code only through analyze_cap_quality, so they are dormant too.
The two helpers color_ceiling_from_plan and top_surface_from_fields are no exception — they are not live either. The module’s only non-test product import is pipeline/blueprint_triage/fields.py:11, which pulls in exactly those two functions; but that consumer (the blueprint-triage engine) is itself computed-but-unwired (see Blueprint triage the unwired engine), so the whole of cap_quality.py is dormant in production. The genuinely-live printability path is the separate pipeline/staged_printability.py diagnostic, which does not import this module at all.
Driving it (for users)

Leave luminance_handler_enabled off for the standard color-faithful solve; the cap then just fills remaining t_max headroom.
Turn it on to bias the cap toward darker image regions; tune luminance_handler_strength (pipeline/state.py:84) and the response curve (pipeline/state.py:88-89).
Detail-cap smoothing only acts when the run is in luminance-detail mode (the Stage 4 gate luminance_handler_enabled(cfg), pipeline/staged_runner.py:10231); in standard mode it is a no-op regardless of the enable flags.
To cap total height, set t_max; to cap just the white cap, set d_wc_max or boundary_cap_authority_mm.
