prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: SolveConfig and SolveResult reference
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: SolveConfig is the current 100+-field dataclass that specifies one solve, and SolveResult is the compatibility container the facade returns — thickness maps, staged/export artifacts, diagnostics, stats, and the predict_image reconstruction methods.

Both live in generator.facade (Prisma/generator/facade.py). The module header still calls itself lith_facade.py (facade.py:2) — that name is stale; cite line anchors, not the header. This page covers the two dataclasses a caller hands in (SolveConfig) and gets back (SolveResult), the effective_* helpers that derive runtime values, and the two forward-prediction methods (predict_image, predict_image_color_only).
For the functions that consume a SolveConfig — solve_preview, solve_full, solve_compare — see The solve facade. For the pipeline they delegate into, see The staged backend (Stage 0-5) and generator.pipeline.runner.

SolveConfig
@dataclass SolveConfig (facade.py:46) — “All parameters needed for a single solve invocation.” Two required fields (palette and white_base), the rest defaulted. The web server builds one in _build_solve_config (server.py:976, return at :1008); the CLI builds its own.
How it is driven
A caller constructs a SolveConfig, then passes it to a facade entry point. The same object flows through _to_pipeline_config (facade.py:497), which copies the supported fields into a PipelineConfig for the runner. Almost every runtime field below is forwarded there — SolveConfig is the public shape, PipelineConfig the internal one. SolveConfig does not hold an image: the image is a separate argument to solve_full(img, config, ...).
__post_init__ — the resolution backstop
__post_init__ (facade.py:153) first canonicalizes palette order through the filament-order registry (:156-:160), then calls _apply_resolution_backstop(self) from config/resolution_schema.py:153. The backstop applies the default pitch pair when both fields are absent, rejects a half-specified pair, and rejects mismatched values (resolution_schema.py:167-185). It also ensures color_region_target_mm has its independent default (:187-:190).
Field groups
The dataclass declares its fields across facade.py:48-151. Grouped by what they do (defaults shown are the dataclass defaults, not server defaults):
Materials & palette













































FieldDefaultMeaningpalette(required)Ordered list of color-filament IDswhite_base(required)White-base filament ID (the substrate)white_capNoneWhite-cap filament ID; None ⇒ reuse white_base (see effective_white_cap)profiles_dirNoneOverrides the default spline-profile directoryappearance_model_provider"photo_stack_bundle"Forward-model backend selector (see Appearance provider)photo_stack_bundle_pathNoneBundle path when the provider is the photo-stack modeluse_corrections / correctionsTrue / NonePair-correction toggle and payload
Geometry budget


















































FieldDefaultMeaninglayer_height0.08mm per layert_max3.0Target total height (mm)d_wb0.20White-base thickness (mm)d_wc_min0.08Minimum white-cap thickness (mm)d_wc_maxNoneMax cap; auto-derived if None (see effective_d_wc_max)max_layersNoneColor-layer cap; auto-derived from t_max if Nonek_max3Max simultaneous color filaments per pixelboundary_cap_authority_mmNoneOptional ceiling on boundary cap thickness
Resolution (canonical pitch fields)
image_sample_pitch_mm (0.20), solver_fine_pitch_mm (0.20), stage1_coarsening_factor (1), stage1_lattice_offset_y_px / _x_px (0). These are the only resolution channel — there are no legacy alias fields on the runtime dataclass (resolution_schema.py:157). See generator.config.resolution_schema.
Cap shaping
cap_mode ("smooth_variable" | "appearance_bounded_smooth"; the server rejects retired "fixed" at request normalization), boundary_cap_de_budget (0.008, the Appearance dE budget within which appearance_bounded_smooth holds the structural boundary cap), cap_continuity_cleanup (True, fills single-pixel cap pinholes), plus the detail-cap family detail_cap_pitch_mm / detail_cap_enabled (True) / detail_cap_max_layers (5). The server rejects detail_cap_enabled=False and the facade-to-pipeline translation forces detail_cap_enabled=True (facade.py:619-625).
Solver behavior
de_threshold (0.01), gamut_mode ("hull" convex hull, or "chroma" legacy), gamut_white_rescale, chroma_weight (1.0, >1 prioritizes color over lightness in the KD-tree), and the luminance_handler_* family governing the optional generator.pipeline.luminance_handler. Luminance handling influences cap guidance; Stage 2 candidate scoring has no separate luminance near-tie control.
Model-domain ingress — model_domain_ingress (True) and model_domain_ingress_lut_path (the camera_transform directory inside the launcher’s active immutable model library) thread the Camera Transform inverse LUT into image ingress. See Model domain ingress.
Staging / printability — a large stage2_* family (continuity weight, fine override, boundary mutation, printability gates/repair), stage4_printability_gate_detail, luminance_detail_authoring_printability, and the printability_* / enforce_printability / color_region_* group. These feed the staged backend and optional staged printability diagnostics. emit_blueprint_printability defaults True; allow_print_despite_hazards defaults False. The web server forces product printability settings through _force_mandatory_product_settings before constructing the config (server.py:982-998).
Smoothing & cells — smooth_kernel (7.5), smooth_iters (3), cell_mode ("felzenszwalb"), smooth_boundaries (False), boundary_smooth_radius (1), and the v2_* cleanup family.
AMS slots — ams_slots (4), white_slots (1). Color slots are derived (see color_slots).
Swap banding — there is no grouping field or grouping module in the current SolveConfig. ams_slots and white_slots determine color_slots(); the runner automatically requests swap banding for a full-preset solve when the palette exceeds that budget. The plan is stored on PipelineState.swap_grouping and copied to SolveResult.swap_grouping.
Preprocessing — preprocessing_params (per-operator kwargs keyed by module name; every registered operator’s params block materializes here at its default). Enablement is resolved separately from module state; there are no current protect_subject_* or protect_mask_* fields in SolveConfig. See Preprocessing pipeline.
Printer / resample — nozzle_diameter (0.20), printer_min_line_width_mm, source_resample_kernel ("lanczos" default, bit-exact with pre-B7 behavior; "area" selects cv2.INTER_AREA).
effective_* and derived helpers
These methods resolve None/auto fields into concrete runtime values. They are the canonical place to read a derived value — callers and the runner use them rather than recomputing.


















































Methodfacade.pyReturnseffective_white_cap()162white_cap or white_baseeffective_max_layers()165max_layers, else int((t_max - d_wb - d_wc_min) / layer_height)effective_d_wc_max()170d_wc_max, else t_max - d_wb - d_wc_mineffective_boundary_d_wc_max()175effective_d_wc_max() clamped by boundary_cap_authority_mm and a runtime override attr, floored at d_wc_mineffective_detail_cap_pitch_mm()184detail_cap_pitch_mm, else first non-None of solver_fine_pitch_mm, image_sample_pitch_mm, else 0.20effective_detail_cap_max_layers()1950 when detail_cap_enabled is false, else max(0, detail_cap_max_layers)effective_white_slots()200max(white_slots, 2) when base ≠ cap (a distinct cap filament needs its own slot), else white_slotscolor_slots()205ams_slots - effective_white_slots()
effective_boundary_d_wc_max reads a private runtime attribute _runtime_luminance_boundary_cap_authority_mm via getattr (facade.py:305) — the luminance handler can stamp a tighter authority onto the config object mid-solve; absent that, only the static fields apply.
Cloning
_replace_solve_config(config, **changes) (facade.py:651) shallow-clones a SolveConfig from config.__dict__ with overrides. solve_compare uses it to swap in each palette (facade.py:939-:942). Because it rebuilds via the constructor, __post_init__ re-runs — palette canonicalization and the resolution invariant are re-checked on every clone.

SolveResult
@dataclass SolveResult (facade.py:234) — “Complete result of a solve operation.” Built by _state_to_solve_result (facade.py:785), which converts a PipelineState back into the public result shape after the runner finishes. Direct tests may construct partial SolveResult objects with many optional fields None.
__post_init__ — thickness-map normalization
__post_init__ (facade.py:270) wraps a raw dict into the typed ThicknessMaps if it is not already one (:276-:277). This is a no-op when the runner already handed over a wrapped container (the webapp path), so it preserves exact object aliasing there. ThicknessMaps (thickness_maps.py:77) is a compatibility-first MutableMapping whose keys normalize to plain strings, so every serializer and frontend payload sees the exact legacy strings. The reserved sentinel keys are the MapKey enum (thickness_maps.py:40): __white_cap__, __white_boundary_cap__, __white_detail_cap__, __de__, __gamut_mask__. Dynamic filament IDs are plain strings, distinguished by not starting with __.
Fields





















































































FieldTypeNotesthickness_mapsThicknessMapsPer-filament + reserved-sentinel arrays; the solve outputcolor_profiles / wb_profile / wc_profiledictsLoaded spline profiles used for predictionstatsSolveStatsAggregate dE / coverage / per-filament usage (facade.py:219)configSolveConfigThe config that produced this resultappearance_providerobject | NoneThe forward-model provider (drives predict_image backend choice)reference_imagendarray | NoneThe ingress image (model-domain), copied from statepalette_fit_image / palette_fit_de / solver_loss_mapndarray | NoneBest-case-fit diagnostics (full-solve only; see below)palette_fit_rms_de / solver_loss_rms_defloat | NoneRMS scalars for the aboveswap_groupingDict[str, object] | NoneAutomatic AMS swap-banding plan, when full-preset overflow handling ranimage_domain_width_mm / _height_mmfloat | NonePhysical extentsolved_planSolvedMaterialPlan | NoneCanonical solve-owned plan (product paths populate it)staged_resultobject | NoneThe raw StagedBackendResultdiagnosticsDict[str, ndarray]Canonical dE/gamut/target-gamut diagnostics copied from the runnerdebug_maps / export_maps / export_metadata / preprocessing_metrics / cap_qualitydictsAuxiliary and export-facing outputsblueprint_triagePrintabilityReport | NoneCompatibility field; the staged runner currently resets it to None
Diagnostics-vs-thickness_maps accessor fallback
The de_map and gamut_mask properties (facade.py:281-291) each prefer the diagnostics dict and fall back to thickness_maps:
@property
def de_map(self):
    if MapKey.DE in self.diagnostics:
        return self.diagnostics[MapKey.DE]
    return self.thickness_maps[MapKey.DE]
This dual lookup exists for a reason spelled out at facade.py:255-260: the staged/webapp runner populates diagnostics (from PipelineState.diagnostics: __de__, __gamut_mask__, __target_gamut_*__), so production results take the first branch. The fallback to thickness_maps serves only diagnostics-less legacy results — the separate legacy CLI engine, and tests that build a SolveResult straight from thickness_maps without a diagnostics dict. The same prefer-then-fall-back pattern appears in _compute_palette_fit_diagnostics (facade.py:679-687).
The other map accessors read thickness_maps directly (no fallback needed — caps are always part of the thickness output): cap_map → WHITE_CAP (facade.py:293), boundary_cap → WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP or None (facade.py:298), detail_cap → WHITE_DETAIL_CAP or None (facade.py:303), filament_ids → the dynamic keys (facade.py:308).
Best-case palette-fit diagnostics
palette_fit_image / palette_fit_de / solver_loss_map are computed by _compute_palette_fit_diagnostics (facade.py:666) and only for preset.name == "full" (returns {} otherwise, :668-:670). It re-queries the LUTs for the per-pixel best achievable match and computes the solver’s loss as max(final_de - best_de, 0) — i.e. how far the actual solve fell short of the palette’s theoretical best. See Solve diagnostics and dE maps.

predict_image and predict_image_color_only
These are the forward reconstruction methods: given solved thickness maps, recompose the predicted backlit image. This page owns the cap-zeroing explanation.
predict_image
predict_image(max_layers=None, *, thickness_maps=None) (facade.py:313) returns an (H, W, 3) uint8 image. Two backends, selected by the appearance provider’s model_kind (facade.py:328-364):

historical_spline (the spline provider — no longer the default) and any diagnostics-less result fall to predict_image_fast (solve.py:674), the vectorised spline composition: T = T_wb · Π T_color(d) · T_cap(d) per pixel, then gamma-2.2 to sRGB uint8 (solve.py:714).
non-spline providers (e.g. photo_stack_bundle, appearance_model.py:224) route to provider.predict_thickness_maps_srgb(...) (facade.py:460).

The thickness_maps= keyword overrides the solved maps for the prediction. Default None uses the solved maps, preserving historical behavior (facade.py:326-327). This override is the hook predict_image_color_only rides on.
max_layers defaults to config.effective_max_layers() (facade.py:326).
Callers (confirmed live): server.py:4061 (preview/gamut-check reconstruction), :4172 (per-palette reconstruction inside the solve_compare loop), :5028 (the full-solve reconstruction), plus evaluation/scripts and tests. predict_image is the live image-reconstruction path for the generator UI.
predict_image_color_only — and white-cap zeroing as multiplicative identity
predict_image_color_only(max_layers=None) (facade.py:406) reconstructs the base + color image with the white cap omitted, so the cap’s luminance shaping does not drown out the color story. The base stays in — it is the substrate. Output is the same model-domain gamma-2.2 sRGB uint8 as predict_image, so it can be baked through the display transform F.
It is a thin wrapper: it calls self.predict_image(max_layers, thickness_maps=self._cap_zeroed_thickness_maps()) (facade.py:415-:417). All the interesting work is in _cap_zeroed_thickness_maps (facade.py:386):
maps = self.thickness_maps.copy()
for cap_key in (WHITE_CAP, WHITE_BOUNDARY_CAP, WHITE_DETAIL_CAP):
    existing = maps.get(cap_key)
    if existing is not None:
        maps[cap_key] = np.zeros_like(np.asarray(existing))
return maps
It shallow-copies the maps (ThicknessMaps.copy(), arrays shared) and replaces every white-cap term — total cap and its boundary/detail components — with an all-zero array.
Why zeroing the cap thickness cleanly drops the term: a zero cap thickness is the multiplicative identity in the transmission model. The composition multiplies a per-channel cap transmission T_cap(d_wc) into the stack (solve.py:710-712; spline provider appearance_model.py:205-206). The transmission of any profile at thickness 0 is [1, 1, 1] — confirmed at lib/transmission.py:107-108:
if d <= 0.0:
    return np.ones(3)
So T_cap(0) = [1,1,1], and multiplying the stack by [1,1,1] leaves base × color untouched. This holds in both spline-composition backends (predict_image_fast and the spline appearance provider both call predict_transmission → predict), exactly as the method’s docstring asserts (facade.py:483-485). The cap term is dropped without touching the composition math — no special-casing, just feeding it the identity input.
Liveness: predict_image_color_only and _cap_zeroed_thickness_maps are defined at facade.py:406 / :386 and are live. The full-solve path invokes result.predict_image_color_only() at server.py:5077, saving the color-only predicted render for the Recipe viewer’s color-region view. The behavior is exercised directly by tests/generator/test_predict_color_only.py, including the non-spline backend cap-zeroing check.

Related

generator.config.resolution_schema — the pitch-pair invariant __post_init__ enforces

Solve diagnostics and dE maps — what lives in diagnostics

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Stage 1 and 2 solver kernels
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: staged_solver_helpers.py is a bag of stateless NumPy kernels that the staged solver uses to carve an image into color zones (Stage 1) and to turn the per-pixel color stacks into a scored grid of cap-thickness color predictions (Stage 2).

What this page is
pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py holds the shared, side-effect-free math kernels for the two early stages of the live solve. They do not own any solver policy — no commitment logic, no zone graph traversal, no budgeting decisions. They take arrays in and hand arrays back. The orchestration that calls them lives in generator.pipeline.staged_runner; this module is the low-level toolbox.
These kernels run on every webapp solve. The webapp solve runs the staged backend (pipeline/runner.py:1222 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path, defined at pipeline/staged_runner.py:11163), not the legacy “6-step” engine in solve.py. So everything below is on the hot path for a real generate.
Origin note (stale-docstring defuse)
The module docstring claims these functions “used to live in the retired dual-resolution solver wrapper” (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:1-8). That is a historical note about where the code moved from, not about its current status. The functions are live — every public name in __all__ (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:339-348) has at least one in-tree caller (see Liveness below). Do not read “retired … legacy … dead solver wrapper” in that header as a claim that this code is dead; the wrapper is gone, the kernels were lifted out and kept.
The kernels

































































FunctionAnchorStageRolegenerate_stage1_zone_labels:2871Carve the planning image into a dense zone-label map_smooth_label_map:2491Majority-vote boundary smoothing of a label map_relabel_contiguous_labels:2801Force label ids into dense 0..n-1_vectorized_stack_ids:212Encode per-pixel layer stacks into unique-stack ids_predict_transmission_batch:582Batch spline transmission for an array of thicknesses_precompute_cap_oklabs:872Spline-model cap-OKLab grid + over-budget inf sentinel_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized:1572Photo-stack cap-OKLab grid (scoring + dense views)_score_candidates_batch:2232Score many candidate stacks against a zone’s pixels_score_stack_for_cell:2132Per-stack fallback scorer (memory-safe path)
Stage 1 — zone-label generation
generate_stage1_zone_labels (pipeline/staged_solver_helpers.py:287) produces a 2-D integer label map the same height/width as the planning image, where each integer is a color zone. It is “dense Stage 1 zone-label map without solver commitment logic” (:297) — it only segments; the runner decides what to do with the zones.
Cell size. If scale is not passed, it is derived as round(color_region_target_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm), floored to ≥1 (:299-302). pixels_per_cell = scale * scale (:305). In the live path the runner passes an explicit scale override (coarse_scale_override, derived from the stage-1 coarsening factor) when staging is active (staged_runner.py:720-736), so the internal derivation is mostly a fallback.
Three cell modes (:307-331), selected by cfg.cell_mode:

























cell_modeMechanismNotes"grid"Plain scale × scale square tiling via np.repeatDeterministic axis-aligned cells; default-ish"felzenszwalb"skimage.segmentation.felzenszwalb, scale = max(1, pixels_per_cell*0.8), sigma=0.8, min_size=pixels_per_cellContent-aware blobsanything elseskimage.segmentation.slic, n_segments = (h*w)//(pixels_per_cell*4), compactness=10SLIC superpixels; the catch-all branch
After segmentation the labels are forced contiguous (:333), optionally boundary-smoothed if cfg.smooth_boundaries is set (:334-335, radius from cfg.boundary_smooth_radius), then relabeled contiguous again on the way out (:336).
_smooth_label_map (:249) iterates radius passes; each pass finds 4-neighbor boundary pixels and replaces each with the majority label in its 3×3 window (np.bincount(...).argmax(), :274-275). It short-circuits when a pass finds no boundary (:265-266) and finishes with a contiguous relabel (:277). _relabel_contiguous_labels (:280) is the trivial “unique + inverse-index reshape” that guarantees ids are 0..n-1 as int32.

The radius/boundary_smooth_radius plumbing here is the same smooth_boundaries feature noted as bug-fixed 2026-04-12 in project memory; this kernel is where the majority vote actually happens.

Stage 2 — from per-pixel stacks to a scored cap grid
Stage 2 (entry at staged_runner.py:6221) turns LUT-queried per-pixel thicknesses into a compact, scorable representation. The kernels do three jobs: encode, predict, score.
Encode — _vectorized_stack_ids
_vectorized_stack_ids (:21) collapses the per-pixel thickness dictionary into a small set of unique stacks. Mechanics:

Round each filament’s thickness to an integer layer count: rint(raw / layer_height) per palette entry (:31-34).
Pack the per-pixel layer-count vector into a single integer using a positional base of max_layers + 1 (:36-38) — a mixed-radix encoding where each filament occupies one “digit”. max_layers defaults to 50 but the live caller passes cfg.effective_max_layers() (staged_runner.py:6312).
np.unique(..., return_inverse=True) gives pixel_stack_ids (per-pixel index into the unique table) and the unique codes (:40-41).
Decode each unique code back into a {filament_id: thickness_mm} dict, dropping zero-layer entries (:43-53).

Returns (pixel_stack_ids, unique_codes, unique_stack_dicts). This is the key compression step: a megapixel image with a handful of distinct stacks becomes a few hundred unique-stack dicts the rest of Stage 2 reasons over.

Palette order is cfg.palette for both lanes. The caller builds the palette as cfg.palette order before encoding (staged_runner.py:6304-6313); config materialization already canonicalizes color-filament order, and stack ids inherit it exactly for both appearance lanes. The order matters especially for the photo-stack model, whose layers are physically stacked. (Earlier revisions sorted the palette for the order-insensitive spline model; current code does not — it hands the same cfg.palette order to both.) The kernel itself just encodes whatever ordered palette it is handed.

Predict — _predict_transmission_batch
_predict_transmission_batch (:58) evaluates the spline transmission model for a whole array of thicknesses at once. It pulls the per-channel splines via lib.transmission._get_splines (:60-62) and:

thickness ≤ 0 → transmission 1.0 (:68, :72);
thickness within knot range → clipped [0,1] spline eval per R/G/B (:74-78);
thickness beyond the last knot → per-element lib.transmission._extrapolate (:80-82).

Returns an (N, 3) RGB transmission array. This is the spline-model batch evaluator; see lib.transmission for the underlying PchipInterpolator splines and the transmission contract T_total = T_wb · ∏ T_fi · T_wc.
Cap-OKLab precompute — the two grids
Stage 2 needs, for every unique stack, the OKLab color it would show at each possible white-cap thickness. There are two implementations, picked by model kind at staged_runner.py:6335.
Spline model — _precompute_cap_oklabs
_precompute_cap_oklabs (:87) builds the cap grid for the historical spline model:

Cap steps 0 .. d_wc_max at layer_height spacing (:101-105); d_wc_max = cfg.effective_boundary_d_wc_max().
White-cap transmission for all cap steps via _predict_transmission_batch (:107-109).
For each unique stack: compose white-base + color layers with compose_stack (:114-132, from generator.model), multiply by every cap transmission, convert to OKLab with to_oklab (:134-135).
Over-budget inf sentinel (:142-152): the cap headroom left by this stack’s color thickness is computed with max_cap_height_for_color_thickness from generator.pipeline.height_budget (remaining = t_max - d_wb - color_thickness, clamped to d_wc_max). Any cap step beyond that headroom has its OKLab row set to np.inf (:150-151). Because the downstream scorer takes a Euclidean distance and then .min() over cap steps, an inf row can never be the chosen cap — so the optimizer is structurally forbidden from selecting an unprintable cap. This is the mechanism that keeps the solve inside the ~3 mm total-height budget.

Returns (cap_values, all_oklabs) where all_oklabs is (unique_stacks, n_steps, 3).
Photo-stack model — _precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized
_precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized (:157) does the same job for the photo-stack provider, but returns two views (:168-177):




















ViewBudget handlingUsed forscoring_oklabsover-budget cells masked with inf (:208-209)zone scoring — the optimizer can’t pick unprintable combosdense_oklabsfinite at every cellStage-4 cap lookup always gets a color answer; budget enforcement is the cap planner’s job
Cap steps come from the LUT cap grid (deduped from each LUT’s cap_thicknesses, :183-192) — never scavenged from the pruned LUT, never routed through the row-shaped predictor (docstring :170-177, behavior :183-210). The actual grid evaluation is delegated to predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid (photo_stack_lut.py:998), which returns (dense_oklabs, within_budget); the budget mask is applied here at :208-209 with budget_mm = t_max - d_wb (:203).
The caller binds the dense view to dense_cap_oklabs and the scoring view to all_oklabs (staged_runner.py:6337); the spline branch sets dense_cap_oklabs = all_oklabs since it has no separate dense view (:6358).
Score — _score_candidates_batch
_score_candidates_batch (:223) scores a set of candidate stacks against a zone’s pixels. For each candidate it computes, per pixel, the OKLab distance to the candidate’s best cap step, then averages over the zone’s pixels — “mean optimal-cap dE” (:213-220). It has two code paths:

Vectorized (:237-241): if the pixels × candidates × steps × 3 tensor is under 50 M elements, it broadcasts the whole thing, squares-sums-sqrts to dE, takes min over cap steps then mean over pixels.
Per-candidate fallback (:243-245): above that size it loops candidates and calls _score_stack_for_cell (:213) one at a time to cap peak memory.

Both return a (candidates,) array of scores; lower is better. This is the kernel the zone-candidate machinery calls in two places: enumerating each zone’s own candidates (staged_runner.py:816) and scoring borrowed neighbor candidates during augmentation (staged_runner.py:911). The candidate ids being scored are unique-stack ids, and the cap grid passed in is the scoring view (all_oklabs), so the inf sentinel rows propagate into these scores as “never selected”.
How the kernels wire together (Stage 2 sequence)
_query_stage2_pixel_stacks (LUT batch query)   staged_runner.py:6297
        ↓ thickness_result
_vectorized_stack_ids                           staged_runner.py:6308  → helpers:21
        ↓ pixel_stack_ids, unique_stack_dicts
_precompute_cap_oklabs[_vectorized]             staged_runner.py:6337/6351 → helpers:157/87
        ↓ all_oklabs (scoring view, inf-masked)
_enumerate_zone_candidates                      staged_runner.py:6369
   └─ _score_candidates_batch                   staged_runner.py:816   → helpers:223
_augment_zone_candidates_with_neighbor_...      staged_runner.py:6389
   └─ _score_candidates_batch                   staged_runner.py:911   → helpers:223

Timings for two of these steps are recorded into the run’s performance profile as stage2_vectorized_stack_ids_s (staged_runner.py:6318) and stage2_precompute_cap_oklabs_s (staged_runner.py:6362) — these show up in run.json files under the run cache.
Reuse by the luminance handler
_predict_transmission_batch is also imported and used outside Stage 2 by generator.pipeline.luminance_handler (pipeline/luminance_handler.py:19). In _sample_white_luminance_curve’s spline branch it computes white-cap transmission for an array of cap thicknesses (luminance_handler.py:526-531), then converts to OKLab. So this one kernel serves both the Stage 2 cap precompute and the white-cap luminance handling — a single source of truth for “spline transmission of many thicknesses at once.” (The photo-stack branch of that same method bypasses the kernel and asks the provider’s own sample_white_cap_oklab directly, luminance_handler.py:519-523.)
Liveness
Confirmed from grep over Prisma/ (not from docstrings). Every public name in __all__ has a live in-tree caller:

The staged backend itself is the live solve path: pipeline/runner.py:1222-1225 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path (defined staged_runner.py:11163). The legacy solve.py “6-step” engine is a separate, non-webapp path and does not use these kernels.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Staged artifacts and the SolvedMaterialPlan contract
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the live webapp solve runs the six passes numbered Stage 0–5 and emits a StagedBackendResult lineage, then a small bridge projects its final recipe map into the canonical solve-owned SolvedMaterialPlan (immutable segment geometry + mutable stack assignment + cap heights) from which downstream rasters — labels, per-filament thickness, predicted render — are one-way derived, never authored.

This page is the data-shape reference for the Solver output. It serves two readers: a USER who wants to know what a “solve” actually produces, and a DEVELOPER who has forgotten how the backend’s artifacts fit together. It is built from the four contract modules, not their docstrings (several of which are stale — e.g. solved_material_plan.py:11-14 still claims the plan “remains None at runtime”, which is false; see Liveness below).
Related: generator.pipeline.staged_runner · generator.pipeline.runner · The staged backend (Stage 0-5) · Blueprint triage the unwired engine · Color-region geometry (dormant) · Fixed-budget layer scheduling (experimental)

Two layers of artifact, one direction of truth
A finished solve produces artifacts at two altitudes:























LayerLives whereOwnsMutabilityStage plans (Stage 0–5)StagedBackendResult on state.staged_resultthe staged backend’s internal raster blueprintbuilt once per stage, then read-only downstreamCanonical planSolvedMaterialPlan on state.solved_plansegment geometry + stack assignment + cap heightsgeometry frozen, stack assignment mutable
The rule that holds the whole system together: truth flows one way. The staged backend authors raster blueprints; the bridge condenses the final blueprint into the canonical plan; the derived-views layer projects the plan back out into legacy rasters for consumers that still want them. Nothing downstream writes truth back into the plan’s geometry. This is the “one-way ownership” pattern documented in pipeline/derived_views.py:1-20.

The five stage plans
The staged backend (run_staged_backend_path, pipeline/staged_runner.py:11163) builds one authoritative plan object per stage. Each is a dataclass in pipeline/staged_artifacts.py. They are assembled in order inside the runner:















































StagePlan dataclassBuilt atCarries (selected fields)0QuantizedDirectiveSetcompiled directivesdirectives, planning_lattice_pitch_mm, solver_shape (staged_artifacts.py:21)1LateralZonePlanstaged_runner.py:11216zone_label_map, zone_flat_indices, adjacency_edges, target_oklab_mean_by_zone (:113)2VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlanstaged_runner.py:11267zone_recipe_labels, fine_recipe_label_map, recipe_table, raw_color_ceiling_mm, implied_cap_height_mm, gamut_mask (:263)3FillerGeometryPlanstaged_runner.py:11277raw_color_ceiling_mm, filler_height_mm, color_ceiling_mm (:310)4CapSynthesisPlanstaged_runner.py:11287cap_height_mm, cap_boundary_top_mm, detail_height_mm, final_visible_top_mm, plus detail/printability summaries (:440)5CompatibilityBundlestaged_runner.py:11790thickness_maps, diagnostics, debug_maps, compatibility_label_map, boundary_label_map (:565)
Stage 5 is not a geometry plan — it is the legacy-raster projection of stages 2–4 (see The staged_bridge).
The Stage 2 recipe table — the color blueprint
Stage 2 is where the color decision is made. Its recipe_table is a tuple of VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:72), each a frozen thickness_by_filament tuple. The per-pixel recipe_label_map (staged_artifacts.py:295) indexes into that table — preferring the fine_recipe_label_map when present, otherwise expanding zone_recipe_labels[zone_label_map]. This recipe map is the seed for the canonical plan.

Disambiguation trap. VisibleRecipe (Stage 2, staged_artifacts.py:72) and StackDefinition (canonical plan, solved_material_plan.py:27) are near-duplicates — both are frozen (filament_id, thickness_mm) tuples normalized to drop zeros. They are NOT the same class. VisibleRecipe is the staged backend’s currency; StackDefinition is the canonical plan’s. The bridge converts one to the other at staged_bridge.py:67.


The lineage object: StagedBackendResult
All nine artifacts are bundled into a single StagedBackendResult (staged_artifacts.py:580) returned by run_staged_backend_path (staged_runner.py:11828) and parked on state.staged_result by _finalize_staged_backend_state (runner.py:682).
StagedBackendResult
├── compiled_directives    : QuantizedDirectiveSet       (Stage 0)
├── receipts               : DirectiveReceiptBook        (per-directive status)
├── planning_diagnostics   : PlanningDiagnosticsStream   (zone-level notes)
├── performance_profile    : StagedPerformanceProfile    (timings_s, counters)
├── lateral_zone_plan      : LateralZonePlan             (Stage 1)
├── visible_plan           : VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan (Stage 2)
├── filler_plan            : FillerGeometryPlan          (Stage 3)
├── cap_plan               : CapSynthesisPlan            (Stage 4)
└── compatibility_bundle   : CompatibilityBundle         (Stage 5)

receipts, planning_diagnostics, and performance_profile are bookkeeping, not geometry: DirectiveReceiptBook (:40) records per-directive status/stage/detail; PlanningDiagnosticsStream (:57) holds zone-scoped notes; StagedPerformanceProfile (:64) is timings_s + counters (the solve writes e.g. stage5_solved_plan_segments at runner.py:696 and stage5_bridge_s at staged_runner.py:11811 into it).

The canonical artifact: SolvedMaterialPlan
This is the solve’s authoritative output and the input to export. Triage, scheduling, and region-geometry modules can consume the plan, but their production wiring is not established by the current caller graph. Defined at solved_material_plan.py:74.
Shape













































FieldTypeMeaningsegment_id_map(H, W) intimmutable geometry identity; dense ids 0..n_segments-1segment_stack_id(n_segments,) intmutable assignment: which stack_table entry each segment usesstack_tabletuple[StackDefinition, ...]canonical, de-duplicated set of color stackscap_height_map(H, W) float32fine-grid white-cap height, mmimage_domain_width_mm / height_mmfloatphysical extentimage_sample_pitch_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mmfloatobservation-grid and solve-grid cell sizescolor_region_target_mmfloatcolor-region geometry target
The central design move (solved_material_plan.py:74-91): geometry identity and material assignment are separated. A segment is a region of pixels that share an id; which material that region prints is a separate, mutable indirection through segment_stack_id → stack_table. A downstream stage that wants to reassign material (e.g. triage shortening a stack) rewrites segment_stack_id — it must never rewrite segment_id_map.
Invariants (enforced in __post_init__, :104)
These raise ValueError/TypeError at construction, so any plan you hold is already valid:

segment_id_map is 2-D (:105).
cap_height_map shares the (H, W) footprint of segment_id_map (:109).
segment_stack_id is 1-D (:115).
Segment ids are dense and contiguous 0..n_segments-1 — np.unique(segment_id_map) must equal arange(n_segments); a gap raises “missing dense segment ids” (:137-146).
Every segment_stack_id entry is a valid index into stack_table (:152-159).
Every stack_table entry is a StackDefinition (:161-166).
Geometry is frozen structurally: segment_id_map.flags.writeable = False (:169). Attempting to mutate the raster raises at the NumPy level — this is what makes the “geometry is immutable” claim a runtime guarantee, not a convention.

StackDefinition (:27)
One unique committed color-layer stack: a frozen, sorted color_thickness_mm tuple of (filament_id, thickness_mm). Color content only — base-white (d_wb config scalar) and cap-white (cap_height_map) are modeled separately on the plan (:29-39). from_mapping (:43) drops zero-thickness entries so two mappings that differ only in absent-vs-zero entries hash equal; being frozen + content-sorted makes stacks hashable and de-duplicable into the canonical stack_table.
Convenience accessors on the plan: n_segments, n_stacks, shape, stack_at(segment_id) (:185), and filament_ids() (:189, deterministic sorted union across all stacks).
Where it is carried
The plan rides on the runtime state objects:

PipelineState.solved_plan (state.py:254) — populated by the solve path, “consumed by export, triage, and scheduling” per the in-code comment (state.py:251-253).
SolveResult.solved_plan on the facade (facade.py:253).


The derived-views layer (one-way)
pipeline/derived_views.py turns a SolvedMaterialPlan back into legacy rasters for consumers that haven’t migrated onto the plan. Every helper is pure: reads plan fields, returns a fresh array the caller may mutate, never writes back (derived_views.py:10-14).



































HelperReturnsLive consumer (grepped)committed_stack_label_map(plan) (:33)(H, W) label map = segment_stack_id[segment_id_map]server.py:1488 (Explorer Rich artifact), scheduling/model.py:435, cap_quality.py:60/572/624/737per_filament_thickness_maps(plan, ids=None) (:49){filament_id: (H, W) float32}; absent filaments → all-zerocalled by compatibility_thickness_maps; no production caller foundcap_height_map_view(plan) (:97)fresh writable copy of cap_height_mapcalled by compatibility_thickness_maps; no production caller foundcompatibility_thickness_maps(plan, ids=None) (:107)per-filament maps + writable "__white_cap__"blueprint_triage/application.py:48; that application path has no production caller foundproject_observation_to_solve_grid(...) (:125)(solve_h*solve_w, 3) OKLab on the solve gridpipeline/target_cloud.py:84 (live)
committed_stack_label_map is the keystone: because the label is segment_stack_id[segment_id_map], pixels in one segment are guaranteed to share a stack id, and per_filament_thickness_maps builds every thickness raster by gathering a stack-indexed lookup through this label map (:69-90). Mutate segment_stack_id and re-derive, and the rasters update — the plan stays the single source of truth.
project_observation_to_solve_grid is OWNED here
Despite being a target-grid resampler rather than a plan view, project_observation_to_solve_grid lives in and is exported from derived_views.py (:125, :172). It maps observation-grid target OKLab onto the solve grid. The contract (:134-164):

When image_sample_pitch_mm == solver_fine_pitch_mm (the common case) it is a zero-cost identity pass — it returns the same object (:154-155).
When the pitches differ, it bilinearly resamples (scipy.ndimage.zoom, order=1) by the pitch ratio to the solve-grid shape (:157-164).

Its live caller is target_cloud.py:84, which feeds it the image_to_target OKLab cloud to produce the solve_oklab used by the solver. So this single function is the boundary between the observation grid (what the camera sampled) and the solve grid (what the solver optimizes).

The staged_bridge build
pipeline/staged_bridge.py is the read-only Stage 5 adapter with two exported builders (:442).
build_solved_material_plan_for_export (:27) — staged plans → canonical plan
This is how a SolvedMaterialPlan actually comes into being on the live path. Called by _finalize_staged_backend_state (runner.py:686) with the Stage 2 visible_plan and Stage 4 cap_plan. Algorithm (:42-97):

Take visible_plan.recipe_label_map (the final fine recipe map). Validate it is 2-D, non-empty, non-negative (:44-51).
For each distinct recipe label present, convert its VisibleRecipe into a StackDefinition (:67) and de-duplicate into a canonical stack_table keyed by stack identity (:70-74) — two different recipe labels with identical color content collapse to one stack.
Each distinct recipe label becomes one dense segment; segment_id_map paints the segment id onto every pixel of that label (:75), and segment_stack_id[segment] points at the de-duplicated stack (:76).
Adopt Stage 4’s cap_height_mm as cap_height_map (shape-checked against the recipe map, :78-84), and set the pitch/domain scalars from solver_fine_pitch_mm (:86-97).

The result satisfies every SolvedMaterialPlan invariant by construction (dense segments, valid stack indices, matching cap footprint).

Note: here a “segment” is one whole connected-label footprint — all pixels of a given recipe label share one segment id, regardless of spatial connectivity. Spatial connected-component splitting is a later concern handled by Color-region geometry (dormant) (geometry/extract.py:210), not the bridge.

build_compatibility_bundle (:100) — staged plans → legacy raster bundle
Called at staged_runner.py:11790 to populate Stage 5. It projects visible_plan + filler_plan + cap_plan into the flat raster world the legacy preview/export code expects (:116-439):

thickness_maps: per-palette-filament (H, W) rasters painted by recipe label (:121-130), plus white-layer channels "__white_cap__", "__white_boundary_cap__" (cap-boundary minus color ceiling, floored at 0), "__white_detail_cap__" (:132-148).
diagnostics: "__gamut_mask__" (:150-152).
debug_maps: a large named dictionary of zone/recipe/ceiling/cap/detail rasters plus optional Stage 2 recipe-pressure, geometry attribution, printability-gate, substrate-repair, boundary-mutation, exterior-white-guard, and blueprint-printability maps — each guarded by a None check and copied (:193-428).
compatibility_label_map / boundary_label_map: copies of the recipe and zone label maps (:435-436).

This bundle is the legacy compatibility surface; the canonical plan (above) is the forward-looking one. Export can recover connected same-stack regions from the plan and avoid the per-pixel raster mesh path (staged_bridge.py:34-41).

Liveness — what is actually wired
Grepped, not assumed (a prior audit was burned by missing callers):

The staged backend is the live solve. runner.py:1222-1225 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path; this is the webapp solve, NOT solve.py’s legacy CLI “6-step” engine. Confirmed live.
SolvedMaterialPlan is populated at runtime. runner.py:686 assigns state.solved_plan on every solve. The solved_material_plan.py:11-14 docstring saying it “remains None at runtime” is stale — disregard it; trust the assignment.
Only the current caller-confirmed derived views are production-live. committed_stack_label_map is used by server.py and cap_quality.py; project_observation_to_solve_grid is used by the live target-cloud path. The per-filament/cap/compatibility helpers are reachable from the blueprint-triage application module but no production caller to that application was found. scheduling/model.py is also test-covered with no production caller found.
extract_regions (geometry/extract.py:210) is exported from the geometry package and consumes state.solved_plan, but I found no production call site inside Prisma/generator/ — it is exercised only by tests/generator/test_phase4_region_extraction.py. Status: wired-by-export, test-covered, no production caller found (unconfirmed whether export currently routes through it).
scheduling/model.py consumes the plan (committed_stack_label_map, cap_height_map) but its derive_*/build_* case functions (model.py:375/505/526/589) are reached only from tests/generator/test_layer_scheduling.py in my grep — no production caller found. Status: plan-consumer, test-covered, production wiring unconfirmed.


Both unconfirmed items are plan consumers downstream of a populated plan — they are not dead in the contract sense; I simply could not trace a production call edge and am flagging that explicitly rather than guessing.


See also

The staged backend (Stage 0-5) — how run_staged_backend_path orchestrates the stages

Blueprint triage the unwired engine — the live mutator that rewrites segment_stack_id and re-derives rasters

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The Joint LUT building and querying
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the joint LUT enumerates every printable (cap + color) stack under a height budget, stores each stack’s OKLab color in a chroma-weighted KD-tree, and the solver answers “which stack reproduces this pixel?” with a nearest-neighbor query.

This page covers Prisma/generator/lut.py (the spline path, the query functions, the disk cache, the convex hull, and the legacy cap-curve helpers) and Prisma/generator/photo_stack_lut.py (the vectorized photo-stack build path). For the surrounding solve flow see The Joint LUT and Staged Solve and the The Joint LUT and Staged Solve concept note. Architecture nodes: generator.lut, generator.photo_stack_lut, generator.appearance_model.
What “joint” means
Older designs solved cap thickness (luminance) and color thickness in two separate steps. The joint LUT folds them together: a single LUTEntry enumerates combinations of (d_wc, d_c1, …, d_ck) jointly and stores oklab(T_wb × T_wc(d_wc) × ∏ T_ci(d_ci)) for each (LUTEntry at lut.py:161, with the builder formula documented in build_luts). White base (d_wb) is fixed and baked into every entry, so the entries already include it. The cap dimension is carried per-entry in cap_thicknesses, and the chosen cap comes back to the caller under the reserved '__white_cap__' key.
A LUTEntry is one filament subset (size 1..k_max), not one filament. The build loops over itertools.combinations(filament_ids, k) for each k (the spline builder begins at lut.py:463, with the subset loop shortly below), so a 3-filament palette with k_max=3 produces 7 entries (3 singles + 3 pairs + 1 triple). Each entry owns its own KD-tree.















































LUTEntry fieldshapemeaningsourcefilamentstuple[str,…]color filament IDs in this subsetlut.py:161–168thicknesses(N, k)color thickness per filament (mm)lut.py:163cap_thicknesses(N,)white-cap thickness d_wc (mm)lut.py:164oklab(N, 3)OKLab of full transmission, unscaledlut.py:165treeKDTreebuilt from chroma-weighted OKLablut.py:166chroma_weightfloatL* divided by this in the treelut.py:167
Entry enumeration under a height budget (stars-and-bars)
For each subset and each cap step, the remaining height budget caps how many color layers fit. The spline builder computes this in build_luts after the current builder entry point (lut.py:463), and the provider builder performs the same calculation in build_luts_with_provider (lut.py:1348). _enumerate_combos_budget(k, remaining_steps) produces all non-negative integer tuples of length k summing to ≤ remaining_steps (lut.py:260–287). This is a direct recursive stars-and-bars generation rather than itertools.product + filter. k=0 returns a single empty row and k=1 returns arange(max_steps+1).
photo_stack_lut.py keeps a local copy of this function to avoid importing lut.py from this helper module. The two implementations are independent and must stay in lockstep; the photo-stack copy is the one used when building provider LUTs.
The budget itself: if t_max is None, the builders default it to d_wc_max + max_layers * layer_height (build_luts and build_luts_with_provider). The live runner passes the post-white-base budget to the active builder; the provider path is visible around runner.py:1156–1160.
Transmission → OKLab → pruning
Both build paths share the same post-processing tail:

Compose transmission. The spline path multiplies precomputed fixed white-base, cap-step, and color-layer transmission tables in build_luts (lut.py:463 onward). The provider path either consumes the vectorized photo-stack arrays or batches StackRequest predictions in build_luts_with_provider (lut.py:1348 onward). Products are clipped to [1e-9, 1.0] before OKLab conversion.
OKLab. to_oklab converts the linear-RGB transmission array to OKLab.
Prune near-duplicates. _prune_entries bins OKLab space at bin_width=0.005 (lut.py:440 onward) and keeps one entry per bin. Per bin it keeps the entry with lowest total color thickness (less material), tiebroken by lowest cap thickness (brighter), via _prune_entry_indices.
Build KD-tree (see below) and append the LUTEntry.

OKLab indexing with chroma weighting
The KD-tree is built from OKLab, but when chroma_weight != 1.0 the L* channel is divided by the weight before tree construction. Dividing L* shrinks lightness distances in the search metric, so nearest-neighbor matching prioritizes color (a, b) over lightness. A chroma_weight > 1 therefore tolerates more lightness error to nail hue/chroma. The stored oklab array stays unscaled — only the tree sees the scaled copy — so reported dE can be recomputed in true (unweighted) OKLab space.
Every query mirrors this: the target’s L* is divided by cw = luts[0].chroma_weight before tree.query, and the returned distance (which is in scaled space) is replaced with the true unweighted Euclidean OKLab distance against the stored oklab whenever cw != 1.0 (query_luts lut.py:1651 onward; query_luts_batch lut.py:1691 onward). See OKLab and Chroma weight.
Querying
All query functions take the List[LUTEntry] and scan every entry’s tree, keeping the global best per pixel. There is no subset pre-filtering — the nearest stack across all subsets wins.
query_luts_batch — the live webapp query
This is the function the running webapp actually calls. It is imported and invoked in the staged backend (staged_runner.py), from the Stage-2 pixel-stack query at staged_runner.py:784 (query_luts_batch(state.luts, targets)). It is the LUT query reachable from run_staged_backend_path — the webapp solve runs the staged backend, not solve.py’s engine.

Input: (N, 3) OKLab targets. Output: a dict filament_id → (N,) float32 thickness array plus '__white_cap__', and a (N,) dE array (lut.py:1691 onward). Filaments not used for a pixel get 0.0.
Parallelism: when parallel=True, n_luts > 1, and n > 1000, each entry’s tree.query runs on a ThreadPoolExecutor; SciPy’s cKDTree releases the GIL so this is real parallelism. The reduction (picking the winning LUT per pixel) is sequential NumPy.
An optional on_lut_done(done, total) callback fires per entry for progress reporting.

query_luts — single-target
Scalar version of the above for one OKLab target; returns (thicknesses_dict, dE) (lut.py:1651 onward). Live in the legacy solve.py engine only (solve.py:106).
query_luts_fixed_cap — two-pass cap smoothing (legacy)
Re-solves color layers with the cap pinned per pixel, used by the legacy two-pass smoothing. For each pixel it queries the min(20, len) nearest neighbors, then among those keeps the best whose cap_thickness matches the supplied fixed_cap within 0.5 × layer_height, falling back to the unconstrained best if none match (lut.py:1814 onward). The returned '__white_cap__' is set to the fixed cap, not the LUT entry’s. Liveness: called only from the legacy CLI engine — solve.py:617 and pipeline_cli.py:619 (inside the solve_regions smoothing branch). Not reachable from the staged webapp path — see below.
query_cap_fixed_color / query_cap_fixed_color_batch — test-facing only
The duals of query_luts_fixed_cap: pin the color stack and sweep the cap to minimize dE (lut.py:1915 and lut.py:1976). They do not use the LUTs (the luts arg is accepted for API symmetry); they recompose transmission directly via compose_stack/predict_transmission. Liveness: unwired in product code. A repo-wide grep finds no caller inside Prisma/generator/ — the only caller is tests/generator/test_query_cap_fixed_color.py. Treat them as a tested-but-dormant utility.
Two build paths
The runner selects the path by the appearance provider’s model_kind (the active builder call is in runner.py:1156–1160):
model_kind == "historical_spline"  →  build_luts(...)
otherwise                          →  build_luts_with_provider()

See Appearance provider for what supplies model_kind.
Path A — build_luts (spline + pair corrections)
build_luts(color_profiles, wb_profile, wc_profile, …) is the historical spline path (lut.py:463 onward). It requires wb_profile and wc_profile, auto-derives d_wc_max via derive_d_wc_max if not given, precomputes transmission tables, enumerates combos per subset/cap, and builds entries.
Pair corrections (k=2 only). When corrections is supplied and k_max ≥ 2, _build_pair_corr_cache restructures the fitter’s correction dict into per-(overlay, base) arrays interpolated to each layer count. Only single-base pairs are kept; multi-base correction entries are dropped. During build, for each 2-filament subset the A-on-B and B-on-A correction curves are looked up; if both exist they are averaged, otherwise the available one is applied, indexed by the overlay filament’s layer count. Corrections never touch k=1 or k=3 subsets.
Live caller: the historical-spline branch in the pipeline runner and pipeline_cli.py:545 (CLI). The current default photo-stack provider uses the provider builder below.
Path B — build_luts_with_provider (live photo-stack model)
build_luts_with_provider(provider, …) is the provider-backed path and returns ordinary LUTEntry objects so the query code stays shared (lut.py:1348 onward). It has two internal sub-paths:

model_kind == "photo_stack_bundle" (the current default model): it iterates iter_photo_stack_lut_arrays(provider, …) from photo_stack_lut.py, prunes, chroma-weights, and builds trees. This is where the heavy vectorized appearance model runs.
Generic provider fallback: for any other non-spline provider it builds StackRequest objects per combo and calls provider.predict_stack_linear_rgb_batch(all_requests) in one batch. Pair corrections are not applied on this path (no corrections argument exists in this function).

Live caller: the normal provider branch in the pipeline runner — the webapp’s path whenever the active model is not the historical spline. This is the path exercised by typical solves today.
The vectorized photo-stack evaluator (photo_stack_lut.py)
iter_photo_stack_lut_arrays (photo_stack_lut.py:1110 onward) yields one PhotoStackLUTArrays (raw, pre-prune) per subset. It builds cap steps, instantiates a _PhotoStackGridEvaluator, and for each subset/cap enumerates combos and calls evaluator.predict_subset(subset, combos, cap_indices) to get model-domain linear RGB, then projects to appearance via provider.project_model_linear_rgb_to_appearance before OKLab conversion. _PhotoStackGridEvaluator is a NumPy mirror of the frozen photo-stack equations — white context, cap attenuation, multicolor interaction, ordered-tint retention, single-color cap transfer / profile blend, two-color endpoint corridor, and a kernel-weighted correction residual. Its physics is owned by lib.photo_stack_model.predictor and is out of scope here; the contract is “grid-aligned counts → OKLab, identical to the row predictor” (verified by the module’s comparison helper and tests).

Note: project_model_linear_rgb_to_appearance and the appearance-named provider methods are pass-throughs that return model-domain values after the projection-slot retirement (appearance_model.py:429–432; predict_stack_linear_rgb_batch aliases the model-domain batch, appearance_model.py:424–427). See Model-domain ingress.

predict_combo_model_linear_rgb (photo_stack_lut.py:925) and predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid (photo_stack_lut.py:998) are sibling entry points to the same evaluator used at solve time (Stage-4 cap planning), not during LUT build. predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid is imported and called by the staged cap planner (staged_solver_helpers.py); it internally calls predict_combo_model_linear_rgb. The appearance provider’s deduplicated row predictor also reaches the same combo predictor. They share the evaluator so hot paths never pay the row predictor’s per-row cost.
Disk cache (npz, trees rebuilt)
LUTs are cached to data_paths.LUT_CACHE_DIR = <cache>/luts/ (data_paths.py:54). KD-trees are never serialized — only the arrays are saved, and trees are rebuilt on load (_save_luts_to_cache lut.py:321 onward; _load_luts_from_cache lut.py:348 onward). Because the tree is rebuilt at load, chroma_weight is re-applied at load time, so the same cached npz can serve different chroma weights — but the cache key includes chroma_weight, so in practice each weight gets its own file.
Two cache-key schemes:























Pathkey functionfilenameversion/metadataspline (build_luts)_cache_key (lut.py:298 onward)lut_<16hex>.npzSHA-256 over sorted filament IDs, all geometry params, per-profile checksums, and a corrections checksum; no stored metadata blockprovider (build_luts_with_provider)_provider_cache_key (lut.py:1320 onward)lut_provider_<16hex>.npzincludes a builder_version string and writes a cache_metadata dict (schema provider_lut_v2) into the npz, validated on load
The provider cache’s builder_version is PHOTO_STACK_LUT_BUILDER_VERSION (photo_stack_lut.py:65) for photo-stack bundles, else "provider_generic". On load, _load_luts_from_cache rejects the file if any expected_metadata key mismatches or if the metadata block is missing entirely — so a builder-version bump auto-invalidates stale provider caches. The provider path also fills a diagnostics dict (cache key/path/hit, LUT/entry counts) for observability.
The spline path’s _save_luts_to_cache is called with no metadata, and _load_luts_from_cache is called there without expected_metadata, so its only guard against staleness is the hash in the filename.
Convex hull construction
build_hull_from_luts(luts) stacks every entry’s oklab, deduplicates by rounding to 4 decimals, and returns a scipy.spatial.ConvexHull of all achievable OKLab colors (lut.py:2064 onward). It is the achievable-gamut surface used for hull-mode gamut projection: out-of-gamut targets are pushed onto the nearest hull facet. Live callers: the runner’s hull-mode gamut mapping path and solve.py’s legacy engine. The hull feeds solve.gamut_map_hull_batch, which the runner calls during target mapping. See Gamut mapping.
Legacy cap-curve helpers
A separate 1-D structure predates the joint LUT and is retained “for dual-resolution cap refinement”:

CapCurve (lut.py:152–158): maps OKLab L* → cap thickness d_wc, holding d_wc_steps, L_values, and a T_wc_table.
build_cap_curve (lut.py:201): builds it by stepping cap thickness and recording L*.
cap_curve_lookup_batch (lut.py:232): vectorised nearest-L* lookup with a broadcast-floats chunking guard.
derive_d_wc_max (lut.py:180): finds the cap thickness where mean transmission drops below a threshold (default 0.05) — beyond this the cap is effectively opaque. This one is not legacy: it is used by both build_cap_curve and build_luts to auto-derive d_wc_max.

Liveness of the cap-curve trio: build_cap_curve and cap_curve_lookup_batch are used by the legacy engine only. build_cap_curve is called by the CLI at pipeline_cli.py:665; cap_curve_lookup_batch is called by solve.py:434. The live webapp goes through run_staged_backend_path and queries LUTs with query_luts_batch. So CapCurve/build_cap_curve/cap_curve_lookup_batch are live in the CLI path, dormant in the webapp path.
Liveness summary

































































SymbolStatusEvidencebuild_lutslive (CLI + spline-provider webapp)pipeline_cli.py:545, runner.py:1111build_luts_with_providerlive (default webapp path)runner.py:1160iter_photo_stack_lut_arrayslive (photo-stack build)lut.py:1348 onward via build_luts_with_providerquery_luts_batchlive (webapp staged backend)staged_runner.py:784query_lutslive (legacy engine)solve.py:106query_luts_fixed_caplive (legacy engine only)solve.py:617, pipeline_cli.py:619query_cap_fixed_color / _batchunwired in product; tests onlyonly tests/generator/test_query_cap_fixed_color.pybuild_hull_from_lutslive (gamut hull mode)runner hull mapping path, solve.py:555build_cap_curve / cap_curve_lookup_batch / CapCurvelive in CLI, dormant in webapppipeline_cli.py:665, solve.py:434derive_d_wc_maxlive (auto d_wc_max)lut.py:180, lut.py:507predict_combo_model_linear_rgb / predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_gridlive (solve-time cap planning, not build)staged cap-planner imports plus provider deduplicated prediction
Driving it (for users)
You never call these functions directly — the generator does. What you control maps to build parameters:

Palette → filament_ids / subsets (more filaments ⇒ more subsets ⇒ bigger LUT, longer first build).
k_max → how many colors may stack per pixel (1–3). Higher k_max multiplies subset count combinatorially.
Height budget (t_max, d_wb, layer height) → how many layers fit, hence how many combos per subset.
Chroma weight → favor color accuracy over lightness in matching.

First solve of a new palette pays the build cost; subsequent solves hit the npz cache. Changing a filament’s measured profile, the pair corrections, or the photo-stack model version (builder_version) invalidates the relevant cache automatically.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The solve target cloud
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the solve target cloud is the single shared step that turns a loaded source image into per-pixel OKLab targets — convert source pixels into the model color domain, flatten to OKLab, project onto the solve grid, and (optionally) rescale to the print’s paper white — so the solver and palette suggestion both compare against filament gamuts in exactly the same space.

What it is for
Three different callers need the same conditioning of the source image before they can ask “which filament stack reproduces this color?”: the solve runner, palette suggestion, and gamut preview. If each re-implemented the color conversion, suggestion could silently drift into a different color-domain interpretation than the solve it is supposed to predict. pipeline/target_cloud.py is the one place that path lives, so it cannot drift (pipeline/target_cloud.py:1–8).
The module produces a frozen SolveTargetCloud dataclass carrying both grids of targets plus the metadata describing how they were built (pipeline/target_cloud.py:23–32):

































FieldMeaningobserved_oklab(H*W, 3) OKLab targets on the observation grid (one row per source pixel)solve_oklab(solve_h*solve_w, 3) OKLab targets on the solve gridobservation_shape(H, W) of the loaded imagesolve_shape(solve_h, solve_w) derived from the pitch ratiodomainalways "model_oklab" (see the domain contract)model_domain_ingresswhether the Camera Transform ingress LUT was used
How it works — the four steps
compute_solve_target_cloud(image, wb_profile, config) is the entry point (pipeline/target_cloud.py:64). It expects a post-load, post-adjustment image — i.e. the source image after loading and any preprocessing has already happened upstream; the target cloud does no preprocessing of its own.
1. Ingress — source pixels into the model domain
The image goes through image_to_target() (pipeline/target_cloud.py:72, defined at model.py:128). The model_domain_ingress flag picks one of two source-pixel conversions (model.py:149–152):

Ingress ON (the default everywhere the webapp drives it — state.py:77, server.py:623, facade.py:100 all default True): the source sRGB image is run through the Camera Transform inverse LUT via _apply_model_domain_ingress_lut → apply_inverse_lut from lib.camera_transform (model.py:123–125, model.py:21). The LUT is loaded from model_domain_ingress_lut_path, which defaults to the camera_transform directory inside the launcher’s active immutable model library (pipeline/target_cloud.py:77–81, model.py:28). This maps display-sRGB source pixels into the model’s transmission color domain.
Ingress OFF (legacy): a plain srgb_to_linear() gamma-2.2 conversion, bit-identical to the old path (model.py:108–115, model.py:148–152).

Note the model_domain_ingress default on the image_to_target function itself is False (model.py:133), but every runtime config that reaches it passes True explicitly, and compute_solve_target_cloud reads the config’s model_domain_ingress attribute (default True) rather than relying on that function default (pipeline/target_cloud.py:76). The wb_profile and d_wb arguments are accepted for API compatibility but unused by image_to_target — the white-base term is already baked into every LUT entry (model.py:142–146).
2. OKLab conversion
The (H, W, 3) target image is reshaped to (H*W, 3) and run through to_oklab() (pipeline/target_cloud.py:83), which calls linear_to_oklab from lib.transmission (model.py:155–160, model.py:22). This is the observed_oklab array. OKLab itself is described in OKLab; this module just calls into it.
3. Observation grid → solve grid projection
project_observation_to_solve_grid() (generator.pipeline.derived_views, derived_views.py:125) resamples the observation-grid OKLab onto the solve grid (pipeline/target_cloud.py:84–90):

When image_sample_pitch_mm == solver_fine_pitch_mm (both default 0.20 — state.py:105–106, facade.py:168–169), this is a zero-cost identity pass that returns the same array object (derived_views.py:154–155). This is the common case.
When the pitches differ, the (obs_h, obs_w, 3) raster is bilinearly resampled (scipy.ndimage.zoom, order=1) to the solve-grid shape, where ratio = image_sample_pitch_mm / solver_fine_pitch_mm and solve_h = round(obs_h * ratio) (derived_views.py:157–164).

_solve_shape_for_observation() computes the matching solve_shape with the same rounding rule, so the reported shape always agrees with the resampled array (pipeline/target_cloud.py:35–48).
4. The result
All four pieces are packed into the frozen SolveTargetCloud (pipeline/target_cloud.py:91–103), with domain set by solve_target_domain(config).
The model_oklab domain contract
solve_target_domain(config) always returns the constant MODEL_OKLAB_DOMAIN = "model_oklab" regardless of the ingress flag (pipeline/target_cloud.py:20, 51–61). The ingress flag only decides how source pixels are converted; it does not change the comparison space. Either way the solver compares these targets to model-domain LUT / gamut points, so the contract for the nearest-neighbor search is model OKLab. The flag is read (bool(getattr(config, "model_domain_ingress", True))) and deliberately discarded — it is carried on the cloud as metadata, not as a domain switch (pipeline/target_cloud.py:60).
This matters because of the projection-slot retirement: the photo-stack model’s appearance-named prediction methods are now exact model-domain pass-throughs (camera-appearance conversion only happens at ingress and display boundaries — solve.py:251–253). So “compare in model OKLab” is the whole story for the solver; there is no separate appearance space in the comparison.
Gamut white-point rescale (optional pre-step)
apply_gamut_white_rescale_to_targets() is a separate, opt-in step the callers apply after building the cloud (pipeline/target_cloud.py:106). It is gated on config.gamut_white_rescale, which defaults OFF (state.py:76, server.py:622, facade.py:216); when off (or when targets/provider are missing) it returns the targets unchanged and None for the white (pipeline/target_cloud.py:114–117).
When enabled, it delegates to two functions in generator.solve:

compute_paper_white_rgb(provider, config) (solve.py:245) — the linear-RGB appearance of the thinnest white-only stack (white base + a d_wc_min white cap) through the active provider. Returns None (so rescale is skipped) when there is no white base or the paper white is already effectively [1,1,1] (solve.py:255–279).
rescale_oklab_targets(targets_oklab, white) (solve.py:282) — a per-channel von Kries adaptation: round-trip the OKLab targets through linear RGB, multiply each channel by the paper white, convert back to OKLab (solve.py:295–297). Because OKLab↔linear is bijective, the only change is the per-channel scale that adapts the source white to the print’s paper white.

The helper returns (rescaled_targets, white_rgb) so the caller can record diagnostics (pipeline/target_cloud.py:124).
Who drives it (liveness — confirmed from callers)






























CallerWhereWhat it doesSolve runnerpipeline/runner.py:1034 onwardBuilds the cloud once as the single owner of observation-grid targets; stores observed→state.observed_target_oklab and solve_oklab→state.solve_target_oklab, which then feed The staged backend (Stage 0-5).Solve runner (rescale)pipeline/runner.py:210–225Applies apply_gamut_white_rescale_to_targets as the white-point pre-step inside _apply_target_white_rescale, before any gamut mapping.Palette suggestionpalette/suggest.py:392–412solve_target_oklab_for_signature() builds the same cloud and applies the same optional rescale, so suggestion mirrors solve ingress.Palette suggestion (domain)palette/suggest.py:101, :171, :532–533Stamps ColorSignature.domain and the gamut-backend domain with MODEL_OKLAB_DOMAIN.
All five exported symbols (pipeline/target_cloud.py:127–133) are live. Four have external importers in runner.py and suggest.py: compute_solve_target_cloud (runner.py:33, suggest.py:57), apply_gamut_white_rescale_to_targets (runner.py:32, suggest.py:56), MODEL_OKLAB_DOMAIN (suggest.py:55), and SolveTargetCloud (returned by compute_solve_target_cloud, consumed at runner.py:793–796). solve_target_domain is exported but called only internally — by compute_solve_target_cloud itself (pipeline/target_cloud.py:101); it is exercised externally through that call (and pinned by tests/generator/test_palette_suggest.py:225), not imported. None are dead.


                  
                  Not the legacy CLI engine 
                  
                

This shared path is what the staged webapp backend consumes. It is distinct from solve.py’s old “6-step” CLI engine; the runner builds the target cloud here and then hands off to run_staged_backend_path, not to the legacy engine.


Defaults at a glance
