prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The staged backend (Stage 0-5)
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: the staged backend is the generator’s sole production solve engine — it turns a prepared image into per-filament thickness maps through six ordered passes (directives → zones → recipes → filler → cap → bridge), each handing a frozen artifact to the next.

The staged backend (Stage 0-5)
When you click Solve in the generator web app, the color decomposition is performed by run_staged_backend_path in generator.pipeline.staged_runner, not by the older solve_image engine in solve.py (that is the legacy CLI region engine — solve.py:480 solve_image, solve.py:647 solve_regions — and is not on the webapp solve path). The webapp path is run_pipeline → the staged backend; the only caller of the staged entry point is the runner: pipeline/runner.py:1222-1225 imports and calls run_staged_backend_path(state, progress=solve_progress).
The function lives at pipeline/staged_runner.py:11163. That one file is ~11,000 lines; this page stays at stage-contract altitude — what each stage consumes, what it produces, and which knobs you control — and deliberately does not narrate gate/beam/mutation internals.
How to drive it
You never call the stages directly. You configure a PipelineConfig (palette, layer height, budgets, region target, feature flags) and run a solve from the web app or pipeline_cli.py. The staged backend reads state.config and state.solve_target_oklab (the prepared OKLab targets on the solve grid) and returns a StagedBackendResult bundle. The runner then copies that bundle onto legacy-facing state (pipeline/runner.py:677 _finalize_staged_backend_state), after which filament grouping, statistics, and mesh export run as usual.
Two hard preconditions, enforced by the stages themselves:

state.solve_target_oklab must be set — Stage 1 and Stage 2 raise RuntimeError otherwise (pipeline/staged_runner.py:698, :783, :6232).
The solve grid shape is taken from state.image.shape[:2]; everything downstream operates on that lattice.

The pipeline at a glance
run_staged_backend_path runs the six stages in strict order, timing each into a StagedPerformanceProfile and emitting progress callbacks (all reported under stage_index: 1, stage_count: 1, pipeline/staged_runner.py:11188-11189). Each stage is a single builder function whose output is a frozen artifact consumed by the next.















































StageBuilder (staged_runner.py)Produces (staged_artifacts.py)One-line contract0 — Directives_compile_directives :589QuantizedDirectiveSet + DirectiveReceiptBookCompile + quantize the authoritative solve lattice and cap-floor directives1 — Zones_build_stage1_zone_plan :693LateralZonePlanSegment the image into lateral color zones on a (possibly coarsened) planning lattice2 — Recipes_build_stage2_visible_plan :6221VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlanAssign one visible filament recipe per zone and emit raw color-ceiling geometry3 — Filler_build_stage3_filler_plan :9582FillerGeometryPlanGeometry-only filler pass (currently a pass-through; filler height ≡ 0)4 — Cap_build_stage4_cap_plan :10287CapSynthesisPlanSynthesize the white cap, edge guards, and optional detail surface; printability gates5 — Bridgebuild_compatibility_bundle (staged_bridge.py:100)CompatibilityBundleProject staged artifacts into legacy per-filament thickness maps + debug maps
The final return value is StagedBackendResult (staged_artifacts.py:581) carrying all six artifacts plus the diagnostics stream, performance profile, and receipts (pipeline/staged_runner.py:11828-11838).

The artifact names are stable; some docstrings still call this an “experimental proof slice” (e.g. staged_artifacts.py headers, staged_runner.py:11164). That language is stale — this is the production path. Trust the caller at runner.py:1225, not the docstring.


Stage 0 — Directives
_compile_directives(state) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:589) builds a tiny, explicit directive set rather than letting later stages re-derive geometry. It computes the planning lattice pitch as solver_fine_pitch_mm × stage1_coarsening_factor (:594) and quantizes the minimum visible cap (d_wc_min) to a whole number of layers (:608-612). The solver_shape it pins is the raw image shape (h, w) (:635).
Each directive is a CompiledDirective with a gate (here "require") and a scope ("image"); each gets a DirectiveReceiptEntry marked status="held", stage="stage0" (:615-630). The output QuantizedDirectiveSet (staged_artifacts.py:22) is consumed by Stage 2 as its evaluation lattice (:6258 reads compiled_directives.solver_shape).
Stage 1 — Lateral zone segmentation
_build_stage1_zone_plan(state, diagnostics) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:693) partitions the image into lateral color zones — contiguous regions that will each receive one recipe in Stage 2.
What it does:

Optionally coarsens the planning grid by stage1_coarsening_factor (_effective_stage1_coarsening_factor, :297), block-averaging both the RGB image (_downsample_rgb_image, :366) and the flat OKLab targets (_downsample_flat_oklab_targets, :421) onto the coarse lattice, with an optional lattice offset (_stage1_lattice_offset_px).
Calls generate_stage1_zone_labels (imported from generator.pipeline.staged_solver_helpers, :731) to produce the integer zone-label raster, honoring cell_mode, the effective color_region_target_mm, smooth_boundaries, and boundary_smooth_radius.
Derives per-zone bookkeeping: flat membership indices (_zone_flat_indices, :666), per-zone OKLab mean/variance (_summarize_zone_targets, :676), and 4-neighbor adjacency with shared-edge lengths (_build_zone_adjacency, :641).

The effective region target can be widened from the printability minimum width when color_region_target_from_printability is on (_effective_color_region_target_mm, used at :719 and :11224); the requested-vs-effective values are both recorded as counters (:11225-11234). Output LateralZonePlan (staged_artifacts.py:114) carries zone_label_map, zone_flat_indices, adjacency_edges, edge lengths, per-zone means/variances, and the coarse_to_fine_scale Stage 2 will reverse.
Stage 2 — Recipe assignment
_build_stage2_visible_plan(...) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:6221) is the heart of the solver: it chooses one visible filament recipe per zone while balancing local color fidelity against seam continuity. This is the single largest stage in the file.
Projection back to fine grid. If Stage 1 coarsened, the zone labels are projected back onto the fine evaluation lattice (_project_zone_labels_to_fine, :6259), optionally refined into source-edge subzones (_split_stage2_source_edge_subzones, :6273, gated by stage2_source_edge_subzones). Adjacency and per-zone variance are recomputed on this evaluation lattice (:6282-6292).
Candidate query. _query_stage2_pixel_stacks (:779) runs query_luts_batch (from generator.lut) over the OKLab targets to get a per-pixel best stack plus a per-pixel ΔE; pixels above de_threshold form the gamut_mask (:785). _vectorized_stack_ids (:6308) quantizes those thickness vectors into a discrete set of unique stack ids under effective_max_layers(). Palette ordering: the palette handed to the encoder is cfg.palette order for both appearance lanes — config materialization already canonicalizes color-filament order and stack ids inherit it exactly (:6304-6313); the physical photo-stack model in particular must keep that order because its layers are physically stacked.
Enumeration + pruning. _enumerate_zone_candidates (:789) collects, per zone, the unique stack ids that appear among that zone’s pixels and scores each candidate against the zone’s targets with _score_candidates_batch (:816); a single-candidate zone gets score 0 (:812-813). Each candidate also carries its total visible thickness (:820-826). The candidate frontier is then enriched — neighboring zones’ strong local-best stacks are injected as extra candidates (_augment_zone_candidates_with_neighbor_local_bests, :837) so a zone can match a neighbor it would not have considered alone. This frontier is what keeps the assignment search tractable instead of enumerating the full LUT.
Coordinate-descent + beam under continuity/seam. Selection is a two-step optimization over candidate indices:

_seed_zone_recipe_labels_with_beam (:1452, called :6515) runs a small beam search (_STAGE2_BEAM_WIDTH = 12, :100) to build a good initial assignment that already respects neighbor continuity.
_optimize_zone_recipe_labels (:1913, called :6603) takes that seed and refines it: _run_coord_descent (:1693, up to _STAGE2_MAX_COORD_DESCENT_PASSES = 4, :90) followed by _repair_worst_boundary_pairs pair repair (:1765).

The objective per zone/candidate is computed in _zone_objective_breakdown (:1606): local_cost + continuity_weight × boundary_cost + retaining_wall_weight × retaining_cost (:1636-1640), where boundary_cost is the edge-length-weighted squared visible-thickness step to each neighbor’s current choice (:1629-1631) and retaining_cost penalizes excess thickness above the zone’s thinnest candidate (:1634-1635). Defaults: _STAGE2_CONTINUITY_WEIGHT = 0.12, _STAGE2_RETAINING_WALL_WEIGHT = 0.02 (:88-89); the continuity weight is overridable via _stage2_continuity_weight. “Seam” quality is the mean shared-boundary thickness step, tracked before/after by _mean_boundary_step_mm (:1649).
Output VisibleRecipeRawGeometryPlan (staged_artifacts.py:264) carries the zone_recipe_labels, the recipe_table of VisibleRecipe entries, the raw color ceiling, the gamut mask, an optional fine_recipe_label_map (when a within-zone detail override fires), and a Stage2ObjectiveSummary. Its recipe_label_map property (:295-299) returns the fine override if present, else the zone-level labels.

VisibleRecipe vs the photo-stack StackDefinition. VisibleRecipe (staged_artifacts.py:73) is the staged backend’s committed recipe — an ordered tuple of (filament_id, thickness_mm) pairs with from_mapping/to_mapping helpers. It is structurally near-identical to but distinct from the model-layer StackDefinition; do not conflate them.

Stage 3 — Filler
_build_stage3_filler_plan(...) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:9582) is the geometry-only filler pass. In current code it is effectively a pass-through: it sets filler_height = zeros_like(raw_color_ceiling) and therefore color_ceiling_mm == raw_color_ceiling_mm (:9589-9590). It still runs every solve (called unconditionally at :11277) and emits a FillerGeometryPlan (staged_artifacts.py:311) so Stage 4 has a uniform color_ceiling_mm field to build on. The stage exists as a wired seam for support/filler logic; today it adds no height. Confirmed live but no-op: the only writer of filler_height is the np.zeros_like at :9589.
Stage 4 — Cap and detail / printability
_build_stage4_cap_plan(...) (pipeline/staged_runner.py:10287) synthesizes everything above the color layers: the white boundary cap, edge guards, an optional detail surface, and the printability gates.
Key contract points:

Budget. The remaining cap budget is t_max − color_ceiling, clamped to effective_d_wc_max() (:10303-10307); the boundary cap is further clamped to effective_boundary_d_wc_max() (:10308-10311). The minimum cap floor is quantized to layers via _quantized_cap_floor (:10298).
Requested cap & guards. _requested_stage4_cap_maps (:9319) returns the requested boundary cap, a detail reference cap, and a boundary_edge_guard_weight map. Stage 4 supports cap_mode ∈ {"smooth_variable", "appearance_bounded_smooth"} (_STAGE4_SUPPORTED_CAP_MODES, :208); the retired "fixed" mode — and any other value — raises ValueError rather than falling back (:9350-9351). "appearance_bounded_smooth" (UI “Detail Aware”, the default) keeps the boundary cap structural and pushes tonal relief into the detail cap within an appearance-ΔE budget (boundary_cap_de_budget, default 0.008); Luminance mode forces smooth_variable.
Lateral boundary shield. When printability is enforced and a non-fixed lateral shield is required, Stage 4 honors the mandatory shield floor handed off by Stage 2 (visible_plan.mandatory_lateral_boundary_shield_floor_mm, :10327), raising a ValueError if its shape disagrees with the cap (:10330-10333).
Detail surface. The detail cap is now mandatory — detail_cap_enabled is force-True (SolveConfig rejects False, server.py:688-692) and drives the detail branch at :10470; its depth is bounded by detail_cap_max_layers (UI “Detail depth”, default 5). The old stage4_optical_detail_surface / stage4_independent_detail_surface mode selectors were retired (2026-07-01); which source fills the detail cap now follows the cap mode. Under the appearance-bounded structural split it is the residual above the boundary cap (:10473-10496); otherwise it is a synthesized optical detail surface (_build_stage4_optical_detail_surface, :8840, called :10498). Detail candidates are scored per connected zone and accepted/rejected with explicit reasons (Stage4DetailZoneSummary, staged_artifacts.py:344); rejection categories include too-small, weak-optical-gain, and weak-signal (_STAGE4_DETAIL_REJECT_*, :220-223).
Printability gates. Two optional gate families run here and surface as Stage4BoundaryCapPrintabilitySummary and Stage4DetailAuthoringPrintabilitySummary / Stage4DetailPrintabilitySummary, all None when disabled (CapSynthesisPlan fields, staged_artifacts.py:454-459).

Output CapSynthesisPlan (staged_artifacts.py:441) carries cap_boundary_top_mm, cap_height_mm, boundary_edge_guard_weight, detail_height_mm, the detail zone maps/summary, and final_visible_top_mm.

Two unrelated PrintabilityReport/printability classes. Stage 4’s printability summaries (Stage4*PrintabilitySummary) and the optional plan-level BlueprintPrintabilityDiagnostic (staged_artifacts.py:502, run via staged_printability.run_blueprint_printability_diagnostic at :11583) live in this pipeline. They are distinct from the mesh-side and blueprint_triage printability types — do not cross-reference them. The blueprint diagnostic and geometry-attribution passes are opt-in, gated by emit_blueprint_printability (:11569) and emit_geometry_attribution (:11513); they are read-only diagnostics that never change geometry.

Stage 5 — Plan bridge
build_compatibility_bundle(...) (pipeline/staged_bridge.py:100) is the read-only adapter that projects the staged artifacts back into the legacy thickness-map shape the rest of the generator (mesh export, previews, dE diagnostics) expects.
It builds one (h, w) float32 thickness map per palette filament by painting each recipe’s thickness_by_filament onto its recipe_label_map mask (staged_bridge.py:124-130), then adds three white-channel maps: __white_cap__ (full cap height), __white_boundary_cap__ (cap-above-ceiling, floored at 0), and __white_detail_cap__ (:140-148). It also exports the __gamut_mask__ diagnostic and a dictionary of debug maps (zone labels, recipe labels, color ceiling, cap tops, detail maps, etc., :151-236). Output CompatibilityBundle (staged_artifacts.py:566) plus the per-pixel image-domain extents.
Back in the runner, _finalize_staged_backend_state (pipeline/runner.py:677) copies bundle.thickness_maps into state.thickness_maps (:702-705), routes bundle diagnostics into state.diagnostics (never into thickness maps, :710-711), merges debug maps (:713), sets state.color_committed = True (:719), and — separately — builds the export-facing SolvedMaterialPlan via build_solved_material_plan_for_export (:686). That is the true Stage 5 handoff to mesh generation; see Thickness map and From solve to mesh the export pipeline.

Diagnostics, receipts, and performance
Throughout, the orchestrator records:

Timings per stage into StagedPerformanceProfile.timings_s (_record_timing, :283) — stage0_compile_directives_s, stage1_zone_plan_s, the Stage 2 sub-timings (stage2_beam_seed_s, stage2_coord_descent_s, stage2_pair_repair_s), stage3_filler_s, stage4_cap_s, stage5_bridge_s, and staged_backend_total_s (:11822-11826).
Counters for grid sizes, zone counts, frontier sizes, detail accept/reject tallies, and printability findings (_set_counter, :288).
Receipts (DirectiveReceiptBook) and a diagnostics stream (PlanningDiagnosticsStream) of human-readable PlanningDiagnosticEntry notes — Stage 1 zone count, Stage 2 seam/pressure notes, printability summaries.

These are what the Color Ceiling / Recipe Viewer UI and the run-record JSON read from; the per-recipe rollups shown in the app derive from the recipe_table and the color_recipe_breakdown artifact, not from re-solving.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The vectorized photo-stack LUT evaluator
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: photo_stack_lut.py re-implements the frozen photo-stack v2 color model as pure NumPy arrays so the generator can evaluate hundreds of thousands of candidate stacks per second when building the The Joint LUT and Staged Solve and precomputing cap curves — without ever changing the model the slow row-shaped predictor exposes.

This page covers the fast path. The trustworthy-but-slow path is the row-shaped predictor on the appearance provider (predict_stack_model_linear_rgb_batch, appearance_model.py:381), which evaluates one stack per pandas row. That is fine for isolated predictions and calibration review, but LUT construction needs a different runtime shape: it sweeps a regular grid of millions of stacks. This module mirrors the same equations over array columns so that hot path never pays the per-row cost. Both routes must agree to floating-point tolerance — compare_vectorized_provider_predictions (photo_stack_lut.py:1111) exists precisely to assert that.
If you just want to drive the generator, you never call this module directly — it runs automatically whenever the active provider is a photo-stack bundle. The “how it works” sections below are for the developer who has forgotten the backend.
Why a second implementation exists
The model is nonlinear and stateful per stack: white-context optical density (OD), cap attenuation, multi-color interaction, ordered tint retention, single-color cap transfer, two-color endpoint corridors, and a learned correction layer. The row predictor walks these stages one DataFrame row at a time. Re-expressing every stage as a batched array op lets one call process an entire filament subset’s grid at once.
The contract is “mirror, don’t reinvent”: every constant and helper is imported from the same lib.photo_stack_model.predictor and lib.photo_stack_model.correction_layer the row predictor uses (photo_stack_lut.py:21–photo_stack_lut.py:62). The builder version string photo_stack_lut_appearance_v2_2026_06_10 (photo_stack_lut.py:65) tags LUT caches so a model change invalidates them.






























Row-shaped predictorVectorized evaluatorWhereappearance_model.py:381_PhotoStackGridEvaluator, photo_stack_lut.py:153Shapeone stack per pandas rowone filament subset’s whole grid per callRolesource of truth / oracleinteractive-speed bulk evaluationUsed bycorner cases, off-grid, the cross-checkLUT build, cap-curve precompute, on-grid dedup
The OD-composition pipeline
predict_subset (photo_stack_lut.py:835) is the core. For one filament subset and a column of per-row layer counts plus cap indices, it composes the stack in optical-density space, where stacking is addition, then converts to linear RGB once at the end.
OD is the natural domain because transmission multiplies (T_total = ∏ T_i) and log turns products into sums. The evaluator builds total_od additively, then maps back with t_from_od (predictor.py:341), which is floor + (1 − floor)·exp(−od) — the floor models the lightbox/material light leak. layer_od (predictor.py:804) samples a filament’s measured OD curve at a thickness, with a frozen high-thickness taper.
The additive composition in predict_subset (photo_stack_lut.py:892) is:
total_od = latent_color
         + white_bulk          # white base OD + white cap OD
         + white_context       # white reacting to color load
         + cap_attenuation     # cap surface darkening
         + interaction         # multi-color cross terms

clipped to [0, 20], then rgb = t_from_od(total_od, floor) and lab = linear_rgb_to_oklab(rgb). After that base OKLab, OKLab-space refinements layer on (these are not OD-additive — they pull hue/chroma/lightness toward learned anchors):























































StageMethodApplies whenLatent color OD_latent_parts photo_stack_lut.py:234alwaysWhite-context OD_white_context_od photo_stack_lut.py:265alwaysCap-attenuation OD_cap_attenuation_od photo_stack_lut.py:282alwaysMulti-color interaction OD_multicolor_interaction_od photo_stack_lut.py:312≥2 distinct colorsOrdered tint retention_ordered_tint_retention_lab photo_stack_lut.py:408≥2 distinct colorsSingle-color cap transfer_single_color_cap_transfer_lab photo_stack_lut.py:459exactly 1 distinct colorSingle-color measured profile_apply_single_color_profile photo_stack_lut.py:563exactly 1 distinct colorTwo-color endpoint corridor_endpoint_corridor_lab photo_stack_lut.py:653exactly 2 distinct colorsLearned correction residual_apply_corrections photo_stack_lut.py:747context key has training rows
The branch by distinct-color count is dispatched at photo_stack_lut.py:897–photo_stack_lut.py:903 (len(set(active_ids)) 1 vs 2). Rows are grouped by an active-filament bitmask key (_active_key, photo_stack_lut.py:200) so every row in a group shares the same set of present colors and can run one stage path together.
The whole grid is sampled from precomputed OD tables built once in __init__: cap_od_table over cap steps (photo_stack_lut.py:185) and color_od_tables per filament over color steps (photo_stack_lut.py:192). A row indexes these tables by its integer counts — no per-row curve sampling.
Model domain vs appearance projection
The evaluator works entirely in the model domain (flatfield-normalized model RGB). The conversion to the camera-appearance domain is a separate, explicit step applied to the finished array:

predict_combo_model_linear_rgb (photo_stack_lut.py:925) returns model-domain RGB — no projection.
iter_photo_stack_lut_arrays (photo_stack_lut.py:1046) and predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid (photo_stack_lut.py:965) call provider.project_model_linear_rgb_to_appearance (photo_stack_lut.py:1098, photo_stack_lut.py:1041) after model evaluation, then OKLab.

Trap, confirmed from code: that projection is currently an exact pass-through. project_model_linear_rgb_to_appearance (appearance_model.py:432) literally return np.asarray(rgb) — its docstring calls it a “compatibility pass-through for the retired solve-domain conversion.” So today the appearance and model domains coincide here; the call sites keep the seam so a real transform could be reintroduced without touching the evaluator. Do not document this as an active color conversion — it is a no-op slot (the docstring at photo_stack_lut.py:980 that says appearance-named methods are “now an exact model-domain pass-through” is accurate). Camera appearance is handled by the camera transform / ingress elsewhere, not here.
The inf over-budget sentinel
predict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid (photo_stack_lut.py:965) returns (dense, within_budget):

dense is (n_stacks, n_caps, 3) OKLab, initialized to np.inf (photo_stack_lut.py:1024) and filled only for representable cells — cells whose per-filament step count exceeds max_layers stay inf because they cannot exist on the evaluator grid (representable, photo_stack_lut.py:1021).
within_budget is a boolean mask: a cell is allowed when its total color steps fit the height left after the cap (allowed_steps, photo_stack_lut.py:1012–photo_stack_lut.py:1020) and it is representable (photo_stack_lut.py:1022).

The split matters. The dense grid is finite at every representable cell so Stage-4 cap lookups always get a color answer; budget enforcement is the cap planner’s job, and a missing color answer would force the slow row predictor (docstring photo_stack_lut.py:984–photo_stack_lut.py:992). The caller _precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized (staged_solver_helpers.py:131) materializes both views: it copies dense and stamps inf onto the over-budget cells to make the scoring view (staged_solver_helpers.py:175–staged_solver_helpers.py:176), so the zone optimizer’s nearest-cap dE (_score_stack_for_cell, staged_solver_helpers.py:180) can never pick an unprintable stack — the inf distance excludes it — while Stage-4 still reads the finite dense view. inf is the sentinel that says “exists in color space but not in the height budget.”
This entry point is live: _precompute_cap_oklabs_vectorized is imported and called from staged_runner.py:27/staged_runner.py:6310, and the staged runner is what the webapp solve actually executes (run_staged_backend_path, staged_runner.py:11034, dispatched from runner.py:877 — not the legacy solve.py CLI engine).
The zero-cap row-provider fallback (correctness guard)
At the top of predict_subset (photo_stack_lut.py:845) is a deliberate escape hatch. Rows whose cap thickness is zero (cap_steps_d[cap_indices] <= 1e-9) are not evaluated by the fast path. They are turned into StackRequests and handed to provider.predict_stack_model_linear_rgb_batch — the canonical row predictor (photo_stack_lut.py:851–photo_stack_lut.py:867).
Why: a zero cap changes the physical evidence context. A base + color + 0-cap stack is color-over-white, not a sandwich — the model’s cap-transfer and white-context machinery were fit on sandwiched evidence and would mis-extrapolate at the boundary. Rather than special-case every nonlinear stage for the cap-absent geometry, the evaluator delegates that rare boundary to the oracle so the fast LUT path “cannot drift from the canonical stack predictor” (comment, photo_stack_lut.py:847–photo_stack_lut.py:850). It is a correctness guard, not a perf path — zero-cap rows are uncommon and the row cost is acceptable for them. Remaining (non-zero-cap) rows proceed through the vectorized stages.
A second, related guard lives inside _latent_parts (photo_stack_lut.py:254–photo_stack_lut.py:260): when there is no color layer and base and cap are the same white filament, the two adjacent white layers are physically one bulk of white, so the evaluator samples the nonlinear white OD curve at the combined thickness (collapsed_same_white_od_table, photo_stack_lut.py:186) instead of summing two separate curve samples — mirroring how the provider collapses the stack.
The learned correction layer
After the geometric stages, _apply_corrections (photo_stack_lut.py:747) applies the same empirical residual the row predictor applies via apply_photo_stack_correction (appearance_model.py:414). The evaluator compiles the correction artifact’s training rows once (_compile_correction_artifact, photo_stack_lut.py:710), groups them by a context key (unordered_color_key | white_key | evidence_class), and for each target row does a Gaussian-weighted local regression over the matching group’s residuals in a scaled feature space (photo_stack_lut.py:813–photo_stack_lut.py:831), capped by norm and authority. The evidence_class (_evidence_class, photo_stack_lut.py:916) is white_only / single_color_sandwich / cross_color_multilayer_sandwich, matching the corrector’s context partitioning. This stays in OKLab and only nudges L within [0,1].
Where the evaluator is wired in (liveness)
All public entry points are reachable from the live solve, confirmed by grepping callers:









































Functionphoto_stack_lut.pyCaller (confirmed)Statusiter_photo_stack_lut_arrays:1046lut.py:740/:744 (photo-stack LUT build, gated on model_kind == "photo_stack_bundle", lut.py:739)livepredict_unique_stack_cap_oklab_grid:965staged_solver_helpers.py:149/:163 → staged_runner.py:6310livepredict_combo_model_linear_rgb:925appearance_model.py:545/:548 (on-grid dedup fast path) and internally at :1028livecompare_vectorized_provider_predictions:1111test-facing cross-check helper (docstring :1115)live, test-facing_PhotoStackGridEvaluator:153constructed by all three abovelive
The on-grid dedup in appearance_model._predict_unique_combo_model_linear_rgb (appearance_model.py:516) is notable: grid-aligned rows go through the vectorized evaluator, but off-grid thicknesses fall back to the row predictor (appearance_model.py:560–appearance_model.py:574) so callers “never lose exactness, only speed.” Same principle as the zero-cap guard — the fast path covers the grid, the oracle covers everything else.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Filesystem layout, caching, and the recipe cookbook
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: runtime_layout.py establishes Generator’s portable visible folders, immutable-library store, and app-owned Workspace before data_paths.py binds server constants to them; cache_admin.py clears only Workspace cache without escaping through a Windows junction, run_naming.py mints chronological collision-free ids for exports and saved runs, and recipe_cookbook.py rolls each solve’s per-recipe color breakdown into the family → combo → recipe tree the recipe viewer browses.

This page covers the portable layout boundary plus four small, pure-ish Generator modules that consume it. See generator.server for the endpoints that wire them together, and The interactive recipe viewer for the UI the cookbook feeds.

Filesystem layout (runtime_layout.py → data_paths.py)
The packaged launcher resolves and prepares the portable tree before it imports the Generator server. resolve_runtime_layout anchors normal state to the folder containing the executable and produces four distinct Generator-owned roots (runtime_layout.py:127-184). Frozen launch ignores inherited developer path overrides; source-maintenance launches may deliberately supply them.
The cache vs. persistent split
The governing rule is ownership plus visibility: source images and completed exports are plainly visible, installed published libraries are a separate immutable store, and mutable implementation state stays inside the app-owned Workspace.







































































ConstantResolves toLifetimeClear endpoints touch it?UPLOAD_DIR (data_paths.py:103)Generator/Imagesuser-facing source artworknoOUTPUT_DIR (data_paths.py:102)Generator/Exportsuser-facing completed exportsnoMODEL_LIBRARY_DIR (data_paths.py:99)selected UUID library under Generator/Model Librariesimmutable runtime inputnoCACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:106)Generator/Workspace/cacheclearable scratch root— (it is the root)RUN_CACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:107)Workspace/cache/runsper-solve working dirsyesLUT_CACHE_DIR (data_paths.py:108)Workspace/cache/lutsbaked LUTsyes (clear-all only)AUTO_RUNS_DIR (data_paths.py:109)Workspace/cache/auto_runsauto-saved run archivesyesSAVED_RUNS_DIR (data_paths.py:111)Generator/Workspace/saved_runsuser-curated archivesnoCONFIG_DIR (data_paths.py:104)Generator/Workspace/configprinter, settings, and app configurationnoLOG_DIR (data_paths.py:112)Generator/Workspace/logslogsno
OUTPUT_DIR receives only complete export directories. The server builds each export in a hidden sibling .export-stage-* directory and publishes it with one same-filesystem directory rename after every deliverable and manifest update succeeds. Failure and cooperative cancellation remove the stage; read/download routes do not create missing export directories. The clear-cache endpoints remain deliberately unable to touch either completed exports or an active export stage.
GENERATOR_DATA_DIR (data_paths.py:100) is the Workspace, the parent of both cache/ and persistent mutable siblings. The structural safety of “clear cache never deletes saved runs” rests on saved_runs/ being a sibling of cache/, not a child — see the caching section below.
One active immutable model library
initialize_generator_runtime creates/reconciles the installed-library store, installs the bundled seed only when no active selection exists, and resolves one complete active library (runtime_layout.py:322-383). The selection record lives inside Generator’s Workspace; the payload lives under Generator/Model Libraries/{library_id}. If the active library cannot be validated, the launcher supplies a separate recovery root and the server starts in Library Recovery mode instead of falling back to Calibration data or combining partial libraries.
The launcher then applies explicit environment paths before importing data_paths.py (runtime_layout.py:390-430). resolve_data_dir now requires PRISMA_MODEL_LIBRARY_ROOT; Workspace, Images, Exports, and config resolution likewise fail with “Start it through the Prisma launcher” rather than guessing a repository path (data_paths.py:30-96). DATA_DIR is therefore the selected published library for compatibility with older consumers—not a shared Calibration/Generator data root.
Boot: ensure_dirs()
prepare_generator_runtime creates and write-probes Generator/Images, Generator/Exports, Generator/Model Libraries, and Generator/Workspace before the Workspace lock is acquired (runtime_layout.py:207-220). After the launcher applies those roots, ensure_dirs() creates the server’s managed cache/save/log descendants (data_paths.py:115-118). It is called once at server import. LOG_DIR is created on boot but is not swept by either clear endpoint.

Run, export, and save ids (run_naming.py)
Three different id schemes coexist; do not conflate them.
Run-cache id = the request’s card_id
A per-solve working directory is cache/runs/{card_id}. The card_id is client-supplied (the UI’s run/card identifier), not minted by run_naming.py. _current_out_dir() (server.py:1910) builds the path; with no card_id it falls back to the literal "current" (server.py:1910–1919). Before use the id is passed through _validate_card_id() (server.py:1902), which rejects anything not matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$ — this is the traversal/slug guard for run-cache and export dirs alike (_export_out_dir reuses it, server.py:1929).
Export id and save id (minted by run_naming.py)
Both make_export_id (run_naming.py:34) and make_save_id (run_naming.py:54) produce a Windows-safe, chronologically-sortable name of the form {timestamp}-{image-stem} — the timestamp leads so listings sort by time, and the image stem follows for readability (run_naming.py:37-38, run_naming.py:57-58). Neither encodes the palette/label: the palette is recorded in the export manifest (run_naming.py:39-40), and the save’s display label is deliberately excluded so renaming never changes identity (run_naming.py:58-59).
Both run their parts through _slugify (run_naming.py:16), which: normalizes / and \ to spaces before the regex so palette dots aren’t eaten by Path.stem (run_naming.py:22-24); lowercases and collapses any non-[a-z0-9] run to a single - (run_naming.py:25); truncates to _MAX_LEN = 64 (run_naming.py:7, applied run_naming.py:26); falls back to "export" if empty (run_naming.py:8, run_naming.py:27-28); and appends -x to Windows reserved device names like con/nul/com1 (run_naming.py:9-13, run_naming.py:29-30).
Collision handling differs by what counts as “taken”:























MintsCollision checkCallermake_export_idexport folder nameoutput_root/{candidate} directory exists (run_naming.py:46)server.py:5841make_save_idsaved-run id{candidate}.zip or {candidate}.json exists (run_naming.py:66)server.py:6609, auto_run_store.py:74
Both append -2, -3, … as a same-second backstop, trimming the base so the suffix stays within _MAX_LEN (run_naming.py:47-50, run_naming.py:67-69).
Timestamp formats (set by the callers, not run_naming.py)
The timestamp is passed in by the caller, so the format lives in server.py:

Export: datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") (server.py:5838) → e.g. 20260621-143005-steve.
Manual save: same %Y%m%d-%H%M%S (server.py:6607), then make_save_id during archive packing.
Auto save: saved_at or datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") (server.py:6642).
Promotion (auto → saved) reuses the auto record’s original saved_at as the timestamp unless overridden (auto_run_store.py:73), re-minting a fresh save_id against the saved-runs root (auto_run_store.py:74).

Saved-run and auto-run archives are stored as a {save_id}.zip + {save_id}.json sidecar pair, validated on every access by run_store.resolve_save_paths against _SAVE_ID_RE = ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (run_store.py:14, run_store.py:31-33) — the same character class as card_id, enforced independently. Listings sort newest-first by (saved_at, save_id) reversed (run_store.py:69). See generator.run_store / generator.auto_run_store.

Caching (cache_admin.py)
cache_admin.py exists to answer one question safely: “delete the contents of this cache directory, and under no circumstances follow a link out of the cache to delete something else.” On Windows that “link” includes directory junctions (reparse points), which pathlib/shutil.rmtree will happily traverse.
The clear endpoints
Two POST endpoints in server.py call into it (grep-confirmed; these are the only callers):























EndpointSweepsSparesCodePOST /api/cache/clear-runsRUN_CACHE_DIR, AUTO_RUNS_DIR + in-RAM solve cacheLUTs, output, saved_runsserver.py:6508POST /api/cache/clear-allRUN_CACHE_DIR, LUT_CACHE_DIR, AUTO_RUNS_DIR + in-RAMoutput, saved_runsserver.py:6525
Both first call _assert_no_active_job() (server.py:6500), which raises HTTP 409 if any solve/export/compare job is running, then clear the in-RAM solve_cache. Every directory is cleared with root=data_paths.CACHE_DIR, so the boundary is the cache root itself.

Why saved_runs/ is structurally safe: it lives under Generator/Workspace, as a sibling of cache/. safe_clear_dir refuses any target not under its root, and the clear endpoints always pass root=CACHE_DIR. There is no code path that would point a clear at saved_runs/; it is outside the permitted root by construction.

safe_clear_dir(target, *, root) — the containment contract
safe_clear_dir (cache_admin.py:47) deletes the contents of target (keeping target itself) and returns the count of top-level entries removed (cache_admin.py:89-90). It refuses anything questionable by raising OutsideRootError (cache_admin.py:9). The guard is layered, and all of it runs on lexical absolute paths — os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(...)) resolves .. but does not resolve symlinks/junctions (cache_admin.py:57-59). This is the whole trick: lexical paths can’t be redirected by a junction, so the checks below see the intended tree, not a relocated one.

Containment — target must equal root or have root among its lexical parents, else OutsideRootError (cache_admin.py:60-61).
Root + every ancestor must be real dirs — it walks root and all its parents up to the filesystem anchor; if any is a link/junction it refuses (cache_admin.py:66-70). A junction anywhere above the cache would physically relocate the whole tree, so deletion can’t be allowed to start.
Every component root→target must be real — each path part between root and target is checked the same way (cache_admin.py:72-76).
Missing target is a no-op returning 0 (cache_admin.py:77-78).

Junction/symlink-aware deletion
Detection is _is_link_or_junction (cache_admin.py:13): it os.lstats the path (never following), treats S_ISLNK as a link, and additionally checks st_file_attributes & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT (0x400) to catch Windows junctions (cache_admin.py:19-23). When the walker hits a link/junction entry it unlinks the entry itself without recursing through it via _unlink_link (cache_admin.py:26), which tries os.rmdir (junction-to-dir / dir symlink) and falls back to os.unlink (file symlink) (cache_admin.py:29-31). Real subdirectories are recursed with _rm_tree (cache_admin.py:34), which uses os.scandir + is_dir(follow_symlinks=False) so it likewise never crosses a reparse point (cache_admin.py:36-44). Net effect: a junction sitting inside the cache is removed as a single entry; its target is left untouched.
This behavior is exercised by tests/generator/test_cache_admin.py (junction-root refusal at lines 83-84, mid-path component refusal at 113-116) and tests/generator/test_cache_clear_endpoints.py.

The recipe cookbook (recipe_cookbook.py)
The recipe viewer needs to answer “which filament combinations make up this image, and in what proportions?” The cookbook is the aggregator that turns the flat per-recipe breakdown into a browsable tree. It is a pure module — no I/O, no numpy, no server deps (recipe_cookbook.py:14), unit-tested in isolation by tests/generator/test_recipe_cookbook.py.
Input, caller, and what’s already been stripped
build_recipe_cookbook (recipe_cookbook.py:35) is called once, from the artifact-saver in server.py:1665 (grep-confirmed sole caller). It consumes the same per-recipe entries that get written to the *_recipe_breakdown.json artifact, feeding it two scalars from that payload’s totals block:

all_plan_pixels= the breakdown’s all_plan_pixels (sourced from segment_id_map.size in the artifact builder) — the denominator for every area fraction.
base_only_pixels= the breakdown’s excluded_empty_recipe_pixels — pixels whose stack has no colored filament.

Crucially, each entry’s recipe is the ordered stack of colored filaments only — the white base and white cap are excluded upstream before the cookbook ever sees them (recipe_cookbook.py:4-6). The cookbook does no color/optics; it is pure counting. The result is written next to the breakdown as {base}_cookbook.json by the same artifact-saver and reported back as cookbook_filename.
The output tree
The taxonomy is three nested levels plus a flat rollup:
N-color family   →   unordered filament combo   →   specific thickness recipe

Walking the build (recipe_cookbook.py:65-89): each entry is bucketed by n_colors = len(recipe) (recipe_cookbook.py:70) and by an order-insensitive combo = the sorted tuple of filament ids (recipe_cookbook.py:71). Entries with pixel_count <= 0 are skipped (recipe_cookbook.py:68-69). The recipe_key is taken from the entry if present, else recomputed by _recipe_key (recipe_cookbook.py:28), whose "{id}:{thickness:.6g}" join is kept byte-identical to the breakdown’s own key format (the matching format string is server.py:1504-1505; the cookbook’s own comment cites it as server.py:1565) (recipe_cookbook.py:29-32) — so cookbook keys match the breakdown’s.
The returned dict (recipe_cookbook.py:165-172) has:








































FieldMeaningAnchorschema"prisma-recipe-cookbook-v1"recipe_cookbook.py:21, :166total_image_pixelsthe all_plan_pixels denominatorrecipe_cookbook.py:167base_only_pixels0-color pixel countrecipe_cookbook.py:168color_pixelssum over families with n_colors > 0recipe_cookbook.py:161-163familiesthe family → combo → recipe treerecipe_cookbook.py:91-146filamentsper-filament rolluprecipe_cookbook.py:148-159
Every node carries pixel_count and area_fraction, the latter via _frac (recipe_cookbook.py:24), which is numerator/denominator or 0.0 when the denominator is 0 (recipe_cookbook.py:25) — so a zero-pixel image yields all-zero fractions instead of dividing by zero.
The 0-color “Base only” family
If base_only_pixels > 0, a synthetic family is prepended with n_colors: 0, label "Base only", and a single collapsed combo/recipe whose recipe_key is the literal "base-only" and whose filaments list is empty (recipe_cookbook.py:95-119). It “collapses” because there is nothing to slice — family  combo  recipe. When base_only_pixels == 0 the family is omitted entirely (the if at recipe_cookbook.py:95).
Sort order (stable, deterministic)
Ordering is fixed so the UI renders deterministically:

Families: 0-color first (prepended), then ascending n_colors (sorted(families), recipe_cookbook.py:121).
Combos within a family: by descending pixel count, ties broken by the combo tuple — key=lambda c: (-combos[c]["pixels"], c) (recipe_cookbook.py:124).
Recipes within a combo: descending pixel count, ties by recipe_key (recipe_cookbook.py:126-128).
Filament rollup: descending pixel count, ties by filament_id (recipe_cookbook.py:158). Each rollup row also reports recipe_count = the number of distinct recipe keys the filament appears in, tracked via a set (filament_recipe_keys, recipe_cookbook.py:63, :89, counted :154).

Relationship to the viewer
This cookbook JSON is what powers the recipe viewer’s “Recipe cookbook” and “Color Regions” surfaces — see The interactive recipe viewer. The viewer ships both the recipe tree and the filament rollup; which one a user leans on is decided by interaction, not by the backend picking for them. The cookbook is the aggregation; it does not render color — the color-only predicted render is a separate path in generator.server.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: Saving, loading, and auto-capturing runs
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: a completed solve can be packed into a portable, self-contained zip archive (plus an authoritative JSON sidecar) and either deliberately saved by the user or silently auto-captured into a 20-slot ring buffer, then later loaded back into a fresh card — with the loader treating every archive (including uploaded ones) as untrusted input.

This page covers how the generator persists a finished solve so you can come back to it later or hand it to someone else. There are two storage tiers, one archive format, and a careful loader. See also Run cache and per-card artifacts, The staged backend (Stage 0-5), and generator.run_archive / generator.run_store / generator.auto_run_store / generator.run_naming.
The two tiers at a glance








































Saved runs (user-curated)Auto runs (ring buffer)DirectoryGenerator/Workspace/saved_runs/ (data_paths.py:111)Generator/Workspace/cache/auto_runs/ (data_paths.py:109)Created byExplicit user Save actionAutomatically after every completed solveSidecar tier"saved" (server.py:6622-6633)"auto", forced on write (auto_run_store.py:40-42)RetentionKept until the user deletes (run_store.delete_save)Newest 20 only; older ones evicted (auto_run_store.py:12, :43)Survives “Clear cached runs”?Yes — under GENERATOR_DATA_DIR, not sweptNo — auto_runs/ is cache; swept by clear_cache_runs (server.py:6508-6522)Promote-to-saved?n/aYes, via Save on the row → /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote
Both tiers use the same on-disk pair ({save_id}.zip + {save_id}.json) and the same archive format. auto_run_store is a thin re-root of run_store: it just points run_store at AUTO_RUNS_DIR and adds eviction (auto_run_store.py:19-28). The list endpoint merges both tiers and re-sorts newest-first (server.py:6666-6672).
Disk layout: zip + authoritative JSON sidecar
For each run, run_store.write_save writes two sibling files under the store root, named by save_id (run_store.py:46-55):

{save_id}.zip — the portable, self-contained archive (see below). This is the only thing you’d hand to another machine.
{save_id}.json — the sidecar: a small dict that is the authoritative source for the run list and its display label. list_saves reads only the sidecars, never opening a zip (run_store.py:64-66), and rename_save edits only the sidecar label, leaving the zip untouched (run_store.py:104, :99).

Both files are written atomically — to .tmp siblings first, then os.replace swaps them into place (run_store.py:51-55) — so a crash mid-write never leaves a half-written run in the list.
The sidecar carries: save_id, label, saved_at, source_image_name, the palette, a trimmed stats block (mean_de / max_de only), schema_version, and tier (server.py:6622-6633). list_saves sorts entries newest-first by (saved_at, save_id) (run_store.py:69).
save_id identity is stable across renames
make_save_id mints the id as {timestamp}-{image-stem}, slugified and Windows-safe, capped at 64 chars, with same-second collisions getting a -2, -3, … suffix; a candidate collides if either {id}.zip or {id}.json already exists (run_naming.py:54, :66). The display label is deliberately not part of the id (run_naming.py:58-60) — renaming changes the sidecar label but never the identity, so existing zip/sidecar paths stay valid. The id is also a strict allow-list ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ (run_store.py:14); anything else raises SaveNotFoundError before any path is built (run_store.py:32-33).
What’s inside the archive
run_archive.pack_run_archive (run_archive.py:98) builds the zip from already-extracted pieces — it touches no disk and no server state. Members:



































MemberRequiredContentsrun.jsonyesheader + full config + palette + image-domain dims + stats + result + sanitized export_metadata (server.py:6589-6601)thickness_maps.npzyesnp.savez_compressed of tm__<key> thickness arrays, dbg__<key> debug arrays, and ex__<key> export arrays (server.py:6577-6584)image/<file>yesexactly one source-image member; required, non-empty (run_archive.py:110-111)solve_state.jsonoptional{ solve_owned_fingerprint } review-tier state (server.py:6603)run_cache/<relpath>optionalthe entire per-card run-cache subtree (png/bin/json/csv + export bundle), nesting allowed (server.py:6581-6588)
The run_cache/ subtree is copied verbatim so that instant review (contours, surface explorer, recipe viewer) works on a loaded run without re-solving (server.py:6581-6583). Because the per-card cache can be large, pack_run_archive enforces the same member-count (MAX_MEMBERS = 4096) and total-uncompressed-byte (MAX_TOTAL_UNCOMPRESSED_BYTES = 512 MB) ceilings the loader checks, so Save can never produce an archive the loader would reject (run_archive.py:121-133, :37-38). JSON members are serialized to the exact bytes that get written so the byte total matches what the reader later sees (run_archive.py:115-118).
Driving it: the user-facing flows
All flows live behind /api/runs/* in server.py and thin wrappers in app/api.js.
Save a completed solve
The Save button calls saveRun(cardId, label) → POST /api/runs/save (api.js:254-255). Server side (server.py:6653): it requires a completed cached solve for that card or returns 409 (server.py:6545-6550); the source image must still exist on disk or it refuses to write a “hollow” archive (409, server.py:6567-6572); then it packs and writes the pair with tier="saved", returning {save_id, label}. An empty label defaults to the save_id (server.py:6610).
Browse, load, download, rename, delete
The Saved Runs browser lists both tiers via GET /api/runs/saved (api.js:258, server.py:6666). Each row is tagged "Saved" or "Autosave" (app.js:6846-6848) and offers:

Load → loadSavedRun(saveId, tier) → POST /api/runs/load with {save_id, tier} (api.js:262-263, server.py:6938).
Download → a direct link to /api/runs/saved/{id}/download or /api/runs/auto/{id}/download (app.js:6866-6869, server.py:6675, :6686) streaming the raw zip.
Rename (saved only) → POST /api/runs/saved/{id}/rename (api.js:278, server.py:6707) — sidecar label only.
Delete → DELETE /api/runs/saved/{id} for saved runs or DELETE /api/runs/auto/{id} for autosaves (api.js:270-276, server.py:6715, :6727).
Save (auto only) → promote (next section).

You can also load an uploaded zip that didn’t come from this machine: uploadSavedRun(file) → POST /api/runs/load-upload (multipart) (api.js:282-288, server.py:6952).
Delete is idempotent but surfaces locked files
run_store.delete_save removes both files with missing_ok=True, so deleting an already-gone run is a benign no-op (run_store.py:91). But a file that exists yet can’t be removed — e.g. a zip locked open on Windows — raises the typed SaveDeletionError (run_store.py:92-95), which the endpoint converts into a clean 409 telling the user to close the program holding it (server.py:6715-6724), rather than crashing.
Auto-capture and promotion
Capture happens automatically on every solve
At the end of a successful solve, once the completed-solve cache entry is written, the staged backend calls _maybe_write_auto_run(card_id, solve, config) (server.py:5689-5690). This packs the identical archive Save would (same _pack_completed_run_archive), but with tier="auto" and an auto-generated label Auto <timestamp> (server.py:6638-6647). The whole thing is wrapped in a try/except that only logs on failure (server.py:6648-6649) — auto-capture is best-effort and must never break a solve. (This is the live The staged backend (Stage 0-5) path, not the legacy CLI engine in solve.py.)
write_auto_run forces tier="auto" onto the sidecar regardless of what the caller passed (auto_run_store.py:40-42), then immediately evicts.
Ring-buffer eviction keeps the newest 20
After each write, evict_old_auto_runs lists the auto sidecars newest-first and deletes everything past index limit (default AUTO_RUN_RETENTION_LIMIT = 20) (auto_run_store.py:46-54, :12). A negative limit is clamped to 0 (:48-49). Because auto runs share run_store’s newest-first ordering, “past index 20” is reliably the oldest records.
Promote an auto run to a saved run
The auto row’s Save button calls promoteAutoRun(saveId) → POST /api/runs/auto/{id}/promote (api.js:266-267, server.py:6697). auto_run_store.promote_auto_run (auto_run_store.py:57):

resolves the auto pair via run_store.resolve_save_paths (no raw f-string paths from endpoint-controlled ids — auto_run_store.py:66-68);
mints a fresh saved-tier save_id under SAVED_RUNS_DIR, preserving the original timestamp (auto_run_store.py:73-74);
rewrites the sidecar with the new id, tier="saved", and a promoted_from_auto_id breadcrumb (auto_run_store.py:75-80);
moves the zip bytes unchanged into saved_runs/, then publishes the new sidecar. A failed initial ZIP move removes the staged sidecar; if sidecar publication fails after the ZIP moved, promotion rolls the ZIP back and removes the stage so the auto record survives for a retry.

Promotion is gated by _assert_no_active_job so it can’t race a running solve/export/compare. The endpoint returns the rewritten sidecar, and promoteSelectedSavedRun derives its new saved:<new save_id> selection key from that response before refreshing the list. The newly promoted row therefore remains selected even when collision handling gave it a suffixed id. Once promoted, the run lives under saved_runs/ and survives a cache clear.
How loading works
Loading a run never restores into the original card; it builds a fresh “loaded-” card and replays the archive into it.
load_run (server.py:6938) and load_run_upload (server.py:6952) both gate on _assert_no_active_job (server.py:6943, :6954), then funnel into _load_from_bytes → read_run_archive → _rehydrate_loaded_archive:

Untrusted parse — run_archive.read_run_archive validates the zip (see safety section) and returns a ParsedArchive (run_archive.py:149). On any ArchiveError, the endpoint returns HTTP 400 (server.py:6448-6449).
Fresh card id — _fresh_loaded_card_id mints a collision-free loaded-<timestamp> card (server.py:6743-6751).
Image — written to a save-scoped unique path {card_id}-{name} under the images dir; config.image_path is rewritten to it (server.py:6872-6875).
Thickness/debug/export maps — the npz is split into thickness_maps (tm__), debug_maps (dbg__), and export_maps (ex__) (server.py:6876-6883).
Run-cache subtree — the whole run_cache/ tree is restored under the fresh card’s dir, so /api/run-cache/files serves contours/explorer/recipe (server.py:6884-6890); relpaths were already validated safe during parse.
URL rebasing — every ?run=<old> in the result payload (top-level and nested url maps/lists) is rewritten to the new card id by _rebase_run_urls (server.py:6754-6764, :6892).
Cache entry — a synthetic status="complete" solve entry is written into session["solve_cache"], with grouping / solved_plan / profiles / material-exposure audit set to None (server.py:6895-6915). The loader also rejects retired preferred-length/soft-warning artifacts and disabled detail-cap configurations before rehydration (server.py:6776-6856).

The frontend then applies the loaded run and (best-effort) restores its palette to the deck (app.js:7260, :7270-7320).
Safety: the loader assumes archives are hostile
read_run_archive is built to be safe on untrusted zips — uploaded archives go through the exact same path as locally-saved ones. It never calls extractall; every byte is read by explicit member name. The guards (run_archive.py:149-194):

Member-count ceiling — > MAX_MEMBERS (4096) → reject (run_archive.py:158-159).
No duplicate member names (run_archive.py:161-162).
Total-uncompressed-byte ceiling — sum of file_size > 512 MB → reject before decompressing (zip-bomb guard) (run_archive.py:163-165).
Closed allow-list of member names — only run.json, thickness_maps.npz, solve_state.json, one image/<leaf>, and run_cache/<relpath> are permitted; everything else is rejected (_member_is_safe, run_archive.py:70-82).
Path-traversal refusal — empty / absolute / drive-letter (:) / backslash / . / .. / ../-escaping relpaths are all rejected, including each nested run_cache/ path (_is_safe_relpath, run_archive.py:56-67).
Symlink / non-regular refusal — any member whose external-attr type field is set and isn’t a regular file is rejected; Windows writestr members (no type field) correctly pass (_zipinfo_is_symlink, run_archive.py:85-95).
Required members present — run.json and thickness_maps.npz must exist (run_archive.py:172-174).
Schema gate — run.json.schema_version must be in ACCEPTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS = {1} or reject (run_archive.py:176-177, :29).
Exactly one image, non-empty (run_archive.py:180-188).

The upload route adds a compressed-upload cap on top: it reads the multipart body in 1 MB chunks and aborts with HTTP 413 once it passes MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (512 MB), before the full read and the uncompressed zip-bomb check, and never trusts a client Content-Length (server.py:6955-6965, run_archive.py:39).
Liveness notes
Every endpoint and helper below was confirmed wired front-to-back by grepping callers:

saveRun/loadSavedRun/promoteAutoRun/renameSavedRun/deleteSavedRun/uploadSavedRun are all defined in app/api.js:254-289 and the solve-run Save button calls saveRun at app.js:6978; the Saved Runs modal loads at app.js:7260, promotes at app.js:7180, and uploads at app.js:12914.
_maybe_write_auto_run is called from the live staged-solve completion path at server.py:5690.
clear_cache_runs (server.py:6508) sweeps AUTO_RUNS_DIR but not SAVED_RUNS_DIR, confirming auto-runs are cache and saved runs are durable.

prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.title: The preprocessing evaluation harness
prisma-lithophane-generator/technical-re.content:
In one sentence: an offline A/B bakeoff that solves two images through the production pipeline under one shared config and reports a fixed metric bundle (mean/p95 dE, out-of-gamut pixels, small-component count, cap total-variation), optionally dropping predicted-PNG + heatmap + report.json artifacts to disk.

This page documents the evaluation/ package under Prisma/generator/: how to drive it from the CLI or a Python caller, what each metric means, and the generator.evaluation internals. It exists to answer “did this preprocessing operator (or solver tweak) actually help?” with comparable numbers instead of eyeballing two renders.
What it is for
The harness compares two versions of an image — a baseline and a candidate — by running each through the full generator solve and diffing the results. It is corpus-agnostic: both images are passed in as explicit arrays, so the difference between baseline and candidate can be anything the caller wants (a preprocessing operator applied to one, a different denoise setting, etc.). It does not generate the candidate; you do that, then hand both to evaluate_pair.
Both arms run through the same SolveConfig, so any metric delta is attributable to the image difference, not config drift.
The contract: evaluate_pair
The single public entry point is evaluate_pair(request, *, modules_path=None, module_state=None) at Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_harness.py:105. It takes an EvaluationInput and returns an EvaluationResult.



































SymbolWhereRoleEvaluationInputpreprocessing_harness.py:73Frozen dataclass: case_id, baseline_image, candidate_image, solve_config, optional out_dir.EvaluationMetricspreprocessing_harness.py:82Frozen dataclass holding all 11 metric fields (see below).EvaluationResultpreprocessing_harness.py:97Carries both SolveResult objects, the metrics bundle, and artifact_paths.EvaluationRunErrorpreprocessing_harness.py:57Raised (not swallowed) when either arm’s solve fails; tags .arm ("baseline"/"candidate") and .original.evaluate_pairpreprocessing_harness.py:105Runs both arms, aggregates metrics, optionally renders artifacts.
Flow

Two solves. _run_arm (preprocessing_harness.py:157) calls solve_full (from generator.facade) once per image. solve_full runs run_pipeline under FULL_PRESET (facade.py:891-912), i.e. the staged production backend — not the legacy 6-step CLI engine in solve.py. If either solve raises, it is wrapped as EvaluationRunError(arm, exc) (preprocessing_harness.py:173-174) rather than crashing silently.
Metric aggregation. _compute_metrics (preprocessing_harness.py:177) reads the two SolveResult objects and builds the EvaluationMetrics bundle.
Optional artifacts. Only when request.out_dir is not None (preprocessing_harness.py:135) does it lazily import render_evaluation_artifacts and write files. The lazy import is deliberate — in-memory metric callers never pull in PIL (preprocessing_harness.py:136).

Metrics are always returned in memory; artifacts are opt-in.
Where the metrics come from
_compute_metrics reads these SolveResult accessors (defined in generator.facade):



































Source fieldAccessorAnchordE mapresult.de_mapfacade.py:282-285 (prefers diagnostics[MapKey.DE], falls back to thickness_maps)Gamut maskresult.gamut_maskfacade.py:288-291Per-filament thicknessresult.thickness_mapsfacade.py:234-263White-cap mapresult.cap_mapfacade.py:293-295 (MapKey.WHITE_CAP)Predicted renderresult.predict_image()facade.py:313-325
The solver pitch used for area scaling is config.solver_fine_pitch_mm (preprocessing_harness.py:188), read off the baseline’s SolveResult.config.
The metric bundle
EvaluationMetrics (preprocessing_harness.py:82) holds eleven fields — for the five base metrics, both arms plus one delta where relevant:



































MetricBaseline / candidate fieldsHow computedMean dEbaseline_mean_de, candidate_mean_de, delta_mean_dede_map.mean() per arm; delta = candidate - baseline (preprocessing_harness.py:184-199). Empty map → 0.0.p95 dEbaseline_p95_de, candidate_p95_de95th percentile of the dE map via _p95 → np.percentile(arr, 95.0) (preprocessing_harness.py:222-225). Empty → 0.0.Out-of-gamut pixelsbaseline_oog_pixels, candidate_oog_pixels_oog_pixels counts True cells in the boolean gamut_mask: int(mask.sum()) (preprocessing_harness.py:228-230).Small-component countbaseline_small_component_count, candidate_small_component_countcount_small_components over the thickness maps (see below).Cap total-variationbaseline_cap_total_variation, candidate_cap_total_variationcap_total_variation over cap_map (see below).
Note dE is the only metric with a precomputed delta_* field; for the rest the caller diffs the two arms themselves (the bakeoff runner does exactly this).
Metric primitives — preprocessing_metrics.py
Two metrics are non-trivial and live in Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_metrics.py:
count_small_components (preprocessing_metrics.py:32) — counts speckle. For each per-filament thickness map (keys starting with __ are diagnostics and skipped, preprocessing_metrics.py:55-57):

Mark a pixel “occupied” if its thickness exceeds 5% of that map’s max (_SMALL_COMPONENT_REL_THRESHOLD = 0.05, preprocessing_metrics.py:28-29; applied at :64).
Run 8-connectivity connected-component labeling — the 3×3 structuring element of ones (preprocessing_metrics.py:52) via scipy.ndimage.label (:67).
Convert each component’s pixel count to physical area as pixel_count × pixel_pitch_mm² (preprocessing_metrics.py:51, :72).
Accumulate the count of components whose area is below min_area_mm2 (preprocessing_metrics.py:73).

The min_area_mm2 threshold is derived in the harness, not hard-coded: feature_scale_mm², where feature_scale_mm comes from resolve_feature_scale_mm (preprocessing_harness.py:192). That helper returns 2.0 × nozzle_diameter (the constant _FEATURE_WIDTHS_PER_NOZZLE = 2.0, feature_scale.py:37; applied at feature_scale.py:73), i.e. 0.40 mm at the default 0.20 mm nozzle, so min_area = 0.40² = 0.16 mm² (preprocessing_harness.py:193). This is the value the retired cleanup_min_area_mm2 carried (preprocessing_harness.py:189-193).
cap_total_variation (preprocessing_metrics.py:77) — measures how “busy” the white-cap surface is. Returns the anisotropic L1 total variation Σ(|Δx| + |Δy|) over the 2-D cap map: abs(diff(axis=1)).sum() + abs(diff(axis=0)).sum() (preprocessing_metrics.py:89). It is a grid-space sum, not a per-mm integral (preprocessing_metrics.py:82) — a non-2-D or empty map returns 0.0 (:85). Lower means a smoother cap.
Artifacts — preprocessing_render.py
When out_dir is set, render_evaluation_artifacts (Prisma/generator/evaluation/preprocessing_render.py:49) writes exactly four files:






























FileConstant / anchorContentbaseline_predicted.pngpreprocessing_render.py:44, written :64Baseline predict_image() as RGB PNG.candidate_predicted.pngpreprocessing_render.py:45, written :68Candidate predict_image().delta_de_heatmap.pngpreprocessing_render.py:46, written :72Signed candidate − baseline dE heatmap.report.jsonREPORT_FILENAME preprocessing_render.py:43, written :76{"case_id": ..., **asdict(metrics)} (:121).
The heatmap (_save_delta_de_heatmap, preprocessing_render.py:89) is signed: it normalizes delta = candidate − baseline by its peak absolute value, then puts positive delta (candidate worse) in the red channel and negative delta (candidate better) in the green channel (preprocessing_render.py:94, :104-111). Mismatched shapes are defensively cropped to the smaller grid (:97-103), though they are expected to match.
report.json’s schema is locked to the EvaluationMetrics dataclass via asdict (preprocessing_render.py:121); the drift-regression test in tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_metrics.py guards it.
How to drive it
From the CLI
Prisma/generator/preprocessing_eval_cli.py is a thin wrapper that loads two images, builds a shared SolveConfig, calls evaluate_pair, and prints the report to stdout (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:97-121). Artifacts are opt-in via --out-dir (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:72-74).
python preprocessing_eval_cli.py \
    --case-id my_case \
    --baseline baseline.png \
    --candidate candidate.png \
    --profiles Prisma/data/filaments/profiles \
    --palette bambu-basic-cyan bambu-basic-yellow \
    --white-base panchroma-matte-cotton-white \
    --out-dir /tmp/eval_out

Required flags: --case-id, --baseline, --candidate, --profiles, --palette (one or more filament IDs), --white-base (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:61-71). Images are EXIF-transposed and forced to RGB uint8 on load (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:84-86). --solver-preset is parsed with full as its only accepted value (preprocessing_eval_cli.py:49, :75-80); the current CLI does not use it to select another preset because the harness always calls solve_full.
From Python
from evaluation import EvaluationInput, evaluate_pair  # evaluation/__init__.py:3
 
result = evaluate_pair(EvaluationInput(
    case_id="my_case",
    baseline_image=baseline_u8,   # np.ndarray HxWx3 uint8
    candidate_image=candidate_u8,
    solve_config=cfg,             # facade.SolveConfig
    out_dir=None,                 # set a Path to also write artifacts
))
print(result.metrics.delta_mean_de)
The package re-exports the full surface (Prisma/generator/evaluation/__init__.py:15): evaluate_pair, the three dataclasses, EvaluationRunError, and the two metric primitives.
The bakeoff runner script
scripts/evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py is the F4 MVT batch runner that sweeps the landed first-wave preprocessing operators across a small real-photo corpus. Its run_bakeoff (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:281) loops a 5-photo corpus (_CORPUS, :84) × the operator set A1/B1/B3/C1/C2 (_OPERATORS, :95). For each cell it:

Applies the operator offline to the source raster via _offline_apply (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:189) to produce the candidate — both arms then solve with an empty preprocessing slot (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:143-145). This sidesteps the single-module_state constraint of the harness while still exercising each operator’s real kernel (:3-8).
Calls evaluate_pair with a per-case out_dir (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:315).
Assigns a coarse _verdict label — promising / neutral / harmful / needs_tuning (evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:219) — by diffing the metrics itself (the bundle only ships the dE delta precomputed).

It writes runs/<image>__<op>/... per-case artifacts plus summary.json and summary.csv (_write_summary, evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py:379-405). Key flags: --out-dir (required), --max-edge-px (default 256, :442-445), --palette, --white-base, --cleanup-enabled/--no-cleanup-enabled (:458-469), and --solver-backend (default dual_resolution; use joint_lut to expose raw per-pixel speckle for the small-component metric, :471-487).
Two sibling runner scripts reuse the harness internals (_compute_metrics + render_evaluation_artifacts, not the evaluate_pair entry point) for narrower studies: scripts/evaluate_b1_b3_preservation.py and scripts/evaluate_b1_parameter_sweep.py.
Liveness
All symbols below are wired and exercised as of 2026-06-21:

evaluate_pair / harness package — imported by preprocessing_eval_cli.py:42, the evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py runner (:59), the package re-export evaluation/__init__.py:3, and tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_harness.py. The two evaluate_b1_* sibling scripts do not call evaluate_pair; they import the harness internals _compute_metrics + render_evaluation_artifacts directly. Live.
render_evaluation_artifacts — called by evaluate_pair under the out_dir branch (preprocessing_harness.py:139-141); exercised end-to-end by tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_harness.py (the out_dir write-out test) and imported directly by both evaluate_b1_* sibling scripts. Live.
count_small_components / cap_total_variation — called from _compute_metrics (preprocessing_harness.py:203, :213), re-exported (evaluation/__init__.py:10), and tested in tests/generator/test_preprocessing_evaluation_metrics.py. Live.
Bakeoff runner scripts — evaluate_preprocessing_first_bakeoff.py, evaluate_b1_b3_preservation.py, evaluate_b1_parameter_sweep.py are standalone scripts/ entry points (run by hand, not imported by the app). They are research tooling, not part of the webapp request path; their last edits date to 2026-04-22..06-13. Live as CLIs, unconfirmed whether re-run recently.

Caveats

Production solve path. Both arms go through solve_full → run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET (facade.py:891-912) — the staged backend, the same engine the webapp uses. The metrics reflect production solver behavior, including grouping/cleanup, not the legacy solve.py CLI engine.
CLI surface versus implementation. preprocessing_eval_cli.py exposes --solver-preset, but accepts only full and does not pass the value separately because evaluate_pair always selects solve_full. The bakeoff parser help text still mentions A2, while the current _OPERATORS map contains five operators: A1, B1, B3, C1, and C2. These are tooling inconsistencies, not additional production paths.
Shapes must match. Metrics assume baseline and candidate solved to the same grid (same config, same image dimensions). The heatmap renderer crops defensively (preprocessing_render.py:97) but the dE mean/p95 do not align grids — feed same-sized images.
Cap-TV is grid-space. cap_total_variation is a raw grid sum (preprocessing_metrics.py:82); it is only comparable between two solves at the same resolution. Do not compare TV across differing solver_fine_pitch_mm.

Related

The staged backend (Stage 0-5) — what run_pipeline / FULL_PRESET actually does
Preprocessing operators — the A/B/C operator kernels the bakeoff sweeps
Delta E and the gamut mask — what de_map and gamut_mask mean
generator.thickness_maps — MapKey, ThicknessMaps, the __-prefixed diagnostic keys
